title: test: make relocate and remove assertions able to fail
body:
Five test assertions checked paths that are never created, so they passed no matter what `wt` did. This points each one at the path the code actually uses, or replaces it with a check that inspects the outcome directly. No production code changes.

- **`step_relocate.rs`, both blocked-occupant tests:** the "not stranded in staging" check looked for `.git/wt/staging/relocate/alpha`. Relocate names its temp entries `<index>-<branch>` ([`relocate.rs`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/322735d78d775985c4ff16fa3f3cf835bad987d1/src/commands/relocate.rs#L771)). The chain test's "misplaced" check looked for `repo.alpha/alpha`, but `git worktree move` into an existing directory nests the source's basename instead. Both tests now assert that the staging directory is gone (the executor removes it once it is empty) and that each path still holds its expected branch.
- **`test_relocate_swap`:** it only checked that `repo.alpha` and `repo.beta` exist, which was already true before the command ran. It now checks which branch each path holds.
- **`test_remove_partial_success`:** it checked `<parent>/feature`, but the worktree lives at `<parent>/repo.feature`. It now uses the path `add_worktree` returns.
- **`test_force_remove_interrupted_status_preserves_worktrees`:** it built the staged name from the branch (`interrupted-status-<epoch>`), but staging uses the worktree's registration id (`repo.interrupted-status`, per `generate_removing_path`). It now asserts that `staged_trash_entries` is empty.

The PR also moves one unisolated `std::process::Command::new("git")` in `test_remove_no_argument_in_moved_worktree_refuses` onto `repo.git_command()`, per the Git-isolation rule in `tests/AGENTS.md`.

The new assertions pass on current `main`. That's expected: they now guard behavior that already works rather than reproduce a bug. All `step_relocate` tests and the 200 `remove::` integration tests pass locally, and clippy is clean.

Found by the nightly survey of `tests/integration_tests/{step_relocate,remove}.rs`.

title: Install the Claude Code plugin with one command
body:
`claude plugin install worktrunk --marketplace max-sixty/worktrunk` adds the marketplace when Claude Code doesn't have it yet, then installs the plugin, so the Claude Code install is one command instead of `marketplace add` followed by `install`. `wt config plugins claude install` now runs that command, and its prompt preview, `--help` and the Agent Integration page show it.

To weigh: `--marketplace` needs Claude Code 2.1.292 (released 2026-10-06). An older CLI rejects the option, and `wt config plugins claude install` reports the failed command. Checked live against 2.1.328 with a fresh config directory: the first run adds the marketplace and installs, a rerun succeeds as already installed, and a same-named marketplace from another source fails the same way `marketplace add` does.

Max asked for the single-line form, after sparkjoy's README. `wt hook pre-merge` passes; the test for a failing second step goes with the second step.

title: fix(switch): keep --path and --execute in the leftover-branch hint
body:
When `wt switch --create` failed after `git worktree add -b` had already written the branch, the leftover-branch hint suggested a bare `wt switch <branch>`. Following it created the worktree at the `worktree-path` template location instead of the `--path` given, and skipped the `--execute` command. `WorktreeCreationFailed` is raised in `execute_switch`, whose errors weren't wrapped in `WithSwitchSuggestion` the way `plan_switch`'s are, so the hint had no flags to draw on.

`SwitchPipeline::run` now wraps that variant with the switch context, and the hint applies it. The hint becomes e.g. `wt switch stranded --path=blocked/stranded --execute='echo hi' -- extra`. `--create` is not in the context, so it stays out of the suggestion, which is correct now that the branch exists. Other `execute_switch` errors pass through unchanged, so their context chains and downcasts are untouched.

`test_switch_create_leftover_branch_hint_keeps_flags` fails on `main` (the hint ends at `wt switch stranded`) and passes with this change. The existing leftover-branch test still covers the no-flags form.

#4705 adds a hint for pre-start failures on the same `execute_switch` path. If it suggests a `wt switch` command, it can reuse this wrapping.

Closes #4839 — automated triage
author: worktrunk-bot

title: fix: give each detached worktree its own summary cache directory
body:
Every detached worktree wrote its LLM summary to the same cache directory, `summary/(detached)/`, because the directory was keyed by the branch string and both `wt list --full` and the picker pass `(detached)` for a row without a branch. `CachedSummary::write` trims that directory to one entry after each write, so two detached worktrees with changes evicted each other, and the next run called the LLM for both again. A detached row's directory key now includes a hash of its worktree path. Named branches keep their existing directories, so no cached summary has to be regenerated. The JSON `branch` field still reads `(detached)`, so `wt config state get` displays these rows the same way, with one row per detached worktree instead of one shared row.

`test_detached_worktrees_keep_separate_cached_summaries` creates two detached worktrees with different uncommitted changes and summarizes each one twice. On the old code, the second summary of the first worktree re-ran the LLM command (`left: "regenerated"`, `right: "Summary A"`). It passes with the fix.

Detached summaries cached by earlier releases sit in the shared `summary/(detached)/` directory. A detached write now removes that directory, so `wt config state get` doesn't keep listing the pre-upgrade summary beside the current one. It is kept when a local branch named `(detached)` exists, because Git allows that name and its summaries use the same directory. `test_detached_summary_prunes_legacy_shared_entry` and `test_detached_summary_keeps_real_detached_named_branch` start with that directory populated and cover both cases.

The callers now pass `Option<&str>` for the branch instead of the `"(detached)"` sentinel, and `summary.rs` maps `None` to the display name.

**Not covered:** two worktrees on the same branch (`git worktree add --force`) still share a directory and can still evict each other. Fixing that means putting the worktree path in every row's key, which forces a one-time regeneration of every cached summary. The issue leaves that trade-off to a maintainer.

Refs #4838 — automated triage
author: worktrunk-bot

title: test(approval): make approval PTY assertions able to fail
body:
Three assertions in `tests/integration_tests/approval_pty.rs` couldn't fail, so the regressions they were written to catch would have passed. This PR changes only the tests. All 19 `approval_pty` tests pass locally with `--features shell-integration-tests`.

- **The merge hook checks matched text the prompt and the skip line both print.** `test_merge_decline_append_keeps_approved_hooks` is the regression test for approved hooks still running when the append is declined. It asserted `output.contains("pre-commit hook")`. But if the hook were skipped instead, `wt` prints "Skipping pre-commit hooks (--no-hooks)", which contains that string. The hook now runs `echo hook-$((40+2))` and the test asserts `hook-42`, which only executing the hook prints. The test also calls `assert_no_spurious_no_hooks`, as the neighbouring decline tests do. `test_merge_prompts_hooks_and_append_separately` gets the same hook change.
- **The "separate prompts" test never checked for two prompts.** It sent `"y\ny\n"` together at the first `[y/N`, so a single combined prompt would also have passed. It now waits for each prompt before answering it and asserts that `Allow and remember?` appears twice.
- **The "only 2 commands" checks were always true.** `output.contains("2")` matched the ANSI reset `ESC[22m` that forced colour always emits. Both mixed approved/unapproved tests now match the ANSI-stripped `needs approval to execute 2 commands`.

title: chore: correct stale comments in switch, config loading, and two test files
body:
Comment-only corrections from the nightly survey, plus one parameter rename. No behavior changes.

- **`plan_switch` docstring** listed an "invalid default branch" warning. Nothing prints it now: when the cached default no longer resolves, `plan_switch` quietly creates from HEAD.
- **`SwitchPipeline::yes`** said `--yes` forces past clobber checks. It doesn't. Only `clobber` reaches `plan_switch` and `validate_worktree_creation`, and `yes` reaches `execute_switch` only as `CommandContext::yes`. That parameter was named `force`, which suggested the same wrong thing, so it is now `yes`.
- **`add_hook_skip_hint`** said `wt switch --create` gets the hint because post-start hooks run. Post-start hooks run in the background and never return this error. The hooks that do return it are pre-switch (`execute_hook`) and pre-start (`execute_planned_hook`).
- **`UserConfig::load`** listed four layers. `load_with_warnings` applies `--config-set` overrides as a fifth.
- **`repository_ext`** referred to a `Branch` remove target. The variant is `RemoveTarget::BranchOnly`.
- **`test_rust_log_overrides_verbose_flag`** said there was nothing to assert at `-vv`. Its body asserts that `RUST_LOG=error` at `-vv` leaves `trace.log` and `subprocess.log` empty.
- **`approval_pty.rs`**: six tests said `configure_shell_integration()` produces a "Restart shell" hint, but none of their snapshots contain one. Its purpose is to keep the shell-install prompt out of the output.

There is no regression test because nothing executable changed apart from the rename. `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean, and the touched `diagnostic.rs` test passes locally.

body:
Updates the generated Tend workflows from 0.3.26 to 0.3.27. The workflow diff only bumps the version pins on `max-sixty/tend/claude` and `setup-runtime`; the changes below ship in those actions and their bundled skills ([compare](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/compare/0.3.26...0.3.27)).

What changes for this repo:

- **Stalled issues get picked up again.** Nightly now runs the open-work checks that used to live in review-runs. It restarts any open `tend-ci-cause` issue with no other assignee, no queued or running Tend run, and no open PR that would close it. Weekly reads the other open issues where the bot commented last and decides which ones need follow-up (max-sixty/tend#1688).
- **Nightly files the bugs it doesn't fix.** A reachable defect the sweep finds but can't fix becomes an issue, or a comment on an existing one, instead of a line in the step summary (max-sixty/tend#1699).
- **Outage trackers closed by other sessions still get drained.** Review-runs now marks the trackers it drains, so it still reads the run rows of a `tend-outage` tracker that a nightly or triage session closed (max-sixty/tend#1700).
- **The sandbox gets its own `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`.** It used to inherit the runner's directory, which the sandbox user can't open (max-sixty/tend#1697).

title: fix(shell): read --source only as the wrapper's first argument
body:
The bash, zsh, and fish shell wrappers treated every `--source` on the command line as their own dev flag: they dropped it and ran wt through `cargo run`. A `--source` meant for a command wt launches was taken too, so `wt step tether -- uv run leaf-dev preview --source page.html` failed with "could not find `Cargo.toml`" (exit 101). The wrappers now take `--source` only as the first argument (`wt --source switch …`) and pass everything after it to wt unchanged.

Stopping the scan at `--` would fix the reported command but still take the flag from custom `wt-<name>` subcommands, which receive their arguments verbatim without a `--`. wt itself has no `--source` flag, so a fixed leading position is the one place the wrapper can claim it. The cost is that `wt list --source` now errors with clap's "unexpected argument" instead of running from source. In completion mode the wrapper now passes the words unchanged, `--source` included, and the binary's completer already handles it (`test_complete_init_shell_all_variations` covers `wt --source config shell init <TAB>`). Nushell and PowerShell have no `--source` and are unchanged. Using `"$@"` instead of a rebuilt array also stops bash 3.2 under `set -u` from failing on `wt` with no arguments.

Requested by max-sixty after the failure above in a leaf worktree. The new `test_source_flag_only_as_first_argument` runs the generated bash, zsh, and fish wrappers against argv-printing stubs and fails on all three with the old templates; the pre-merge gate passes locally.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max-sixty_

title: fix(config): reject vars keys git would lowercase or refuse
body:
`wt config state vars set Ticket=ABC` printed "Set **Ticket** for main", but git stores config variable names lowercased, so the value reads back as `ticket`. A hook or custom column that references `{{ vars.Ticket }}` renders empty, and `vars list` / `state get` show a different key than the one that was set. A key that starts with a digit (`1st=…`) passed validation and then failed with git's bare `error: invalid key`.

`validate_vars_key` now requires a lowercase first letter followed by lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, which is the subset git stores verbatim. The `vars` help text and its generated doc mirrors say so.

**Interface note:** the validator is shared by `set`, `get`, and `clear`, so `vars get Ticket` and `vars clear Ticket` now error too, where before git's case-insensitive lookup let them match the stored `ticket`. No stored key can contain uppercase, so the lowercase spelling always works. Lowercasing input on `set` would be the alternative if keeping existing scripts that pass mixed-case keys working matters more than a clear failure. Neither choice fixes a template that already spells the key in mixed case.

Found by the nightly survey of `src/commands/config/state.rs`. The new `test_vars_set_rejects_keys_git_cannot_store_verbatim` (uppercase and leading-digit cases) failed before the change and passes after it. The existing invalid-key snapshot and `test_docs_are_in_sync` are updated.

title: ci: publish release binaries to PyPI as platform wheels
body:
Adds a PyPI channel for the release, as requested in #4822: `uvx --from worktrunk wt`, `worktrunk` as a `pyproject.toml` dependency, and PEP 723 scripts. Instead of building with maturin, a new job turns the five GitHub Release archives into wheels with `wt` and `git-wt` in the scripts directory. PyPI then ships the same bytes as GitHub Releases, Homebrew and winget, including the SignPath-signed `wt.exe`.

**Needs before the first publish:** a pending trusted publisher on PyPI for project `worktrunk` (still unregistered — `pypi.org/pypi/worktrunk/json` returns 404), with owner `max-sixty`, repo `worktrunk`, workflow `release.yaml` and environment `release`. Until that exists, `publish-pypi` fails on the next release. That doesn't block the rest of the release, because the job isn't in `announce`'s needs.

### Changes

- **`.github/build-wheels.py`** (stdlib only) reads each `worktrunk-<target>.{tar.xz,zip}` and writes `worktrunk-<version>-py3-none-<platform>.whl` containing the two binaries plus METADATA (README as the description, with relative links pointed at the release tag so the logo renders on PyPI; `License-Expression: MIT OR Apache-2.0`), LICENSE, WHEEL and RECORD. The timestamps are fixed, so the same archives give identical wheels. It errors if any of the five targets is missing, or if the version isn't plain `X.Y.Z`.
- **`build-pypi-wheels`** runs after `host`. It downloads the release archives, checks them against their `.sha256` files, builds the wheels, runs `twine check --strict`, and install-smoke-tests the Linux wheel. On PRs it runs against the latest release and doesn't publish, so the packaging gets exercised on every PR. That adds one ~100 MB download job per PR.
- **`publish-pypi`** (environment `release`, `id-token: write`) uploads the wheels with `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish`, pinned to the SHA of v1.14.3. Prereleases are skipped, as Homebrew skips them.
- The PyPI long description opens with a one-line note marking the package experimental, naming GitHub Releases, Homebrew and cargo as the main install channels.
- The release skill (`.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md`) now lists AUR and PyPI (experimental) among the channels `release.yaml` publishes to.
- `.github/AGENTS.md` now lists PyPI among the `release` environment's OIDC uses.

Platform tags: the Linux archives are static musl builds, so they get both `manylinux_2_17` and `musllinux_1_1` tags. macOS uses Rust's default floors (`macosx_10_12_x86_64`, `macosx_11_0_arm64`), and Windows uses `win_amd64`.

### Verification

I ran the job's steps locally against the v0.82.0 release assets: all five checksums matched, all five wheels passed `twine check --strict`, and the x86_64 Linux wheel installed with pip, `uv pip` and `uvx --from worktrunk wt --version`. All three printed `wt v0.82.0`, and the installed `wt` is byte-identical to the one in the archive. I haven't installed the macOS or Windows wheels on those platforms. The publish step itself can only run on a releas

--- .github/build-wheels.py (+164/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,164 @@
+"""Repackage release archives as PyPI wheels.
+
+Each wheel carries the `wt` and `git-wt` binaries from one release archive,
+byte for byte, so PyPI ships the same (signed, on Windows) binaries as GitHub
+Releases. The wheels contain no Python code: installers place the binaries in
+the environment's scripts directory, as maturin's `bindings = "bin"` does.
+
+Usage: build-wheels.py --version 0.82.0 --out-dir wheels ARCHIVE...
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import base64
+import hashlib
+import io
+import re
+import sys
+import tarfile
+import zipfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+NAME = "worktrunk"
+BINARIES = ("wt", "git-wt")
+
+# Release target → wheel platform tag. The Linux binaries are static musl
+# builds with no dynamic dependencies, so they qualify for both the glibc
+# (manylinux) and musl (musllinux) tags. The macOS floors are Rust's default
+# deployment targets.
+PLATFORM_TAGS = {
+    "x86_64-unknown-linux-musl": "manylinux_2_17_x86_64.manylinux2014_x86_64.musllinux_1_1_x86_64",
+    "aarch64-unknown-linux-musl": "manylinux_2_17_aarch64.manylinux2014_aarch64.musllinux_1_1_aarch64",
+    "x86_64-apple-darwin": "macosx_10_12_x86_64",
+    "aarch64-apple-darwin": "macosx_11_0_arm64",
+    "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc": "win_amd64",
+}
+
+ARCHIVE_RE = re.compile(r"^worktrunk-(?P<target>.+?)\.(?:tar\.xz|zip)$")
+
+# PyPI renders the long description without a base URL, so relative links in
+# the README (the logo) would break. Point them at the release tag instead.
+RELATIVE_LINK_RE = re.compile(r'\b(src|href)="(?![a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:|#|/)')
+
+EXPERIMENTAL_NOTE = (
+    "> **Experimental:** the PyPI package is new; GitHub Releases, Homebrew and "
+    "cargo are the main install channels."
+)
+
+# Fixed timestamp so rebuilding the same archives yields identical wheels.
+ZIP_DATE = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
+
+
+def read_archive(path: Path) -> dict[str, bytes]:
+    """Map each regular file's basename to its contents."""
+    files = {}
+    if path.name.endswith(".zip"):
+        with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as zf:
+            for info in zf.infolist():
+                if not info.is_dir():
+                    files[Path(info.filename).name] = zf.read(info)
+    else:
+        with tarfile.open(path, "r:xz") as tf:
+            for member in tf.getmembers():
+                if member.isfile():
+                    files[Path(member.name).name] = tf.extractfile(member).read()
+    return files
+
+
+def record_hash(data: bytes) -> str:
+    digest = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hashlib.sha256(data).digest()).rstrip(b"=")
+    return f"sha256={digest.decode()}"
+
+
+def metadata(version: str, readme: str) -> str:
+    headers = [
+        "Metadata-Version: 2.4",
+        f"Name: {NAME}",
+        f"Version: {version}",
+        "Summary: A CLI for Git worktree management, designed for parallel AI agent workflows",
+        "License-Expression: MIT OR Apache-2.0",
+        "License-File: LICENSE",
+        "Project-URL: Homepage, https://worktrunk.dev",
+        "Project-URL: Repository, https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk",
+        "Project-URL: Changelog, https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md",
+        "Description-Content-Type: text/markdown",
+    ]
+    raw_base = f"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/v{version}/"
+    readme = RELATIVE_LINK_RE.sub(lambda m: f'{m[1]}="{raw_base}', readme)
+    return "\n".join(headers) + "\n\n" + EXPERIMENTAL_NOTE + "\n\n" + readme
+
+
+def build_wheel(archive: Path, version: str, out_dir: Path) -> Path:
+    match = ARCHIVE_RE.match(archive.name)
+    if not match or match["target"] not in PLATFORM_TAGS:
+        raise SystemExit(f"{archive.name}: not a known release archive")
+    target = match["target"]
+    platform = PLATFORM_TAGS[target]
+    exe = ".exe" if target.endswith("-windows-msvc") else ""
+
+    files = read_archive(archive)
+    missing = [n for n in (*(b + exe for b in BINARIES), "LICENSE", "README.md") if n not in files]
+    if missing:
+        raise SystemExit(f"{archive.name}: missing {', '.join(missing)}")
+
+    data_dir = f"{NAME}-{version}.data"
+    dist_info = f"{NAME}-{version}.dist-info"
+    wheel_tag = f"py3-none-{platform}"
+    # (path in wheel, contents, executable)
+    entries = [(f"{data_dir}/scripts/{b}{exe}", files[b + exe], True) for b in BINARIES]
+    entries += [
+        (f"{dist_info}/METADATA", metadata(version, files["README.md"].decode()).encode(), False),
+        (f"{dist_info}/licenses/LICENSE", files["LICENSE"], False),
+        (
+            f"{dist_info}/WHEEL",
+            "\n".join(
+                [
+                    "Wheel-Version: 1.0",
+                    "Generator: worktrunk build-wheels.py",
+                    "Root-Is-Purelib: false",
+                    *(f"Tag: py3-none-{p}" for p in platform.split(".")),
+                ]
+            ).encode()
+            + b"\n",
+            False,
+        ),
+    ]
+    record_path = f"{dist_info}/RECORD"
+    record = "".join(f"{p},{record_hash(d)},{len(d)}\n" for p, d, _ in entries)
+    record += f"{record_path},,\n"
+    entries.append((record_path, record.encode(), False))
+
+    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    wheel_path = out_dir / f"{NAME}-{version}-{wheel_tag}.whl"
+    buf = io.BytesIO()
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
+        for path, data, executable in entries:
+            info = zipfile.ZipInfo(path, date_time=ZIP_DATE)
+            info.external_attr = (0o100755 if executable else 0o100644) << 16
+            info.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
+            zf.writestr(info, data)
+    wheel_path.write_bytes(buf.getvalue())
+    return wheel_path
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
+    parser.add_argument("--version", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--out-dir", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("archives", nargs="+", type=Path)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    # Release tags like 0.82.0 are already valid PEP 440 versions; prerelease
+    # suffixes would need normalizing, and prereleases aren't published.
+    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d+\.\d+\.\d+", args.version):
+        raise SystemExit(f"{args.version}: expected a MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version")
+
+    targets = {ARCHIVE_RE.match(a.name)["target"] for a in args.archives if ARCHIVE_RE.match(a.name)}
+    if targets != set(PLATFORM_TAGS):
+        raise SystemExit(f"expected archives for {sorted(PLATFORM_TAGS)}, got {sorted(targets)}")
+
+    for archive in args.archives:
+        print(build_wheel(archive, args.version, args.out_dir), file=sys.stderr)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

title: skills(running-tend): rerun transient CI failures instead of leaving it to the maintainer
body:
The `running-tend` overlay told tend sessions to leave reruns of transient CI failures to the maintainer. It said "The maintainer will rerun CI" for CI failure triage, and "the maintainer can rerun the failed job directly" for reviews. On #4737 a review diagnosed three GitHub-504 failures, wrote that "a rerun of the failed jobs should clear it", and then stopped. Its session log gives the reason as "Following the repo guidance". `max-sixty` replied: "ok then rerun? why aren't you rerunning?"

This change keeps both rules (no PR for a transient failure, and no self-dismissal over an unrelated flake). It replaces the hand-off with an instruction to rerun the failed jobs through the bundled `tend runtime rerun-failed-jobs` helper and report the result. The bundled review flow already treats a rerun as usually worth it for an infrastructure fault, so this removes the local text that overrode it. The note about GitHub's 403 while sibling jobs run is still there, now as the reason to rerun a run's jobs once it completes, not as a reason to skip the rerun. It also limits reruns to the PR's current head. Every PR CI workflow here uses a concurrency group keyed by PR number with `cancel-in-progress`, so rerunning an older head's run cancels the live head's run.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- Review run [42557353245](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/42557353245) on #4737: "All three failures came from GitHub returning 504 errors… Following the repo guidance, I'll leave the approval in place and post a short note." It posted the diagnosis without rerunning anything.
- Review run [42557366351](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/42557366351) on #4738 hit the same kind of 504 failures in the same window and did run `tend runtime rerun-failed-jobs`. Sessions are inconsistent about this, and the overlay text decided the #4737 case.
- After the maintainer's question, review run [42579472585](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/42579472585) reran the jobs, and every check on the head went green.
- Mention run [42589340741](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/42589340741) reran #4737's jobs on the head that was current before Dependabot rebased. That cancelled the current head's in-progress `feature-powerset`, and the job had to be rerun again.
- Tracking: #4657.

</details>

title: fix(switch): point Enterprise PR 404s at the API host setting
body:
When a GitHub Enterprise PR lookup has no selected API hostname, a 404 only points at `gh repo set-default`. That can already be correct even though `gh api` used its default host.

For a 404 on an explicit Enterprise PR URL, when no API host was selected, the hint names the host for `gh auth login` and points to `forge.hostname` if the API host differs. Short PR references keep the ordinary 404 hint because a Git remote can use an SSH alias. Host selection itself stays as in #4710 and #4722.

Checked with the 107 switch PR integration tests, including the new URL, remote, and configured-host cases, and with rustfmt, all-target/all-feature Clippy, doctests, and documentation generation. The full pre-merge hook could not complete locally because `pre-commit` and `cargo insta` were unavailable. The tests use a stub `gh` and do not require an Enterprise account.

Refs #4709

AI assistance was used for the patch and tests.

Review follow-up: the SSH alias and missing-login cases reproduced against the previous head. All 104 matching switch integration tests, all-target/all-feature Clippy, rustfmt, documentation generation, and doctests passed. The full local pre-merge hook still lacks `pre-commit` and `cargo insta`.

title: Publish JSON Schemas for user and project config
body:
Closes #4639. This is the files-and-tests scope agreed in the issue: no `wt config schema` command and no SchemaStore submission.

## What's in it

- `docs/public/schema/user-config.json` and `project-config.json` are generated from the `UserConfig` / `ProjectConfig` schemars derives, and published at `https://worktrunk.dev/schema/{user,project}-config.json`.
  - They use the **deserialize** contract, so fields with a serde default stay optional.
  - Object schemas get `additionalProperties: false`, so editors flag misspelled keys. Map-valued tables (`projects`, `aliases`, `custom-columns`, named hook commands) keep their own `additionalProperties`.
  - The deprecated `pre-create` / `post-create` hook aliases are left out, so editors flag them as unknown keys. The loader still accepts them with its deprecation warning.
- `test_docs_are_in_sync` regenerates both files next to `list-v2.json`. The config types live in the library crate, so the test calls the generator directly instead of shelling out.
- Unit tests in `src/config/schema.rs`:
  - representative user and project TOML configs validate. Each fixture also has to deserialize into the real config type, so the tests can't drift from what the loader reads.
  - misspelled keys are rejected at the root, in nested tables, and inside `[projects."…"]`, and the project schema rejects user-only keys.
- A short `## Editor schemas` section at the end of the `wt config` help explains the `#:schema` directive for Taplo / Tombi. The docs site test that pins the config page's table-of-contents count moves from 36 to 37 for the new heading.

## Testing

- Local `wt hook pre-merge --yes` on macOS: all pre-commit hooks pass. 5,471 of 5,494 tests pass. The 23 failures are local-environment only: 22 need `fish`, which isn't installed here, and `in_process_git_reads_only_the_hermetic_config` picks up the system git config. CI on the fork is green apart from the jobs that need repo secrets (Codecov upload, review bot).
- I checked the generated schema against Taplo and Tombi using a `#:schema` directive. Both accept a valid `.config/wt.toml` and flag misspelled keys (`pre-starts`, `[forge] platfrom`).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Add a retry-setup hint when pre-start fails during wt switch --create
body:
When `pre-start` fails during `wt switch --create`, the error now names the command that retries setup, with the same variables the switch used:

```
✗ pre-start project:env failed (exit code 1)
↳ To retry setup, run wt -C ~/code/myproject.feature-auth hook pre-start --base-worktree-path=/home/me/code/myproject
```

The failed switch leaves the new branch and worktree in place, and a later `wt switch <branch>` only runs `post-switch` because the worktree already exists, so nothing re-runs setup unless the user knows to. This failure is the one point where wt knows setup didn't finish, so the hint goes here instead of on the later `Branch already exists` collision (#4172 put it there, so it showed on every ordinary branch conflict).

At this site the hint replaces the `--no-hooks` suggestion. Re-running `wt switch --create --no-hooks` would stop at `Branch … already exists`, which is the trap #4143 reported. Every other hook failure still shows the `--no-hooks` hint as before.

A manual `wt hook pre-start` binds `base` and `base_worktree_path` to the worktree it runs in and knows no PR. So the retry passes the switch's own `--base`, `--base-worktree-path`, `--pr-number`, and `--pr-url`, but only those the frozen pre-start templates reference, because `wt hook` forwards an unreferenced `--KEY=VALUE` into `{{ args }}`. With that, a hook like `cp {{ base_worktree_path }}/.env .` reruns the same setup. A hook that references none of them gets a bare `wt -C <path> hook pre-start`.

Verified by:
- `test_user_pre_start_failure_retry_reruns_same_setup`: a hook copies a file from `{{ base_worktree_path }}` and fails; running the hinted command afterwards copies from the original worktree. Without the flag, the manual run would read from the new worktree.
- A unit test of the flag selection, including shell quoting.
- The inline error-render snapshot and the two `pre-start` failure integration snapshots.

Closes #4143

title: feat(list): expose worktree last activity in schema 2 JSON
body:
Closes #4515.

## Problem

Dashboards and cleanup tooling that want a per-worktree last-activity timestamp currently have to re-run `git status` per worktree, because schema 2 list JSON has no such field.

## Change

Adds `worktree.modified_at` to schema 2 list JSON: the later of `head.committed_at` and the newest mtime among the changed or untracked files `git status` reports for that worktree. The statusline's schema 2 JSON envelope carries the same field for its single item and collects the mtimes as well — before this, it never set `needs_mtime`, so a dirty worktree silently reported the HEAD commit time.

No-value semantics follow the existing `Tri` pattern:

- Branch-only rows have no worktree object, so the field is absent there.
- `null` when the status is unresolved.
- A clean worktree reports the commit time without extra filesystem stats.

To collect the file mtimes reliably, the shared cached status query behind `wt list` gains `-z`, and the paths that collect mtimes run it with `--untracked-files=all` instead of `normal`, still one subprocess per worktree. Only the schema 2 JSON paths collect mtimes — `wt list --format=json` and the statusline's schema 2 JSON — so the table, the text statusline, and the picker keep the `normal` query and never pay the per-file stat loop. The old text output quoted unusual filenames and collapsed untracked directories, so paths could not be trusted for stat calls; the NUL-delimited form also expands untracked directories into individual files. `parse_working_tree_status`, the conflict checks, and the picker diff state all read the same byte-oriented records now. Missing or deleted files are skipped rather than failing the row, and renames use the destination path.

Docs: the worktree field table in the list command help (source for the generated command page and skill mirrors) gains the `modified_at` row, and `docs/public/schema/list-v2.json` is regenerated.

## Verification

Validated with Rust 1.99 (the pinned 1.98 toolchain install is broken in this environment; no toolchain files were changed):

- `cargo fmt --check` — pass
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — pass
- `cargo test --lib --bins commands::list` — 300 passed
- `cargo test --lib --bins` — 2597 passed (run with root's `cap_dac_override` dropped; one permission-based picker test fails under unrestricted root because a read-only directory stays writable there, unrelated to this change)
- `cargo test --test integration integration_tests::list::` — 103 passed, including a new test proving a clean worktree reports the commit time and a dirty worktree with a nested untracked file (with a newline in its name) reports that file's mtime
- `cargo test --test integration integration_tests::readme_sync::test_docs_are_in_sync` — pass
- Six list-JSON snapshots updated; their diffs contain only 33 added `modified_at` lines

title: skills(running-tend): post nightly ci-fix diagnoses on the auto-filed nightly issue
body:
When a scheduled nightly fails, `create-issue-on-nightly-failure` opens a `Nightly tests failed` issue before `tend-ci-fix` starts. ci-fix's dedup only searches the bot's `ci-fix:`-titled issues, so it can't see that issue. When ci-fix can't produce a fix for a durable cause, it opens a second, open tracker for the same run. This adds a short `running-tend` section: look up the open `Nightly tests failed` issue by title and post a durable diagnosis there instead of opening a `ci-fix:` tracking issue. A fix PR closes it with `Fixes #<n>`. Transient diagnoses still file their closed `tend-outage` tracker, because ci-fix's repeat-occurrence escalation counts only those. The lookup command in the section returns #4509 today.

The fix belongs in the overlay rather than upstream because the auto-filed issue comes from this repo's own `nightly.yaml` job and `.github/nightly-failure.md` template, not from tend.

Today's case left two open trackers for one failure. ci-fix [39211195743](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/39211195743) opened #4511 for nightly run 39206247278, which #4509 already tracked with a triage diagnosis. A second triage run then had to read #4511 as well. The earlier pairs were transient diagnoses, opened and closed within seconds. Those stay as they are, since they are the record the escalation check reads.

<details><summary>Occurrences and gate assessment</summary>

| Nightly run | Auto-filed issue | ci-fix issue |
|---|---|---|
| 39206247278 | #4509 (06:39Z) | #4511 (07:17Z), left open |
| 32935569443 | #3917 (06:11Z) | #3918 (06:21Z), closed as transient |
| 31077344052 | #3751 (07:50Z) | #3752 (08:06Z), closed as transient |
| 30519615581 | #3667 (07:37Z) | #3668 (07:40Z), closed as transient |

In the 39211195743 session log, the dedup searches were `ci-fix: in:title` (bot-authored), `foreground_jobs in:body` and `startup_interrupt in:body`. #4509's body is only the run link, so none of them matched it.

- **Evidence**: High. The same pattern shows up in 4 sessions. Prior review-runs entries on the review-runs tracker #4330 recorded the related triage/ci-fix double diagnosis (#4404, #4476) as cost-only.
- **Type**: structural. The search can never match the template's title or body.
- **Change**: one targeted new section, which needs 3 or more occurrences and has 4.

</details>
author: worktrunk-bot
diff:
--- .claude/skills/running-tend/SKILL.md (+10/-0)
@@ -126,6 +126,16 @@ failure, not a broken link:
 When in doubt, post a comment on the failed run summarizing the diagnosis and
 wait — don't open a PR.
 
+## CI Fix: A Failed Scheduled Nightly Already Has Its Issue
+
+When a scheduled `nightly` run fails, its `create-issue-on-nightly-failure` job opens (or updates) an open `Nightly tests failed` issue labelled `ci`, and `tend-triage` diagnoses it there. That issue is the tracker for the failure. The `ci-fix:` title search in `/tend-ci-runner:ci-fix` cannot find it, so look it up by title before filing anything:
+
+```bash
+gh issue list --state open --label ci --search '"Nightly tests failed" in:title' --json number,title
+```
+
+Post a durable diagnosis on that issue, unless a comment there already covers it, instead of opening a `ci-fix:` tracking issue. A fix PR closes it with `Fixes #<n>`. A transient diagnosis still files its closed `tend-outage` tracker, since the repeat-occurrence escalation in `/tend-ci-runner:ci-fix` counts only those.
+
 ## Applying GitHub Suggestions
 
 Apply the literal suggestion only — change the lines it covers, nothing more.

title: feat(templates): add expected_worktree_path_of_branch() template function
body:
Adds an `expected_worktree_path_of_branch(branch)` template function that returns the path `wt switch --create` would use for a branch, whether or not a worktree exists there. This is option (1) from the discussion on #4480, which @max-sixty approved. It gives @BenJurewicz's wrapper the missing piece: after `wt switch feature` fails because the worktree at `feature`'s path now holds another branch, a script can get that path and switch to it, and that works with custom and per-project `worktree-path` templates:

```bash
wts() {
  wt switch "$@" && return
  local rc=$? p
  p=$(wt step eval "{{ expected_worktree_path_of_branch('$1') }}") || return "$rc"
  [ -d "$p" ] && wt switch "$p" || return "$rc"
}
```

`worktree_path_of_branch` can't do this, because it returns where the branch is checked out and comes back empty in exactly this case.

**What changed**

- The path computation moves from `compute_worktree_path` in the binary to `UserConfig::expected_worktree_path` in the library, so the template environment can call it. `compute_worktree_path` now delegates to it, so `wt switch` and the template function share one implementation, including the default branch resolving to the repo root.
- Rendering the `worktree-path` template goes through the same template environment, so a `worktree-path` template that calls `expected_worktree_path_of_branch` would recurse. A thread-local guard turns that into an error.
- The hook docs' functions table and a short paragraph cover the new function. Generated docs are regenerated.

**Verification**

- New `wt step eval` integration tests check the expected path when another branch occupies it (where `worktree_path_of_branch` is empty), the default-branch case, and the recursion error.
- Manually in a scratch repo, with `repo.feature` switched to `other`: `wt step eval "{{ expected_worktree_path_of_branch('feature') }}"` printed `…/repo.feature`, `wt switch` on that path landed there, and `--config-set 'worktree-path = "/tmp/wts/{{ branch }}"'` produced `/tmp/wts/f`.

The name follows the existing `worktree_path_of_branch`, so both functions that take a branch end in `_of_branch`.

**codecov/patch is red because of moved lines.** The six misses in `src/config/user/accessors.rs` are the "Repository path has no filename" and "contains invalid UTF-8" error closures, moved from `compute_worktree_path` without changes. They were already uncovered on main at `5e5c65b` (`src/commands/worktree/resolve.rs` lines 47–56). Every new line in `expansion.rs` and `resolve.rs` is covered. Reaching those closures would need a repository at `/` or at a path that isn't valid UTF-8, so I left them as they were. Per `AGENTS.md`, merging with this check red needs explicit approval.

title: fix(push): read the push range from the target branch, not a same-named tag
body:
When a tag shares the target branch's name, `wt step push <target>` and `wt merge` compared against the tag instead of the branch. With a tag `main` at the feature commit, both reported "Already up to date with main" and left `refs/heads/main` where it was. This PR makes every range in the push path read the target SHA that `MergeContext::prepare` already snapshots from `refs/heads/<target>`.

Git resolves a bare `main` to `refs/tags/main` before `refs/heads/main`. The fast-forward check already used the qualified ref, but four later reads passed the bare name: the commit count, the overlap check against the target worktree's uncommitted changes, the commit graph, and the diffstat. A tag pointing elsewhere also skewed the count, graph, and diffstat shown before the push.

Two regression tests in `tests/integration_tests/push.rs` fail on `main` and pass here. One checks that the push advances the branch despite the tag. The other checks that a dirty target worktree's overlapping file is still refused. Before this fix, the overlap went unchecked because the zero commit count made the push a no-op, so nothing was overwritten. Without the zero count, that check would have read an empty range. The existing push and merge tests pass. The exception is `test_merge_no_ff_signs_merge_commit`, which fails identically on unchanged `main` in this sandbox (ssh rejects the signing key's 0644 permissions).

<details><summary>Scope</summary>

This matches what #694 did for the integration checks (`resolve_preferring_branch`). Other `wt merge` steps that run before the push, such as rebasing onto the target, may take the bare name too. They aren't in this diff.

</details>
author: worktrunk-bot

title: fix(switch): return `wt switch -` to the worktree it left, not the first checkout of its branch
body:
Follow-up to #4496. `wt switch -` recorded only the branch it left (`worktrunk.history`) and found the worktree again by branch name. From the second checkout of a branch checked out twice it returned to the first checkout; from a detached worktree it had no branch to record, so it returned to an older branch or failed with "No previous branch".

A switch now also records the path of the worktree it leaves, in `worktrunk.history-path`, and clears `worktrunk.history` when that worktree is detached, so the two keys always describe one worktree. As a worktree argument, `-` resolves to the recorded path while a worktree is still registered there and still holds the recorded branch; otherwise it falls back to the branch, as before. Every worktree argument resolves `-` this way, so `wt remove -` now removes the worktree `wt switch -` would return to (its dirty and integration checks unchanged). As a ref (`--base -`, merge targets) `-` still reads the branch. `wt list` marks the previous worktree by the same rule, and `wt config state` set/clear keep the two keys in step.

Behaviour that changes: after leaving a detached worktree, `wt config state` shows no previous branch, `--base -` errors instead of using an older branch, and an older wt reading the key sees no history. Known limit: if an older wt later records the *same* branch without a path, the stale path still matches, which matters only for a branch checked out twice.

New integration tests return to a second checkout and to a detached worktree (both fail on `main`), and pin the fallbacks to the branch: when an older wt recorded another branch, and when the worktree left was removed. The full pre-merge gate passes locally; Codex reviewed it.

title: fix: resolve worktree arguments once and pass the resolved worktree through
body:
Follow-up to the survey on #4493. Several commands resolved a worktree argument, kept only the branch or only the path, and looked the other half up again. Each re-lookup could disagree with the first. This resolves the argument once and passes the resolved worktree through.

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `wt switch origin/feature` (`feature` has a worktree) | pre-switch hook got `branch=origin/feature` and no `target_worktree_path` | hook gets `branch=feature` and the worktree path |
| `wt step promote <second copy>` of a branch checked out twice | acted on the first copy, failed partway, left the main worktree and that copy detached | refuses before touching anything, listing both checkouts |
| the same with no argument from the second copy, or with the default branch checked out twice | same partial failure | same refusal |
| `wt switch @` from a second copy or a detached worktree | landed in the first copy, or errored | `already_at` the current worktree |
| bare-repo worktree-path warning for `@` / `-` / `pr:N` | skipped through a hand-kept list of shortcuts | names the branch the shortcut resolves to; the list is gone |

### `wt switch`

`SwitchTarget` holds the resolved destination (an existing worktree, or a branch to create one for) plus the forge's answer for `pr:`/`mr:`. The bare-repo warning, the pre-switch hooks, and `plan_switch` all read it, so the hooks no longer run their own copy of resolution. Arguments other than `pr:`/`mr:` and `--create` names go through `Repository::resolve_worktree`, which is what makes `@` resolve by path; the remote-prefix strip applies to a `BranchOnly` result.

A pre-switch hook can change what the argument names: the fetch-if-stale hook the docs suggest makes a remote-only branch appear. So when a hook actually ran (`execute_hook` now reports whether one did), the pipeline locates the argument again through the same `SwitchTarget::locate`, on a fresh `Repository`, and plans against that. The forge is not queried twice. `--base` and `--create` validation still run after the hooks.

Two behaviour changes follow. Naming errors (`wt switch -` with no history, a path holding no worktree) now fail before the pre-switch hooks run rather than after. And when a hook ran, the rest of the switch reads repository state as the hook left it, `.config/wt.toml` included.

### Promote and the other `--branch` callers

`Repository::require_worktree` returns the branch along with the path, so `CommandEnv::for_selector`, `copy-ignored`, and promote use the resolved pair instead of looking one up from the other. Promote resolves every route (argument, `@`, `^`) to a worktree and refuses when either branch is checked out more than once.

### Not covered

`wt switch -` still records the previous location as a branch name, so it can't return to the second copy of a duplicated branch or to a detached worktree. Changing what the history records is a separate change.

### Testing

New integration tests cover each row

title: Honor resolved paths and forge settings
body:
Several paths reconstructed default values instead of consuming the configured or server-provided result. This could configure an unusable fork push URL, recommend editing the wrong zsh file, or report misleading worktree information.

- Preserve Gitea's API clone URLs for fork pushes and missing-remote suggestions, including HTTP schemes, ports, and deployment paths.
- Scope GitHub and GitLab protocol lookups to the selected host.
- Name the resolved zsh configuration path and selected command in compinit advice.
- Compare prune candidates through project-config resolution, so shared absolute overrides do not falsely imply different hooks.
- Deduplicate statusline branches only when a linked checkout still matches its configured path and its displayed directory contains the branch. Main checkouts and checkouts whose branch has drifted from the configured path retain the branch label.

The audit followed the default-template assumption fixed in [#4491](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4491).

title: fix(switch): resolve a worktree path for pre-switch hook variables
body:
`run_pre_switch_hooks` found the destination with `worktree_for_branch`, so it only matched a branch name. A worktree path, which is what the interactive picker passes, matched nothing. `branch` and `target` then held the raw path, while `worktree_path`, `worktree_name`, `upstream`, and `commit` described the source worktree. The hook now runs the same `resolve_selector` ladder that `plan_switch` uses: branch first, then the argument as a worktree path, and branch-only under `--create`. With that change, `wt switch ../repo.feature` renders the same variables as `wt switch feature`. A detached worktree can only be named by path. For one, `branch` and `target` stay unset, matching #4009, and `commit` comes from the destination's HEAD instead of the source's.

title: fix(switch): name the configured worktree path in the bare-repo warning
body:
In a bare repo at a hidden path (e.g. `project/.git`), `wt switch` warns that the configured `worktree-path` will place worktrees badly. The "worktrees will be at …" path in that warning was hard-coded to the default template's `{{ repo }}.{{ branch }}` shape, but the warning fires for any template that references `{{ repo }}`. So a custom template got a wrong prediction:

```
worktree-path = "{{ repo_path }}/../{{ repo }}-wt/{{ branch | sanitize }}"

▲ Bare repo at project/.git — worktrees will be at project/.git.feature
✓ Created branch feature and worktree @ …/project/.git-wt/feature
```

The example is now computed with `compute_worktree_path`, the same function the switch uses to place the worktree. It is shown relative to the project's parent, so the default template's output is unchanged (the existing `bare_repo_worktree_path_prompt_non_interactive_warning` snapshot still passes).

`test_bare_repo_worktree_path_warning_uses_configured_template` sets the template above and asserts that the warning names `project/.git-wt/feature` and that the worktree lands there. Before the fix, it fails with the `.git.feature` message.

title: feat(plugin): route OpenCode 2 worktrees through wt switch and wt remove
body:
Under OpenCode 2, the plugin that `wt config plugins opencode install` writes now registers a `worktrunk` worktree strategy. Worktrees that OpenCode creates and removes then go through `wt switch --create` and `wt remove`, the same way the Claude Code plugin's `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` hooks already route them. This was requested in #4488. I ran the strategy locally against a scratch repo with this branch's `wt` and a fake OpenCode context. I haven't run it inside a real OpenCode 2 session, which CI can't drive.

How each callback maps ([`dev/opencode-plugin.ts`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/1c906f5599d7a16df832c56c51aa82d13c82bbd3/dev/opencode-plugin.ts)):

- **create**: runs `wt switch [--create] <name> [--base <ref>] --no-cd --format=json` in the source checkout and returns `.path`. OpenCode's `branch` input is a [starting ref, not a branch name](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugin/src/worktree.ts), so `<name>` is the basename of the directory OpenCode suggests (the name the user typed, or a generated slug). The path comes from `worktree-path`, since OpenCode accepts a different directory than the one it suggested. An existing branch is reopened, as in #4487. Passing a starting ref for an existing branch is refused rather than ignored.
- **remove**: runs `wt remove --foreground [--force] <dir>`. It does nothing if the checkout is already gone.
- **list**: reads `git worktree list --porcelain -z` and reports the first record as `root`. Bare and prunable entries are skipped.

Things a maintainer may want to weigh:

- **On by default.** OpenCode selects a strategy as soon as a plugin adds one. Every OpenCode 2 user with the plugin installed switches to worktrunk-managed worktrees, and OpenCode's `worktree.directory` setting stops applying. This matches the Claude Code plugin. The docs page says so.
- **No force prompt on a dirty worktree.** OpenCode only offers to force when the error is an instance of its own `Worktree.OperationError` ([`operationError`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/core/src/worktree.ts) uses `instanceof`). A standalone plugin file can't import that class: the CLI's runtime shim for `@opencode/plugin` doesn't export `Worktree`. A dirty removal fails with worktrunk's own message instead (`Cannot remove worktree: … has uncommitted changes`), and nothing is deleted.
- **Default base.** With no starting ref, the new branch starts from worktrunk's default (the default branch). OpenCode's `git` strategy uses the source checkout's HEAD instead.

<details><summary>Local check</summary>

A Node harness imported the plugin, called `setup` with a stub `ctx.worktree.transform`, and ran each callback against a fresh repo with `target/debug/wt` on PATH:

- create → `ocrepo.brave-tiger` (the `worktree-path` default), and `list` returned root + that worktree
- create with `branch: "brave-tiger"` → a second worktree based on it
- create for an existing branch with a sta

title: fix(plugin): reopen an existing worktree from the WorktreeCreate hook
body:
Since Claude Code 2.1.300, plugin `WorktreeCreate` hooks run for `claude --worktree NAME`, and Claude Code fires the hook again when NAME is a worktree an earlier session kept. The plugin always ran `wt switch --create NAME`, so reopening failed with `Branch NAME already exists`. The hook now omits `--create` when local branch NAME exists, so `wt switch` prints the existing worktree's path, matching Claude Code's built-in behavior ("Passing `--worktree` a name whose directory already exists opens that existing worktree", [worktrees docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees)).

The fix covers both hook paths:

- **`plugins/worktrunk/hooks/hooks.json`**: the command users run today. It checks `git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/$name` before choosing the flag. It uses only commands every installed `wt` already has, so it fixes the problem as soon as the marketplace serves the merged `main`.
- **`wt config plugins claude hook`**: the same check through `Repository::branch(..).exists_locally()`, so the fix survives #4305's switch to the subcommand. #4305 rewrites the same `hooks.json` line, so whichever lands second has to resolve the conflict.

`test_claude_hook_worktree_create` previously asserted that a second create with the same name fails. It now asserts that the second create reopens the same path. Before the fix it failed with the error from the issue. The failure path (no stdout and a nonzero exit, #3545) is still asserted, using a project dir that is not inside a repository.

**What wasn't verified:** the run inside Claude Code itself. I ran the `hooks.json` command by hand against a scratch repo with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`/`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` set: create, reopen, an existing branch without a worktree, and a non-repo project dir. I did not test it under `claude --worktree`.

One behavior to weigh: `claude --worktree NAME` where NAME is a pre-existing branch the user made by hand now opens (or creates a worktree for) that branch rather than failing. A clean exit then fires `WorktreeRemove` on it. That hook runs `wt remove` without force, so it refuses dirty worktrees and keeps unmerged branches (#2939).

Closes #4486 — automated triage

title: test(copy-ignored): set the comparison file's mode instead of inheriting the umask
body:
`test_copy_ignored_preserves_file_executable_permissions` fails for anyone whose umask isn't `022`. It creates `node_modules/.bin/config.json` with `fs::write` and asserts that the copy is `0644`. Under umask `002`, a common default for Linux user accounts, the source file is created `0664`. `wt step copy-ignored` correctly preserves that, so the test fails with `expected 0644, got 0664`. This PR sets the source file's mode to `0644` explicitly, as the test already does for its two executables. The assertion and the copy code are unchanged.

Verified locally with the test under `TMPDIR=/tmp`: it passes at umask `022` and fails at `002` on `main`, and passes at both with this change.

<details><summary>How this surfaced</summary>

The tend sandbox's `$TMPDIR` has a default ACL (`default:user:runner:rwx`), which also makes new files `0664`. On #4346, mention run [38808931955](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/38808931955) saw this test fail locally and spent part of the session working out whether the reflink copy path had a real permissions bug, before tracing it to the environment. CI runners use umask `022`, so CI never saw the failure.

</details>

title: fix(switch): branch --create from a remote-tracking default branch
body:
`wt switch --create` used the configured default branch as its base only when a local branch of that name existed; otherwise it dropped the base and `git worktree add` branched from the current HEAD, with no message. A remote-tracking default such as git-p4's `p4/master`, which never has a local branch, therefore never took effect. The default now qualifies whenever it resolves to a commit (`rev-parse --verify <ref>^{commit}`), the same rule `--base` values already follow. A default that resolves to nothing still falls back to HEAD as before.

`test_switch_create_from_remote_tracking_default_branch` sets the default to `origin/release` (remote-tracking only), moves HEAD past it, and checks that `--create` branches from `origin/release`. It fails on `main` (the new branch lands on HEAD) and passes with the change; the `switch` and `default_branch` integration tests (410) pass locally.

Not changed: `wt config state default-branch set p4/master` still warns "Branch p4/master does not exist locally", which is now overcautious for `--create`. Other default-branch consumers (`wt merge`, integration checks in `wt list`/`wt remove`) were not exercised with a remote-tracking default.

Closes #4481 — automated triage

title: chore: correct stale comments and tighten a statusline width test
body:
Corrects comments and docs that no longer match the code, found in tonight's rolling survey, and tightens one test whose assertion couldn't fail on the behavior it names. No runtime behavior changes.

- **`src/commands/remove.rs`**: the comment at the hook-approval call site said each removed worktree's `pre-remove`/`post-remove` is approved against *that worktree's* config. The `approve_remove` helper it points to selects every hook from the invoking worktree's config via `repo.load_project_config()`, and its own doc says so. The comment also said the helper "dedups by template". It dedups destinations by path.
- **`src/trace/parse.rs`**: `start_time_us` was documented as microseconds since the Unix epoch. `ts` comes from `now_us()`, which is microseconds since `trace_epoch()`, as the module doc already says.
- **`benches/AGENTS.md`**: it said large imported fixtures are opt-in and must not run on hosted CI. In fact `bench_large_repository` in `benches/list.rs` runs the imported rust-lang/rust fixture by default, and `benchmarks.yaml` caches it for the daily `cargo bench`. Only the large-repository prune fixture is gated, behind `large-repository-benches`.

- **`statusline_segment.rs` test**: `test_statusline_segment_fit_to_width_prefers_priority_over_width` used a budget of 25, which fits the 22-wide segment plus one narrow one (22+2+1). It asserted only that the wide segment survived, so it never checked that the narrow low-priority segments are dropped. It now uses a budget of 23 and asserts the exact result.

- **`tend-ci-fix` no longer drops a pending failure from a different trigger.** Its concurrency group now includes the failed run's event (`push`, `schedule`, …) as well as the workflow and branch. One side effect: the generator pins `astral-sh/setup-uv` at v10.2.0 in `tend-mention.yaml` and `tend-notifications.yaml`. That reverts Dependabot's bump to v10.3.0 (#4446) in those two generated files. Dependabot will likely propose the bump again, and the next regeneration will revert it again until tend's own pin moves.

title: fix(tests): stop wt immediately in the startup-interrupt foreground test
body:
The nightly `feature-powerset` failure in #4476 was a race in `startup_interrupt_preserves_already_started_child_cleanup`, not in `wt`. The test needs `wt` stopped partway through spawning 120 concurrent `post-start` commands. Before it ran `kill -STOP "$PPID"`, its stopper command (`a001`) busy-waited for the Python worker to write `worker-info`. `wt` kept spawning siblings during the worker's startup. The already-started siblings busy-loop too, which slows that startup further. In the [failed run](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/38688393486), the full suite's load let `wt` spawn all 120 commands first, so the test's precondition failed with `startup already completed: 120`.

`a001` now stops its parent at once. The worker still runs while `wt` is stopped, and the test already waits for `worker-info` before it sends Ctrl-C, so the wait inside `a001` wasn't needed for ordering.

To measure the margin, I temporarily printed the number of children started before the stop:

| | idle 4-core runner | with 6 extra CPU-bound loops |
|---|---|---|
| before | 50–70 | 58–73 |
| after | 3–4 | 2–3 |

2 is the minimum (`a000` and `a001`) and is still inside the accepted `2..120` range. I couldn't make the original assertion fail locally; the table shows how close it came. The `foreground_jobs` tests pass with `--no-default-features --features default,shell-integration-tests`, the feature set that failed.

Closes #4476 — automated triage

title: fix(picker): show an orphan branch's commits in the log tab
body:
On an orphan branch row, `wt switch`'s log tab says "`<branch>` has no commits" even though the branch has commits. The preview ran `git merge-base <default> <head>` through `run_command` and treated any failure as "no commits", but `git merge-base` exits 1 when the two commits share no ancestor — a valid answer, not an error. The same path serves `--prs` rows through `compute_log_for_head`.

The fix calls `Repository::merge_base`, which already maps exit 1 to `Ok(None)` (the exit-code distinction AGENTS.md asks for), and shows every commit bright in that case, since all of an orphan's commits are its own. A real failure still falls back to the old message.

`Repository::merge_base` resolves the default branch with an uncached `rev-parse` before its SHA-keyed lookup, so the dim/bright split still tracks the default branch's current tip (`log_cache_dim_split_tracks_main_advance` still passes). The comment that steered away from it to save a subprocess is gone: the merge-base result itself is now served from the disk cache, so a warm render forks the same number of times as before.

The new `log_orphan_shows_its_commits` test fails on `main` with the "has no commits" output and passes with the fix.

title: Reclaim stale temporary indexes with age-based cleanup
body:
Abruptly terminated commands can leave full temporary Git index copies behind. The contributor reported 52,786 files totaling 127 GB after three days of frequent statusline cancellations.

Reclaim index copies and their Git lock siblings older than one hour when a command next creates a temporary index. Keep the existing filename prefix so cleanup also handles files left by older versions. Sweep the system temp directory once per process, without making other probe threads wait, and retain best-effort cleanup in the Git-directory fallback. Normal exits still remove their own temporary indexes.

This uses age alone: no PID-tagged filenames, process checks, or platform-specific liveness behavior. Move commit-preview approval before temporary-index creation so an unattended approval prompt cannot age out an index needed afterward. The one-hour limit is a retention policy; a suspended operation or unusually slow Git filter can still exceed it. Statusline computations are unchanged.

Validation: regression tests cover stale indexes and locks, recent/future/unrelated files, both storage locations, cleanup failures, real-index preservation, and the actual approval wait. The approval test fails with the old ordering and passes with the fix. Independent review, lint, docs sync, and docs build passed. The local full gate passed 5,412 tests; three PowerShell tests failed because the installed pwsh also crashes with Stack overflow on a standalone arithmetic command outside the repository.

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_
author: jonah-osmo

title: docs: drop references to the removed gh auth status gate and CAS tail
body:
Two comments and one demo note still describe code that the last day's commits removed.

- **Demo fixtures** (`docs/demos/AGENTS.md`, `docs/demos/shared/fixtures/gh-mock.sh`): both said a successful `gh auth status` (via `CiToolsStatus::detect`) is needed before CI cells appear. #4449 deleted `CiToolsStatus`, and nothing in `src/` runs `gh auth status` any more; `wt list` gates only on `gh --version`. title: fix(approvals): don't read approvals.toml under --yes
body:
With a malformed `approvals.toml`, `wt hook pre-merge --yes` (the project's own test gate), a project alias run with `--yes`, and `wt merge`/`wt step commit --yes` with a project `commit.template-append` all abort with "Approvals … failed to parse", even though `--yes` neither reads nor records approvals. `wt switch` and `wt remove` already skip the load under `--yes` — [`ApprovedHookPlan::approve`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/b280a6ac3bc4634bfbac19505d8d3c55148e42ec/src/commands/hook_plan.rs#L196-L201) documents that "a malformed `approvals.toml` therefore never aborts a command that would not consult it" — but the other three gates (`approve_hooks_filtered`, `approve_alias_commands`, `approve_commit_template_append`) loaded it before calling `approve_command_batch`.

The fix moves the load into `approve_command_batch`, after its `yes` short-circuit, so every gate follows the same rule. Two simplifications fall out:

- The second `Approvals::load()` before saving is gone. `approve_commands` reloads from disk under the lock before mutating, so it was dead work — and its `?` turned a load failure after the user had answered "y" into a hard error, contrary to the comment that a failed save only warns.
- The `commands_already_filtered` parameter is gone: its one `true` caller pre-filtered with the same `is_command_approved` check the batch does itself.

`test_yes_ignores_malformed_approvals_file` in `tests/integration_tests/approvals.rs` covers the hook and alias paths; both cases fail on `main` with the parse error and pass here, and the file is left untouched.

title: fix(tests): stop git auto-maintenance from deleting the promote test's new worktree
body:
`test_promote_bare_repo_with_worktrees` failed during setup in nightly [run 38353472092](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/38353472092). Its plain `git worktree add` against the bare fixture died with `fatal: could not open 'worktrees/worktree/locked' for writing: No such file or directory`. This is the second occurrence: #3918 recorded the same failure in August and closed it as a one-off.

The cause is Git's own auto-maintenance. The test's `git push` into the bare repo makes `receive-pack` start `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach` in that repo, which keeps running after the push returns. Under Git 2.55, auto-maintenance includes the `worktree-prune` task, and that task deletes any `worktrees/<name>` directory without a `gitdir` file. `git worktree add` leaves exactly that state for a moment, between creating `worktrees/<name>` and writing its `locked` file. If the detached maintenance scans during that moment, it removes the directory, and the write fails with ENOENT.

The test now sets `maintenance.auto=false` in the bare repo before pushing. It has to be repo config: `receive-pack` strips `GIT_CONFIG_*` from its environment for local transports, so the suite's hermetic env never reaches it.

<details><summary>What was verified locally (git 2.55.0)</summary>

- A GIT_TRACE2 trace of the push shows `receive-pack` spawning `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach`.
- In a bare repo, `git maintenance run --auto` deletes a hand-made `worktrees/x` directory that has no `gitdir` file.
- Passing `maintenance.auto=false` through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` does not stop the push's maintenance child. The same setting in the bare repo's config does: the trace then shows no maintenance child.
- The timing overlap itself did not reproduce. 300 serial runs of the fixture sequence all passed, so the race needs CI-level load. The fix removes the deleting process rather than narrowing the window.
- `cargo test --test integration step_promote` passes.

</details>

`git commit` also spawns detached auto-maintenance, but the suite's hermetic env could turn that off. Every failure seen so far came through the push path, so this PR leaves the commit path alone.

The other failure in the same run, `dirs` reported unused by udeps, is fixed separately in #4465.

Refs #4464 — automated triage

title: fix(remove): warn when a submodule holds commits on no remote
body:
Removing a worktree deletes its submodules' module stores, and with them any commit no remote-tracking ref reaches, including reflog-only ones. Removal now warns before proceeding:

```
▲ Submodule submod has commits on no remote; removing the worktree deletes them
```

It still removes, so shallow or SHA-fetched pins (which can look the same) never need `--force`. `--force` skips the check, having already consented to losing what the worktree holds. The picker removes silently, as it does for everything else.

This replaces the earlier refuse-unless-`--force` version of this PR, per the decision to warn instead. The test-only commit routing `GIT_EXEC_PATH` to Git's real exec path is kept, since `git submodule` needs Git's helpers when wt runs as `git wt`.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

title: Report removal failures with the surviving checkout and branch state
body:
A branch-deletion failure can be lost after its checkout has already been removed. Return a contextual error through foreground and silent callers after arranging teardown, while preserving partial JSON results, including `retained_failed`, and the underlying cancellation signal. Later failures in an already detached cleanup child continue to go to its log.

The destructive Git command owns checkout-removal errors and surviving-entry details. Preflight and staging refusals keep their own diagnostic, so they do not imply that deletion partly succeeded; actual partial failures still list survivors.

Validation: 160 removal integration tests, 83 prune integration tests, and the cancellation and silent-picker unit regressions pass. The full project gate passes: 5,447 tests plus Clippy, formatting, docs, doctests, and lockfile checks. Independent source review found no remaining defects.

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

title: fix(remove): recheck cleanliness after stopping the fsmonitor daemon
body:
Removal's dirty-worktree gate runs before wt stops the fsmonitor daemon, since the daemon answers that `git status` cheaply. A file written while the daemon shuts down therefore reached the rename unchecked. With `core.fsmonitor` configured, removal now runs the gate once more after the stop, with fsmonitor disabled, which rescans without starting a new daemon in the worktree about to go.

The first gate stays, so a dirty worktree is still refused off the daemon's answer with its daemon left running. Under fsmonitor the post-stop rescan is what a clean removal passes: one full re-stat per removal there, which also makes `wt` stricter than `git worktree remove` against a stale daemon answer. Without fsmonitor nothing changes. `--force` skips both gates, as before.

This narrows the earlier version of this PR, which bypassed fsmonitor for every removal and stacked on #4454; it now targets `main` on its own.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

title: Preserve native Git paths and pass removal arguments without shell interpolation
body:
Lossy path decoding and shell interpolation can change the filesystem target. Preserve native Git paths, carry native argv through the existing command runner, and pass cleanup paths as positional arguments to fixed scripts. Remove the path-conversion errors and duplicate detachment code.

Use the existing Rust branch-deletion logic in the detached fallback, replacing the shell topology parser. Capture the invoking target and expected tip before scheduling; recheck live checkout ownership before deleting. This incorporates and supersedes https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4462.

Validation: 272 focused tests pass under Rust 1.98. Claude reviewed the source; its technical findings are addressed, with the follow-up reviewed independently by Codex.

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

title: Find Windows Git Bash through Git's installed runtime
body:
Deriving Bash from a PATH shim or searching beyond its installation can select an unrelated executable. Ask the selected Git for its runtime path and resolve Bash within that installation in both Rust and the Windows hook launcher.

Validation: 1 focused test passes under Rust 1.98. Native Windows checks run in CI. Claude reviewed the source; its technical findings are addressed, with the follow-up reviewed independently by Codex.

title: Give stdin to the foreground pipeline that owns it
body:
Concurrent prune hooks and picker removals can compete with the caller for terminal input. Carry stdin ownership through foreground execution: standalone removal and aliases inherit input, while concurrent prune and picker removal hooks receive closed stdin.

Validation: 156 focused tests pass under Rust 1.98. Claude source review is clean; Codex reviewed the import-only follow-up.

title: fix(list): leave CI blank when the forge CLI isn't logged in
body:
Since #4436, any failed forge call shows ⚠. That includes a CLI that is installed but not logged in, which then puts a permanent ⚠ in `wt list --full`, the shell prompt, and the Claude Code statusline. This change leaves the cell blank when the CLI holds no login for the forge's host, and keeps ⚠ for a failure from a CLI that does (offline, rate limit, expired token).

Each CLI answers from its own local state, so a lost connection never reads as logged out:

- **GitHub**: `gh` exits with its documented code 4 when it has no login for the host it resolved for the request. The backend reads that exit code, so SSH host aliases resolve the way `gh` resolves them.
- **GitLab / Gitea / Azure DevOps**: after a failed call, `remote_ref::is_authed_for(forge, host)` asks `glab config get token --host`, `tea logins list --output json`, or `az account show`, for the `forge.hostname` if configured, else the remote's host. The answer is cached per forge and host for the process.

`wt config show --full` uses the same check for the repo's host and names that host in its warning. It replaces `CiToolsStatus`, which probed all four CLIs to report one, and asked `gh auth status` / `glab auth status`, which contact the server and accept a login for any host. `tea`'s host-agnostic `has_any_login` is gone with it.

Behavior changes:

- `wt list --full` / statusline: a CLI with no login for the host leaves the CI cell blank instead of ⚠. The legend now lists that under blank, and ⚠'s examples say "expired login".
- `wt config show --full`: a login for another host no longer counts, and the warning says which host it checked (`gh installed but not authenticated for github.com`).

Known limits: a GitLab or Gitea remote through an SSH host alias is checked under the alias, so a failure there shows blank unless `forge.hostname` names the real host; Azure DevOps counts only an `az login`, not a PAT from `az devops login`.

Tests: the failed-list test now covers logged-in and logged-out cases for `gh` (exit 1 vs 4) and `glab` (token vs none); the `tea` CI mocks hold a login for the test host; the `tea` login-discovery test adds a login for another host.

Follows #4436.
