title: chore: bump minijinja from 2.24.0 to 3.0.0
body:
Bumps [minijinja](https://github.com/mitsuhiko/minijinja) from 2.24.0 to 3.0.0.
Changelog

Sourced from minijinja's changelog.

3.0.0

MiniJinja 3 is a major release. It aligns template behavior and the value model more closely with Jinja2, makes Serde optional, makes mutable State the canonical way to call back into the engine, adds built-in automatic reloading of templates, reworks the JavaScript bindings and makes the Python bindings considerably faster. Errors involving undefined values and the debug info shown for errors were improved as well.

Most projects will need some changes when upgrading. See UPDATING.md for migration instructions. The changes below are relative to 2.24.0 and include everything from the 3.0.0 alpha releases.

Breaking Changes

  • Made serde optional, explicit and disabled by default. The rendering APIs, context! and args! now consume values and convert exclusively through Into<Value>. Serde conversion is requested with the new value::Serde wrapper which also replaces ViaDeserialize for deserializing function arguments. Value::from_serialize was removed. The deserialization feature was removed and is now part of the serde feature. Disabling the feature fully removes the dependency. #528
  • The json feature no longer depends on serde and serde_json. The tojson filter and JSON auto escaping now use a built-in JSON serializer. Invalid values now fail the serialization rather than being emitted as null. Floats are formatted like recent versions of serde_json do (for instance 1e+16 instead of 1e16). The speedups feature now uses zmij and itoa to format numbers in JSON; the output is the same without it.
  • Made mutable State the canonical path for functions, filters, tests, objects, methods, formatters, unknown method callbacks and nested macro calls. Read-only typed callbacks can continue to use &State; state mutation and dynamic calls now require &mut State. Added typed render-local extensions that persist through includes, blocks and macros. State::get_or_set_temp_object was removed in favor of these extensions.
  • Removed Rust APIs deprecated before 3.0: Template::render_and_return_state, Template::render_to_write, Template::eval_to_state, the Filter, Test, TestResult and ViaDeserialize aliases, value::intern<

title: fix(templates): don't suggest a different variable for an unset Worktrunk variable
body:
When a template reads a Worktrunk variable that the current operation left unset, the undefined-variable error no longer offers a "Did you mean" suggestion. Before this change it suggested a similarly named variable, which points the user at a different value.

The reachable case is a `post-switch` hook containing `echo {{ target }}`, run when switching to a detached worktree. `TemplateVars::for_post_switch` leaves `target` unset there but sets `target_worktree_path`. Rendering fails with `undefined variable target`, and #4350's suggestion logic matched `target_worktree_path` (Jaro–Winkler ≈ 0.86, above the 0.7 cutoff). The right fix for the user is a `{% if target %}` guard, not a rename. `base` / `base_worktree_path` have the same shape.

`build_undefined_vars_error` now skips the suggestion when the missing name is in `vars_available_in` for some hook scope. Typos of real names (`brnch` → `branch`) still get the hint, and the "Available variables" list is unchanged.

`test_unset_worktrunk_variable_gets_no_suggestion` failed before the fix (`Some("target_worktree_path")`) and passes now. The existing suggestion tests in `config::expansion` and the template-related integration tests also pass.
author: worktrunk-bot

title: chore: update tend workflows (0.3.11 → 0.3.13)
body:
Regenerates the Tend workflows with tend 0.3.13 (from 0.3.11). The one behavior change in the generated files is that `tend-ci-fix` now starts only when a watched workflow on `main` **fails**; a cancelled run no longer starts a session, and the prompt drops its `Conclusion:` line since it is always a failure ([max-sixty/tend#1535](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1535)). Every other workflow changes only its action pin.

Other changes riding in with the new action version:

- The bundled Claude Code CLI moves to 2.1.296 (max-sixty/tend#1536).
- The CI skills weigh whether rerunning an unrelated CI failure is worth it before triggering the rerun (max-sixty/tend#1541).
- A new opt-in `workflows.review.await_ci` setting lets a review finish without waiting for CI (max-sixty/tend#1538). This repo doesn't set it, so reviews behave as before.

The PR also updates the nightly overlay (`.claude/skills/running-tend/references/nightly-cleaner.md`), which said `tend-ci-fix` fires on cancelled runs and reads a `Conclusion:` line. Neither holds after this upgrade.

Full upstream diff: https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/compare/0.3.11...0.3.13

title: refactor: stop refining failed forge calls and missing nu/pwsh
body:
Applies `AGENTS.md`'s **Other Tools Own Their Conventions** (#4435) to what #4106 left: where worktrunk refined how it handles a case outside standard use, stop handling the case.

**CI status: a failed forge call shows the error indicator.** The classifier that searched `gh`/`glab`/`az`/`tea` output for English phrases ("rate limit", "403", "connection", …) to choose between ⚠ and a blank "no CI" cell is deleted. Any failed call now shows ⚠. Gitea reads only whether the HTTP status is an error, not which one. The two lookups by commit SHA (GitHub check runs, Gitea combined status) now run only when some remote-tracking ref contains the head, since the forge answers a commit it doesn't have with an error and ordinary unpushed work would otherwise show ⚠. GitLab and Azure look pipelines up by branch and are unchanged.

**PowerShell on Unix.** When `pwsh` can't be queried there is no PowerShell profile, rather than a guessed `~/.config/powershell` one (left by #4422).

**Nushell.** When `nu` can't be queried there are no autoload candidates, rather than a reconstruction of Nushell's data-dir rule. Install can't write into a legacy directory, since the candidate list is empty.

Behavior changes:

- `gh`/`glab`/`az` installed but not logged in now shows ⚠ under `wt list --full` instead of a blank cell. Detection checks that the tool is installed, and `wt config show` reports that it isn't logged in. The ⚠ legend now names "not logged in".
- A Gitea 404 shows ⚠.
- `wt config shell install powershell` (or `nu`) without the tool fails with "No shell config files found", and uninstall no longer finds a wrapper left behind after `nu` was removed.

**Fish's completion path.** `Shell::completion_path` answered for every shell, but only fish installs a completion file; its other arms, including the Nushell one this change touched, were dead. `shell::fish_completion_path` replaces it.

Tests: the retriable-classifier unit tests are gone, and the Gitea test that only distinguished a blanked 500 body. Mocks now answer for branches other than the one under test, since those would otherwise show ⚠. New tests: a failed `gh pr list` / `glab mr list` shows ⚠; an unpushed head skips the GitHub and Gitea lookups by SHA, each with a pushed control. Shell unit tests and the PowerShell integration tests no longer depend on a real `nu` or `pwsh`; they pass with only `/usr/bin:/bin` on `PATH`. Full integration and unit suites pass locally.

Ref #4106.

title: docs(agents): let other tools own their conventions
body:
Adds **Other Tools Own Their Conventions** under Code Quality in `AGENTS.md`, and folds "Use Existing Dependencies"' closing sentence ("Let dependencies own their own rules") into it:

> Where another tool owns a convention, such as its config location, file format, URL syntax, or error reporting, ask that tool or a library that implements its rules instead of encoding them in Worktrunk: `nu` reports its own directories, and `gh auth token --hostname` reports whether a host is authenticated. Worktrunk's role is the standard uses of those conventions. Where neither the tool nor a library answers, support the standard case and remove rather than refine: an input that only misbehaves outside standard use is a reason to stop reading it, and a tool that isn't installed has nothing to integrate with, so needs no fallback table.

#4169 is the case it comes from: filtering relative `XDG_CONFIG_DIRS` entries became, on review, no longer reading `XDG_CONFIG_DIRS` at all.

Code the rule implies removing, to be done in a follow-up rather than found piecemeal: `nushell_data_dir_fallback` in `src/shell/paths.rs`, which re-encodes Nushell's data-dir rule for when `nu` can't be queried, and the PowerShell `~/.config/powershell` fallback for when `pwsh` can't answer.

title: fix(copy): fall back to a byte copy when reflink is rejected with EPERM
body:
reflink-copy 0.1.30's `reflink_or_copy` passes `PermissionDenied` from the clone attempt straight through instead of falling back to `fs::copy` (it does the same for `NotFound` and `AlreadyExists`). On the reporter's kernel `FICLONE` returns `EPERM` rather than `EOPNOTSUPP`, so `wt step copy-ignored` failed with "Operation not permitted" on a file that `cp --reflink=auto` copies without trouble.

`copy_leaf` now goes through a small wrapper that retries with a byte copy when the reflink attempt returns `PermissionDenied`. The file is then reported as written in full rather than reflinked. A real permission problem on the source or destination fails the retry with the same error, so it is still reported. The crate's `AutoRemovedFile` deletes the destination it created before returning the error, so the retry doesn't call `fs::copy`, which could overwrite a file another process puts there in that gap. It copies into a temp file beside the destination, gives it the source's mode, and moves it into place with a no-clobber rename (`persist_noclobber`, as `utils::write_new_atomically` does). The destination only ever appears complete. If something already occupies it, the retry fails with `AlreadyExists`, which `copy_leaf` already skips. A failed copy removes only its own temp file, and if that removal fails the error says so.

No CI filesystem rejects `FICLONE` with `EPERM`, so the regression test `test_reflink_rejected_with_eperm_falls_back_to_copy` covers the retry decision with synthetic errors: `PermissionDenied` falls back, a failing retry still errors, and success and `AlreadyExists` pass through without a retry. `test_rejected_reflink_fallback_does_not_overwrite_racing_destination` creates a file at the destination between the rejected reflink and the retry, and checks that the file survives. `test_failed_copy_cleanup_leaves_racing_destination` checks that a failed copy leaves a file at the destination alone and leaves no temp file. `test_discard_temp_reports_cleanup_failure` checks that a failed temp-file removal is reported. `test_copy_to_new_file_copies_contents_and_mode` checks the contents and mode. The full path was not run on an EPERM-rejecting filesystem.

#4346 also edits this call site in `src/copy.rs` and keeps the bare `reflink_copy::reflink_or_copy`. Whichever lands second should route its call through the wrapper.

Closes #4433 — automated triage

title: Fix hook filtering, source isolation and template failure handling
body:
Hook name filters previously ran after template validation and argument routing, so an excluded command could reject the invocation or consume its arguments. Filtered background hooks also combined user and project sources, and runtime template failures bypassed foreground Warn handling.

Select raw commands before parsing or binding arguments. Live execution and frozen approval plans share preparation; the announcer owns one background pipeline per source. Runtime expansion follows the existing Warn/FailFast policy, while errors retain hook identity and alias diagnostics. Selected templates still receive syntax validation before execution. No flags or configuration keys change.

The production change removes 24 lines overall (+183/−207 across 11 files). The full diff is +911/−267 across 34 files, mostly regression tests and snapshots. It includes current main’s JSON output, stdin ownership and Ctrl-C behavior.

Validation: the required project gate passed 5,411 tests with one skipped, plus lint, lockfile, doctests and rustdoc. Independent integration and simplification review found no unresolved defects. Regression coverage includes excluded malformed templates, argument binding, independent background sources, foreground serial/concurrent failure policy, picker diagnostics and alias errors.

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- docs/src/content/docs/hook.md (+2/-2)
@@ -356,9 +356,9 @@ $ wt hook post-start
 
 ## Passing values
 
-`--KEY=VALUE` binds `KEY` whenever `{{ KEY }}` appears in any command of the hook — the same smart-routing rule `wt <alias>` uses. Built-in variables can be overridden: `--branch=foo` sets `{{ branch }}` inside hook templates (the worktree's actual branch doesn't move). Hyphens in keys become underscores: `--my-var=x` sets `{{ my_var }}`.
+`--KEY=VALUE` binds `KEY` whenever `{{ KEY }}` appears in any selected hook command — the same smart-routing rule `wt <alias>` uses. Built-in variables can be overridden: `--branch=foo` sets `{{ branch }}` inside hook templates (the worktree's actual branch doesn't move). Hyphens in keys become underscores: `--my-var=x` sets `{{ my_var }}`.
 
-Any `--KEY=VALUE` whose key isn't referenced by a hook template forwards into `{{ args }}` as a literal `--KEY=VALUE` token. title: feat(switch): add [switch.picker] preview setting to open the picker list-only
body:
Adds `[switch.picker] preview = false`, which opens `wt switch`'s picker with the preview hidden. `Alt-p` still shows it. The default stays `true`.

The change appends skim's `hidden` modifier to the preview-window spec (`right:N:hidden` / `down:N:hidden`). skim's `toggle-preview` flips that same `preview_window.hidden` flag, so the existing `alt-p` binding reveals the pane at the size the picker already computed. Background preview pre-rendering is unchanged, so the first reveal is just as warm as an always-visible preview, and the setting costs no more work than today's open-then-`Alt-p`.

Verification:

- A new PTY test, `test_switch_picker_preview_hidden_by_config`, checks that the picker opens without the preview controls line and that `Alt-p` brings it back. The test fails when the `:hidden` append is removed.
- Unit tests cover parsing, the accessor default, and merging.
- `wt switch --help`, `wt config create`, and the generated docs mention the key. Help snapshots were refreshed.

Closes #4072

title: fix(test): gate the highlighted hook-template snapshot on syntax-highlighting
body:
The nightly `feature-powerset` job ([run 38115848986](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/38115848986)) fails in `cargo test --no-default-features` on `git::error::tests::snapshot_worktrunk_error_display`. #4352 added a case to that test where an unnamed hook failure renders its template (`echo test`) through `format_bash_with_gutter`. This change moves that case into its own test, `snapshot_unnamed_hook_failure_shows_template`, gated on `#[cfg(feature = "syntax-highlighting")]`. `snapshot_worktree_creation_failed` in the same module is already gated this way for the same reason. The other assertions in `snapshot_worktrunk_error_display` still run in every feature configuration. This only changes tests.

title: test: fail the re-exec'd signal tests when the child runs no test
body:
`run_custom_propagates_signal_exit_code` (`src/commands/custom.rs`) and `operation_cancellation_survives_scope_retirement_and_resets` (`src/signal_forwarder.rs`) re-run the test binary with `--exact <test path>` so they run alone in their own process, then only check that the child exits successfully. If the module or test is renamed and the hard-coded path isn't updated, `--exact` matches nothing, libtest exits 0 with `0 passed`, and the parent test passes without running anything.

The parent now captures the child's stdout and also requires libtest's ` 1 passed;` summary.

Verified locally: with the `--exact` path in `custom.rs` changed to a nonexistent test, the test passed on `main` and now fails. With the correct paths, both tests pass under `cargo test` and `cargo nextest`.

title: docs: correct comments left stale by recent step, diagnostic and merge changes
body:
Corrects internal comments and notes that recent changes left describing old behavior. No code behavior changes; the one test edit is a rename.

- `src/commands/for_each.rs` — the module's design note listed `step` as holding only `commit`, `squash`, `rebase`, `push` and `for-each`. It now also has `diff`, `copy-ignored`, `eval`, `promote`, `prune`, `relocate` and `tether`, so the note describes the grouping without an inventory that goes stale again.

title: fix(shell): discover the Unix PowerShell profile from the installed pwsh
body:
On Unix, shell installation now asks the installed PowerShell runtime for `$PROFILE.CurrentUserCurrentHost`, so a custom `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` selects the profile PowerShell actually loads. Install, uninstall and configuration detection share the cached result. The local query uses `-NoProfile`, disables telemetry and update checks, and uses the existing five-second probe timeout. Missing, failing or invalid runtime output retains the conventional fallback. Windows continues to use the known Documents folder candidates for both PowerShell editions.

Native SIGINT/SIGTERM cancels installation before profile writes, including when descendants keep the probe's output pipes open. The shared timed-command primitive now observes the child's native terminal status without reaping its leader until process-group teardown completes, preserving the existing process-ID safety guarantee. Typed interruption also propagates through diagnostics, switch/remove warnings, and installation offers before another probe or hint mutation starts.

Validation covers custom-XDG installation and removal, malformed/unavailable runtime fallback, native interruption versus ordinary exit 130, pipe-holding descendants, bounded timeouts, and real pwsh profile discovery without executing user profiles. Regression tests exercise both the shell-installation flow and the shared timeout primitive.

An obsolete profile previously written under `~/.config` while a custom XDG location was active is no longer an install/uninstall candidate; PowerShell did not load it, and treating it as configured would preserve the original bug.

Closes #4419.

title: fix: parse remote URLs with gix-url so IPv6 hosts and SSH ports get distinct project identifiers
body:
`GitRemoteUrl::parse` split SSH authorities at the first `:`, so `ssh://git@[2001:db8::1]/owner/repo.git` and `ssh://git@[2001:db8::2]/owner/repo.git` both became `[2001/owner/repo`. Because that identifier selects both saved approvals and `[projects]` settings, the two servers shared them. The parser also dropped explicit SSH ports, merging servers on different ports. The parser now delegates transport syntax to `gix-url` 0.40, and the identity keeps the full IPv6 host and any non-default SSH port.

What changes:

- **Syntax from `gix-url`.** It handles scheme, SCP form, userinfo (split at the final `@` of the authority, which is the host git connects to), IPv6 literals and ports. Worktrunk still owns the namespace/repo split and the forge policy. HTTP(S), git and SSH remotes are accepted, plus SCP when it has a non-empty user (the existing rule). Remote helpers, `file://`, local paths, option-like hosts and out-of-range ports are rejected.
- **Escaped paths.** The path comes from `original_path()`, not the decoded `path`, so `evil%2Frepo` stays a single segment in SSH, SCP and git forms, as it already did for HTTPS.
- **IPv6 hosts** are always bracketed (`[2001:db8::1]`), since `gix-url` strips the brackets for SSH but keeps them for HTTP(S).
- **SSH ports.** A new `ssh_port` field goes into `project_identifier()` (`host:2222/owner/repo`) but not into `host()`, which feeds web and API URLs; an SSH port is not the web port. An explicit `:22` is treated as no port. HTTP(S) and git keep their explicit port in `host()`, as before.
- **No new identity API.** `project_identifier()` is still the only identity; there is no separate one.

Approvals and settings: the ordinary forms of one project still share an identifier (`git@host:o/r`, `ssh://git@host/o/r`, `ssh://git@host:22/o/r`, `https://host/o/r`). Corrected identities get fresh keys, so old IPv6-truncated or port-merged approvals don't carry over. The same applies to `[projects]` settings: a user on `ssh://…:2222` with a `[projects."host/o/r"]` entry needs to re-key it to `host:2222/o/r`. Nothing warns about this. The config docs now say that a non-default port stays with the host.

Smaller identifier changes from delegating normalization:

- DNS-style hostnames are lowercased (`GitHub.com` → `github.com`).
- `git+ssh://` and `ssh+git://` now parse; before, they fell back to the raw-URL identifier.
- Some inputs `gix-url` rejects now fall back to the raw-URL identifier in `Repository::project_identifier`: URLs containing whitespace, and SCP `user@[ipv6]:path`. Each still gets a distinct identifier.

Tests:

- New unit tests cover the IPv6 collision, port isolation (including a port inside hostile userinfo), escaped paths across transports, and rejected forms.
- `tests/integration_tests/repository.rs` checks that `Repository::project_identifier` keeps the two IPv6 remotes apart. It also checks that `Approvals::is_command_approved` and `UserConfig::worktree_path_for_project` pick the right entry fo

title: fix: delegate tea login discovery and preserve settings key order
body:
Delegate tea login discovery to its local `logins list --output json` command, replacing Worktrunk's YAML scanner and platform-specific config-path guesses. Forge routing matches both web and SSH hosts; diagnostics share the same probe. Native cancellation stops subsequent probes, while ordinary command failures retain the existing unauthenticated fallback. The local-only command was also checked with real tea v0.12.0.

Preserve existing JSON object order when installing the Claude statusline, including nested settings. Generated schemas and documentation retain canonical sorting; command JSON snapshots now follow construction order, with unchanged values. Regression coverage includes login discovery, routing, cancellation, and settings key order. Ref #4106.

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

title: fix(test): run the run_custom SIGTERM test in its own process
body:
`run_custom_propagates_signal_exit_code` runs a child that dies of SIGTERM, and `wait_foreground_child` then calls `cancel_foreground(SIGTERM)`, which marks every live foreground scope in the process as interrupted. When `run_custom_spawn_failure_resolves_trace` (or any other test in the `wt` binary that installs `ForegroundSignals`, such as the `output::concurrent` tests) had installed its scope but not yet spawned, its spawn error came back as `WorktrunkError::Interrupted` ("Terminated"). The signal test now re-execs the test binary filtered to itself, the same isolation [`signal_forwarder`'s operation-lifetime test](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/4ff0569000fab055afaff710a2d5b820dbc91cc9/src/signal_forwarder.rs#L518-L536) uses, so its process-wide cancellation can't reach a sibling test. Production code is unchanged.

Looping the `commands::custom` tests 200 times failed 16 times before this change and 0 times after it.

Closes #4416 — automated triage
author: worktrunk-bot

title: Gate signing and host OIDC through the release environment
body:
The release workflow's `host` job granted OIDC token access without an environment gate. It now uses the tag-only `release` environment, and Windows signing shares that environment because `signing` had the same admin-controlled tag policy.

The SignPath CI token has been rotated and provisioned in both environments before this change. Credentials remain explicit inputs to their consuming steps; the shared environment makes all release secrets available through the jobs' secrets context. This also gives `host` the documented `release` scope used by crates.io Trusted Publishing.

Validated with the project pre-merge checks, actionlint, an independent security-boundary review, and Tend's credential-environment check against live GitHub policies: the original workflow fails on `host`, and this workflow passes.

Fixes #4312.

+- release admits tags and holds AUR_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY, TEND_BOT_TOKEN, and SIGNPATH_API_TOKEN; it also gates packslip signing and crates.io Trusted Publishing through OIDC.

title: Have wt-switch-create read the new repo's root instructions
body:
When `wt-switch-create` moves a Claude Code session into another repo's worktree, the session keeps the launch repo's root `AGENTS.md` (and its auto-memory) in context and never loads the new repo's root file; only the new repo's nested instruction files load, lazily, as files under them are read. So the agent ends up following the wrong project's top-level rules mixed with the right project's nested ones.

With a repo argument, the skill now has the agent read whichever of the new worktree's root `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` exist once it is working there, and treat them as superseding the launch repo's. `rationale.md` records the verification against Claude Code 2.1.296: headless sessions through `EnterWorktree({path})` and `EnterWorktree({name})` both kept the launch repo's root file, a session started in the worktree loaded the new one, and the `name` route can't cross repos anyway because the `WorktreeCreate` hook creates in `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`.

 narrow symlink-resolving-to-the-same-cwd fixup), so a repo reachable by neither

+### Re-rooting keeps the launch repo's instructions
+
+Re-rooting into another repo changes the cwd but not the instruction context.
+Verified 2026-10-10 against Claude Code 2.1.296 with three headless sessions.
+Two launched in another repo, then ran `cd` plus `EnterWorktree({path})` or
+`cd` plus `EnterWorktree({name})`; each context still held the launch repo's
+root `AGENTS.md` and auto-memory index, with nothing from the new repo. The
+third, started in the worktree, loaded the new repo's. Nested instruction files of the

+instruction files but doesn't rebuild the root block, which reloads only at

+So with a repo argument, the skill has the agent read the new root files after

+context, as does its auto-memory.

 The Bash tool is not a bare shell: Claude Code replays the user's shell startup

title: Keep public documentation concise and reader-focused
body:
Clarify that public docs should use readers’ terms, keep detail proportional to its audience, and correct false claims with the smallest sufficient edit. Keep implementation rationale and unchanged-usage regression details in code and tests.

Validation: full pre-merge gate passed (5,208 tests); independent guidance review and 14 controlled composition checks passed.

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- AGENTS.md (+1/-1)
@@ -26,7 +26,7 @@ Each worktree maps to one branch. Worktree arguments resolve branch first throug
 
 ## Documentation
 
-Public docs are curated product guidance, not an exhaustive specification. Document new capabilities and changed usage; correct existing claims that become false. A correctness fix with no change to usage needs no new prose: an omitted failure case is not an inaccurate claim. Keep regression conditions in tests and commit messages.
+Public docs help users choose and use Worktrunk. Keep them concise, in the reader’s terms, with detail proportional to how many readers need it. Document new capabilities and changed usage; correct false claims in place with the smallest sufficient edit. Implementation rationale belongs in code. A correctness fix that preserves usage needs no new guide prose; keep regression conditions in tests and commit messages.
 
 src/cli/mod.rs is primary for command help and generated command pages; docs/AGENTS.md explains sync. Check that --help matches behavior. Run cargo test --test integration test_docs_are_in_sync, then refresh help snapshots when help text changes.

title: docs: require full release documentation review
body:
Require an independent review of every documentation change since the previous release, including changes already on main and edits arriving during release preparation. Review purpose and proportion before clarity, accuracy, examples, links, and rendered context; verify corrections and block tagging on unresolved findings.

Apply the 0.81.0 review's source corrections: remove implementation exposition, repair the bare-repo navigation example, clarify merge hook timing and branch-only removal JSON, and include squash backups in the metadata inventory. Canonical help, generated pages, shipped skill mirrors, and help snapshots remain synchronized. Candidate-only release-note edits stay with the release PR.

Validation: independent source, workflow, and rendered-page reviews; project pre-merge gate (5,208 tests, lint, Rustdoc, and doctests); documentation sync, 56 help cases, both site builds, and 16 built-site checks.

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md (+25/-2)
@@ -27,7 +27,7 @@ metadata:
      ```
      Launch a ci-reporter to monitor `$RUN` to completion (avoid `gh run watch` — it can hang). Fix any failure before continuing.

-4. **Review commits**: Check commits since last release to understand scope of changes. Audit the cumulative diff for the data-loss surface (see [Data-Loss Surface Review](#data-loss-surface-review)) before proceeding.
+4. **Review commits**: Check commits since last release to understand scope of changes. Audit the cumulative diff for the data-loss surface (see [Data-Loss Surface Review](#data-loss-surface-review)) and documentation (see [Documentation Review](#documentation-review)).

If it reports breaking changes, that's fine; under semver the bump must still be minor (pre-1.0) or major (post-1.0). See "Library API Compatibility" below.

+11. **Merge to main**: complete the documentation review on the final candidate, then push the release branch, open a PR, wait for CI, and merge it. Keep the worktree — the remaining steps run from it. Then move the branch onto the merged tip:

     ```

The list only grows across passes — the drifted commits stay, joined by the follow-up's own squash commit — so each pass re-checks coverage over a longer list.
 
+    Extend the documentation review to any changes since its reviewed SHA, including corrections and commits that arrived during CI. Record the final reviewed SHA and resolve findings before tagging.
+
     Once clean, tag `origin/main`. The check and the tag then name the same ref, and it's main's tip, so the tag is reachable from `main`:
     ```bash
     git tag vX.Y.Z origin/main && git push origin vX.Y.Z
@@ -93,6 +95,27 @@ Pool the candidates, dedupe, and analyze each against the data-safety invariants
 
 Surface the full adjudicated list and get explicit sign-off before tagging. Do not tag a release with an unresolved deletion-surface candidate, even if it looks acceptable.
 
+## Documentation Review
+
+The release reviews all documentation changes since the previous release, including changes already on `main` and edits made during release preparation. Public docs are curated product guidance: each passage should help readers understand or use Worktrunk, with detail proportional to how many readers need it.
+
+Start from the full release diff to inventory documentation wherever it lives:

Review canonical sources once and check their generated copies for agreement; `docs/AGENTS.md` defines ownership and sync.

+- **Purpose and proportion:** does it change what readers understand or do? Cut redundant explanations and implementation or regression details that belong in tests or PRs. A correctness fix needs prose only when usage changes or an existing claim becomes false.
+- **Clarity and concision:** use concrete, consistent terminology; introduce concepts before relying on them; rewrite definitions in place rather than layering caveats. Shortening must preserve necessary instructions and qualifications.
+- **Accuracy and usability:** verify claims against behavior and examples against their commands. Check links and read affected rendered sections as a reader encounters them.
+
+For each finding, give the location, reader impact, and a concrete replacement or deletion. Apply corrections in the canonical source, regenerate mirrors, and run the checks in `docs/AGENTS.md`. Have the reviewer check the corrected passages before closing findings. Record the reviewed range and SHA, coverage, findings, and their disposition in the release review; unresolved findings block tagging. title: fix: find Git Bash when git resolves under Git\mingw64\bin
body:
Inside a Git Bash session, MSYS puts `<Git>\mingw64\bin` ahead of `<Git>\cmd` on PATH, so `which git` returns `<Git>\mingw64\bin\git.exe`. `find_git_bash` derived bash only from the git path's grandparent (`<Git>\mingw64`). Neither `mingw64\bin\bash.exe` nor `mingw64\usr\bin\bash.exe` exists there, and the two hard-coded fallbacks only cover default install locations. A custom install location therefore failed every check, and anything using `ShellConfig::get()`, such as background removal and background hooks, failed with "Git for Windows is required but not found".

The derivation now lives in `git_bash_beside_git`. If the first root misses, it tries one level higher, the real install root, checking `bin\bash.exe` and then `usr\bin\bash.exe` at each level. The existing `cmd`, `bin`, and `usr\bin` layouts still resolve as before because their first root still hits first. The Codex hook shim `plugins/worktrunk/hooks/wt.cmd` says it resolves bash "the way find_git_bash does", so its `:derive` gets the same two extra candidates.

`test_git_bash_beside_git_install_layouts` builds each Git for Windows layout in a tempdir and checks the derived path. It runs on every platform, and it fails on the `mingw64\bin` cases with the old one-level lookup. Linux CI cannot run the `wt.cmd` change. The Windows shim tests cover its existing paths, but none plants a `mingw64\bin` git.

Closes #4410 — automated triage

title: fix(picker): keep text after an ANSI reset dark on the selected picker row
body:
In the `wt switch` picker, a branch-only row whose branch isn't removable (for example a diverged branch) draws its branch name in the terminal's default foreground when the row is selected. On a dark theme that means light text on the light selection bar. This PR makes that text inherit the selected row's dark `current:237` foreground, like every other unstyled cell on the row.

Reported in https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/1264#issuecomment-6086377802 on v0.80.0 with wezterm and kanagawa-paper-ink. In the screenshot, the selected `/ chore/tsdown-update` row's text is `#DCD7BA`, the theme's default foreground, on `#C6C6C6` (palette 251). The `main` worktree row in the same report renders `#3A3A3A` (palette 237) as expected.

**Cause.** A branch-only row starts with a dim `/ ` gutter that `wt list`'s renderer closes with `\x1b[0m`. ansi-to-tui parses everything after that reset with an explicit `fg = Color::Reset`, and a span-level `Reset` overrides the line-level `current` style that skim applies to the selected row. `ansi_to_line` already cleared the reset `bg` for the same reason, so this change also maps a `Reset` fg to `None`. On unselected rows nothing changes, because `normal` is `fg:-1`, which is `Reset` already.

Removable rows aren't affected: their branch name is dim, and `anchor_faint_under_selection` already redraws it as gray 245 on the selected row. That is why the earlier fix didn't cover this case.

**Test.** `ansi_to_line_leaves_reset_foreground_to_the_row_style` feeds the exact gutter-plus-branch ANSI that `wt list --branches` emits for a diverged branch. It failed before the change (`("feature ", Some(Reset))`) and passes after. The picker unit tests pass locally. PTY snapshots capture plain text, so they don't change.

I can't drive the picker in a real terminal from CI, so the on-screen result hasn't been checked visually.

Refs #1264

title: fix(copy-ignored): let directory patterns cover files inside the directory
body:
A `.worktreeinclude` or `[step.copy-ignored].exclude` pattern naming a directory (`config/`) now covers the ignored files inside it, as the same line would in `.gitignore`. Before, it silently missed any ignored file that shares its directory with tracked files.

The cause: `git ls-files --ignored -o --directory` collapses a directory to `config/` only when everything in it is ignored. With a tracked `config/app.yml` beside an ignored `config/local.yml`, it lists `config/local.yml` itself, and both matchers in [`list_and_filter_ignored_entries`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/fb7a28003f9cb7cb8f2d7e9bb04aabd880b3b892/src/commands/step/shared.rs#L108) used `Gitignore::matched`, which tests only the path given. As a result:

- `.worktreeinclude` = `config/` → `wt step copy-ignored` reported "No matching files to copy".
- `exclude = ["config/"]` → `config/local.yml` was copied anyway.

Both matchers now call `matched_path_or_any_parents` on the worktree-relative path. A negation on the file itself (`!config/local.yml`) still wins, because the file is checked before its parents. `wt step promote` uses the same include filter, so it now swaps those files as well, which is what its docs describe ("filtered with `.worktreeinclude`").

Two regression tests in `step_copy_ignored.rs` cover the include and exclude cases. Both failed before the change, and they pass with it alongside the rest of `step_copy_ignored` and `step_promote`. The exceptions are two existing tests that also fail on `main` in this sandbox: one depends on umask (expects 0644, gets 0664) and one creates a Unix socket.

title: fix(test): make the sibling step ignore SIGINT in the caught-interrupt alias test
body:
`test_alias_caught_sigint_preserves_successful_descendant_output` failed on [the 2026-10-09 nightly macOS run](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/37890340903) with `assertion failed: job.wait().success()`. The test sends SIGINT to the whole job group once both alias steps have written their ready markers, but the second step (`two`) could still be alive between writing `second-ready` and exiting. A native SIGINT death there correctly cancels the alias, so `wt` exited non-zero. The test was racing, not `wt`.

`two` now runs `trap '' INT`, so only the trapping `one` step exercises the caught-interrupt path the test is about. No production code changes.

Verification: with a `sleep 1` added after `two`'s marker to widen the window, the original test fails on Linux with the same assertion as the nightly. Adding `trap '' INT` makes it pass, and the final version (without the sleep) passed 5 local runs in a row.

title: fix: find batch-launcher CLIs like az.cmd on Windows
body:
On Windows, `std::process::Command` resolves a bare program name like `az` to `az.exe` only. It doesn't walk `PATHEXT`. Azure CLI's WinGet install ships `az.cmd` and an extensionless bash script, with no `az.exe`, so every `az` spawn failed with `NotFound` and `wt` reported an installed, working CLI as missing. `Cmd::direct_command` now resolves a bare name through `which`, which follows `PATHEXT` and skips files Windows can't execute. When the match is a `.cmd` or `.bat`, `Cmd` spawns that full path, and std applies its batch-file argument quoting. Any other result keeps the bare name and std's own search order. Each name is resolved once per process, so the hot `git` path pays for one PATH scan, not one per call.

The new Windows-only test `test_config_show_finds_batch_launcher_az` copies the WinGet layout into the mock bin directory: an `az.cmd` that forwards to the mock binary, the extensionless `az` script, and no `az.exe`. It asserts that `wt config show --full` reports `az installed & authenticated`. I couldn't build for Windows in this sandbox, so this PR's Windows CI is the first run of both the test and the fix. Before the fix, nothing named `az.exe` is on that PATH: the runner's own Azure CLI is also `az.cmd`. So the bare spawn has nothing to find, the same failure the reporter isolated in a standalone Rust program.

Closes #4401 — automated triage
author: worktrunk-bot

title: fix: preserve native foreground job control
body:
Foreground hooks could hang when they changed terminal settings: Worktrunk created a separate process group without giving it the terminal, so the kernel stopped the child with SIGTTOU. Foreground commands now stay in the caller's native job group, consistently for single and concurrent commands. Terminal access, Ctrl-C and job suspension follow the shell's native behavior.

### Design

- `signal_forwarder` owns foreground cancellation and child admission. Native SIGINT/SIGTERM deaths stop later hooks and worktree steps; a child that catches Ctrl-C keeps its ordinary exit semantics, including exit code 130. SIGTERM addressed to wt cancels its owned work even when a child catches it.
- `shell_exec` and concurrent output share that lifecycle. Output drains stop on cancellation; complete buffered stdin uses an anonymous temporary file instead of writer threads. Real process pipelines remain pipes. Buffered stdin therefore requires temporary storage and is seekable.
- Help and preview pagers use Git's pager selection and the same process primitives. Interactive pager cancellation propagates silently, and preview deadlines cover output and child waits.
- Shell wrappers apply directory directives and clean temporary files while preserving native interrupt behavior. Nushell integration now requires 0.113 or newer and uses native `finally` cleanup.

Nushell 0.116's `finally` itself can abort a noninteractive script after Ctrl-C even when the child catches it and exits successfully. Worktrunk's directory change and cleanup still complete; the same script-continuation difference reproduces in a minimal Nushell `try/finally` without Worktrunk.

Bash applies aborted-line cleanup through a writable `PROMPT_COMMAND`. With a readonly prompt command or `set -a`, it applies ordinary cleanup while preserving that configuration; Ctrl-C can leave the pending directory directive unapplied.

The main behavioral coverage uses real children and PTYs: terminal ownership/settings, raw and caught Ctrl-C, PID-targeted cancellation, stopped jobs, concurrent output, pagers, and generated shell wrappers. Module contracts describe ownership and platform differences.

### Validation

The complete project pre-merge gate passes locally, including the real-shell/PTY suite, Clippy, formatting, locked dependencies, and documentation checks. The change also received an independent Opus correctness and simplicity review, with fixes reviewed through convergence. macOS runtime validation is local; Linux and Windows run in CI.

Closes #4389. Thanks to @user753 for the reproduction.

title: fix(picker): apply per-project pager override to the diff preview
body:
The `wt switch` picker ignored a per-project pager. `diff_pager()` in `src/commands/picker/pager.rs` loaded the user config itself and called `switch_picker(None)`, so a `[projects."<id>".switch.picker] pager` override never applied; the preview used the global `[switch.picker] pager`, or `GIT_PAGER`/`core.pager` when that was unset. The `[projects]` help says scalar settings can be overridden per project, and `UserConfig::switch_picker` already merges those overrides when it is given a project id.

The fix reads the pager from `repo.config().switch_picker`, which `Repository::config()` resolves for the current project. That also reuses the repo's cached user config instead of reloading it from disk for the preview. `page_diff` and `diff_pager` now take the repository; the cache stays process-wide because the picker runs against a single repository.

`test_switch_picker_project_pager_override` in `tests/integration_tests/switch_picker.rs` sets a pager only under the test repo's `[projects.'<id>'.switch.picker]` and checks that its marker line appears in the diff preview. It fails on `main`, where the preview shows the unpaged diff, and passes with the fix. The removed `test_get_diff_pager_initializes` only called `diff_pager()` and asserted nothing.

title: fix(alias): forward `--args=X` and `--vars=X` instead of dropping them
body:
`wt <alias> --args=x` and `wt <alias> --vars=x` (and the same tokens on `wt hook`) were silently dropped whenever the template referenced `args` or `vars`. They now forward into `{{ args }}` like any other unbound flag.

Argument routing binds `--KEY=VALUE` to `{{ KEY }}` when the template references KEY. But the runtime sets both reserved keys *after* the CLI bindings: [`run_alias`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/3a8d5446d2a943180cdd3fb9323add7b8b2bfabb/src/commands/alias.rs#L692-L696) overwrites `args` with the positional list, and `expand_template` replaces `vars` with the per-branch vars object. So the bound value was discarded and the token was in neither place. With `run = "echo got [{{ args }}]"`:

```console
$ wt -y run --args=x y
got [y]
$ wt config alias dry-run run -- --args=x y
  # bound: args=x
  # args: y
  echo got [y]
```

The dry-run output claimed a binding that never reached the command. After this change, both commands render `got [--args=x y]`.

The fix adds one predicate, `binds_cli_var` in `src/config/expansion.rs`. The alias parser (both the `=` and space forms) and `wt hook`'s shorthand routing now call it instead of a bare `referenced.contains`. It refuses to bind `args` and `vars`. Forwarding was chosen over an error because it is what the routing rule already does for any key it cannot bind, and it keeps the user's token intact. The deprecated `wt hook --var args=x` force-bind is left as is.

**Tests:**
- `test_step_alias_args_flag_forwards_to_args` (alias) and `test_var_shorthand_args_key_forwards` (`wt hook pre-start`) fail on `main` with `got y` and an empty file respectively, and pass with the fix.
- `test_parse_reserved_keys_forward_even_when_referenced` pins the parser routing for both reserved keys and both token forms.

Updates the generated Tend workflows from 0.3.9 to 0.3.10. The workflow diff is only the version stamp and the `max-sixty/tend/claude@0.3.10` action pin; the behavior change comes with the action and bundled skills.

What changes for this repo:

- **Flaky PR tests get an owner instead of just a rerun.** When a review finds a check failing for reasons unrelated to the PR, it now waits for the rerun's result and routes the failure: infrastructure blips are named in the summary, failures `main` also shows are left to `ci-fix`, and a project test that fails on the PR while `main` passes it gets an issue (or an appended run on the existing one), which `tend-triage` then picks up (max-sixty/tend#1518). Expect occasional new bot-filed issues naming an intermittently failing test.
- **The action's runtime ships as the `tend` package** and runs through `tend runtime …` commands rather than loose scripts (max-sixty/tend#1512). No consumer configuration changes; it should be invisible apart from setup logs.

No model defaults changed for the Claude harness, and `.config/tend.yaml` carries no model pins, so nothing there was edited.

title: fix(priority): run the self-lowering helpers through shell_exec::Cmd
body:
`priority::lower_current_process` started `renice` and `ionice` (or `taskpolicy` on macOS) with a bare `std::process::Command`. AGENTS.md requires external commands to go through `shell_exec::Cmd`, and these calls weren't detached or interactive, so no exemption covered them. In practice a `post-start = "wt step copy-ignored"` hook runs with `WORKTRUNK_FOREGROUND=-1`, so [`step_copy_ignored`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/aa0f7f829d473b69041983c89cc07d237374c3a5/src/commands/step/copy_ignored.rs#L61-L62) lowers its own priority, and until now those helper calls never appeared in `trace.log` or the `-vv` output. This PR runs them through `Cmd::run` and ignores the result as before, so a missing or failing helper still leaves the process at normal priority.

The new `test_copy_ignored_background_priority_helper_is_traced` runs `wt -vv step copy-ignored` with `WORKTRUNK_FOREGROUND=-1` and checks the trace for the platform's helper. It fails on `main` and passes with the change. It is Unix-only because the function does nothing on Windows.

Local `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes`: clippy and fmt pass. Seven tests fail in the CI sandbox only, none of them in the changed code: Unix sockets are blocked (`Address family not supported`), umask and key-file permissions differ, and the PowerShell snapshot depends on the environment. CI runs them on real runners.

title: test(docs): serve a local stand-in for the shields.io badge in browser tests
body:
`publish-docs` [run 37425036753](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/37425036753) failed on `desktop code examples fit the content column` with `page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded ... waiting until "load"` on `/`. That timeout is a side effect of #4382, which switched every browser-test navigation from `domcontentloaded` to `load`. Every page header loads the GitHub-stars badge from `img.shields.io` ([`SocialIcons.astro`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/220e59ef641ad34d770143959ed103e541275264/docs/src/components/SocialIcons.astro#L8)), so `load` now also waits on that third-party host. One slow badge response stalls the navigation.

**Fix.** A `newPage` helper in `docs/tests/browser-site.test.mjs` routes `https://img.shields.io/**` to a local SVG sized to the badge's declared 90×20, and all five page-creation sites use it. That leaves the local server and the Google web fonts as the only things `load` waits for. The fonts have to stay real, because the layout assertions measure text set in JetBrains Mono. Analytics doesn't load on `127.0.0.1` (it's gated on `hostname === 'worktrunk.dev'`), and the docs content has no other remote images.

**Verification.** I ran a local Chromium probe against the built site, routing the badge to a request that never answers:
- With the stalled badge, `page.goto(..., { waitUntil: 'load' })` times out, which is the same failure as in CI.
- With the stand-in, `/` loads in about 200 ms. The JetBrains Mono faces in use report `loaded` after `fonts.ready`, and the badge renders at 90×20.

I couldn't run the WebKit suite locally because it needs sudo-installed system libraries. This PR's `check-docs` job runs it.
author: worktrunk-bot

title: test(docs): wait for web fonts before browser layout checks
body:
The `link-check` job on [nightly run 37414713723](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/37414713723) failed `desktop code examples fit the content column` with `/claude-code/ wt list scrolls horizontally at 1401px`. The docs content at that commit is identical to `3e233ef26`, where `publish-docs` ran the same suite green a few hours earlier, so this was a race in the test rather than a site regression.

**Cause.** The browser tests measure layout right after `DOMContentLoaded`. At that point the JetBrains Mono faces, which `custom.css` loads from Google Fonts with `display=swap`, are still `loading`, so code renders in the fallback monospace face. Since #4214, the content column is sized for exactly 99 columns of JetBrains Mono (0.6em, or 8.4px at 14px). On the Ubuntu runner the fallback is DejaVu Sans Mono at about 8.43px, roughly 2.8px wider across 99 columns. That is more than the test's 1px tolerance, so the result depends on whether the font swap has happened by the time the test measures.

**Fix.** All test navigations now go through an `openPage` helper that waits for `load` and then `document.fonts.ready`, so every layout assertion measures the settled page. The helper covers every call site because the mobile, copy-button, and contrast tests take the same unsettled measurement.

**Verification.** In a local Chromium probe of the built site:
- At `DOMContentLoaded`, the JetBrains Mono faces report `loading`, and the `wt list` block measures the same as it does with Google Fonts blocked.
- After `load` plus `fonts.ready`, the faces report `loaded`.

I couldn't run WebKit here because it needs system libraries that require sudo. Chromium's headless shell rounds glyph advances to whole pixels, so its geometry numbers don't stand in for WebKit's. This PR's `check-docs` job runs the WebKit suite and is the real check.
author: worktrunk-bot

title: chore: bump jdx/packslip from 1.4.0 to 1.5.1
body:
Bumps [jdx/packslip](https://github.com/jdx/packslip) from 1.4.0 to 1.5.1.
Release notes

Sourced from jdx/packslip's releases.

v1.5.1: Fix packslip install under a group-writable umask such as Debian's 002

packslip install now works for ordinary users on Debian, Ubuntu, and other systems whose login umask is 002. In 1.5.0 it failed for these users. The packslip format is unchanged and still version 1.

Fixed

  • packslip install no longer refuses its own directories under umask 002. With a user-private-group umask, the directories the installer created were group-writable (0775), and its safety check then rejected them (#188, @​jdx): 
    $ packslip install github.com/jdx/mise
Error:
   0: /home/u/.local/share/packslip/.packslip-stage-X0jH5v has unsafe directory ownership or permissions
    The installer now sets directory modes explicitly instead of relying on the umask. Staging, transaction, command-export, and state directories are 0700. The extracted tree and the download cache are 0755. The safety check has not changed and still refuses any directory another user can write to. Root installs and CI usually run with umask 022, so they were not affected.
  • Library: install_extract::extract now creates a missing parent directory as 0755, matching the rest of the extracted tree. Before, it used the process umask and could leave the directory group-writable. packslip install itself was not affected because it always passes a parent that already exists. (#189, @​jdx)

Documentation

  • The getting-started guide now shows the two install methods added in 1.5.0. For the packslip.sh script, it covers curl -fsSL https://packslip.sh | sh, the PowerShell equivalent, PACKSLIP_BIN_DIR, per-release checksum-pinned URLs, and gh attestation verify. For the ghcr.io/jdx/packslip container image, it shows how to pin it by digest. (#181, @​jdx)

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jdx/packslip/compare/v1.5.0...v1.5.1

v1.5.0: packslip install, signer fingerprints, and new ways to install packslip

packslip install adds a new way to consume releases

title: chore: bump smol-toml from 1.8.0 to 1.9.0 in /docs
body:
Bumps [smol-toml](https://github.com/squirrelchat/smol-toml) from 1.8.0 to 1.9.0.
Release notes

Sourced from smol-toml's releases.

v1.9.0

Huge update!!! This is most likely the largest update the library received since its release, with lots of new features and improvements.

Performance improvements

Significant parts of the internal parse logic have been rewritten, improving performance by 1.5x-2x. The library was already comfortably ahead of the others, but it is now faster than ever, sitting at 4x faster parse performance than the closest maintained implementation.

Problematic code paths have also been replaced by safer implementations, solving potential DoS vectors. See GHSA-r4xh-jqrq-34v2.

Note: the objects returned by the library now have a null prototype. This is a transparent change for 99.9% of users, and is one of the most significant contributors to the major performance gains in this version.

Full Temporal support

Version 1.8.0 brought support for Temporal in stringify; now the library is also able to emit Temporal objects instead of its own ad-hoc TomlDate object. It is not enabled by default, but it will become the default in v2. Enable by setting useLegacyDate: false in the parser's options.

Better Temporal support in stringify

Temporal support has been improved since it released: Temporal objects that cannot be represented (such as Temporal.PlainMonthDay) now throw an error (instead of silently emitting a bogus object).

A new option has been added to stringify to disallow Temporal objects that cannot be fully represented in TOML. This includes ZonedDateTime objects with a IANA timezone attached instead of a plain offset, and dates with a specific calendar value set. Enable by setting strictTemporal: true in the options.

Handling of unsafe keys

Since its release the library has been protected against prototype pollution attacks, setting properties like __proto__ using safe mechanisms that do not trigger prototype pollution. However, while the returned objects are safe on their own, they may become problematic if used carelessly.

Inspired by secure-json-parse, the library now offers a way to either drop unsafe properties from the returned object, or to throw an error and reject documents altogether. By default, these potentially unsafe keys are preserved and returned.

Miscellaneous updates

  • Unicode BOM is now gracefully accepted and ignored.
  • Table array headers are now properly checked again. Reported in #65.
  • Closed certain g

title: test: make remote-detection tests check what their names claim
body:
Three tests in `default_branch.rs` and `ci_status.rs` passed whether or not the behavior they're named for worked. This PR tightens them; test code only.

- **`test_effective_remote_url_is_cached`** called the function twice and compared the results, which passes with no cache at all. It now changes `origin`'s URL between the two calls and asserts the second call still returns the first value.
- **`test_get_default_branch_with_custom_remote`** added `upstream` but left the fixture's `origin` in place, and expected `main`. Local inference returns `main` too, so `upstream` was never exercised. The test now removes `origin` (as `test_primary_remote_detects_custom_remote` already does), points `upstream`'s HEAD at `develop`, and expects `develop`.
- **`test_list_full_with_branch_fallback_using_fork_pushremote`** had an empty check-runs mock meant as the negative control. It was keyed on `upstream-owner/test-repo`, which no remote points at. It now names `test-owner/test-repo`, origin's repo. I checked that swapping the two mocks makes the test fail, so its assertion distinguishes the fork lookup from the origin lookup.

The PR also removes three comments that cite `get_gitlab_host_for_repo`, which no longer exists, and rewrites the `primary_remote` comment, which still described the `git config --get-regexp` call it no longer makes. One `\n\` continuation escape becomes a plain literal, per AGENTS.md.

title: docs: correct docstrings that describe a removed ref cache and wrong validation examples
body:
Comment-only change: four docstrings in `src/git` and `src/config` describe behavior the code no longer has. No code changes, so there's no regression test.

- **`validate_template` examples were backwards.** It claimed validation catches `{{ args }}` in a hook and `{{ target }}` in a `pre-start` hook. Both validate: `vars_available_in(Hook(_))` adds `args`, and the `PreCreate` extras include `target`. The new examples, `{{ base }}` in `pre-merge` and `{{ args }}` in `--execute`, are mismatches that `test_validate_template_scope_rejects_out_of_scope_vars` and the `SwitchExecute` case already assert are rejected. The `ValidationScope::Hook` doc now lists `args` too.
- **"Ambient ref→SHA cache".** #2528 removed `RepoCache::commit_shas`, but comments on `is_ancestor_by_sha`, `has_added_changes_by_sha`, `merge_base_by_sha`, `branch_diff_stats_by_sha`, `compute_integration_lazy`, and the `wt list` snapshot fields still describe the `_by_sha` forms as bypassing it. They now say what those forms do: skip ref resolution and read the snapshot's point-in-time state.
- **`is_squash_merged_via_patch_id`.** The docstring said it returns `Ok(false)` when patch-id computation fails. In fact git errors propagate through `?`, and the only caller turns them into "no match" with `.unwrap_or(false)`.

title: ci: upgrade Tend and install Codecov uploaders from PyPI
body:
Upgrade the nine generated Tend workflows to 0.3.9. Repository setup now checks the Actions event policy needed for GitHub’s November 2 `pull_request_target` restriction; the active policy is scoped to `.github/workflows/tend-review.yaml` and its declared event.

Install the Codecov CLI for coverage and test-result uploads from PyPI at 11.3.1 using the action’s supported `use_pypi` input. The coverage run failed twice, and test-result uploads silently failed under their existing soft-failure policy, because `cli.codecov.io` terminated the TLS handshake before the uploader downloaded. PyPI installation avoids that endpoint while preserving report artifacts, tokens, and each uploader’s existing failure policy. This uses the [action’s package-install path](https://github.com/codecov/codecov-action/blob/v7.1.1/dist/codecov.sh#L67), which replaces its standalone binary and GPG validation with PyPI package distribution.

Validation: the published Tend generator reproduces every generated workflow; administrator event-policy check passes; the Rust suite (5,071 tests), doctests, docs build, clippy, workflow lint, and pre-commit checks pass. Both live uploader jobs install `codecov-cli` 11.3.1 successfully. Ingestion currently fails after request retries in CI; independent strict TLS checks show that `ingest.codecov.io` serves an expired certificate. The runner logs expose the request failures, without the underlying TLS exception, and uploads remain unavailable. Coverage computation completed and its report is retained as a GitHub Actions artifact; all other PR checks passed. The repository owner explicitly authorized landing without waiting for Codecov recovery. This is a one-time exception for the service failure: TLS validation, upload failure gates, and branch protection remain unchanged.

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_

body:
Weekly MSRV/toolchain bump to latest stable − 1: Rust 1.99.0 is the current stable (released 2026-09-28), so `rust-version` in `Cargo.toml` and `tests/helpers/wt-perf/Cargo.toml` moves `1.97` → `1.98`, and `rust-toolchain.toml` moves `1.97.0` → `1.98.0`.

Verified locally on 1.98.0: `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` is clean, and in `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes` the `lockfile`, `pre-commit`, `doctest`, and `doc` steps pass. `insta` ran 5,072 tests with 7 failures, all from the CI sandbox rather than the toolchain: `AF_UNIX` sockets are blocked (the non-regular-file and fsmonitor tests), a temp key file gets mode 0644 so `ssh-keygen` refuses to sign, and PowerShell is installed in the sandbox. The four that ran before nextest stopped also fail on 1.97.0 at `main`. `cargo msrv verify` isn't installed here; this PR's `msrv` CI job runs it.

**`flake.lock` needs no change.** The locked `rust-overlay` revision (`f60c1b57ff805a46b5175c76fc981fb4f81efbcc`, 2026-08-23) already ships `manifests/stable/1.98.0.nix`, so the dev shell's `rust-bin.stable.${channel}` lookup resolves 1.98.0 as locked; the `nix-flake` CI job evaluates it. (`nix flake update rust-overlay` can't run in the tend sandbox anyway — no access to the nix daemon socket; max-sixty/tend#1197.)

The `nightly-2026-08-01` pins in `nightly.yaml` are about two months old, inside the three-month window, so they stay.

title: fix(switch): suggest a dev.azure.com URL when the Azure remote is SSH
body:
For a user whose Azure DevOps remote is SSH (`git@ssh.dev.azure.com:v3/...`), `wt switch pr:N` could suggest adding a remote at `https://ssh.dev.azure.com/...`, which isn't a web host. This PR makes the suggestion use `https://dev.azure.com/...`.

**Path:** when `az repos pr show` returns no `repository.webUrl`, `fetch_pr_info` falls back to the `(host, org)` that [`detect_azure_target`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/981b91661e61538ab3f7e512c9400300cf8da0d0/src/git/remote_ref/azure.rs#L120-L149) reads from local remotes. Before this change it returned the remote's raw host. If the PR then belongs to a repository with no local remote (PR ids are org-scoped, so another repo in the org qualifies), [`azure::fork_remote_url`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/981b91661e61538ab3f7e512c9400300cf8da0d0/src/git/remote_ref/mod.rs#L274-L279) builds the "Add the remote" hint on that SSH host. The PR link printed just above it was already correct, because `pr_web_url` maps every non-visualstudio host to `dev.azure.com`.

**Fix:** `detect_azure_target` now returns a web host, the same shape `parse_web_url` returns from the response: `*.visualstudio.com` keeps its hostname, and every other Azure remote (only `dev.azure.com` and `ssh.dev.azure.com` are detected as Azure by host) maps to `dev.azure.com`. `az_org_url` already treated both cloud hosts the same, so the `--org` argument doesn't change.

I didn't put the normalization in `fork_remote_url`. `GitRemoteUrl::repo_info` passes a custom on-prem host through it when `[forge].platform` forces Azure DevOps, and rewriting that host to `dev.azure.com` would break Azure DevOps Server.

**Test:** `test_switch_pr_azure_ssh_remote_suggests_web_host` uses an SSH origin, a response without `webUrl`, and a PR in a sibling repository. On `main` the snapshot shows `git remote add upstream https://ssh.dev.azure.com/myorg/myproject/_git/other-repo`; with the fix it shows `https://dev.azure.com/...`. All 28 Azure integration tests and the Azure unit tests pass locally.
author: worktrunk-bot
diff:
--- src/git/remote_ref/azure.rs (+18/-10)
@@ -122,22 +122,30 @@ struct AzForkRepository {
 /// Prefers the primary remote (typically `origin` or whatever the user pushed
 /// with) so fork workflows hit the right tenant. Falls back to the first
 /// Azure remote found if the primary isn't Azure DevOps.
+///
+/// The host is a web host, the same shape [`parse_web_url`] returns: an
+/// `ssh.dev.azure.com` remote reports `dev.azure.com`, since the URL builders
+/// that consume it put the host into an HTTPS URL.
 fn detect_azure_target(repo: &Repository) -> Option<(String, String)> {
+    let target = |parsed: &GitRemoteUrl| {
+        let org = parsed.azure_organization()?;
+        let host = if host_is_within(parsed.host(), "visualstudio.com") {
+            parsed.host()
+        } else {
+            "dev.azure.com"
+        };
+        Some((host.to_string(), org.to_string()))
+    };
     if let Ok(remote) = repo.primary_remote()
         && let Some(url) = repo.effective_remote_url(&remote)
         && let Some(parsed) = GitRemoteUrl::parse(&url)
-        && let Some(org) = parsed.azure_organization()
+        && let Some(found) = target(&parsed)
     {
-        return Some((parsed.host().to_string(), org.to_string()));
-    }
-    for (_, url) in repo.all_remote_urls() {
-        if let Some(parsed) = GitRemoteUrl::parse(&url)
-            && let Some(org) = parsed.azure_organization()
-        {
-            return Some((parsed.host().to_string(), org.to_string()));
-        }
+        return Some(found);
     }
-    None
+    repo.all_remote_urls()
+        .into_iter()
+        .find_map(|(_, url)| target(&GitRemoteUrl::parse(&url)?))
 }
 
 /// Build the `--org` URL for the `az` CLI from a host and organization.
--- tests/integration_tests/switch.rs (+35/-0)
@@ -6787,6 +6787,41 @@ fn test_switch_pr_azure_fork(#[from(repo_with_remote)] repo: TestRepo) {
     });
 }
 
+/// With no `webUrl` in the response, the org and host come from the local
+/// remote. An `ssh.dev.azure.com` remote must still suggest an HTTPS
+/// `dev.azure.com` URL for the PR's repository, not one on the SSH host.
+#[rstest]
+fn test_switch_pr_azure_ssh_remote_suggests_web_host(#[from(repo_with_remote)] repo: TestRepo) {
+    repo.run_git(&[
+        "remote",
+        "set-url",
+        "origin",
+        "git@ssh.dev.azure.com:v3/myorg/myproject/test-repo",
+    ]);
+
+    let az_response = r#"{
+        "title": "Fix in a sibling repository",
+        "createdBy": {"uniqueName": "alice@example.com"},
+        "status": "active",
+        "isDraft": false,
+        "sourceRefName": "refs/heads/feature-auth",
+        "repository": {
+            "name": "other-repo",
+            "project": {"name": "myproject"}
+        },
+        "forkSource": null
+    }"#;
+
+    let mock_bin = setup_mock_az(&repo, az_response);
+
+    let settings = setup_snapshot_settings(&repo);
+    settings.bind(|| {
+        let mut cmd = make_snapshot_cmd(&repo, "switch", &["pr:101"], None);
+        configure_mock_cli_env(&mut cmd, &mock_bin);
+        assert_cmd_snapshot!("switch_pr_azure_ssh_remote_suggests_web_host", cmd);
+    });
+}

title: docs(config): correct stale examples and lists in wt config help
body:
Fixes four pieces of `wt config` help text that no longer match behavior. The most user-visible is the `wt config state vars clear` example labelled "Clear all keys for a specific branch", which ran `clear env --branch=feature` and so cleared only the `env` key; it now shows `--all --branch=feature`.

The other three are lists that missed newer behavior:

- **`wt config plugins`** described the Codex plugin as "Worktrunk configuration skill" only. It also installs activity-marker hooks ([`.codex-plugin/plugin.json`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/main/plugins/worktrunk/.codex-plugin/plugin.json)), as the `wt config plugins codex` help already says.
- **`wt config state marker`** said only the Claude Code plugin sets markers automatically. The Codex, OpenCode, Pi and oh-my-pi plugins do too.
- **`wt config state logs`** listed the background post-hooks as post-start, post-switch, post-commit and post-merge. post-remove also runs in the background through `register_planned` in `src/output/handlers.rs` and logs under the removed branch's subtree.

The generated docs mirrors and the three affected help snapshots are regenerated (`test_docs_are_in_sync`, `help` tests pass locally). I ran the new example against a branch with no vars, and it parses and runs. This is a docs-only change, so there's no regression test.

title: chore: update tend workflows (0.3.5 → 0.3.7)
body:
Regenerates the Tend workflows with tend 0.3.7 (from 0.3.5). The effect for this repo: the generated workflows now pin third-party actions and `uv` to commits and checksums, and the bot's sessions pick up 0.3.6–0.3.7's skill and runner fixes. No `.config/tend.yaml` change was needed.

What changes for worktrunk:

- **Supply-chain pinning** — `actions/checkout` and `astral-sh/setup-uv` are pinned to commit SHAs (version kept as a comment), and the `uv` download (bumped to 0.12.22) is verified against a per-arch checksum (max-sixty/tend#1463).
- **Mention prompt moves into a skill** — `tend-mention` now invokes `/tend-ci-runner:mention` and passes only the triggering event; the per-event "read the context, respond, make changes" instructions that were inlined in the workflow now live in the skill.
- **`fetch-tags: true` is dropped from checkouts.** Every Tend checkout uses `fetch-depth: 0`, which already fetches all tags, so `build.rs`'s `git describe` still sees them.
- **CI polling no longer waits on a job held for environment approval** (max-sixty/tend#1473), and nightly reads the last successful run more robustly so a cached listing can't widen its review range (max-sixty/tend#1468).
- **Triage opens a PR when a maintainer is reasonably likely to merge it** rather than defaulting to a comment (max-sixty/tend#1471), and repair sessions resume unfinished bot work from the live PR state (max-sixty/tend#1479).
- Claude Code is bumped to 2.1.288 (max-sixty/tend#1491).

Full upstream diff: https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/compare/0.3.5...0.3.7

title: fix(remove): name trash staging dirs by worktree registration
body:
A `wt step prune` printed every per-item line quickly, then sat for about 10s before its `Pruned …` summary. Two of the pruned worktrees were Codex worktrees, which all live at `~/.codex/worktrees/<id>/<repo>` and so share the basename `Mackup`. Removal staged each worktree at `.git/wt/trash/<basename>-<epoch-second>`, so the two concurrent removals picked the same path in the same second. The second rename failed onto the existing directory, and prune's synchronous fallback ran `git worktree remove` in the foreground; the summary waited for that recursive delete. The run's logs show it: nine worktrees got a detached `internal/remove.log`, the tenth (`codex/promptfoo-followups`) none.

Staging names now use the worktree's registration id under `<common>/worktrees/`, which git keeps unique among a repository's worktrees. `ensure_holds_this_worktree` already resolves and verifies that git dir, so it now returns it. A failed rename also logs its error at debug level instead of discarding it.

The collision predates #4337: v0.80.0 shows the same 3.4s stall on a two-worktree repro (50k ignored files each), which drops to 0.17s with this change. The new prune test relies on the suite's pinned `epoch_now()`, which makes the collision deterministic under the old naming; it fails without the fix.

title: Add branch-addressed merge with --branch
body:
## Status

Proposal for https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/1637. The CLI spelling is proposed for maintainer review, following the existing `wt step commit --branch` interface introduced by https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1750.

## Summary

- Add `wt merge [target] --branch/-b <source>`. Resolve through the existing worktree selector, including branch names, paths, and `@`; require a checked-out, non-detached source branch.
- Carry the selected source environment through commit, squash, rebase, target advancement, approved hooks, and cleanup. Reuse the source's project-config cache so a rewrite cannot silently replace approved commands.
- Keep caller identity separate. Merging another checkout emits no `cd` directive and does not approve/run a `post-switch` hook. Explicitly selecting the current checkout retains normal cleanup navigation, including linked worktrees of bare repositories.
- Resolve source-sensitive Git operations through `WorkingTree` and captured object IDs, so inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, and `GIT_INDEX_FILE` cannot turn the caller into the merge source.
- Generate squash prompts from the selected source index instead of rediscovering the process cwd.
- Preserve source checkouts containing another registered worktree. Merge cleanup rechecks fresh, canonicalized topology after pre-remove hooks and before directory changes and final ownership/lock/dirty checks; uncertain path resolution fails closed. Ordinary remove, picker, and batch prune retain their upstream staging sequence without the added topology scan.

## Why the removal change is necessary

A source may contain the invoking checkout under an ignored `.worktrees/` directory. Git's ordinary dirty check does not see that independent checkout. Removing the source could otherwise delete the caller's staged and untracked work. The new guard protects any registered nested checkout, including the target or a checkout created by a pre-remove hook.

The merge-specific registry read can block, so it precedes the final dirty/lock/ownership gates. A deterministic race test writes an untracked source file during that wait and verifies cleanup refuses it. The original shared-staging concurrency regression is restored, preserving the behavior introduced by #3954.

## Scope decisions

- No new checkout is created for a branch that lacks a worktree.
- No global process cwd/environment mutation, temporary retargeting of an existing checkout, remote fetch, or remote push is introduced.
- A conflict is left in the source checkout, with its location printed. Existing conflict resolution and source safety rules remain applicable.
- `commit.generation` subprocess working-directory behavior remains consistent with existing `wt step commit --branch`: the configured command inherits the invoking process's cwd. The generated prompt/index is correctly source-scoped. Changing the subprocess cwd is a separate product decision, particularly for relative executable paths.

title: docs(list): drop the stale-branch and dirty-tree skips from JSON help
body:
`wt list --help` (and the generated `list.md` pages, skill mirrors, and `list-v2.json` schema) explains `·`, JSON `null`, and `default_branch.integration` in ways the collector no longer matches. This corrects three claims. No behavior changes.

- **"branch too stale" for `·` and `null`.** #2098 removed the stale-branch skip (`stale_branches`), and nothing in `src/commands/list/collect/` skips tasks by branch age now. The remaining sources of `null` are a timeout, a skipped probe (column plan or unborn branch), or a failed forge fetch.
- **`integration` "null when a dirty tree skipped the checks".** Dirty trees don't skip the probes. They run on the committed HEAD either way, as `json_default_branch` says and `test_integration_positive_match_ignores_cleanliness` pins with a dirty `trees_match` result. A dirty integrated branch reports its reason, not `null`.
- **"every reason renders as the same `⊂`".** `"same_commit"` renders as `_` (or `–` with uncommitted changes), per `IntegrationReason::SameCommit` and the Default-branch symbol table in the same help page. `⊂` also needs a clean tree.

The same commit updates the `JsonDefaultBranch::integration` docstring, which generates the published schema description, and four internal comments in `collect/execution.rs` that still listed the stale-branch skip.

No test is added because this changes only prose. Help snapshots and doc mirrors are regenerated, and `test_docs_are_in_sync` passes.
