title: fix(config): skip a rejected env override in every command, not just wt list
body:
A rejected `WORKTRUNK_*` env override now warns and falls back in every command, the same way it already did in `wt list` and other tolerant loads. Before this change, commands that load config through `UserConfig::load()` treated it as fatal. These are `wt switch`, `wt merge`, `wt remove`, `wt for-each`, and the `wt step` commands. Each printed `▲ Ignoring env var overrides: …` during the startup prewarm, then exited 1 with `✗ Failed to load config` for the same variable. The two paths shouldn't disagree, so the tolerant behavior now applies to all of them.

`load_with_cause` now skips `LoadError::Env`. The rejected setting falls back to the file layers or its default, and other valid overrides still apply. User-file parse errors, `--config-set` failures, and validation failures stay fatal for these commands.

In practice, a mistyped override such as `WORKTRUNK__MERGE__REMOVE=flase` or `WORKTRUNK__REMOVE__DELETE_BRANCH=nope` no longer stops `wt merge` or `wt remove`. The command warns once and uses the file or default value instead.

Verification: with `WORKTRUNK__LIST__BRANCHES=not-a-bool`, `wt step eval '{{ branch }}'` prints the single startup warning and outputs `main` (exit 0). `test_eval_skips_invalid_env_override` pins this and replaces the test that pinned the old exit 1. The `LoadError` docstrings are updated to match: since #4348, `LoadError::Env` is emitted once per rejected setting, and strict loading no longer treats it as fatal. The public docs no longer describe this case (#4412 removed that sentence), so no doc change is needed.

title: fix(remove): continue after per-target execution failures
body:
A pre-remove hook or synchronous Git failure in one target currently stops a multi-target removal before later targets are attempted. Continue with the remaining valid targets, report each ordinary failure, and return exit status 1 if any target failed. JSON includes successful targets in execution order, including branch-only removal and the current worktree executed last.

SIGINT and SIGTERM cancel the batch immediately with exit status 130 or 143. Preserve the underlying error in foreground removal diagnostics so a captured Git interruption reaches the batch cancellation check.

Validation: 5,068 tests passed (one skipped), doctests and documentation build passed, and all final pre-commit checks passed. Integration coverage exercises hook and execution-time removal failures in foreground/background modes, correct JSON attribution, and hook/Git interruptions, including a detached checkout. Four Git-interruption regressions fail against the original executable and pass with this change; independent review found no remaining issues. Help and generated documentation checks passed after updating from main.

title: test(shell): isolate fish startup configuration in PTY fixtures
body:
Fish PTY tests currently load startup configuration, which can prepend PATH and replace a fixture's stub command with a host command. Launch fish with `--no-config`, matching the existing non-PTY shell helper, and keep the error-forwarding fixture's HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME inside its temporary directory.

The regression fixture installs a fish startup config that would select a fake cargo exiting with status 23; the expected CLI error must still come from the intended cargo stub. This changes test isolation only.

Validation: the full project pre-merge gate passed: 5,021 tests, one skipped, plus formatting, lint, documentation and doctests. Real fish PTY tests exercise the startup-config regression.

title: fix(process): retain command identity and native failure causes
body:
Hook failures could lose the command’s source and native OS cause, and a failed concurrent spawn could cancel runnable siblings. Spawn and exit failures now retain names such as `pre-merge project:check`, carry the typed OS error through foreground diagnostics, background logs and traces, and preserve each concurrent member’s result so runnable siblings finish.

Child failures retain physical exit/signal status separately from observed cancellation. One shared status formatter and hook wrapper produce the diagnostics; unnamed background failures retain their configured command for identification.

Validation: full project pre-merge gate passed (5,245 tests passed, 1 skipped; Clippy, formatting, docs and doctests passed); Rust 1.98 all-target/all-feature check with warnings denied; actual Claude design and closure reviews. Focused LLVM coverage exercises concurrent preparation-failure cleanup.

title: Separate config state, advice and parser diagnostics
body:
Config views report plugin, shell and tool state neutrally, with installation and authentication advice on separate rows. Missing project config and existing config with no hooks remain distinct. Typed config and approvals errors preserve their source and share one parser diagnostic through reports, hook commands and strict loading.

String rendering no longer propagates impossible formatting failures from CI-tool status or the project parser diagnostic. The absent-directory errors remain: they prevent config and approvals writes when the OS cannot locate a home directory. These errors were already uncovered on main before the typed-error rename.

Validation: the required pre-merge gate passed 5,029 tests with one skipped, including real config/hook/approvals commands, strict invalid-environment loading, unreadable approvals sources, successful commit-generation probing and both home-relative and quoted absolute path forms. Lint, documentation and independent local review passed. Linux, macOS and Windows suites, all affected-test suites and project coverage pass on the current head. Automated review found no new code issues.

Current patch coverage is 97.14% against the 98.38% target. The remaining eight missed lines are six pre-existing absent-directory safeguards and two changed call endings in the already-uncovered GitHub/GitLab diagnostic routes. Maintainer max-sixty explicitly approved this patch-coverage exception and merge after reviewing these retained lines.

title: Name undefined template variables and suggest corrections
body:
A hook containing `{{ brnch }}` names the undefined variable, shows its source line, and suggests `branch`. MiniJinja's failing expression span selects the reached output; compound expressions, nested values and locally bound names retain a general diagnostic when the missing input is ambiguous. Preflight validation uses MiniJinja's undeclared-variable analysis and accepts engine globals.

Config migration and diagnostics share the existing AST visitor, and similarity suggestions have one shared implementation. MiniJinja stays on 2.x (minimum 2.24); compiled source-span support leaves the environment's runtime debug defaults unchanged.

Custom filters now reject undefined inputs instead of silently converting them to empty strings. This includes an absent optional value, such as `upstream`, passed directly into a custom filter; guard it or supply a default. Defined non-string values retain their existing behavior.

The CLI signal matrix also checks that raw SIGTERM from a custom child reaches the shell as status 143.

Validation: actual Claude full review found no material code downsides. All 48 defined-input/filter contrasts preserve output, all eight custom filters reject undefined input, and focused config and CLI regressions pass. Pinned Rust 1.98 project validation passed: 5,278 tests, Clippy, formatting, lockfile, doctests and rustdoc (one test skipped). The hook-error composition snapshot also passes with default features, no default features, and CLI support without syntax highlighting. The no-default-features CLI unit suite passes all 1,011 tests; all 11 real CLI signal cases pass, including raw SIGTERM.

title: Make switch diagnostics describe the requested operation
body:
Switch diagnostics now name the requested operation: invalid new branch names get a concise error, missing base references name `--base`, and missing path selectors use the worktree selector diagnostic. Existing checkouts with directory changes disabled report their location without claiming the shell switched there. Noninteractive picker failures show the explicit branch command.

Branch creation uses Git's own validation and requires the echoed name to match the requested literal name, rejecting checkout-history expressions that would create a different branch. Validation subprocess interruptions retain their native signal. The alias-decline regression exercises a real terminal prompt and checks that declining prevents execution while explicit approval permits it.

Validation: the required pre-merge gate passed on pinned Rust 1.98: 5,207 tests passed, one skipped; Clippy, lockfile, formatting, documentation and doctests passed. Focused creation checks cover invalid names, existing and deleted checkout-history targets, nested and Unicode literal names, and native cancellation without mutation. Independent source review found no remaining issues.

title: Retain valid environment overrides when another setting is invalid
body:
One invalid environment override currently discards the entire environment layer. Validate each independent setting against the same file configuration, retaining valid overrides and attributing warnings only to rejected settings.

Custom-column fields form one setting, including project-scoped columns, so a required template and its integer width are accepted together. Deprecated names migrate before type selection. Valid environment values can repair an empty worktree path while unrelated invalid overrides are rejected. Typed validation issues identify their setting paths, and the loader preserves the current structured config diagnostics.

Validation: the required pre-merge gate passed 5,058 tests with one skipped, plus lint, doctests, and documentation generation. Real CLI regressions cover merged system/user layers, mixed valid/invalid overrides, lower-layer repairs, and project-scoped compound settings. Documentation sync passes.

title: Explain discarded changes and provide safe squash recovery
body:
Removing a dirty worktree recommends `git stash -u` when untracked files need preserving. Forced removal lists the changes it will discard from a fresh inventory after approved pre-remove hooks. An unreadable index produces Git’s diagnostic and still permits forced removal; SIGINT and SIGTERM cancel before deletion and stop the remaining batch through the existing native cancellation path.

Squashing staged work prints the backup ref and a command to recover its exact saved commit in a new worktree. Recovery preserves current branches, staging, and unstaged or untracked files. Git continues to own the backup and reflog.

Validated against main `913ff0547`: the required pre-merge gate passed 5,208 tests with one skipped, including forced-removal disclosure, corrupt-index diagnostics, native cancellation, and executed recovery commands. Formatting, Clippy, documentation sync and doctests pass. Independent source/caller review found no remaining issues.

body:
GitHub PR-not-found errors keep the selected repository and its source in the diagnosis, preserve the CLI error, and render `gh repo set-default` as a separate recovery hint. Relocation warnings identify the blocking path and explain that `--clobber` backs it up; config migration hints name the command that applies the updates.

title: fix(prune): serialize safe deletions and run hooks concurrently
body:
Concurrent prune deletions can exhaust Git's packed-refs lock timeout. An unchanged branch was then reported as "moved during deletion", and removal could absorb the Git failure while reporting success. This change serializes safe ref deletions within the repository, reports movement only when the surviving SHA changed, and propagates other failures after arranging cleanup and teardown hooks. A missing snapshot SHA fails closed.

Each safe deletion uses one `git update-ref -d` with the original expected SHA. The repository mutex covers that mutation and its failure classification; interruptions cancel waiting deletions before they can mutate anything. Integration and checkout reads remain outside the mutex. Checkout protection remains best effort; Git's atomic expected-SHA comparison protects concurrent commits to the candidate branch. Worktree registry coordination independently keeps enumeration and teardown from overlapping.

Prune runs pre-remove hooks concurrently across worktrees. Each worktree's hook pipeline finishes before fresh ownership, lock, and cleanliness checks. Hooks coordinate shared writes themselves, avoid writing into other removal candidates, and can race Git configuration readers on Windows; these limits are documented in help and its generated mirrors. The command lock only coordinates terminal output for foreground/current removals. Trash cleanup starts before waiting for ref deletion, and current-worktree placeholder cleanup removes only an empty directory.

The ref deletion path has no request queue, batch transactions, or batch recovery. The coordinator drops from 256 production lines to 61. Three alternating pairs comparing the former batch path with the actual mutex implementation measured 540 → 645 ms for 80 packed orphan branches and 598 → 641 ms for 40 worktrees; all 12 samples verified complete cleanup. Machine load was high, so these fixture timings are limited evidence of the cost. The simpler implementation accepts that measured penalty.

Regression coverage exercises real packed-ref contention, original-SHA protection, per-ref error isolation, interruption of waiting deletions, cleanup while deletion is blocked, pre-hook rendezvous, and post-hook overlap. Existing tests cover checkout retention and foreground/background error teardown.

Validation: the full local pre-merge gate passes with 5,040 tests and one skipped, plus formatting, Clippy, documentation, and doctests. Generated docs and skill mirrors are in sync. Independent review found no remaining issues.

title: fix(list): disclose clipped rows in the loading footer
body:
The progressive loading footer reported the entire inventory as “Showing” even when terminal height limited the table to its first rows. Keep the inventory totals and add the actual displayed count when clipped: `63 worktrees, 35 branches — first 50 of 98 shown — loading details…`. A fitting table omits the clipping qualification.

The count comes from the renderer's row limit and stays accurate before details arrive, during updates, and in slow-loading diagnostics. Inventory formatting is shared with the final summary.

The selected wording uses “loading details…” instead of the old completed/total task counter. That counter counted detail-collection tasks, not entries; on a clipped table, off-screen task progress is no longer quantified. Slow-loading diagnostics still identify pending tasks.

Validation: all nine progressive-list tests, 297 list unit tests, and direct Leaf runs at both heights passed. The project gate passed lint and documentation checks and 5,016 of 5,017 tests. Its remaining ambiguous-remote snapshot failure also reproduces on the unchanged base with Homebrew Git 2.56; normalization is already part of [PR #3129](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/3129).

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_

title: docs: pass --code to the aichat commit-generation example
body:
Closes #4331.

With a reasoning model, aichat prints the reasoning in a `<think>` block before the answer, so the documented aichat command produced commits whose subject was `<think>`. This adds `--code` to the aichat example, which strips that block. Without a code fence in the output, the message passes through unchanged, and the default prompt already asks for no code blocks. A one-line note explains the flag.

`src/cli/mod.rs` and `docs/src/content/docs/llm-commits.md` are the hand-edited sources. The mirrors (`docs/src/content/docs/config.md`, `skills/` and `plugins/` references, `dev/config.example.toml`) the two help snapshots, and the `bench-llm-commits` command in `Taskfile.yaml` carry the same change.

### Testing

- Checked with aichat 0.30.0 and Spark-X2.5 (a reasoning model) by running the command the way Worktrunk does: `bash -c '<command>'` with the default commit prompt on stdin. Before the change the first line was `<think>`; after it, `refactor(config): return Result from load`. With thinking disabled, `--code` output was an ordinary message (details in #4331).
- I couldn't run `test_docs_are_in_sync` or the help snapshot tests locally (no MSVC linker on this machine), so I edited the mirrors and snapshots by hand to match the generator's existing output for the neighbouring Codex entry. CI will confirm.

title: fix(completion): stop offering --dry-run and --var after an alias
body:
`wt <alias> --<Tab>` (and `wt step <alias> --<Tab>`) offered `--dry-run` and `--var`, but neither does anything useful after an alias. `AliasOptions::parse` rejects `--dry-run` with "`--dry-run` is no longer supported; use `wt config alias dry-run <name>` instead" (unless the template references `dry_run`), and passes `--var KEY=VALUE` through to the alias as plain positional arguments. Completion was steering users into an error or a flag that silently does nothing.

The flags come from `build_alias_completion_command` in `src/completion.rs`, a stub that predates alias argument routing (added in #1641; `--dry-run` was retired for aliases in #2291 and #2304). This PR removes the stub's own `--dry-run`, `--yes` and `--var` declarations, so the stub declares nothing beyond the alias name and help text. Aliases that wrap a built-in (`co = "wt switch {{ args }}"`) still mirror that built-in's flags through `mirror_alias_command`, which this PR doesn't touch.

**Test:** `test_complete_step_alias_shows_flags`, which asserted the stale flags were present, becomes `test_complete_step_alias_offers_no_misleading_flags` and asserts `--dry-run` and `--var` are absent. It fails on `main` (`Unexpected --dry-run flag`) and passes with the fix. All 80 completion integration tests pass.

**Not covered:** `--yes` still completes after an alias, and so do `--config` and `--verbose`, because they are clap `global = true` flags on the root command and propagate into every subcommand's completions. After an alias they also forward as arguments (the alias parser tests note that `global = true` doesn't cross `external_subcommand`). Removing them would mean hiding globals per alias stub, which is a separate decision. The stub's own `--yes` declaration duplicated the global, so dropping it changes nothing.

title: docs(switch): say that wt list flags a --path worktree off its template path
body:
The new `--path` help section (from #4317) says that "only `wt step relocate`" treats a worktree created with `--path` differently. That isn't true: `wt list` marks the row `⚑` (`worktree.branch_mismatch`, "Worktree isn't at the path its branch implies"), because `is_worktree_at_expected_path` compares every branch worktree against the `worktree-path` template. #4317's own PR description says as much ("`wt list` still marks these rows `⚑`"), but the help text didn't carry it over.

This rewords the sentence to name both: commands still reach the worktree by branch or path, `wt list` flags it `⚑`, and `wt step relocate` offers to move it back. The change is in `src/cli/mod.rs`, plus the regenerated docs/skill mirrors and the `help_switch_long` snapshot.

Verified against a local build: after `wt switch --create feature/x --path ../custom`, `wt list` shows `+ feature/x ⚑_ … ../custom`, while a template-path sibling shows no `⚑`. This changes docs only, so there's no regression test. `test_docs_are_in_sync` and the help snapshot tests pass.

title: fix(list): scope the Azure DevOps PR lookup to this repository
body:
On an Azure DevOps remote, the `wt list --full` CI column could show a PR from a different repository. When a sibling repository in the same Azure project had an active PR from a branch with the same name, that PR's number, merge status, and link appeared on this repository's row, dimmed as stale. This PR passes `--repository` to `az repos pr list`, taking the name from the remote URL.

**Why the lookup was unscoped.** `az repos pr list` only infers the repository from the git remote when `--org` is absent ([`resolve_instance_project_and_repo`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-devops-cli-extension/blob/master/azure-devops/azext_devops/dev/common/services.py)). Worktrunk always passes `--org`, so the repository came through as `None`. With no repository, [`list_pull_requests`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-devops-cli-extension/blob/master/azure-devops/azext_devops/dev/repos/pull_request.py) calls `get_pull_requests_by_project`, which searches every repository in the project. The lookup took the first active PR from any repository's matching source branch.

**Test.** `test_list_full_azure_pr_lookup_names_the_repository` in `tests/integration_tests/ci_status.rs` records the mock `az` argv and checks that every `repos pr list` call carries `--repository test-repo`. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix. The existing `azure_context` unit test now also checks the repository name parsed from the URL.

**Not covered here.** The pipeline fallback, `az pipelines runs list --branch … --top 1`, has the same project-wide scope, but that command has no repository flag. Fixing it would mean fetching more runs and filtering on each run's `repository` field, which changes which run is reported, so it is left for a separate change. `wt switch pr:N` is not affected, because `az repos pr show --id` looks up a PR ID, and PR IDs are unique across the organization.
author: worktrunk-bot

title: fix(relocate): move the shell with its worktree through a swap, and not out of a nested worktree
body:
`wt step relocate` could leave the user's shell in the wrong worktree in two cases. This PR moves the shell only when the worktree it actually stands in moves, and on both of the routes a relocation can take.

- **Swaps.** When two worktrees sit at each other's expected paths, one of them goes through a temporary location. Only the direct-move path sent the shell's `cd`, so a user standing in the worktree that took the temporary route stayed at its old path, which by the end holds the other branch's worktree. `git branch --show-current` there printed the other branch.
- **Nested worktrees.** The `cd` fired for any cwd under the moved path. With the documented `worktree-path = ".worktrees/{{ branch | sanitize }}"` layout, every linked worktree is nested inside the main worktree. So relocating the main worktree's branch pulled a shell standing in `.worktrees/other` over to `.worktrees/feature`, even though `other` never moved.

The fix works out once, before anything moves, which pending worktree holds the shell: the one with the longest path containing the cwd. It then sends the `cd` when that worktree reaches its destination, whether it moved directly or by way of the temporary location. The `cd` logic (preserving the subdirectory, and warning about a retired shell wrapper) is now a single helper that both routes call.

Two regression tests in `tests/integration_tests/step_relocate.rs` fail on `main` and pass with the fix:

- `test_relocate_swap_moves_shell_with_its_branch` runs a swap while the shell stands in each of the two worktrees, so it covers whichever one takes the temporary route.
- `test_relocate_main_leaves_shell_in_nested_worktree` runs relocate from inside a nested worktree and checks that no `cd` is written.

The swap test is ignored on Windows, for the same reason as `test_relocate_preserves_subdir`: Windows refuses to move a directory that a live process is using as its cwd.

The nightly survey found this. It also reported a third `relocate` problem that this PR does not change. If the default branch is checked out in a linked worktree while the main worktree is on another branch, `git switch` fails and the whole run stops before the remaining worktrees are processed. Whether to skip that candidate or detach the other worktree is a design choice, so it is left for a later decision.
author: worktrunk-bot

title: chore: update tend workflows (0.3.4 → 0.3.5)
body:
Upgrades the generated Tend workflows from 0.3.4 to 0.3.5 ([compare](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/compare/0.3.4...0.3.5)). The regenerated YAML changes little on its own: the action pin moves to `max-sixty/tend/claude@0.3.5`, and most of the behavior change arrives through the new action's bundled skills and scripts.

What maintainers will notice:

- **Bot PRs get their review findings applied.** The review workflow now decides whether to apply its own findings by who authored the PR, so a review on a bot-authored PR follows through with a fix instead of stopping at the comment (max-sixty/tend#1433).
- **Relayed PR-review mentions are named after the PR.** `tend-mention` runs triggered through `tend-mention-relay` now get the PR title as their run name rather than the event type, and the notifications poll uses that name to tell which PR a live run is handling (max-sixty/tend#1450). The relay job also skips when `TEND_ENABLED` is `false`, instead of dispatching a run that does nothing (max-sixty/tend#1452).
- **CI waits run to completion instead of a fixed cap.** CI polling and integration-test waits now wait for checks to settle instead of timing out at about 9 minutes, so a slow matrix reports its real result rather than "unverified" (max-sixty/tend#1448, max-sixty/tend#1451).
- **Fewer truncated listings.** Pagination now reads every page of notifications, failed-run jobs, and workflow listings (max-sixty/tend#1435, max-sixty/tend#1442, max-sixty/tend#1457). The inline pagination helpers in `tend-mention` and `tend-notifications` now use `gh api --paginate --slurp`.
- **Weekly dependency review matches Dependabot and Renovate PRs again.** It now matches on the `app/…` author login that `gh` reports (max-sixty/tend#1441).
- **Nightly and review behavior.** Repo overlays can now skip advisory checks, review findings are ranked by severity, and the nightly issue sweep rotates across issues (max-sixty/tend#1450). `ci-fix` recurrence comments now lead with what changed (max-sixty/tend#1446).

Also bumps the pinned `uv` from 0.12.17 to 0.12.19 in the pre-check steps. `.config/tend.yaml` has no model pin, so there was no model to update.

title: docs(tips): configure origin fetch refspec in the bare repository layout
body:
`git clone --bare` stores the `origin` URL but writes no `remote.origin.fetch` refspec, so a bare clone following the [bare repository layout](https://worktrunk.dev/tips-patterns/#bare-repository-layout) never gets `origin/*` remote-tracking branches — `git branch -r` stays empty however often you fetch, and lazygit and editor integrations see no remote branches. The recipe now sets the standard refspec, fetches, and runs `git remote set-head origin --auto` right after the clone, with one sentence explaining why the extra lines are needed.

Verified locally with git 2.55: a fresh `git clone --bare` has no `remote.origin.fetch` and an empty `git branch -r`; after the three added commands, `git branch -r` lists `origin/HEAD -> origin/master` and `origin/master`. The `skills/` and `plugins/` mirrors were regenerated by `test_docs_are_in_sync`, which passes.

This fixes the docs only. worktrunk could also detect a bare repo with an `origin` but no fetch refspec (it already prompts about `worktree-path` on first `wt switch` in a bare repo), but #1258 settled that worktrunk shouldn't prescribe a clone layout, so this PR leaves that out.

Closes #4322 — automated triage

title: fix(squash): run pre-commit hooks before staging so their edits reach the commit
body:
`wt step squash`, and the squash path `wt merge` takes by default, staged changes before running `pre-commit` hooks. Anything a formatter hook changed was therefore left out of the squash commit and stayed in the working tree. `wt step commit` already runs hooks first and then stages. This PR gives [`handle_squash`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/28cc4d14ccf1f289b729d90fec33f1469295d0c1/src/commands/step/squash.rs#L161-L175) the same order. The `wt hook` docs list `pre-commit` for "Formatters, linters, type checking … `wt step squash`, and the commit `wt merge` makes".

**Effect on `wt merge`:** after the squash commit, the hook's edits leave a dirty tree, so the merge lands but cannot remove the worktree ("Cannot remove worktree after merge: feat has uncommitted changes"). The existing `user_pre_commit_executes` snapshot had locked that in. Its hook writes `user_precommit.txt`, and the merge committed only `uncommitted.txt`. The snapshot now shows both files in the commit.

**Verification:**
- New test `test_step_squash_includes_pre_commit_hook_edits`: a pre-commit hook writes `fmt.txt` during `wt step squash`. Before the fix, `feature:fmt.txt` did not exist; now it is in the squash commit and the worktree is clean.
- The other three snapshot updates only move the `Auto-staging N untracked paths` warning after the hook output, which is the order `wt step commit` already prints. When the hook fails, the warning disappears, because nothing is staged.
- The merge, hook, approval and commit integration tests pass locally. The exception is `test_merge_no_ff_signs_merge_commit`, which fails the same way on unmodified `main` in this sandbox (it rejects the test signing key's 0644 permissions).

<details><summary>Related behavior this PR leaves alone</summary>

Squash still runs `pre-commit` (and prompts for its approval) before checking whether there is anything to squash, so a single clean commit or zero commits ahead still runs the hooks and then reports "Nothing to squash". Moving the hooks after that check is a separate design question: a formatter hook on a single unformatted commit is exactly the case where running it produces a commit. With this PR, those edits are now staged and squashed together with the commit instead of being left dirty.

</details>
author: worktrunk-bot

--- src/commands/step/squash.rs (+8/-7)
@@ -158,13 +158,9 @@ pub fn handle_squash(
         .unwrap_or_else(|| integration_target.clone());
     let template_vars = TemplateVars::new().with_target(&integration_target);

title: fix(list): register untracked files literally so a ':x' name can't fail the diff
body:
An untracked file whose name starts with `:` makes `wt list`'s working-tree diff fail. The row loses its `HEAD±` value and `?` marker, and the footer reports `▲ 1 task failed: main: working-tree diff (fatal: pathspec ':x' did not match any files)`. This PR registers those files literally.

The cause is in `register_untracked_paths`: it feeds the NUL-separated names from `ls-files --others` to `git add --intent-to-add --pathspec-from-file=-`, and git parses each name as a pathspec. `:x` reads as magic, and `*`, `?` and `[` read as globs (the glob case is silent: a name like `b[1].txt` can match a different file or none). The fix sets `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1` on that one command. Git refuses the literal setting alongside `GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS` or `GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS` ("global 'literal' pathspec setting is incompatible with all other global pathspec settings"), so the command also drops those two variables if the user exported them.

Call path: `wt list` → `compute_working_tree_diff` → `working_tree_diff_stats_with_untracked` → `register_untracked_paths`.

**Verification:**
- A new unit test, `working_tree_diff_stats_with_untracked_counts_pathspec_magic_names`, creates untracked `:x`, `b[1].txt` and `*`. It failed before the fix with `git add … failed (exit 128)` and passes after.
- A built `wt list` on a repo with an untracked `:x` shows `? … +2` both plainly and with `GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS=1` exported.
- There is no test for the env-var removal, because setting a process-wide env var in a unit test would race other tests.

Found by the nightly survey of `src/git/repository/working_tree.rs`.

title: fix(copy-ignored): stamp copied files with one mtime so cargo keeps its cache
body:
On Linux, `wt step copy-ignored` gives each copied file the time its copy happened to finish. Leaves are copied in parallel, so inside `target/` a dependency's `.rlib` can end up newer than the dep-info of a crate that depends on it, and cargo marks that crate dirty. This PR gives every file the step copies a single mtime, taken before the copy starts. @max-sixty asked in #4248 for a repro where this matters before adding it, and @paul-hansen [supplied one](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/4248#issuecomment-5883336111).

Their repro, run against this repo at `ffbfcaf7b` on ext4:

| Seeding the new worktree | Units `cargo build` recompiles |
|---|---|
| `wt step copy-ignored` on main | 203 |
| `cp -a` (source mtimes preserved) | 2 |
| `wt step copy-ignored` with this PR | 2 |

With `CARGO_LOG=cargo::core::compiler::fingerprint=info`, main's rebuild starts from `StaleDependency { dep_mtime, max_mtime }` entries a few hundred ms apart, and `StaleDepFingerprint` carries them up the graph. With this PR, the only dirty item left is `MissingFile { .git/HEAD }`: worktrunk's build script watches that path, and in a linked worktree `.git` is a file. So the 2 remaining units are worktrunk and wt-perf, unrelated to the copy.

**Why one stamp instead of the source mtimes.** `git worktree add` writes the tracked files before `copy-ignored` runs. Preserved outputs therefore end up older than those sources. In the `cp -a` row, worktrunk's build script reran because the checked-out `build.rs` was newer than its dep-info, and the thread's earlier measurements found the same with cargo, make and `tsc -b`. A stamp taken after the checkout keeps the copied outputs newer than the sources, and makes files inside the copied tree compare as equal.

Details:
- The stamp covers regular files only. Symlinks keep their copy-time mtime, because `std` can't set a link's own times without following it. Directories keep theirs too.
- A failure to set the time is logged at debug and doesn't fail the copy.
- Copy time didn't change: 2.1s for 3.3 GiB / 3759 files, warm, before and after.
- `wt step promote`'s cross-device fallback passes `None`, so its behavior is unchanged.

New unit tests check that every copied file in a tree gets the stamp, and that a read-only (0o444) file gets it and stays 0o444. Both fail with the `set_modified` call removed.

Refs #4248. The Mix case in that issue isn't fixed by this: @dmy-gh tested a single stamp there and Mix still recompiled.

title: feat(switch): add --path to create a worktree outside the worktree-path template
body:
Adds `--path <PATH>` to `wt switch`, so one worktree can live in a directory of the user's choosing while its branch keeps its own name. This is the opt-out from the `worktree-path` template that #1982 asked for:

```console
$ wt switch --create feat/JIRA-1234/dark-mode --path ../dark-mode
✓ Created branch feat/JIRA-1234/dark-mode from main and worktree @ ~/code/dark-mode
$ wt switch ../dark-mode          # by path
$ wt switch feat/JIRA-1234/dark-mode   # or by branch
```

Semantics:

- **Relative paths resolve from the current directory** (or `-C`), as `git worktree add <path>` does, through the same `resolve_input_path` that already resolves `wt switch ../repo.feature`. A leading `~` expands.
- **Works without `--create`** when the branch exists but has no worktree yet.
- **A branch that already has a worktree elsewhere is an error**, not silently ignored: `✗ feature-z already has a worktree @ …, not …; to switch to it, run without --path`. Naming the directory it already has just switches.
- **Error hints keep `--path`.** The `--clobber` suggestion for an occupied directory now reads `wt switch --create --clobber feature-y --path=../occupied`. Without `--path` it would have backed up the template's directory instead.
- Occupancy by another worktree, `--clobber`, hooks, and `{{ worktree_path }}` all go through the existing plan, which now takes the requested path in place of `compute_worktree_path`.

Nothing is persisted: git already records where each worktree is, and resolution, `list`, `merge`, `remove`, and hooks read paths from `git worktree list`. The one command that notices is `wt step relocate`, which offers to move an off-template worktree back to the template path. The long help now says so. `wt list` still marks these rows `⚑` and shows the `Path` column.

**Open question for review:** I resolved relative paths from the cwd (git's rule) and not from the template's parent directory, which the closed #2275 did. The cwd rule is predictable and matches every other path argument wt takes. Its cost: running `--path dark-mode` from the main worktree nests the new worktree inside the repo, so users write `../dark-mode`.

Tests: new integration snapshots cover create-with-path, an existing branch with no worktree, the existing-worktree-elsewhere error, and the `--clobber` hint. Help and doc mirrors are regenerated. Locally, the switch and picker integration tests (312), clippy, and pre-commit pass. The only unit-test failures are two tests that bind Unix sockets, which the CI sandbox forbids.

Closes #1982

title: fix(config): read a git config key with no value as true
body:
Git treats a config key written with no value as boolean `true`. For example:

```ini
[core]
	fsmonitor
```

`git config --bool core.fsmonitor` prints `true` for that file. `git config --list -z` emits the entry as `core.fsmonitor\0`, with no newline. [`parse_config_list_z`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/51770314440466e50185435b047550121adbf463/src/git/repository/mod.rs#L2233-L2250) stored that as `""`, so `config_bool` read it as `false`. Its docstring had the two formats swapped: an explicitly empty value (`key = ""`) is the one that keeps its newline, and git reads it as false.

Three readers go through that parse:

- `is_builtin_fsmonitor_enabled` (`core.fsmonitor`): `wt list` skipped starting the fsmonitor daemons for such a repo.
- `is_bare` (`core.bare`).
- `worktree_config_enabled` (`extensions.worktreeConfig`): the config preload stayed on in a layout where it's known to miss per-worktree values (#2779).

This PR parses a bare `key\0` as `"true"`, and updates the two docstrings that described the old parse (`config_regexp_entries`, and the reason `signs_commits` gives for shelling out to git). Most string keys reject a valueless entry in git anyway. The one string reader that does change is a hand-written valueless `worktrunk.state.<branch>.vars.<key>`: `{{ vars.<key> }}` now renders as `true` instead of empty. That matches git's boolean reading, though `git config --get` prints an empty line for it.

Tests:

- `config_bool_reads_key_without_value_as_true` writes the bare `fsmonitor` line into a real repo's `.git/config`, so it checks what git actually emits. It fails on `main`.
- `parse_config_list_z_entry_without_newline_tolerates_key_only` encoded the old assumption, so this PR replaces it with `parse_config_list_z_key_without_value_is_true`, which covers both forms.

Locally, the lib suite and the `config` integration tests pass. The exceptions are two tests that bind Unix sockets, which the CI sandbox forbids; they fail the same way on `main`.
author: worktrunk-bot

title: fix(remove): don't point at a detached worktree removed in the same run
body:
#3791 made a branch-only `wt remove` name the detached worktree still sitting at the branch's path, with a hint to run `wt remove <that path>`. When the user does that in the same command, `wt remove feature ../repo.feature`, the worktree removal runs first. The branch-only line then still reports the now-deleted directory and suggests removing it:

```
✓ Removed worktree @ ~/repo.both-detached (detached HEAD, no branch to delete)
○ No worktree found for branch both-detached; a detached worktree is @ ~/repo.both-detached
↳ To remove the detached worktree, run wt remove ~/repo.both-detached
✓ Removed branch both-detached (same commit as main, _)
```

`--format=json` carries the same stale `detached_worktree` path. The annotation is computed per target inside `validate_remove_targets`, before the other targets are known. This PR clears it after the loop when another plan in the same run (`others` or `current`) removes that path. The check runs after the loop because the path argument can come before or after the branch. A path target that failed validation isn't removed, so its hint stays.

`test_remove_branch_and_its_detached_worktree_together` fails on `main` with the output above and passes with the fix. All 142 `remove::` integration tests, including the new one, pass locally.

title: Release v0.80.0
body:
Bumps 0.79.0 → 0.80.0 and adds the `## 0.80.0` changelog section, cut from `12efb5159`. The bump is minor because the library API breaks (see Verification).

## Verification

- `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes` on the cut tip: 4985 passed.
- `nightly.yaml` on `12efb5159`, all jobs green including feature-powerset: https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/36338233859
- `cargo semver-checks check-release -p worktrunk` reports five major-level lints, the removals and signature changes listed in the Internal entry.
- Changelog: repeated verification passes against source until one came back clean. Fixed headlines name the condition a bug needed rather than its worst case, and near-zero-reach fixes are folded into two roll-up bullets, per #4295.
- Data-loss surface review over `v0.79.0..HEAD` with independent finders. The one real finding, a nested stale detached worktree read as the enclosing repo's rebase so `wt step prune` could unregister it, was fixed in #4302. The review also found a squash regression in the backup path, fixed in #4303. The remaining candidates were adjudicated acceptable and signed off: #4228 unregistering stale worktrees whose directory remains (files stay on disk; the branch is deleted only if integrated), #4206 leaving a detached `HEAD` on Ctrl-C during a slow commit hook, #4251 allowing `--no-squash` merges with untracked files, #4219 dropping `--no-hooks` from the skill example, and #4279's `docker stop` recipe. #4252 closes a submodule data-loss path.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max-sixty_

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- CHANGELOG.md (+46/-0)
@@ -1,5 +1,51 @@
 # Changelog
 
+## 0.80.0
+
+### Improved
+
+- **`wt list` and the `wt switch` picker settle faster in repos with many worktrees**: rows fill from the top down, and on macOS with `core.fsmonitor=true` no daemon start is forked for a worktree whose daemon is already running. On a 50-worktree repo the picker's per-row work starts at 47ms, down from 120ms. ([#4286](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4286), [#4290](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4290), [#4288](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4288), [#4284](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4284))
+
+- **CI status skips branches that were never pushed**: `wt list --full`, the picker, and the statusline no longer query the forge for a local branch no remote has, so a repo with 239 local branches made 25 `gh` calls instead of 249. A PR opened from a branch another clone pushed shows once you fetch. GitLab looks up its project ID once per command, not per row. ([#4289](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4289), [#4216](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4216))
+
+- **Leaner Codex commit generation**: the recommended Codex command moves to `gpt-6-luna` with reasoning off and unneeded Codex features disabled, so each message sends fewer input tokens. Accepting the first-run Codex prompt now also creates `~/.codex/worktrunk-commit-instructions.txt`, which the command reads. [Docs](https://worktrunk.dev/llm-commits/) ([#4261](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4261))
+
+- **Releases ship a signed packslip**: each GitHub release includes `packslip.sigstore.json`, a manifest of the archives' digests, platforms, completions, and agent skills, signed by the release workflow so installers such as mise can verify downloads before unpacking. ([#4301](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4301), thanks @jdx)
+
+### Fixed
+
+- **A squash whose commit fails keeps the branch**: when a git commit hook or signing stopped the commit in `wt merge` or `wt step squash`, the branch was left at the merge base with its changes staged, recoverable from the reflog. Now the branch is untouched. (Breaking: git commit hooks run on a detached `HEAD` during a squash.) ([#4206](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4206), thanks @Bennyjitsu for finding it in [#4193](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4193))
+
+- **`wt step diff` when local `main` lags `origin/main`**: for a branch built on the newer `origin/main`, the diff included the upstream commits in between. It now uses the same base as `wt merge`. ([#4281](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4281), thanks @starlightromero, whose [#3519](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/3519) reported the same case for `wt merge`)
+
+- **Submodules with an `ignore` setting**: when `submodule.<name>.ignore` or `diff.ignoreSubmodules` hid uncommitted changes inside a submodule, `wt remove` and `wt step prune` read the worktree as clean and removed it along with them; they now keep it. With `ignore=all`, `wt step commit` and squashes now commit a staged submodule pointer instead of leaving it staged. ([#4252](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4252), [#4192](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4192), [#4206](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4206), [#4303](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4303), thanks @Duang777)
+
+- **Worktrees whose `.git` was deleted but whose directory remains** (macOS `$TMPDIR` cleanup can do this): `wt remove <branch>` failed, and `wt step prune` skipped or errored on them. Both now unregister the worktree and leave its files; one with staged changes or an operation in progress is kept by `wt step prune`, and refused by `wt remove` without `--force`. ([#4228](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4228), [#4226](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4226), [#4302](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4302))
+
+- **`wt merge --no-squash` with a stage mode that stages nothing**: with `--stage=none` and only unstaged changes, `--stage=tracked` and only untracked files, or only dirty submodule contents, it stopped at "Nothing to commit"; it now merges the branch's commits. ([#4251](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4251), thanks @Duang777)
+
+- **Nushell 0.116**: the first `wt` tab completion in each session printed a `Positional completer input deprecated` warning. The completer now takes Nushell's new input and still works on older versions. ([#4297](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4297))
+
+- **Hook-log JSON's `branch` field**: `wt config state logs --format=json` put the sanitized log directory name (`feature-x-x2d`) there; it now holds `feature/x`, or `null` when no local branch owns the directory. (Breaking: filters on the sanitized form need updating.) ([#4279](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4279))
+
+- **`wt config show --full` outside a git repository**: it printed only a `git rev-parse` failure; it now shows the user config and diagnostics. ([#4255](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4255))
+
+- **Fixes for unusual git setups**: `--no-ff` merges are signed when `commit.gpgSign` is set without a value or only for one worktree; after `git worktree repair`, `--separate-git-dir` repos put worktrees beside the work tree and `wt remove` works (fixes [#4235](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/4235)); removing an orphan worktree before its first commit no longer errors; with a custom merge driver, leaving the picker during a conflict check no longer strands `.merge_file_*` files (fixes [#4273](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/4273)). ([#4206](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4206), [#4236](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4236), [#4233](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4233), [#4274](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4274), thanks @zengzheqing and @brndnmtthws for reporting)
+

title: feat(plugin): run every Claude hook through `wt config plugins claude hook`
body:
Routes all eight Claude Code hook events through the existing Rust dispatcher added in #4304. Hook commands become literal invocations that pass the plugin directory validator, and the plugin no longer requires `jq`. The README requires `wt` v0.81.0 or later.

On `wt` v0.80.0 or earlier, worktree creation and removal fail, and activity markers and EnterWorktree auto-approval stop working. The latter hooks retain `|| true`, so the failures stay nonblocking and EnterWorktree falls back to a permission prompt. The dispatcher preserves existing-branch reopening and safe removal of unmerged work. Updates the hook layout assertions and the skill's create-or-reopen guidance, and removes the obsolete shell pipeline explanation.

Local validation: the project gate passed for the corrected skills at `1a9ebd12c` in an isolated target directory (5,392 tests passed, one skipped, plus Clippy, formatting, docs, and snapshots). Docs mirror sync and all five dispatcher integration tests pass. The later documentation-only follow-ups clarify the README's attribution of payload parsing and the measured cleanup behavior. `claude plugin validate plugins/worktrunk` passed its directory checks with the existing missing-version warning; it excludes the catalog's safety scan and policy review.

Independent Opus 5.5 review found no code defects and verified the older-version failure. Further passes reviewed the corrected skills, mirrors and live cleanup evidence with no remaining findings.

Cleanup was verified live on Claude Code 2.1.308 in an isolated repository: reopening an existing worktree through both `claude --worktree` and `EnterWorktree({name})`, then `/exit`, shows Keep / Remove with Keep selected. Keep leaves its branch and checkout intact and emits no `WorktreeRemove`. A fresh CLI-created worktree shows the same prompt; choosing Remove emits `WorktreeRemove` and removes the synthetic checkout and merged branch. The rationale now reflects that confirmation instead of claiming automatic cleanup.

Reopening is already present in the [base create hook](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/d965d819f226ad7ac853efed8b2a996bb0c880a6/plugins/worktrunk/hooks/hooks.json#L72): it clears `--create` for an existing local branch. Both the [base remove hook](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/d965d819f226ad7ac853efed8b2a996bb0c880a6/plugins/worktrunk/hooks/hooks.json#L82) and the dispatcher check for `.git` and invoke `wt -C <path> remove --foreground <path>`, with no force flags. This cutover preserves that deletion scope and its safeguards.

title: feat(plugin): add `wt config plugins claude hook` for the Claude hooks
body:
Adds a hidden `wt config plugins claude hook` subcommand that reads Claude Code's hook payload from stdin and acts on its `hook_event_name`: activity markers, the `EnterWorktree` approval, and `WorktreeCreate` / `WorktreeRemove`. This is the first half of getting the Claude Code plugin into Anthropic's plugin directory, whose validator blocks our current `hooks/hooks.json` because its commands compute paths (`-C "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"`) and carry inline programs (`bash -c '…$(jq …)…'`). Once `hooks.json` runs this subcommand, every hook command is the same literal line and the plugin no longer needs `jq`.

`hooks.json` itself is unchanged here. The marketplace serves the plugin from `main`, so switching it before a release ships `hook` would break worktree creation for everyone on v0.79. The switch is a separate draft PR, to merge a few weeks after the release that ships this.

- `src/commands/config/plugins.rs`: `handle_claude_hook` dispatches on the event and re-runs the same `wt` binary with the command a user would type, so each action behaves exactly as the old hook command did. Its doc comment carries the per-event contracts (#2939, #3545, #3754, #3921).
- `approve-enter-worktree` stays, sharing its check with `hook`, for plugin copies installed before `hook` existed: marketplace installs don't update on their own.
- `tests/integration_tests/claude_hook.rs` covers the new subcommand directly; the existing shell-integration tests still run the real `hooks.json` commands.
- `plugin.json` gains the listing metadata the directory reads (`license`, `homepage`, `repository`, `keywords`, `icon`, with `icon.png` copied from `docs/public/logo.png`), and the plugin README describes what each hook runs, which the directory's security scan checks for.
- The direnv example in the tips docs builds its path with direnv's `expand_path` instead of `$PWD`, which the directory scanner read as a credential.

title: fix(squash): back up the index with plumbing so hidden submodule changes don't abort the squash
body:
#4192 (unreleased) made `has_staged_changes` see a staged submodule pointer hidden by `submodule.<name>.ignore=all`, which sends such a squash into the safety backup. The backup used `git stash create`, which honors that ignore setting, saw nothing, and returned an empty SHA, so `wt step squash` and a default-squash `wt merge` aborted with `✗ git stash create returned empty SHA - no changes to backup`. In 0.79.0 a multi-commit squash in that setup succeeded (leaving the pointer out), so this would ship as a regression. The 0.80.0 changelog verification found it.

The backup now snapshots the index with plumbing — `write-tree`, then `commit-tree --no-gpg-sign <tree> -p HEAD`, recorded in `refs/wt-backup/<branch>`'s reflog as before — so no config hides part of it. By the time the backup runs, squash has already staged per its stage mode, so the index is exactly what the squash absorbs; unstaged and untracked files, which the squash leaves in place, are no longer in the backup. `--no-gpg-sign` keeps the backup from prompting for a signature, as `stash create` never signed.

`test_step_squash_backs_up_submodule_bump_hidden_by_ignore` covers the two-commit, one-commit, and commits-cancel-out shapes, each with a hidden staged pointer: all three failed with the stash error before, and now squash including the pointer, with the backup's tree equal to the squash tree and its parent the pre-squash tip. Nine snapshots change only on their `Backup created @ <sha>` line.

     );
 }
 
+/// A staged submodule bump that `submodule.<name>.ignore = all` hides from
+/// porcelain is still squashed in and backed up, whatever the branch's commits
+/// add up to: the backup snapshots the index with plumbing, which that config
+/// cannot hide. `None` restores the file's content from main, so the last case's
+/// commits cancel out and the bump is all that remains.
+#[rstest]
+#[case::two_commits(&[("a.txt", Some("a")), ("b.txt", Some("b"))], "a.txt\nb.txt\nsub")]
+#[case::one_commit(&[("a.txt", Some("a"))], "a.txt\nsub")]
+#[case::commits_cancel_out(&[("file.txt", Some("changed")), ("file.txt", None)], "sub")]
+fn test_step_squash_backs_up_submodule_bump_hidden_by_ignore(
+    mut repo: TestRepo,
+    #[case] commits: &[(&str, Option<&str>)],
+    #[case] squashed_paths: &str,
+) {
+    use worktrunk::git::PlumbingDiff;
+
+    // A gitlink `sub` on main; uninitialized, so no clone is needed.
+    fs::write(
+        repo.root_path().join(".gitmodules"),
+        "[submodule \"sub\"]\n\tpath = sub\n\turl = ./sub\n",
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    let old_pointer = repo.git_output(&["rev-parse", "HEAD"]);
+    repo.run_git(&["add", ".gitmodules"]);
+    repo.run_git(&[
+        "update-index",
+        "--add",
+        "--cacheinfo",
+        &format!("160000,{old_pointer},sub"),
+    ]);
+    repo.run_git(&["commit", "-m", "add submodule"]);
+    repo.run_git(&["config", "submodule.sub.ignore", "all"]);
+
+    let feature_wt = repo.add_worktree("feature");
+    for (i, (file, content)) in commits.iter().enumerate() {
+        match content {
+            Some(content) => fs::write(feature_wt.join(file), content).unwrap(),
+            None => repo.run_git_in(&feature_wt, &["checkout", "main", "--", file]),
+        }
+        repo.run_git_in(&feature_wt, &["add", file]);
+        repo.run_git_in(&feature_wt, &["commit", "-m", &format!("commit {i}")]);
+    }
+    let pre_squash_tip = repo.git_output(&["rev-parse", "feature"]);
+    let new_pointer = repo.git_output(&["rev-parse", "main"]);
+    repo.run_git_in(
+        &feature_wt,
+        &[
+            "update-index",
+            "--cacheinfo",
+            &format!("160000,{new_pointer},sub"),
+        ],
+    );
+
+    let output = repo
+        .wt_command()
+        .args(["step", "squash", "--no-hooks"])
+        .current_dir(&feature_wt)
+        .env(
+            "WORKTRUNK_COMMIT__GENERATION__COMMAND",
+            "cat >/dev/null && echo 'feat: combined'",
+        )
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        output.status.success(),
+        "step squash failed: {}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
+    );
+
+    assert_eq!(
+        repo.git_output(&["rev-parse", "feature^"]),
+        repo.git_output(&["rev-parse", "main"])
+    );
+    assert_eq!(repo.git_output(&["rev-parse", "feature:sub"]), new_pointer);
+    assert_eq!(
+        repo.git_output(&PlumbingDiff::Tree.args(&["--name-only", "-r", "main", "feature"])),
+        squashed_paths
+    );
+    // The backup holds the squashed tree on top of the pre-squash tip.
+    assert_eq!(
+        repo.git_output(&["rev-parse", "refs/wt-backup/feature^{tree}"]),
+        repo.git_output(&["rev-parse", "feature^{tree}"])
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        repo.git_output(&["rev-parse", "refs/wt-backup/feature^"]),
+        pre_squash_tip
+    );
+}
+

title: fix(list): read a stale worktree's rebase state from its registration
body:
A detached worktree mid-rebase takes the name of the branch it is rebasing, found by running `git rev-parse --git-dir` from the worktree's path. For a stale entry whose directory remains but whose `.git` is gone, that lookup walks up to whatever repository encloses the directory, so a detached worktree nested inside the main worktree (e.g. `repo/.worktrees/x`) was named after the main worktree's rebase.

#4228 (unreleased) lets `wt step prune` and `wt remove` unregister such entries, which turned the mislabel into data loss: with the main worktree rebasing an integrated branch, `wt step prune` judged the stale detached entry by that branch and deleted its registration, leaving commits held only by its detached HEAD unreferenced. `wt remove <path>` did the same instead of refusing. The 0.80.0 release's data-loss review found it; reproduced end-to-end before the fix, and after it prune keeps the entry and `wt remove` refuses.

A stale entry's git dir is its registration `<common>/worktrees/<id>`, so `finalize_worktrees` now reads a stale entry's rebase state from there via the existing `Repository::registration_at`; live detached worktrees still use `rev-parse`. `test_finalize_worktree_stale_reads_its_own_rebase` covers both a nested stale entry (must get no label) and a stale entry that is itself mid-rebase (labelled from its registration).

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

title: ci(release): publish a signed packslip with each release
body:
This adds one step to the `host` job in `release.yaml`. The step writes a signed [packslip](https://packslip.dev) manifest, `packslip.sigstore.json`, and it ships as a release asset alongside the archives.

A packslip lists each archive's digest, its platform, and where `wt` and `git-wt` sit inside it, plus the completions and agent skills that go with the release.

## What this gets you and your users

- **Better security.** Installers such as mise and aqua find worktrunk's downloads through a registry entry someone else wrote, and at best compare them to a checksum file hosted on the same release. With a packslip, an installer first checks that the manifest was signed by `max-sixty/worktrunk`'s own release workflow (keyless Sigstore signing through GitHub OIDC), then checks each archive's digest and size against it before unpacking anything. mise also remembers the signer, so a release that turns up signed by a different workflow or key is not installed until the user explicitly decides to trust it. There's no signing key for you to store or rotate.
- **Direct control over how worktrunk is installed.** The manifest comes from your release workflow, so you decide which archives exist for which platforms, where the executable sits in each, and what ships with it. Installers no longer depend on third-party registry entries that infer all of that from asset names and drift when a name or platform changes.
- **Completions that just work.** Users get bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell completions from `wt config shell completions` for the exact version they have installed, with nothing to add to their shell rc files.
- **Your agent skills, matched to the version.** The `worktrunk` and `wt-switch-create` skills ship with each release, pinned to the release commit, so an agent working with a given worktrunk release reads the skill written for that release, not whatever is on the default branch. `mise skills ls` shows them, and `mise skills sync` links them into a project's agent directory.

Once a release ships a packslip, I'll switch mise's registry entry for worktrunk to use it, so users get all of this from a plain `mise use worktrunk` with nothing to change on their end. Other installers can check the same file with `packslip verify`.

## What it declares

- Artifacts: the five `worktrunk-*.tar.xz` / `worktrunk-*.zip` archives. It leaves out checksums, installers, `source.tar.gz`, and `wt.rb`.
- `bin: wt git-wt`
- Resources:
  ```
  completion/bash,zsh,fish,powershell/wt=exec:wt config shell completions {shell}
  completion/bash,zsh,fish,powershell/git-wt=exec:git-wt config shell completions {shell}
  skill/worktrunk=repo:skills/worktrunk
  skill/wt-switch-create=repo:skills/wt-switch-create
  ```
  The completions use the same command Homebrew's formula runs. Nushell is left out because `wt config shell completions nu` prints the full shell integration, not only completions.

## Release flow

Releases are immutable, and v0.79.0 is marked immutable, so
author: jdx
diff:
--- .github/workflows/release.yaml (+35/-0)
@@ -313,6 +313,11 @@ jobs:
     env:
       GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
     runs-on: "ubuntu-24.04"
+    # id-token and attestations are for the packslip step below.
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+      id-token: write
+      attestations: write
     outputs:
       val: ${{ steps.host.outputs.manifest }}
     steps:
@@ -357,6 +362,36 @@ jobs:
         run: |
           # Remove the granular manifests
           rm -f artifacts/*-dist-manifest.json
+      # A manifest of the archives (digests, wt/git-wt paths, completions, and
+      # skills/ at this commit), signed with this workflow's OIDC identity so
+      # installers such as mise can verify a download against this repo.
+      # Releases are immutable, so the bundle goes into artifacts/ and ships
+      # with `gh release create` below instead of being uploaded after it.
+      # See https://packslip.dev.
+      - name: Create packslip
+        id: packslip
+        # Optional channel: a packslip or Sigstore failure must not block the
+        # release and every publish job that needs `host`.
+        continue-on-error: true
+        # continue-on-error only covers a step that exits; bound a stalled
+        # Sigstore call so it cannot hold the release until the job timeout.
+        timeout-minutes: 10
+        uses: jdx/packslip@87479dfc6443253dff69601cace5fc6ea07e6df5 # v1.4.0
+        with:
+          artifacts: artifacts/worktrunk-*.tar.xz artifacts/worktrunk-*.zip
+          bin: wt git-wt
+          resources: |
+            completion/bash,zsh,fish,powershell/wt=exec:wt config shell completions {shell}
+            completion/bash,zsh,fish,powershell/git-wt=exec:git-wt config shell completions {shell}
+            skill/worktrunk=repo:skills/worktrunk
+            skill/wt-switch-create=repo:skills/wt-switch-create
+          out: packslip
+          upload: false
+      - name: Stage packslip
+        if: steps.packslip.outcome == 'success'
+        env:
+          BUNDLE: ${{ steps.packslip.outputs.bundle }}
+        run: cp "$BUNDLE" artifacts/
       - name: Create GitHub Release
         env:
           PRERELEASE_FLAG: "${{ fromJson(steps.host.outputs.manifest).announcement_is_prerelease && '--prerelease' || '' }}"

This is in its own PR because Nushell's version moves PTY snapshots under `--all-features`, and this PR's CI is the only place the bump is tested on macOS and Windows.

The release's one breaking change that touches this repo is the unified completer input ([nushell/nushell#18791](https://github.com/nushell/nushell/pull/18791)). `templates/nushell.nu` already handles it: #4297 moved the completer to the new `place` input, so 0.116 no longer warns when the integration is sourced. Locally, with 0.116.0 on `PATH`, the `shell` integration-test subset gives the same results as with 0.115.1: 193 passed, and the same 16 failures, which are sandbox-environment snapshot failures present on main.

title: ci: bump pinned worktrunk to 0.79.0
body:
Weekly CI pin bump: `worktrunk` `=0.78.0` → `=0.79.0`, at three sites (`ci.yaml` ×2, `nightly.yaml`).

This is the `wt` that runs the suite (`wt hook pre-merge`) on all three platforms, so it has its own PR: this PR's CI matrix is the only place the bump gets tested. This week's other drifted pins (cargo-nextest and Nushell) are in their own PRs.

Compatibility: worktrunk 0.79.0 declares `rust-version = 1.97`, which matches the pinned toolchain (`rust-toolchain.toml` channel `1.97.0`).

Neither of 0.79.0's two breaking changes reaches CI. CI calls `wt` only as `wt hook pre-merge --yes <filters>`. The breaking changes are to `wt switch --no-cd -x` (the program now runs in the new worktree) and to `wt merge`/`wt step rebase`, which now pass `--no-update-refs`. CI invokes none of those commands.

<details><summary>Weekly checks that found no drift</summary>

- **MSRV/toolchain**: current stable is `1.98.1`, so latest−1 is `1.97`, which `Cargo.toml`, `tests/helpers/wt-perf/Cargo.toml`, and `rust-toolchain.toml` already pin. The `nightly-2026-08-01` pins in `nightly.yaml` are about 8 weeks old, inside the three-month window. With no toolchain change, `flake.lock` needed no refresh.
- **Other `cargo-install` pins**: `cargo-affected` 0.4.1, `cargo-insta` 1.48.0, `cargo-llvm-cov` 0.9.1, `cargo-msrv` 0.19.3, `cargo-udeps` 0.1.61, and `lychee` 0.24.2 all match their current crates.io releases.
- **Codex Cloud tools**: PowerShell `7.6.6` is still the latest `PowerShell/PowerShell` release. `cloud.sh`'s cargo-nextest and Nushell pins move in the sibling PRs.

title: fix(shell): stop Nushell 0.116 warning that the wt completer's spans input is deprecated
body:
Nushell [0.116.0](https://github.com/nushell/nushell/releases/tag/0.116.0) (released 2026-09-26) binds custom completer inputs by parameter name ([nushell/nushell#18791](https://github.com/nushell/nushell/pull/18791)). Our completer's parameter is still named `spans`, the old name, so sourcing the `wt` integration on 0.116 prints a multi-line `nu::shell::deprecated` warning ("Positional completer input deprecated") at every shell startup. Completions still work, but only through a compatibility bridge that Nushell says will be removed in a future release. After that, the completer would receive `nothing` and `wt` tab completion would stop working.

This PR renames the parameter to `place`, the name Nushell's migration table suggests. On 0.116, `place` is a record whose `command` field holds the same token list `spans` used to. On older versions the argument is still the plain spans list, because they pass it positionally regardless of the parameter's name. The completer checks which of the two it received, so a single template works on both.

Tested by generating the integration (`wt config shell init nu`) from this branch and running `commandline complete` against it on Nushell 0.115.1 and 0.116.0:

- Neither version prints a warning. On main, 0.116.0 prints it.
- Both versions give identical results for `wt ` (subcommands), `wt switch ` (branches), and `wt config sh` (→ `shell`, `show`). These match what the `spans` version returns today.
- Integration tests matching `nu`/`completion`/`git_error_display` under `--features shell-integration-tests` give the same results on both versions. The only two failures are fish `config show` snapshots, which fail identically on unmodified main in this sandbox.

The `init_nu` snapshot changes to match the template. The CI Nushell pin bump to 0.116.0 is in a separate PR and doesn't depend on this one.

title: skills(running-tend): hold approval on contributor PRs whose code outweighs the fix's reach
body:
The PR reviewer approves contributor PRs once they are correct and green. It doesn't ask whether the amount of code is justified by how many users the fix reaches, or whether the codebase already has a way to do the same thing. Over the last two days `max-sixty` raised that question on five PRs the bot had approved, and on #4271 he asked the bot directly to "review skeptically, do not allow any needless code complications through". This adds a **Proportionality and the canonical approach** criterion to `references/review-pr.md`. It sits next to the **Documentation cruft** check from #4283, which already covers the doc-sentence half of the same feedback. When the criterion applies, the review posts `COMMENT` naming the cost and any smaller alternative, instead of `APPROVE`.

This is a repo-local overlay, not a bundled-skill change. How much code a fix is worth is this maintainer's call, and other tend consumers would weigh it differently. The bundled review skill has only the generic "does it avoid unnecessary complexity?" line, which these approvals got past.

Each PR below was bot-approved, and the maintainer then pushed back on its size or approach:

title: Tie a changelog fix's prominence to its reach
body:
The 0.80.0 changelog draft followed the release skill's "Name the conditions a bug needed" rule to the letter — every Fixed entry named its conditions, joined with "and" — yet still read as severe. Each of fourteen fixes got its own bold bullet, and most headlines stated the consequence (**`wt remove` no longer deletes submodule changes hidden by config**), so extreme corner cases such as a pre-remove hook corrupting the user config read as general breakage. Readers skim headlines; conditions in the body arrive too late. The drafter's own research had labelled most of these fixes "rare" or "near zero" reach, and three verifier passes came back clean because the template checked accuracy, length, and ranking only.

The rule becomes "Match a fix's prominence to its reach": conditions go in the headline and the consequence in the body, and a fix of near-zero reader interest folds into a closing "Fixes for unusual setups" bullet instead of getting its own. It reuses the skill's existing definition of reader interest (reach combined with obligation), so a rare breaking change still keeps its own bullet. The verifier template gains a check that reads each headline alone.

`evals/` gains the 0.80.0 research notes and the first draft as a case. Pasting the old and new guidance with those notes, 3 runs each:

| | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| Drafter headlines the submodule fix by its setup | 1/3 | 3/3 |
| Drafter folds near-zero-reach fixes into a roll-up | 0/3 | 3/3 |
| Verifier proposes the roll-up for the original draft | 0/3 | 3/3 |

The failed-squash fix, which anyone with a failing commit hook hits, kept its own top bullet in every drafting run.

title: ci(affected): stop shallowing the full clone before computing the merge-base
body:
The `affected tests` job computes its cache key with `git merge-base origin/main "$PR_HEAD"`, but first runs `git fetch --no-tags --depth=200 origin main`. That fetch runs on top of a `fetch-depth: 0` checkout, and a `--depth` fetch into a full clone makes it shallow: git writes `.git/shallow` and grafts main's history at 200 commits. For a PR whose fork point is more than 200 commits behind main, which is about three weeks of main here, `merge-base` finds nothing and the step exits 1. The job is advisory, so the run stays green, but that PR loses its affected-tests signal. The graft also cuts off older cached `collect_sha` commits that `cargo affected run` expects to reach.

`origin/main` is already complete from the checkout, so this PR deletes the fetch and leaves a comment explaining why it must not come back.

<details><summary>Reproduction</summary>

On a full `file://` clone with main 10 commits deep and a PR branched 7 commits back:

```
$ git merge-base origin/main $PR          # before
5b9c202b1c76a05cb76d09e5551a4940c112c845
$ git fetch -q --no-tags --depth=3 origin main
$ git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository
true
$ git merge-base origin/main $PR; echo exit=$?
exit=1
```

None of the last 100 PR runs of `affected.yaml` failed at this step; current PRs are based recently enough. This PR's own `affected tests` jobs exercise the step without the fetch.

</details>

This is a CI config change, so there is no regression test. The repro above is the evidence.
author: worktrunk-bot
diff:
--- .github/workflows/affected.yaml (+4/-1)
@@ -203,7 +203,10 @@ jobs:
       env:
         PR_HEAD: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
       run: |
-        git fetch --no-tags --depth=200 origin main
+        # `origin/main` is already complete from the full checkout above. A
+        # `git fetch --depth=N` here would graft main's history at N commits
+        # and make the repo shallow, so a PR branched further back would have
+        # no merge-base.
         sha=$(git merge-base origin/main "$PR_HEAD")
         echo "sha=$sha" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
         echo "merge-base with origin/main: $sha"

title: test(fsmonitor): keep other test threads from filtering out the fork trace event
body:
Fixes #4291. `start_fsmonitor_daemon_skips_fork_when_daemon_answers` failed in the [nightly `feature-powerset` job](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/36298021394) because its trace capture lost the fork event. The fork itself ran. The test now holds a second live `tracing::Dispatch` for its duration, and that closes the race.

**Cause.** tracing-core 0.1.36 treats "exactly one dispatcher registered" as a special case (`Dispatchers::has_just_one` in `callsite.rs`). A callsite registered for the first time is resolved against the default dispatcher of the thread that hits it. It is not checked against the registered dispatchers. The result is cached globally. This test is the only code in the lib test binary that registers a dispatcher, so its subscriber is always that single one. Before it is registered, `LevelFilter` is `OFF`, so no `debug!` callsite is registered at all. Once it is registered, the level is `TRACE`, and any parallel test whose git command reaches the shared `cmd_completed` callsite in `trace/emit.rs` before this thread does caches `Interest::never` for it. The fork's record is then dropped. Only `cargo test` runs lib tests as threads of one process, which is why `feature-powerset` fails and the per-process nextest `full-tests` jobs pass.

**Fix.** With two live dispatchers, tracing-core resolves new callsites against every registered dispatcher. Both are `Registry` subscribers, so the result is `always`. The change is test-only, and nothing in production code changes.

**Verification.** A standalone program against tracing-core 0.1.36 reproduces the race: a background thread hits a shared callsite while a scoped subscriber is live on the main thread. Without the pin the first capture counted `0` events. With the pin both captures counted `1`. Clippy and fmt pass with `--all-features`. This sandbox blocks `AF_UNIX` sockets, so I couldn't run the test itself locally (its `bind` fails). PR CI on macOS and Linux runs it.

title: perf(list): build the ref snapshot from the branch inventories
body:
`wt list` and the picker open their task pool only once the post-skeleton ref snapshot is built. That snapshot rescanned `refs/heads/`, which the phase before the skeleton had already scanned into the cached branch inventory, and then `refs/remotes/`, one after the other. In the picker the preview panes' comparison base ran the same pair of scans a third time.

`Repository::inventory_snapshot(base)` replaces `capture_refs_with_ahead_behind` and builds the snapshot from the cached inventories, scanning only one that nobody has fetched yet. Tasks now resolve refs to the same SHAs the rows were built from. The comparison base builds its snapshot the same way, and the `Remote⇅` upstream primer reads the same inventories, so it runs beside the snapshot instead of after it. `capture_refs` still scans fresh, and every command that moves a ref keeps using it; the docs that pointed at "a `RefSnapshot` captured at the moment of read" now name it.

The phase before the skeleton still scans `refs/remotes/` only when remote rows are shown. Doing it unconditionally would make first paint wait on it in a repo with many remote branches and few worktrees, so plain `wt list` runs that scan once, after the skeleton.

Measured on a repo with 50 worktrees, 52 local branches and 103 remote-tracking branches, alternating with `main`, medians in ms from the start of collect:

| | skeleton | task pool opens | last result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `wt list`, main | 58 | 93 | 240 |
| `wt list`, this branch | 58 | 78 | 221 |
| picker, main | 49 | 120 | — |
| picker, this branch | 38 | 47 | — |

`for-each-ref` scans per run went from 3 to 2 for `wt list` and from about 4.4 to 2 for the picker. The picker's skeleton difference is likely noise; nothing before its skeleton forks less.

`inventory_snapshot_reuses_cached_inventories` checks that the snapshot reads the cached scans; the existing ahead-behind tests now run through `inventory_snapshot`.
