title: perf(list): skip the PR/MR lookup for branches never pushed
body:
A forge opens a PR/MR only from a branch it hosts, so a local branch that no remote has under its name can't head one. `wt list --full`, the statusline and the picker still asked the forge about every such branch whenever the CI cache (30–60s) had expired. On a repo with 239 local branches, of which 19 exist on `origin`, that was 249 `gh` calls at ~450ms and ~65ms of CPU each, about 15 CPU-seconds per run.

`detect_ci` now skips the PR/MR lookup for a local branch that was never pushed: no remote has a branch by that name, and the branch's push remote (or the primary remote, when none is set) has a fetch refspec that would have recorded it under `refs/remotes/`. `git push` updates the remote-tracking ref only where the fetch refspecs map the branch. So a `--single-branch` or `--depth` clone, which maps only the cloned branch, still asks the forge about every other branch. A URL push remote (`gh pr checkout` of a fork's PR) has no refspecs and is still asked about too. Both checks read the ref inventory and config map already cached for the command. The branch-workflow fallback is unchanged, and the rule applies to every forge.

The push remote now comes from the existing local-branch scan (`%(push:remotename)`, no measurable cost) instead of one `for-each-ref` per branch. `Branch::push_remote_url` forks nothing after the first scan, and the per-branch cache that existed only to avoid that fork is deleted.

Measured with `wt list --full` on that repo, CI cache cleared, 5 runs each at load average ~30:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| `gh` calls | 249 | 25 |
| last CI result (median) | 9.25s | 5.2s |
| total wall (median) | 12.0s | 9.6s |

Under that load the local git work was the bottleneck, and the 25 calls started only at 2.3–5s. On a quiet machine the CI tail should be close to one round trip; that's an estimate, not a measurement.

The trade-off: a PR opened from a branch pushed by another clone, and not yet fetched here, shows no PR until the next fetch. The help text's blank-CI row now reads "Branch never pushed", replacing "No upstream", which was never exactly when the cell goes blank.

`test_pr_lookup_skips_branches_on_no_remote` checks the `gh` call log for four cases: pushed, URL push remote, a push remote set up like a `--single-branch` clone, and never pushed. Dropping either the remote check or the refspec check fails it. `refspecs_track_ref_follows_the_fetch_mapping` covers the refspec matching, including negative refspecs.

title: perf(picker): take the path seed and forge lookup off the collect thread
body:
After the picker paints its rows, the collect thread ran two steps one after the other before the ref snapshot could start. The task pool opens only once that snapshot finishes, so every row's results waited on both steps:

- `prime_worktree_path_caches`, which canonicalizes and reads `.git` for each worktree: 5–7ms warm, 20–82ms loaded or cold on leaf (~130 worktrees).
- The comments fetch's `ci_platform()` call, whose first use forks `git remote get-url`: 20–48ms. It runs only when a row's cached CI status is still fresh (within 30–60s of a `wt list`).

The seeding now runs as a spawn in the post-skeleton `rayon::scope`, alongside the ref snapshot. The fsmonitor probes are nested under it because each probe reads the git dir the seeding fills in. The comments fetch now resolves the forge inside its pool job, through the same `spawn_comments_fetch` path the `--prs` rows use, so `on_skeleton` and `on_update` start no processes. That removes the last production caller of `fill_external`; tests call `fill` directly.

In a trace with a fresh CI cache, `main` spends 93→168ms on these two steps before the snapshot starts. On this branch the snapshot starts at the skeleton handoff. The expected saving is ~10ms on an idle machine and up to ~130ms under load. An end-to-end timing wasn't possible: the load average was 55–164 during the runs, and time to pool start varied 430–660ms on both builds, mostly from the snapshot's own `for-each-ref` scans.

The pipeline diagram in `src/commands/list/collect/mod.rs` is updated to show where both steps now run.

title: perf(list): settle picker rows top-down and fork rebase lookups concurrently
body:
In a repo with many worktrees, the `wt switch` picker took up to ~1.6s after painting its rows before the visible ones dimmed (dim marks a row whose branch is integrated and safe to remove). Two causes, one commit each:

- **Work items now run in queue order** (`par_bridge` instead of `into_par_iter`). The queue is local tasks in display-row order, then network tasks. `into_par_iter` gave each pool worker a contiguous slice of it, so one worker ran a row's dozen tasks one after another, and the slices holding the bottom rows and the network tasks started as early as the top rows. With `par_bridge`, each idle worker takes the next item, so the top row's tasks run at once and rows settle from the top down.
- **Rebase branches of detached worktrees are looked up concurrently.** `git worktree list` reports a mid-rebase worktree only as `detached`, so `list_worktrees` resolves each detached worktree's git dir to read its rebase `head-name`. That was one serial `git rev-parse --git-dir` fork per detached worktree, before the skeleton. They now fork together through a new `Cmd::run_concurrently`, which spawns every child before waiting on any. It deliberately avoids a thread pool: this runs inside the `list_worktrees` cache initializer, and a rayon thread waiting there runs other pool jobs, one of which may read the same cache (`wt step prune` does, and a `par_iter` version deadlocked it).

The module docstring of `src/commands/list/collect/mod.rs` now specs the collect pipeline: each phase, the thread it runs on, every blocking wait, and the rule that keeps the waits deadlock-free.

### Measurements

On a real repo with ~140 worktrees (16 detached), 5 runs each:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Picker: visible rows dimmed, after rows appear | 275–1584ms | 150–230ms |
| `wt list` skeleton (median) | 178ms | 103ms |
| `wt list` total (median), `par_bridge` change alone | 417ms | 461ms |

`cargo bench --bench list -- full/warm` (the `full` fixture detaches 6 of its 24 worktrees), run alternately on the same machine at load average 3–13:

| Round | main median (min–max) | this PR median (min–max) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 185.0ms (161.9–315.6) | 160.6ms (149.2–272.9) |
| 2 | 203.2ms (175.8–317.5) | 196.8ms (174.9–309.3) |

### Cost: CI results arrive later

`par_bridge` starts network tasks only once every local task has been handed out, where `into_par_iter` happened to start some early. On the same repo with `wt list --full` (CI cache cleared, 249 `gh` calls, 5 runs each), the last CI result arrives at a median of 6168ms against 5549ms on main, and the first CI request starts at 592ms against 438ms. The underlying limit is that network tasks share the pool workers and the 32-permit command semaphore with local work, so starting them first would stall every row; giving them their own budget would let them start immediately. This PR leaves that as it is.

The ~40ms rise in the `wt list` total also comes from `par_bridge`; I haven't attributed it furth

title: test(bench): detach six worktrees in the `full` list fixture
body:
`wt list` resolves each detached worktree's branch from rebase state, which forks `git rev-parse --git-dir` in that worktree before the first paint. On main these forks run one after another. The generated fixture put every linked worktree on a branch, so no benchmark ran that lookup.

The generated recipe gains a `detached_worktrees` count, a subset of the linked worktrees. The builder creates the worktrees as before, then detaches the last N in place with `git checkout --detach`: each keeps its rotation state (dirty, staged, ahead), and its `wt-*` branch stays behind as a branch-only row, the shape a mid-rebase or scratch checkout leaves. `full` detaches 6 of its 24 linked worktrees; every other recipe keeps 0, so only `full`'s baseline moves. `wt-perf setup generated` takes the count as a fourth positional argument, so `wt-perf setup generated 24 120 0 6` rebuilds `full` for tracing.

A trace of `wt list --branches --progressive` on the new fixture shows the six `rev-parse --git-dir` forks on one thread, ~7.5ms each. `full/warm` on a loaded laptop, alternating fixtures back to back: 0 detached 267 / 297 ms, 6 detached 314 / 328 ms.

title: perf(list): skip fsmonitor daemon starts when the daemon is running
body:
On macOS with the builtin fsmonitor enabled (`core.fsmonitor=true`), `wt list` and the `wt switch` picker fork `git fsmonitor--daemon start` for every worktree inside the post-skeleton `rayon::scope`, and the per-row task pool can't start until all of them return. In the steady state nearly every start exits 128 "already running"; in a 128-worktree repo those forks cost 100–300ms before the pool opens.

`Repository::start_fsmonitor_daemon_at` now first connects to `<git-dir>/fsmonitor--daemon.ipc` and returns without forking if a daemon answers. That's the check git's own `start` makes before refusing (`ipc_get_active_state` connects and closes). Any failure — no daemon, stale socket, unresolvable git dir, or a socket path longer than `sun_path` — falls through to the existing fork. The git dir is already primed from the worktree list on this path, so the probe runs no git command.

The socket basename is now shared as `git::fsmonitor::IPC_SOCKET_NAME` with the `wt remove` stop path.

The new unit test binds a `UnixListener` at the repo's socket path and checks, via captured trace records, that no `git fsmonitor--daemon start` runs while it answers and that the start does run for a path with no git dir. It fails with the early return removed.

title: fix(step): diff against the target's upstream when the local target is stale
body:
`wt step diff` diffed from `merge-base(HEAD, target)`. When a branch is built on `origin/main` and local `main` lags it, that merge base is local `main` itself, so the diff counted every upstream commit the branch sits on as the branch's own. In the case that surfaced this, a one-commit branch 9 commits ahead of a stale local `main` showed 39 files instead of its 3.

#3549 fixed this topology for `wt merge`, `wt step squash` and `wt step rebase` via `span_upstream`, but `wt step diff` was left out, even though its help says it shows "what `wt merge` would include". It now uses the same rule, so its diff matches what `wt merge` would squash and what the `wt list` columns and picker diff pane already measure against. Explicit targets with no upstream (`origin/main`, a SHA) are unchanged.

The new test sits with the other #3519 tests in `merge.rs` and reuses their stale-`main` fixture. With the fix reverted, it fails and lists the upstream commits' files.

The currently published snapshot predates the prompt repair, and visitors still receive the old guide. The page is intentionally unlinked so it can be merged and tested on the accepted production origin before broader exposure. The corrected snapshot must finish saving, then the new guide must be published and tested in a fresh visitor session.

title: fix(logs): report real branch names in hook-output JSON; fix tips recipes wt rejects
body:
Two recipes on the Tips & Patterns page fail when copied. This PR fixes both, adds a test that runs the database recipe straight from the page, and makes the hook-output JSON report real branch names so the log recipes can scope to the current branch.

- **Database per worktree**: the `set-vars` step passed three `KEY=VALUE` pairs to one `wt config state vars set`, which accepts exactly one (`error: unexpected argument 'port=…' found`). Because the step failed, `vars.container` and `vars.port` were never set for the `db` step or `pre-remove`. The step now runs three `vars set` calls chained with `&&`. The recipe also stored `db_url`, and vars keys have rejected underscores since #2285 (Git config variable names can't contain them). It's now `db-url`, in the `vars get` example too. #1848 had moved this key from hyphens to underscores because Jinja parses `vars.db-url` as subtraction. That doesn't apply here: the recipe reads the key only with `wt config state vars get db-url`, never in a template.
- **Monitor hook logs**: `wt config state logs get --hook=user:post-start:server` and the `wtlog` alias built on it fail with `unexpected argument '--hook'`, because #2161 removed that flag. Its replacement, a `jq` filter over `wt config state logs --format=json`, couldn't scope to the current branch. The JSON `branch` field was the sanitized log directory (`feature/x` became `feature-x-<hash>`), so the help example used `startswith` and `head -1` and tailed whichever worktree's `server` log was newest.
- **Hook-output JSON `branch`**: the field now holds the real branch name. It maps each log directory back through `sanitize_for_filename` over the local branches, and is `null` when no local branch writes there: a deleted branch, a detached HEAD, or a directory two branches share. The recipes in the help and on the page match `[.branch, .source, .hook_type, .name]` exactly. The extending page's `hook-log` alias compared `.branch` with `{{ branch | sanitize_hash }}`, the on-disk form, and now passes `{{ branch }}` to jq with `--arg`, like its other values. The `wtlog` alias becomes a shell function taking the hook name.

`test_doc_example_database_set_vars_step_runs` pulls the `set-vars` step from the page's TOML block, runs it as a `wt` alias with `wt` on `PATH`, and checks the stored `port`. It fails on `main` with the argument error above. After the first fix it also caught the `db_url` rejection. `test_logs_get_json_branch_is_unsanitized` covers the branch mapping, including the deleted and shared-directory cases. I ran the new recipe by hand from a `feature/x` worktree next to an `other/y` worktree, and it tailed only the `feature/x` log.

The `skills/` and `plugins/` copies of the page are regenerated by `test_docs_are_in_sync`.

body:
Regenerates the tend workflows for tend 0.3.3 → 0.3.4. The diff here is the version stamp and the `max-sixty/tend/claude` action pin; the behavior changes ship in the action and bundled skills:

title: Read config from dash-prefixed default branches
body:
## Summary

- pass `--end-of-options` to `git show` before the project-config revision
- cover bare repositories whose configured default branch starts with `-`

## Problem

When no worktree has the default branch checked out, Worktrunk reads the committed `.config/wt.toml` with `git show <branch>:.config/wt.toml`. Git parses a revision such as `-x:.config/wt.toml` as an option. The best-effort fallback then returns no project config, so hooks, aliases, and other project settings disappear without an error.

## Tests

- Confirmed the new integration test failed before the fix with `project.config = null`.
- Confirmed the targeted test and the adjacent object-store fallback test pass after the fix.
- Ran `PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH mise exec rust@1.97 -- cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes`: 4,968 tests passed and 1 skipped; fmt, clippy, rustdoc, and doctests passed.
author: Duang777

title: Reuse user config snapshot for removal hooks
body:
## Summary

- reuse the command-entry `UserConfig` snapshot when rendering approved removal hooks
- pass the snapshot through direct remove, merge cleanup, step prune, and picker removal paths
- add a regression test where `pre-remove` corrupts the config file and the approved `post-remove` hook still runs

## Why

Removal hook approval and execution used different `UserConfig` loads. If the config changed or became unreadable after approval, execution silently skipped hooks that the user had already approved. Keeping the matching snapshot with `ApprovedHookPlan` makes hook selection and rendering consistent.

## Testing

- `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.97.0-aarch64-apple-darwin cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes`
- 4,968 tests passed; 1 skipped
author: Duang777

title: fix(list): let merge-tree probes finish when the picker cancels background work
body:
Leaving the `wt switch` picker while a `git merge-tree` probe is inside an external merge driver no longer strands `.merge_file_*` files in the worktree. Git writes the driver's three inputs as plain temp files in its cwd and removes them only when the driver returns normally, so the SIGTERM that `cancel_background_commands()` sends on picker exit left them behind. SIGTERM is the right signal for the preview diffs (git cleans `index.lock` on it), but not for this case.

The change adds `Cmd::finish_once_started()`. A command marked that way still honors the cancellation latch, so a cancelled probe that hasn't spawned never will. Once running, though, it isn't registered for signalling and runs to completion. `compute_merge_tree_outcome` opts in. This is the first fix proposed in the issue.

Verification:

- `merge_tree_cache_tests::merge_tree_probe_is_not_signalled_on_cancel` runs a conflicting probe through a merge driver that records its parent PID, then checks that the running `git merge-tree` isn't a cancellation target. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- End to end, I drove `wt switch` from a PTY using the issue's `sleep 3; exit 1` driver and pressed Esc after 1.5 s. The unfixed binary left three `.merge_file_*` files each run, and the fixed binary left none.

Tradeoff: an abandoned probe now outlives `wt` for as long as the driver takes, and its result isn't cached because the in-process cache exits with `wt`. A Ctrl-C during `wt list` still reaches `merge-tree` via the terminal's process-group broadcast, and that path is unchanged.

Closes #4273 — automated triage
author: worktrunk-bot

title: fix: preserve multiline state variable values
body:
## Summary

- read regex-matched git config entries with NUL record delimiters
- preserve embedded newlines in vars and marker values
- cover vars get, JSON list, and clear-all with a multiline value

## Root cause

`git config --get-regexp` uses newlines both between records and inside multiline values. Splitting stdout with `.lines()` truncated each value after its first line. `git config --null --get-regexp` emits NUL-terminated records, allowing the parser to split each record only at the first key/value newline.

## Verification

- `cargo test integration_tests::config_state:: -- --nocapture` (143 passed)
- `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes` (4,968 passed, 1 skipped)
author: Duang777

title: fix: support slash-named remotes in branch inventory
body:
Git permits remote names such as `team/fork`. Splitting `team/fork/feature` at its first slash prevented `wt switch feature` from finding the remote branch and misidentified remote names in list and CI consumers.

Resolve remote-tracking refs against the longest configured remote prefix once per inventory scan, and retain that boundary through list JSON, CI lookup, and picker deduplication. Read local branches’ upstream remote directly from Git’s tracking metadata. Remote HEAD queries remain supported, and orphaned refs retain the conventional first-segment fallback.

Validation: regression reproduction fails with the original parser; 263 focused tests pass, including slash-named and overlapping remotes, remote HEAD queries, and local tracking. Pre-commit/Clippy and documentation checks pass. The full local suite reports 5,316 passes and three PowerShell failures; standalone PowerShell also crashes with “Stack overflow” on this machine.

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_
author: Duang777

title: test(switch): make the worktree-path hint suppression test able to fail
body:
`test_switch_create_no_hint_with_custom_worktree_path` could never fail. It checked that stderr did not contain `"Customize worktree locations"`, but the hint in [`handlers.rs`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/f732cbda7296bb019c92128615e8e823136f488d/src/output/handlers.rs#L669-L671) reads "To **c**ustomize worktree locations, …". Because of the lowercase `c`, the needle never matched, so the test would have passed even if the hint were printed with a custom `worktree-path`.

This PR switches to the lowercase text, which a sibling test already uses. It also adds a control step: the test clears the config and runs `wt switch --create` again, then asserts the same needle does appear. With that control, the test fails if the needle ever drifts from the message again. Suppressing the hint doesn't mark it as shown, so it still appears once in the control run.

Verification: the updated test passes, and with the old uppercase needle it fails at the new control assertion. The other 230 `switch::` integration tests pass. The change is test-only.
author: worktrunk-bot

title: docs(step): correct squash --stage=none and prune skip-list help
body:
Two statements in `wt step` help were wrong about behavior, and the generated docs pages repeat them. This PR corrects both in `src/cli/step.rs` and regenerates the synced pages.

- **`wt step squash --stage=none`.** The help said this squashes "only committed changes". In fact changes already in the index are folded in too: `has_staged` drives the squash path in [`squash.rs`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/f732cbda7296bb019c92128615e8e823136f488d/src/commands/step/squash.rs#L188-L240). `--stage=none` only skips staging new changes. The help now says "squash commits plus what's already staged", which matches the `wt step commit` row above it.
- **`wt step prune`.** The help said locked worktrees and the main worktree are always skipped. A worktree with uncommitted changes (untracked files included) is skipped as well. It gets no removal plan and is filtered without a message, as the `CheckOutcome::plan` doc in [`prune.rs`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/f732cbda7296bb019c92128615e8e823136f488d/src/commands/step/prune.rs#L404-L412) says. The skip list now includes it.

Verification: I built `wt` and ran it in a scratch repo. `wt step squash --stage=none` over two empty commits plus a staged `s.txt` produced one commit containing `s.txt`. `wt step prune --min-age=0s --dry-run`, run with one integrated clean worktree and one integrated worktree holding an untracked file, listed only the clean one. `test_docs_are_in_sync` and the help snapshot tests pass. No regression test is added because this changes only documentation.

title: fix: fence leading-dash remote names from git options
body:
## Summary

- resolve cached remote HEADs through a verified full ref, so a leading-dash remote cannot be echoed back as a bogus `HEAD` branch
- place `--` before remote operands in `git ls-remote` and `git remote get-url`
- cover both default-branch detection and effective URL lookup with leading-dash remote regressions

## Root cause

Git accepts remote names beginning with `-` when creation uses an option separator. The earlier flag-injection audit in #3317 assumed those names were invalid, so three call sites remained unfenced.

For a remote named `-x`, `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref -x/HEAD` exits successfully and echoes `-x/HEAD`; Worktrunk stripped the remote prefix and cached `HEAD` as the default branch. If local HEAD lookup failed, `git ls-remote --symref -x HEAD` and `git remote get-url -x` parsed the remote as an option. Option-shaped names can be more than a lookup failure: a remote named `--upload-pack=touch` made unfenced `ls-remote` invoke `touch HEAD` during the local reproducer.

The local lookup now verifies `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD`, which cannot begin with an option marker. The two commands that require a raw remote operand now use `--`.

## Red/green evidence

Before the fix, the new regressions failed with:

- default branch: `left: Some("HEAD")`, `right: Some("main")`
- effective URL: `left: None`, `right: Some("../origin.git")`

After the fix, both pass. A CLI reproducer with remote name `--upload-pack=touch` returns the remote's `target` branch and does not create a `HEAD` file.

## Verification

- `cargo nextest run --test integration -E 'test(default_branch)'`: 67 passed
- `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes`: 4,967 passed, 1 skipped
- clippy, rustfmt, rustdoc, doctests, and pre-commit hooks passed

title: fix(config): resolve Claude Code's config dir by its own home rule
body:
`wt config plugins claude install-statusline` and `wt config show` resolved Claude Code's config directory with a `HOME`-first home rule, while Claude Code itself — and every other home lookup in worktrunk — uses the OS lookup. On Windows the two disagree whenever `HOME` holds the POSIX-style path Git Bash, MSYS2 and Cygwin set, and the disagreement is silent in both directions.

## Problem

`src/commands/config/show.rs::home_dir` read `HOME`, then `USERPROFILE`, before falling back to `worktrunk::path::home_dir`. Claude Code is a Node program: its config directory is `process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR || os.homedir()`, and Node's `os.homedir()` on Windows reads `USERPROFILE` and ignores `HOME` entirely. In a Git Bash session `HOME` is `/c/Users/<name>`, which is not a Windows path at all — Windows resolves it against the *current drive's* root.

So `install-statusline` reports `✓ Statusline configured` after writing to a directory Claude Code never opens, and `wt config show` reports a statusline that *is* configured as missing. `wt config show` reads back from the same path install just wrote to, so the two agree with each other and neither agrees with Claude Code.

## Evidence

Windows 11, two binaries built from the same tree with `cargo +stable-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu build` — one at `main` (`f88b827c`), one with this change — run in an identical environment: `HOME=/c/…/posix`, `USERPROFILE=D:\…\real`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` unset.

```
=== BEFORE  upstream main f88b827c
USERPROFILE=D:\…\wt-evidence-before\real
HOME=/c/projects/…/wt-evidence-before/posix
install-statusline -> ✓ Statusline configured (exit=0)
settings.json at USERPROFILE\.claude: False
settings.json at POSIX-HOME mirror: True

=== AFTER   this branch
USERPROFILE=D:\…\wt-evidence-after\real
HOME=/c/projects/…/wt-evidence-after/posix
install-statusline -> ✓ Statusline configured (exit=0)
settings.json at USERPROFILE\.claude: True
settings.json at POSIX-HOME mirror: False
```

The mirror is `D:\c\projects\…\posix\.claude\settings.json` — the POSIX path re-rooted on whichever drive `wt` happened to run from.

Detection, with the statusline already where Claude Code reads it:

```
=== BEFORE  upstream main f88b827c (statusline already configured)
wt config show -> ↳ Statusline not configured. To configure, run wt config plugins claude install-statusline

=== AFTER   this branch (statusline already configured)
wt config show -> ✓ Statusline configured
```

Claude Code's rule, read off the installed bundle (its config path is `join(process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR || os.homedir(), ".claude…json")`) and confirmed against Node on the same machine with `HOME` set to something else:

```
$ node -e "console.log(require('os').homedir())"
C:\Users\35417
```

## What changes

`claude_config_dir()` resolves all three of its branches through `worktrunk::path::home_dir()`, and the module-local `home_dir()` is deleted. On Unix nothing moves — the `home` crate is `HOME` there, with the passwd entry behind i

title: docs: use supported lean Codex commit generation settings
body:
The Codex commit-message example passed `-c system_prompt=''`, which Codex 0.156.1 rejects under `--strict-config` as an unknown setting. It also implied an empty prompt, though global `AGENTS.md` and Codex's other context remain.

The single recommended command now uses Luna without reasoning, limits project instructions and the skills catalog, disables unneeded web, shell, app, plugin, subagent, and goal capabilities, and replaces built-in model instructions with a one-character file. It preserves user provider settings and authentication. Accepting Worktrunk's first-run Codex setup creates that file and reports its path; the FAQ inventories it and explains that the saved command requires it. File setup errors name the path. Config help, the sample config, benchmark command, generated skill docs, and snapshots use the same command.

For `Reply exactly OK.`, the one-character file reduced a normal-home Codex query from 27,890 to 24,371 input tokens in one comparison. In a separate normal-home comparison, `skills.max_context_tokens=1` reduced input from 24,572 to 18,208 tokens; the four shell/app/plugin disables reduced that to 16,352, `agents.enabled=false` to 14,339, and disabling goals to 13,721. `codex debug prompt-input` showed the skills catalog shrinking from 22,170 to 501 characters. In a controlled fresh home, the global `AGENTS.md` added 6,504 tokens. We found no supported per-command flag to omit global `AGENTS.md` while retaining the normal Codex home; remaining agent context keeps this above a tens-of-tokens prompt.

Validated the exact saved stdin → Codex → `jq` command with strict config parsing and the user's normal Codex home: `Fix typo in README`, 13,729 input and 8 output tokens. Nine PTY commit prompt cases cover creation, reuse, preview decline, and setup failure; docs sync, help snapshots, docs build, and pre-commit passed.

The remaining direct-query work is tracked in [#4264](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/4264).

title: Fix push conflicts for non-UTF-8 paths
body:
## Summary

- Compare target status paths and pushed paths as raw Git bytes in `wt step push` conflict checks.
- Use one byte-oriented porcelain parser and changed-files API, with checked raw stdout methods for Git commands.
- Cover distinct non-UTF-8 filenames with a Linux end-to-end push regression.

## Root cause

`ensure_no_target_conflicts` decoded `git status -z` and `git diff-tree -z` output with `String::from_utf8_lossy` before comparing paths. Distinct names such as `collision-\xFE` and `collision-\xFF` both became `collision-�`, so an unrelated dirty target path could block the push.

## Verification

- `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes` passed locally.
- Linux CI and `codecov/patch` passed on the current head.

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_
author: Duang777

title: Preserve non-UTF-8 ignored paths
body:
## Summary

- Preserve raw Git path bytes from `git ls-files -z` when locating ignored entries for `step copy-ignored` and `step promote`.
- Convert entry names for JSON output only, so non-UTF-8 paths can be copied without a serialization panic.
- Cover a non-UTF-8 ignored filename in a Linux CLI regression, including dry-run and actual-copy JSON output.

## Root cause

`list_ignored_entries` decoded Git path bytes with `String::from_utf8_lossy` before using the result as a filesystem path. An invalid UTF-8 byte became a replacement character, so Worktrunk looked up a different path.

## Verification

- `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes` passed locally.
- Linux CI and `codecov/patch` passed on the current head.

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_
author: Duang777

title: Fix relocate temp path collisions
body:
## Summary

- make each relocation cycle use a unique temporary worktree path
- prevent colliding sanitized branch names from partially relocating disjoint cycles
- add an end-to-end regression test with two real legacy short-hash collisions

## Root cause

`RelocationExecutor::break_cycle` derived its staging directory only from `sanitize_for_filename(branch)`. That helper appends a three-character hash, so distinct branch names can still collide. Because all cycles remain staged until finalization, a later cycle could reuse a live staging path and leave the relocation partially applied.

The executor already has a unique candidate index, so the staging path now prefixes the sanitized name with that index without changing the public sanitization contract.

## Verification

- red: the new test failed before the fix when the second staging worktree reused the first path
- green: all 36 `step_relocate` integration tests passed
- full `wt hook pre-merge --yes`: 4970 tests passed, 1 skipped; fmt, clippy, pre-commit, doctest, and rustdoc passed
author: Duang777

title: fix(config): keep config show --full working outside a git repository
body:
Running `wt config show --full` from a directory that isn't a git repository threw away the whole report. All the user saw was `✗ git rev-parse --git-common-dir failed (exit 128)`. Plain `wt config show` in the same directory works: it notes "Not in a git repository" under PROJECT CONFIG and renders every other section.

The cause is `render_diagnostics`, which called `Repository::current()?` for itself. `handle_config_show` builds the whole report in a buffer and pages it at the end, so that one error discarded the USER CONFIG, SHELL and other sections that had already rendered. The caller already resolves the repo with `Repository::current().ok()`, so this PR passes that `Option<&Repository>` into the diagnostics:

- Outside a repo, the CI-tool check falls through to its existing "CI status requires GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, or Azure DevOps remote" hint.
- The version check and the commit-generation test still run, with no project identifier.

Inside a repository the output is unchanged.

`test_config_show_full_outside_git_repo` runs `--full` from a tempdir and asserts that it exits successfully and that the USER CONFIG and DIAGNOSTICS sections render. It fails on `main` with the `rev-parse` error above and passes with this change. The rest of the `config_show` integration tests (216) and the pre-commit hooks also pass.
author: worktrunk-bot

title: docs(list): correct stale phase comments in collect/mod.rs
body:
The module docstring in `src/commands/list/collect/mod.rs` is the phase contract that `src/commands/list/AGENTS.md` points readers at, and three parts of it no longer matched the code. This PR updates those comments only; there is no behavior change.

- **The post-skeleton diagram listed `integration_targets()` as a spawn inside the `rayon::scope`.** It can't run there: `Repository::integration_targets` takes the `RefSnapshot`, so it runs after the scope joins ([`collect/mod.rs`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/d65adb038c74ec0ed749d81622638f06af2708f0/src/commands/list/collect/mod.rs#L1648-L1659)). The diagram also left out the spawn that does run there: the snapshot capture, with `prime_upstream_ahead_behind_cache` nested inside it. The diagram now shows both, and places `integration_targets` after the join.
- **The "stale default branch warning" paragraph sat under Post-Skeleton Operations and called the check post-skeleton.** The warning is actually computed and emitted before `render_skeleton()`. The paragraph also said the check reuses the branch list "fetched for `--branches`". But `wt list` (`DeferredToParallel`) always fetches local branches, so an extra `for-each-ref` only happens on the picker's `Resolved` path with branches hidden. The paragraph now sits next to fork #5 in the critical-path section and says exactly that.
- **A comment named `collect_worktree_progressive` and `collect_branch_progressive` as the place where URL templates get expanded.** Neither function exists anymore. Expansion happens in `work_items_for_worktree` on the main thread, and branch-only rows have no URL, so the comment's "parallelizes the work" claim was dropped too.

These comments had no regression test to add. `cargo doc --document-private-items` builds cleanly, and the pre-commit hooks pass (fmt, clippy, typos).
author: worktrunk-bot

title: Fix background force-delete for flag-like branches
body:
## Summary

- Pass the branch name after `--` in the detached background force-delete fallback.
- Add an end-to-end regression test for a plumbing-created `-x` branch when the staged rename fails.

## Root cause

The rename-failure fallback generated `git branch -D <branch>`. Git interpreted a valid flag-like ref as an option, so the worktree disappeared but the branch remained.

## Tests

- Confirmed the new regression test timed out on the old command while waiting for `refs/heads/-x` to be deleted.
- Confirmed the regression test and all four background fallback integration tests pass after the fix.
- `cargo test test_build_remove_command`
- `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes` (4964 passed, 1 skipped)
author: Duang777

title: Prevent removal of submodule changes hidden by config
body:
## Summary

- make worktree clean checks override `submodule.<name>.ignore`
- preserve initialized submodule changes during ordinary `wt remove`
- add an end-to-end regression test for `ignore=all`

## Root cause

`WorkingTree::is_dirty` and `dirty_files` inherited the user's submodule ignore setting. With `submodule.<name>.ignore=all`, Git reported a modified initialized submodule as clean. Worktrunk then used the internally required `git worktree remove --force`, deleting the worktree and its uncommitted submodule change.

The clean checks now pass `--ignore-submodules=none`, matching the existing plumbing diff behavior and keeping display preferences out of destructive safety decisions.

## Verification

- Red: the new test reproduced successful removal and loss of the modified worktree on the old code
- Green: targeted regression and related tests passed
- `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes`
  - 4,963 tests passed
  - 1 skipped
  - fmt, Clippy, doctests, rustdoc, lockfile, and snapshot checks passed
author: Duang777

title: fix(merge): respect stage scope before auto-commit
body:
## Summary

- decide whether merge auto-commit can produce a staged diff using the selected `--stage` mode
- evaluate `all` and `tracked` in a temporary index without modifying the user index
- freeze that decision before hook approval and skip redundant staging simulations for squash

## Problem

When a source worktree had existing feature commits plus only untracked files, `wt merge --stage=none|tracked --no-squash` treated the worktree as committable, attempted an empty commit, and failed with `Nothing to commit` before merging the existing commits. The same status-vs-staging mismatch could occur for dirty submodule contents under `--stage=all`.

## Test plan

- `cargo test --lib has_committable_changes`
- `cargo test --test integration test_merge_ignores_untracked_only_changes_outside_stage_scope`
- `cargo test --test integration integration_tests::merge::test_merge_auto_commit`
- `cargo test --test integration integration_tests::merge::test_merge_pre_commit`
- `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes` (4,966 passed, 1 skipped)
author: Duang777

title: fix(config): expand a bare tilde in CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
body:
A literal `~` (rather than `~/...`) in `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` was not expanded: `str::strip_prefix("~/")` misses a bare `~`, so the value fell through to `PathBuf::from("~")` and `install-statusline` wrote a directory literally named `~` under the cwd.

The tilde is now expanded through the same `home_dir()` the `~/.claude` fallback two lines below already uses, which is the rule that honors an explicit `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`. That keeps `claude_config_dir` on one home rule instead of two, and an unresolvable home stays a refusal — `home_dir()` returns `None`, so `require_settings_path` bails instead of joining onto a relative `~` path. (Routing the fallback through `worktrunk::path::home_dir` would settle the split in the other direction, but it would leave this module's `home_dir()` with no callers, and `~` is expanded by the shell from `HOME`.)

Verified on Windows, temp home + scratch repo, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~`:
- upstream `main`: `HOME_SETTINGS=False CWD_TILDE_DIR=True CWD_TILDE_SETTINGS=True` — a `~` directory under the cwd
- this branch: `HOME_SETTINGS=True CWD_TILDE_DIR=False` — `settings.json` at `<home>/settings.json`
- `cargo test --test integration test_plugins_claude_install_statusline_expands_tilde_in_claude_config_dir` passes, so the `~/custom-claude` case is unchanged

On the third point: yes please, push the bare `~` case onto that test — it is the exact shape that would have caught this, and the missing `~` directory under the cwd makes the assertion explicit.

title: docs: share project instructions through AGENTS.md
body:
Make `AGENTS.md` the canonical project instructions in nine directories. Each directory also has a one-line `CLAUDE.md` importing its adjacent `AGENTS.md`, so Claude Code loads the instructions even on accounts where native `AGENTS.md` support is gated off. The root `AGENTS.md` replaces the old symlink; ordinary files work on Windows checkouts without symlink support. References in source comments, CI, Clawpatch metadata, maintainer skills, and the demo fixture point to the canonical paths.

I verified Claude Code's `@` import in a live isolated probe with tools disabled: a `CLAUDE.md` import loaded a marker found only in the imported file. The wrappers keep the existing Claude Code instruction-loading path while Codex reads `AGENTS.md` directly.

title: docs(test): drop the stale per-test inventory in diagnostic.rs
body:
The `# Test Coverage` block at the top of `tests/integration_tests/diagnostic.rs` listed 10 tests. The file has 26. Everything added since the list was written — the `RUST_LOG` and `WORKTRUNK_VERBOSE` level tests, the `subprocess.log` split-and-join tests, the control-byte escaping test from #2991 — went unlisted, so a reader taking the block as the file's scope saw under half of it.

Refreshing the list would restate 26 names that already carry their own per-test docstrings, and it would be stale again at the next test. title: chore: update tend workflows (0.2.15 → 0.3.1)
body:
Regenerates the nine `tend-*.yaml` workflows from tend 0.3.1, up from 0.2.15. Behavior here is unchanged: the only substantive diff is two new action inputs, `merge: maintainer` and `control_plane_owner: ""`, both of which are the action's own defaults. `maintainer` is the merge authority this repo already runs under — the bot proposes, a maintainer merges.

What the upgrade changes for this repo:

- **`tend check` audits protected refs and credential environments more strictly** ([max-sixty/tend#1382](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1382)). A protected branch must now restrict creation, update and deletion together rather than update alone, and the credential audit no longer treats a ref-qualified reusable workflow as this tree's copy. This repo does not clear the new bar yet — the nightly filed #4242 with the single ruleset gap and the remediation.
- **Yolo merge mode exists, and is off** ([max-sixty/tend#1172](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1172), [#1390](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1390)). The new inputs are how a repo would opt into letting the bot merge its own PRs; leaving them at the defaults keeps the current arrangement, and the `merge: maintainer` value is what the mitmproxy cache step is now gated on.
- **`review-runs` sees the whole night** ([max-sixty/tend#1377](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1377)). Run listing now pages to the Actions ceiling instead of stopping at the first page, so a busy night's early runs stop falling out of the census; [#1374](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1374) keeps each correction row's author alongside it.
- **CI polling is bounded by elapsed time, not iteration count** ([max-sixty/tend#1376](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1376), reinstating [#1371](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1371) after [#1375](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1375) reverted it). A settle loop against slow checks now stops on a sleep budget, so a long matrix can't quietly stretch a session.
- **Install-test drift detection tightened** ([max-sixty/tend#1381](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1381)): generator output a PR never committed now fails tend's own drift check, which is the check that makes a regeneration PR like this one trustworthy.

Full comparison: [0.2.15...0.3.1](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/compare/0.2.15...0.3.1).

This PR does not touch `.config/tend.yaml`, whose `sandbox_setup:` key 0.3.1 now warns "will be refused in a later release". That migration is a separate change.


#4240 overlaps this completely: it was generated with the same 0.3.1, so it carries the identical headers and the identical `merge: maintainer` / `control_plane_owner: ""` on the same lines, underneath a Claude → Codex harness swap. The only thing that distinguishes the two is which harness the action runs. Whichever lands first leaves the other conflicting on the eight `uses:` lines, resolved by regeneration rather than by hand. So this PR is worth landing on its own only

title: fix(plugin): make the Codex Windows hook commands parse in PowerShell
body:
Windows Codex hooks failed before updating activity markers because their cmd-specific command strings did not parse in PowerShell. The Windows commands now invoke the quoted wrapper through `cmd /d /c call`; the wrapper keeps marker failures best-effort by returning zero while preserving stderr diagnostics.

The invocation rationale lives in `hooks/wt.cmd`. Regression coverage runs the shipped commands through cmd, Windows PowerShell, and PowerShell 7 from a plugin path containing spaces, checking marker updates, Unicode arguments, and failures. This installed-shell coverage uses the existing `shell-integration-tests` feature, enabled in CI; the manifest guard runs on every platform. Shell discovery uses the existing `which` dependency.

The invocation retains a documented tradeoff: in a cmd session, the bare `cmd` name can resolve from the project directory. `/d` disables AutoRun only for the cmd hop this command creates.

The tests reproduce Codex's process invocation; an installed Windows Codex session has not been exercised.

Closes #4239. Thanks to [wstczyw](https://github.com/wstczyw) for the report and reproduction.

title: fix(git): resolve repo_path through the separate-git-dir backlink
body:
`repo_path()` resolved a non-bare repository to `parent(git_common_dir)`, which is the work tree only when the git directory sits inside it. With `git init --separate-git-dir` the git directory is a store elsewhere and that parent names the store's neighbourhood instead, so `{{ repo_path }}.{{ branch }}` placed every new worktree beside the store and `wt list` rendered the main worktree's path as the store. `repo_path()` now consults the `gitdir` backlink git keeps next to the common dir, so both surfaces name the work tree.

`wt remove` failed outright in this layout rather than misplacing anything — it runs git from the resolved repo path, and the store's parent is not a repository, so the command died on `fatal: not a git repository`. That is the same root cause and is fixed here too; the issue reports it as a second symptom.

The same wrong path reached `wt list` through the correction in `list_worktrees` that already existed for submodules: git's `get_main_worktree()` derives its main-worktree entry by stripping a trailing `/.git` from the common dir, and a separate git dir has no such suffix, so git reports the store there too. That correction defers to `repo_path()`, so this one change fixes both.

The backlink is the same file format as a linked worktree's `.git/worktrees/<name>/gitdir`, including the relative form git writes under `worktree.useRelativePaths` and resolves against the directory the file sits in. So it is read through the existing `registration_worktree_path`, which already implements that rule, rather than through a second parse — a re-derived rule here would be correct on the absolute form and silently wrong for anyone with that setting on.

The backlink is one-way, so it is confirmed rather than trusted: the work tree it names must point back at this common dir, via the existing `git_dir_at` helper. A backlink left by a work tree that has since moved or been replaced falls through to the old `parent(git_common_dir)` answer rather than to a path that no longer holds the repository.

**What this leaves.** Only `git worktree repair` writes the backlink — `git init --separate-git-dir` and `git clone --separate-git-dir` leave the store without one, and a repository that has never been repaired still records its work tree nowhere for `wt` to find. Running `git worktree repair` from the work tree is now an effective remedy where before it changed nothing, but a freshly created repository of this shape still resolves to the store's parent until it is run. Closing that gap needs a decision this PR doesn't take: the work tree is derivable from `wt`'s own discovery path, but only when `wt` runs in the main work tree, so using it would make `{{ repo_path }}` depend on where the command was invoked. The alternatives — having `wt` write the backlink itself, or caching the work tree in git config the way `worktrunk.default-branch` is — both put a write on a read path.

title: test(picker): steer cursor waits within the item area
body:
The picker PTY wait could overshoot `wt-drop` onto a streamed PR row and keep sending Down until it timed out ([Windows failure](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/35705096628)). Re-issued arrows now move toward the target visible in the current frame, recovering from both async cursor resets and overshoots.

Cursor readiness and steering share the same item-area reader. The fixed test terminal uses the production reverse layout: query, one header row, then items. Reading that area excludes query/header matches and accepts blank loading gutters without classifying gutter glyphs. Preview text remains outside the match area. Existing removal guards use the same reader, and filtered tests wait for selection to reach a matching item before reading row order.

Regression coverage includes the recorded overshoot, header exclusion, missing rows, typed queries with blank gutters, and a real PTY test that deliberately overshoots a filtered row and steers back. All 37 picker-related tests pass locally. The full pre-merge hook passes on the final revision: 4,957 tests passed, one skipped, plus formatting, Clippy, documentation, and doctests. This changes only test helpers and their regression coverage.

title: fix(remove): plan no branch deletion for an orphan worktree's unborn branch
body:
An orphan worktree (`git worktree add --orphan`) has an unborn branch until its first commit: `HEAD` names `refs/heads/<branch>`, but no such ref exists. `wt remove` planned a branch deletion for it anyway, so it misreported the branch or failed:

- A live orphan worktree: `wt remove fresh` printed `↳ Branch unmerged; to delete, run wt remove -D fresh`, a command that then fails with `No branch named fresh`. With `--foreground` it removed the worktree and then exited 1 with git's `fatal: Needed a single revision`.
- A stale one (directory or `.git` gone): `wt remove fresh` printed `✓ Pruned stale worktree for fresh` followed by `○ Branch fresh retained; has unmerged changes` and the same `wt remove -D` hint.

Now the removal planner treats an unborn branch as having nothing to delete and plans `Keep` for it, the way it already handles a branch that a sibling checkout still uses. The output is just `✓ Removed fresh worktree` (or `◎ Removing fresh worktree in background`) or `✓ Pruned stale worktree for fresh`. The planner reads this from the ref snapshot it already holds, so it adds no git call. The picker's removal goes through the same planner.

`test_remove_orphan_worktree` removes a live and a stale orphan worktree, each with a remote-tracking branch of the same name. The remote branch catches a check that counts remote branches, which would take the branch for existing.

title: docs(shell): correct who reads is_shell_integration_line
body:
The `# Usage` block on `is_shell_integration_line` lists uninstall as a caller. Uninstall has not read it since `is_shell_integration_line_for_uninstall_any_cmd` was introduced — `scan_rc_file_for_uninstall` and `is_worktrunk_managed_content` both call that one instead. The two docstrings now both claim the destructive path: the sibling's says "Used by `wt config shell uninstall`, which deletes the lines it matches. That makes a false positive destructive", which is the reasoning that should govern one function and not the other.

The list also omits the caller that matters most for how carefully this function has to behave. `contains_shell_integration`, install's idempotency check, is gated on `is_shell_integration_line` at both call sites (`configure_shell.rs`, in the exists-check before the append and again in `append_shell_integration_if_missing`). So the closing claim — "false negatives only cause incorrect messaging" — is wrong for install: a miss there reads an already-configured rc file as unconfigured and appends a second copy of the line to a user-owned file. Uninstall removes every line it matches, so the duplicate isn't stranded, but a write is a different cost from a wrong hint, and the docstring is what a later change to this function would be read against.

The `# Impact of False Negatives` section had a second inaccuracy of the same kind: it claimed detection is consulted only while shell integration is inactive, and that no warnings are shown once the wrapper is active. That holds for `Shell::is_shell_configured()`'s consumers in `src/output/shell_integration.rs`, which only ask off the not-active path, but not for `wt config show` — it calls `scan_for_detection_details` unconditionally and reports an unmatched line as a possible false negative regardless of `shell_active`. The exemption is now scoped to `is_shell_configured()`, with `wt config show` described on its own.

So the rewrite lists the three real callers, says explicitly that uninstall is not one, and splits the false-negative analysis three ways: the gated messaging cases, `wt config show`'s ungated warning, and install's write.

Comments only; no behavior changes, so there is nothing to regress-test. `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-Dwarnings' cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items` (the repo's `doc` pre-merge step) passes, which is what checks the new intra-doc link.

title: chore: update tend workflows (0.2.14 → 0.2.15)
body:
Regenerates the nine `tend-*.yaml` workflows with tend 0.2.15 (from 0.2.14). The version bump and the `astral-sh/setup-uv` pin (v10.1.0 → v10.2.0, in the `tend-mention` and `tend-notifications` preflight jobs) are mechanical; one step actually moves, in `tend-mention.yaml`.

**`tend-mention` measures its queue delay before checkout and setup.** The "Compute queue delay" step used to run after `actions/checkout` and `./.github/actions/tend-setup`, so the number it recorded was the wait for the job to start *plus* the several minutes this repo's setup action takes to install the Rust toolchain and sandbox tools. It now runs first, and the delay reports the queue wait alone ([max-sixty/tend#1365](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1365)).

Behavior that arrives inside the action rather than in these files, and that shows up in what the bot posts here:

- **PR reviews lead with a finding.** A review body now opens with something actionable instead of restating the verdict GitHub already renders in its own header ([max-sixty/tend#1362](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1362)), and a follow-up review scopes itself to what the latest push changed while still reading the whole PR ([max-sixty/tend#1368](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1368)).
- **Fewer self-directed fix rounds on bot PRs.** On a PR with no human author the review session applies its own findings; each further round now has to clear a higher bar, so a bot PR stops accumulating marginal follow-up commits ([max-sixty/tend#1366](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1366)).
- **`AGENTS.override.md` joins the pinned instruction paths.** Codex reads it in preference to `AGENTS.md`, so on a PR-derived checkout it is now restored from the base commit alongside `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/`, and `.agents/` — a fork can no longer reach the session through that filename. The same release makes a restrict-updates ruleset a `tend check` requirement; this repo already satisfies it (`tend check` passes every line today) ([max-sixty/tend#1367](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1367)).

Full comparison: [0.2.14...0.2.15](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/compare/0.2.14...0.2.15).

title: fix(prune): unregister stale worktrees whose directory remains
body:
Git calls a worktree entry prunable once the `.git` its registration names is gone. That happens when the whole directory is deleted, and also when only the `.git` file goes: macOS's `$TMPDIR` sweep deletes idle files and keeps directories, which left two such checkouts registered in a real repo. Worktrunk unregistered stale entries with `git worktree remove`, which refuses an entry whose directory remains (`validation failed … .git does not exist`, `--force --force` included). #4226 stopped that from failing `wt step prune` by skipping the entry, so it stayed `⊟` forever, and `wt remove` refused it with `WorktreeMissing`.

`Repository::prune_worktree_entry` now reproduces `git worktree prune` for the one named entry. Under the registry write lock it finds the registration whose `gitdir` names the path, repeats git's `should_prune_worktree` test (no `locked` file, nothing at the recorded `.git`), and deletes `.git/worktrees/<id>`, which is git's `delete_git_dir`. The directory and any files in it stay. The test runs at deletion time, so an entry locked or reconnected since the scan is refused rather than unregistered.

No git command does this for one entry: `git worktree prune` takes no path, `remove` and `move` fail validation, and `repair` relinks rather than unregisters. A repo-wide `git worktree prune` also unregisters entries `wt step prune` deliberately keeps: branches with unmerged commits, detached HEADs holding the only reference to their commits (which `git gc` can then delete), the default branch's worktree, and unborn orphans. The rationale sits in the `prune_worktree_entry` docstring.

What changes for users:

- `wt step prune` and `wt remove <branch>` unregister a stale entry whether its directory is gone or only its `.git` is. `wt remove feature` on a recreated directory used to fail with `✗ Worktree directory missing for feature`. It now prints `✓ Pruned stale worktree & removed branch feature (same commit as main, _)` and leaves the directory in place.
- The picker's branch-only removal now unregisters the stale entry before deleting the branch. Before, it deleted only the branch, leaving an entry that named a deleted branch, which `wt step prune` skips as unborn.
- A worktree path that became a regular file counts as having no `.git`, matching git, instead of refusing.
- Messages no longer call every stale entry "directory missing". The switch/merge/push error reads `Worktree for X is stale; its directory or .git is gone`, the `⊟` legend reads `Prunable (worktree directory or its .git gone)`, and the retained-branch line reads `Pruned stale worktree for X`. Where the directory remains, that error's hint offers `git worktree repair <path>` instead of `git worktree prune`, which would sweep every stale entry in the repo.

Unregistering deletes the entry's index, per-worktree reflog and any in-progress rebase, merge, cherry-pick, revert or bisect state. While the entry exists, `git worktree repair <path>` restores all of it (recre

title: fix(prune): leave a stale detached entry whose directory remains
body:
Git calls a worktree entry prunable when the `.git` file its registration points at is gone, which also happens when only that file went and the directory stayed. A detached checkout under macOS's `$TMPDIR` turned up this way, with its idle files deleted and its directories kept. `wt step prune` selected such an entry and unregistered it with `git worktree remove`, which skips its validation only while the directory is absent:

```
✗ pruning stale worktree for (detached 59b73365)
  fatal: validation failed, cannot remove working tree: '…/checkout/.git' does not exist
```

The failure aborted every removal still queued and failed the run, so each later prune in that repo failed the same way.

The scan now selects a detached stale entry only when its directory is gone, the precondition `prune_worktree_entry` already documents. An entry whose directory remains stays registered, as its branch-bearing twin already does: `prepare_worktree_removal` refuses that one with `WorktreeMissing` (#3785).

Since #3785, no `Prunable` entry can plan the worktree removal that runs `pre-remove`/`post-remove`, so the pessimistic hook plan stops registering them, and the two comments that said a stale entry with a surviving directory plans a full removal are corrected. Live worktrees are registered as before.

`test_prune_keeps_stale_detached_entry_whose_directory_remains` deletes a detached worktree's `.git` file, then checks that prune succeeds, removes an integrated sibling, and leaves the entry and its directory in place. With the fix reverted, it fails with the error above.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max-sixty_

title: docs(ci): correct the tend sandbox model for 0.2.14's copy-on-write view
body:
tend 0.2.14 (landed today in #4222) moved the agent off Anthropic Sandbox Runtime and onto a hardened systemd unit over a copy-on-write view of the job's own checkout and home. Four files here still describe the 0.2.5–0.2.13 arrangement they were written for, and their central claims are now observably false from inside a session. That matters because `.github/CLAUDE.md` and `running-tend` are what an agent reads before touching CI: told the runner's home is unreadable, it keeps building hand-offs nothing needs and rules out a cache that would now work. Comments and instructions only — no step, key, or behavior changes.

## What stopped being true

Probed from tend 0.2.14 sessions:

| Documented claim | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| Agent PATH rewrites a leading `/home/runner` to `/home/tend-sandbox` | `$HOME` is `/home/runner`, and PATH entries resolve there |
| The agent builds in a disposable `/tmp` clone | cwd is `/home/runner/work/worktrunk/worktrunk`, the runner's own checkout |
| Sandbox Runtime denies reads across the runner's home and checkout | `~/.cargo`, `~/.rustup/toolchains` and `~/.cargo-install` all read fine |
| The cargo tools reach the agent through `/usr/local/bin` | `which -a cargo-insta` lists `/home/runner/.cargo-install/cargo-insta/bin/cargo-insta` first, `/usr/local/bin` second |
| `.config/tend.yaml`'s probe runs inside the sandbox, and a missing tool files a tend-outage issue | 0.2.14's generator emits the block as an ordinary runner step *before* `max-sixty/tend/claude`, and the filing is `report_failure.py`, a step *inside* that action under `if: failure()` — so a probe failure skips it and leaves only its `::error::` annotation |
| `running-tend`: the weekly `nix` commands fail with a permission error | `nix store info` reports `cannot create Unix domain socket: Address family not supported by protocol` |
| `running-tend`: `-home-runner-work-worktrunk-worktrunk/` "appears only in runs predating the bump" | This session's logs are under `/home/tend-sandbox/.claude/projects/-home-runner-work-worktrunk-worktrunk/` — the prefix is back |

Only the errno was wrong, in two places — `.github/actions/tend-setup/action.yaml` said `EPERM` and `running-tend` said "a permission error"; both now carry the message the probe actually prints.

- **`sandbox_setup:` stays.** #4222 gave the reason: keeping the key means a release reverting 0.2.14 still finds it. The comment above the block now says so, so a later sweep reads it as a deliberate hold rather than drift to fix. Its closing probe is still worth its place — it asserts the five tools the pre-merge gate needs, whichever step installed them, and fails the job naming the one that went missing.

title: skills(worktrunk): drop --no-hooks from the sub-Agent example
body:
The "Parallel sub-Agents" example runs `wt switch --create <branch> --no-cd --no-hooks`. On a machine with a `pre-start` hook in **user** config — mine symlinks the primary worktree's Python venv, which is gitignored and so never arrives with the checkout — that flag skips the provisioning, and the sub-Agent gets a worktree with no interpreter. Every command it runs fails, and nothing in the worktree says why.

The prose is already conditional, but the example is what an agent copies: it reads the command block, not the paragraph three blocks down. So the example now omits `--no-hooks`, and the sentence states when to add it — only when no user or project hooks provision the worktree and each sub-Agent does its own setup.

Docs only; the flag's behaviour is unchanged.

title: skills(running-tend): drop the sandbox path facts tend 0.2.13 changed
body:
`main` now pins `max-sixty/tend/claude@0.2.13` (#4215, merged as `c5e17139a`), and two sandbox facts this overlay asserts stopped being true of the sandbox sessions actually run in.

**Root `/tmp` is writable.** [max-sixty/tend#1324](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/1324) ("Make /tmp writable inside the sandbox") merged 2026-09-19, after 0.2.11 and before 0.2.12. In the `0.2.11...0.2.13` diff the sandbox's own SRT test flips its probe: `touch /tmp/tend-unscoped` must fail at 0.2.11, while at 0.2.13 `touch /tmp/tend-sandbox-scratch` must succeed and `/var/tmp` is the refused one. Tend dropped the matching paragraph from its bundled `run-tend` skill in the same range, along with the `TMPPREFIX` override whose comment said it existed only because zsh's here-document default "sits in the read-only root /tmp".

**The agent workspace container moved to `/var/tmp`.** `prepare_agent_workspace.py` at 0.2.13 calls `mkdtemp(prefix="tend-agent-workspace-", dir="/var/tmp")`, so the slugified session-log directory is `-var-tmp-…`, not `-tmp-…`.

Neither edit changes what a session should do. `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}` is still where scratch files belong, and the log-path section's conclusion — there is no literal to match on, so use `find "$DEST" -name '*.jsonl'` — is if anything better supported by a container that moves between releases. What goes is the justification attached to each, which is the part that could go stale and did.

The old text was accurate right up to the merge: a write probe in this run, still on 0.2.11, is refused with `Read-only file system`. It is wrong from the next session on, which is why this is a deletion rather than a rewrite — the overlay is better off not restating a boundary tend owns and moves.

<details><summary>Where this was found</summary>

The `tend-review` session on #4215 ([run 35570800500](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/35570800500)) noticed the overlay would go stale on merge and deliberately left it alone, on the grounds that `.claude/**` is restored from the base branch during a review session and a separate PR is the cleaner home. This is that PR, opened from the `tend-review-runs` sweep that can edit `.claude/skills/` from a `$TMPDIR` worktree.

</details>

title: perf(list): resolve the GitLab project ID once per command
body:
`wt list --full` on a GitLab remote spends one `glab repo view` API call **per row** resolving a value that is the same for every row. `gitlab_project_id` is called from `detect_gitlab`, which runs once per branch, and the project ID it fetches is a repo-level constant used only to filter MRs by source project. This memoizes it for the process.

`wt list` renders progressively but cannot *finish* until every row's task returns, so each of those round trips extends the command the user is waiting on — the case CLAUDE.md's **Network Access** section calls out for run-to-completion commands. It also spends N times the GitLab API quota for one answer.

The cache is a `LazyLock<DashMap<PathBuf, Option<u64>>>` keyed by the worktree root, matching the path-keyed process-wide caches in `git::repository` rather than a bare static — tests run many commands in one process, and a bare static would let one repo's answer leak into another's. The `entry` API holds the shard lock across the fetch, so concurrent rows sharing the key wait on the first call instead of each spawning their own; a failed lookup caches as `None`, since retrying it per row is exactly the cost being removed.

The regression test asserts the spawn count through `mock_calls` rather than the rendering, because the table looks identical either way. On this branch's parent it fails with 5 `glab repo view` calls against an expected 1.

A drive-by in the same doc comment: it described `gitlab_project_id` as "the GitLab equivalent of `get_origin_owner` for GitHub", and `get_origin_owner` no longer exists — the GitHub side now resolves its owner through `branch_owner_repo`, from local git config with no network call at all.

Verified locally: `cargo test --test integration ci_status` (63 passed), `cargo test --bins ci_status` (42 passed), `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features`, `cargo fmt --check`.

title: chore: update tend workflows (0.2.11 → 0.2.13)
body:
Regenerates the `tend-*` workflows with tend 0.2.13 (from 0.2.11). Mechanically the diff is the action pin `max-sixty/tend/claude@0.2.11` → `@0.2.13` in the eight workflows that run the agent, the `astral-sh/setup-uv` pin `0.12.13` → `0.12.17` in the two that install uv directly (`tend-mention`, `tend-notifications`), and a regenerated header comment in all nine.

The upgrade that matters for this repo is in CI polling. `poll_pr_checks.py` previously treated any gating check that settled without a red conclusion as green — so a required check belonging to a **cancelled** or **stale** run, or a `COMPLETED` check carrying no conclusion at all, let the bot report a PR as green when nothing had actually verified it. 0.2.13 splits those out as `unverified` and gives `poll` a distinct exit code for them (max-sixty/tend#1323). Practically: fewer "checks went green" claims on PRs whose required jobs were cancelled, at the cost of some polls ending unverified rather than green.

The rest, in rough order of how visible it is here:

- **Sandbox reliability** — the sandbox runtime now retries past a transient bridge-socket failure at launch (max-sixty/tend#1327). That failure is one of the shapes that produces a `tend-outage` issue, so it should show up as fewer of those.
- **Sandbox environment** — root `/tmp` is writable inside the sandbox (max-sixty/tend#1324); the `run-tend` skill's note that it was read-only is gone. This repo's `running-tend` skill still restates that note, so it goes stale when this merges — I'll follow up separately rather than mix a skill edit into the generated-workflow diff.
- **Instruction-path pinning** — the `run-tend` skill's description of which paths get restored from the PR base, and on which events, was wrong in 0.2.11; `.agents/` is now named alongside `.claude/`, and the event list is corrected (max-sixty/tend#1311). The restore behavior itself is unchanged.
- **Auth hygiene** — the bot's claude.ai account is kept out of CI sessions (max-sixty/tend#1328).
- **Harness pins** — claude-code 2.1.278 (max-sixty/tend#1330), uv 0.12.17 (max-sixty/tend#1331).

`.config/tend.yaml` pins no model, so the harness-default check found nothing to adjust.

Full comparison: https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/compare/0.2.11...0.2.13

<details><summary>Copy-on-write sandbox view: landed and reverted within this range</summary>

max-sixty/tend#1333 and max-sixty/tend#1334 moved the agent into the job's own checkout and home through a copy-on-write view; max-sixty/tend#1339 reverted both before 0.2.13. Nothing from that work is in this diff — noted so a later reader doesn't chase it out of the commit list.

</details>

title: docs: mention copy-on-write build caches in the lede
body:
The lede named hooks as its one example of the quality-of-life features. Cold, heavy checkouts are the other standard objection to worktrees, so it now also names the feature that answers it: `wt step copy-ignored` reflinking build caches into new worktrees.

The edit is in `docs/src/content/docs/worktrunk.md` and the hand-written README lede; the skill mirrors and `llms.txt` are regenerated by the docs sync test.

title: test(prompt): read the prompt the LLM receives, not --show-prompt's stdout
body:
`test_show_prompt_ignores_diff_display_config` was meant to pin that the LLM prompt ignores `color.ui`, `diff.external`, and `diff.noprefix`. It compared `--show-prompt` stdout, which `.output()` pipes, so anstream stripped ANSI and the `color.ui = always` case passed whatever the diff code did.

Now `test_generation_prompt_ignores_diff_display_config`, it points `commit.generation.command` at a script that saves its stdin, and compares the bytes the LLM command actually receives for `wt step commit --dry-run` and `wt step squash --dry-run`. It asserts no escape byte directly and checks the prompt matches the default-config prompt byte for byte. The branch-summary prompt had no such test; `picker/summary.rs` gets the same check. With `PreparedDiff::capture` reverted to porcelain, both tests fail on the escape-byte assertion.

An earlier version of this PR also moved `has_staged_changes` onto plumbing; #4192 makes that change with more coverage, so it's dropped here.

title: fix(squash): commit on a detached HEAD so a failed squash keeps the branch
body:
`wt step squash` and `wt merge`'s squash step ran `git reset --soft <merge-base>` and then `git commit`. When the commit failed — a `pre-commit` hook rejecting it, a broken signing setup — the branch was left rewound to the merge base with its commits collapsed into anonymous staged changes, on a path that reported failure. #4193 found it.

The squash now rewrites history the way `git rebase` does. It detaches HEAD onto the merge base with `update-ref --no-deref`, which leaves the branch, the index and the working tree untouched; commits there; then moves the branch to the new commit with one compare-and-swap `update-ref` and puts HEAD back on it. The branch keeps its commits until the commit exists, so a rejected or failed commit leaves it exactly as it was, and the reattach restores HEAD.

Committing through `git commit` rather than plumbing is what keeps git's own hooks, `commit.cleanup`, signing and identity resolution behaving as they do for any other commit. Those hooks see a detached HEAD, as they do under `git rebase` — verified on git 2.55, where a real `rebase -i` squash runs `prepare-commit-msg` and `post-commit` with no current branch and skips `pre-commit` and `commit-msg` entirely. The `wt step squash` help says so.

Two smaller changes ride along:

- The no-net-changes check compares the index tree against the merge base's tree instead of asking `git diff --cached`, which is porcelain and reads `submodule.<name>.ignore`. A squash whose only change is a submodule pointer hidden by that setting is now committed rather than reported as empty. That path still leaves the branch at the merge base, so `wt merge` goes on treating a branch whose commits cancel out as already integrated.
- `signs_commits` asks git from the current worktree instead of reading the cached config map, which is read from the common dir and so missed worktree-scoped config, and which read a valueless `gpgsign` as false where git reads it as true. `wt merge --no-ff` builds its merge commit with `commit-tree` and asks this helper whether to sign it.

`test_step_squash_failed_commit_leaves_branch_intact` covers the path end to end: a `.git/hooks/pre-commit` that exits 1 fails the squash and leaves the branch, HEAD and the history untouched; without the hook the same squash lands. It fails against the old code on the branch-tip assertion, and against a plumbing-based squash on the hook assertion. Two more hooks drive the failure paths the new sequence adds: one moves the branch mid-squash, so the compare-and-swap refuses rather than clobbering the other write, and one seals the worktree's git directory before rejecting the commit, so the reattach fails and has to say how to put HEAD back. The ORIG_HEAD write is best-effort, as `git reset` makes it — the branch has already moved by then, so failing there would report a squash that landed as an error.

title: changelog: correct the 0.79.0 entries before the tag
body:
Verification passes against the v0.78.0 binary found five inaccuracies in the 0.79.0 changelog. The tag publishes this text as the GitHub release body, so each is corrected here rather than after the fact.

- **The `--output` entry described behavior 0.78.0 already had.** Replacing an existing destination is not new; what #4204 changed is that `--output` pointed at the config being migrated is no longer refused. The entry now claims only that, and moves out of the shared bullet with #4153.
- **`wt step prune` shares the integration-check defect**, not just `wt remove` — both reach it through the same check, so both are named.
- **Any earlier command could poison the `has-added-changes` cache**, not only the removal itself, so the condition reads "a Worktrunk command run from a subdirectory" rather than "the command".
- **Only `submodule.<name>.ignore = all` triggers it.** `untracked` and `dirty` leave a submodule pointer bump visible, so the value is named.
- **The headline "no longer changes what Worktrunk reads" overstated completeness** — `git status` has no plumbing equivalent. Scoped to the prompts and the integration check, which is what this release fixes.

Two further changes: "entirely" is restored to the `diff.relative` condition, where a repro confirmed it load-bearing (a branch also touching a file inside the subdirectory is retained), and `wt config create`'s dangling-symlink fix from #4204 gets the entry it was missing.

Entry order within Fixed follows reader interest; no code changes.
