title: shell_exec: preflight direct spawn failures
body:
Rust's Command API normally reports execve and current_dir setup failures synchronously when spawn/output fails. Under qemu-user, glibc's `posix_spawn` path can use `CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK` and expect the child to write those errors back to the parent, but qemu-user does not preserve that shared-stack error channel. The parent can then observe a successful spawn and only see the child exit with status 127.

This fixes the riscv64 qemu-user failures in shell_exec::tests::test_cmd_stream_spawn_failure_is_errored and git::repository::tests::repo_path_error_when_is_bare_fails, both of which expect missing executable or invalid current_dir failures to surface as spawn errors instead of ordinary child exit status 127.

This is a portability issue in the child-side exec failure reporting path, not just a qemu-user quirk. Not all posix_spawn() implementations use errno to report execv() failures from the child process, such as qemu-user, OpenBSD and HPPA.

Check the pieces that worktrunk already knows before spawning: explicit current_dir values must name directories, and direct commands with absolute program paths must already name executable files. stream() keeps the existing 'Failed to execute command' wrapping and trace behavior, while run() and pipe_into() continue to return io::Error directly.

Add regression tests for direct run() failures and update the existing stream() test to describe the externally visible behavior instead of depending on cmd.spawn() being the failing call.

Ref:
https://gitlab.com/qemu-project/qemu/-/work_items/140
https://lists.nongnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2025-03/msg04706.html
author: Xeonacid

title: git: avoid racy temp-index stats for untracked files
body:
`working_tree_diff_stats_with_untracked()` used a copied index to make untracked files visible to git diff: first `git add --intent-to-add .`, then `git diff --shortstat HEAD` against that temporary index. That means the copied index also has to rediscover tracked working-tree modifications.

On a slow riscv64 machine, the test passes by itself and the full lib test suite passes with `--test-threads=1`, but the default concurrent lib test run reliably exposes a failure. Diagnostic output from the failing test showed tracked.txt already contained the new contents, while git status and git diff through the temporary index reported only untracked.txt. The tracked rewrite was same-size, so the copied index could treat it as racily clean under this slow riscv64 machine.

Do not use the temporary index to rediscover tracked changes. Keep the existing `git diff --shortstat HEAD` path for tracked, staged, and unstaged changes, then list untracked files with `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z`, stage only those paths into the temporary index, and sum their cached numstat output. The real index remains untouched, while the racy-index window is avoided.

title: test(help): route all help snapshots through one settings builder
body:
## Consolidate help-snapshot insta settings

Follow-up to #3006, which fixed one instance of this in `test_help_list_narrow_terminal`.

### The bug

Insta's `info:` / `env:` block is metadata — written to the `.snap` file but **not** part of insta's pass/fail comparison (only `stdout`/`stderr`/`exit` are compared). Several help tests in `tests/integration_tests/help.rs` constructed their own `insta::Settings` inline and skipped `add_standard_env_redactions`, so host-specific env baked into their committed snapshots and passed forever on the machine that generated them. Three snapshots (`help_md_root`, `help_md_merge`, `nested_subcommand_hook_pre_start`) carried a developer's literal `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE` temp path (`/var/folders/…/wt-test-profraw/…`); it only diffs when the snapshot is regenerated elsewhere.

### The fix

One private `help_settings() -> Settings` builder (snapshot path + `add_standard_env_redactions`); every help/version/usage snapshot test now routes through it, so the redaction can't be forgotten. The seven affected snapshots are force-regenerated — env blocks now uniformly redacted, command-output bodies byte-identical.

This is latent-correctness hygiene: because the env block isn't part of the comparison, it never fails CI; the payoff is that the next regeneration on any machine won't reintroduce host churn.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max_

The module docstring is billed as the "Complete Spec" for shell-integration warning messages. Three of its "Git subcommand" Hint cells still quote the old hint text `Use git-wt directly (via shell function) for automatic cd`, but the function that actually renders that hint — [`git_subcommand_warning()`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/1160d33196e28833eb6c0f06585de9d062be84ee/src/output/shell_integration.rs#L128) — returns `For automatic cd, invoke directly (with the -): git-wt`. title: docs: alias template-expansion timing; fix narrow help-test env redaction
body:
## Docs: alias template-expansion timing

The main addition documents a gotcha that's easy to hit and hard to diagnose: an alias body renders its `{{ … }}` once at dispatch, in the invoking worktree, so a per-worktree variable like `{{ branch }}` is baked to a single value *before* a nested `wt step for-each` / `wt switch --execute` iterates — printing the same value in every worktree. The fix is `{% raw %}…{% endraw %}` deferral (plus a quoted `sh -c '…'` for `for-each`, since the deferred `{{ branch }}` contains spaces).

- `extending.md` — rewrote "Deferring expansion to a nested `wt` command" around the `for-each` symptom; improved the `up` rebase recipe.
- `faq.md`, `troubleshooting.md` — symptom-first entries with `wt config alias dry-run` as the diagnostic.
- `hook.md` / `config.md` / `step.md` — distinguish repo-level (constant) vs per-worktree (active) variables; note `{{ default_branch }}` needs no deferral; cross-link the `{{ default_branch }}` variable vs the `wt config state default-branch` shell command.

## Factual corrections

- `integration_reason` JSON values are hyphenated (`trees-match`, `no-added-changes`, `merge-adds-nothing`) — the docs had underscores. Verified against `src/commands/list/model/state.rs`.
- `SKILL.md`: 7 → 10 hook types (5 events × pre/post), added an aliases/multi-worktree task section, fixed stale anchor links.

## Test fix: narrow help-test env redaction

`test_help_list_narrow_terminal` built its own `insta::Settings` but skipped `add_standard_env_redactions` (every other help snapshot routes through `snapshot_help`, which calls it). Its snapshot env block therefore leaked host-specific paths (`LLVM_PROFILE_FILE` = the machine's temp dir, plus the `WORKTRUNK_*` paths), which churn whenever the snapshot is regenerated on a different machine. Adding the one call mirrors `snapshot_help` and makes the snapshot reproducible.

Worth noting (and a candidate follow-up): this gap was masked under `cargo test` (libtest) because the `repo` fixture's `mem::forget`'d `bind_to_scope()` guard leaks redaction settings across the shared process's reused threads. Under nextest (process-per-test, what the pre-merge hook uses) there's no leak, so a test missing its own redactions is exposed. A few other help tests (`test_help_md`, `test_version`, `test_nested_subcommand_suggestion`) have the same gap and could be consolidated through one settings helper — left out of this PR to keep it focused.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max_
author: max-sixty
diff: --- dev/config.example.toml (+2/-0) @@ -21,6 +21,8 @@ # - `{{ branch | sanitize_db }}` — database-safe: lowercase, underscores, hash suffix (e.g., `feature_auth_x7k`) # - `{{ branch | codename(2) }}` — deterministic friendly name from a ~1.26M-combo pool (e.g., `malleable-opah`) # +# This is a smaller set than the variables hooks and aliases get (https://worktrunk.dev/hook/#template-variables). +# # **Examples** for repo at `~/code/myproject`, branch `feature/auth`: # # Default — sibling directory (`~/code/myproject.feature-auth`): --- docs/content/config.md (+6/-0) @@ -83,6 +83,8 @@ Controls where new worktrees are created. - `{{ branch | sanitize_db }}` — database-safe: lowercase, underscores, hash suffix (e.g., `feature_auth_x7k`) - `{{ branch | codename(2) }}` — deterministic friendly name from a ~1.26M-combo pool (e.g., `malleable-opah`) +This is a smaller set than [the variables hooks and aliases get](@/hook.md#template-variables). + **Examples** for repo at `~/code/myproject`, branch `feature/auth`: Default — sibling directory (`~/code/myproject.feature-auth`): @@ -832,6 +834,8 @@ Useful in scripts to avoid hardcoding `main` or `master`: {{ terminal(cmd="git rebase $(wt config state default-branch)") }} +In a hook or alias template, prefer the `{{ default_branch }}` [template variable](@/hook.md#template-variables); `$(wt config state default-branch)` is for plain shell scripts. + Without a subcommand, runs `get`. Use `set` to override, or `clear` then `get` to re-detect. ### Detection @@ -851,6 +855,8 @@ The local inference fallback uses these heuristics in order: - Checks `git config init.defaultBranch` - Looks for common names: `main`, `master`, `develop`, `trunk` +If none of these match, detection fails; set it explicitly with `wt config state default-branch set BRANCH`. + ### Command reference {% terminal() %} --- docs/content/extending.md (+16/-4) @@ -119,29 +119,41 @@ Every step sees the same `{{ args }}` and bound variables. `wt release -- --dry- ### Deferring expansion to a nested `wt` command -Alias templates render once at dispatch, using the alias-invocation worktree's context. A nested `wt` command in the alias body (for example `wt switch --execute '…'`) therefore receives already-rendered text, so a variable like `{{ worktree_path }}` inside the inner command's template resolves to the *outer* worktree rather than the one `wt switch` is targeting. Wrap the inner template in `{% raw %}…{% endraw %}` so it passes through unrendered and the inner `wt` command expands it in its own context: +A `wt step for-each` alias that prints the same branch in every worktree is rendering `{{ branch }}` too early. An alias body renders once at dispatch, in the invoking worktree, so a bare `{{ branch }}` is baked to that worktree's branch before for-each iterates. (`wt config alias dry-run ` shows the rendered body, with the value already baked in.) + +`{% raw %}…{% endraw %}` defers the variable: it survives the dispatch render as a literal `{{ branch }}`, and for-each expands it per worktree. title: fix(help): render inline code in --help section headings
body:
Terminal `--help` applied heading styling to the raw header text without stripping inline-code markers, so a heading authored as `` ### `--stage` `` rendered with literal backticks. Header rendering now reduces inline `code` and links to plain text, letting the heading's single uniform style (color/weight) cover the whole line. A dim ANSI reset inside a colored heading would otherwise terminate the heading color partway through — visible on the `wt config state logs` heading `Command log (`commands.jsonl`)`, where the trailing `)` follows the code span. That heading is now fixed too.

Separately, renamed the `--stage` / `--dry-run` subsection headings in `wt step commit` and `wt step squash` to sentence case ("Staging", "Dry run"). They were the only flag-literal, inline-code headings in the entire help system; every other heading uses sentence-case topic wording, which the `writing-user-outputs` skill also prescribes. The flag name is still surfaced by the clap `Options:` block and each section's usage example.

The markdown source feeds three render contexts (terminal `--help`, web docs, skill mirrors); only the terminal path was wrong. Doc mirrors regenerated via `test_docs_are_in_sync`.

title: docs(faq): add entry on moving uncommitted changes to a new worktree
body:
Adds an FAQ entry for moving uncommitted changes from the current branch onto a new worktree: the `git stash -u` → `wt switch --create` → `git stash pop` relay, plus `--base=@` for branching off the current commit instead of the default branch. Placed next to the stacked-branches how-to.

The entry exists because the worktree model collides with `git switch -c` muscle memory — reaching for the in-place flow either retargets the main worktree or silently leaves the changes behind. The gap is discoverability, not capability (the two-line stash relay already covers it), so a doc fits better than a new flag.

title: refactor(config): store bare-repo prompt opt-out as a hint
body:
`worktrunk.skip-bare-repo-prompt` was stored as a top-level git-config key, which made it the only piece of persistent `worktrunk.*` state escaping the `state get`↔`state clear` parity invariant (documented at `src/commands/config/state.rs:6-31`). The `hints` subcommand globs the `worktrunk.hints.` prefix and the aggregate get/clear walk the same namespace, so a top-level key fell through both nets.

It's semantically a hint — a per-repo sticky "don't ask me this again" flag — so this stores it under `worktrunk.hints.skip-bare-repo-prompt` and reads/writes it via `has_shown_hint` / `mark_hint_shown`. It now lists under `wt config state hints` and clears with `wt config state clear`, with no new state category or docstring entry. The boolean opt-out maps onto the count-based hint API cleanly: `has_shown_hint` is `count >= 1`, and a single `mark_hint_shown` on decline sets the count to 1.

**Migration:** clean cutover, no migration. Existing users who already opted out get re-prompted once on their next `wt switch --create` in a dotted-name bare repo, after which the opt-out is recorded as a hint. Their orphaned legacy key is left in git config, unread. This is internal git-config state (flexible per project conventions), and the prompt only fires for bare repos with dotted names, so a single re-prompt is low-stakes.

**Testing:** the PTY decline test now asserts the hint key is written (and the legacy key is not), then round-trips the opt-out through `wt config state hints` → `wt config state clear`. Existing accept/preview/non-interactive prompt tests cover the unchanged paths.

title: fix(clobber): fall back to non-atomic backup rename on NFS/overlayfs/FUSE
body:
## Problem

`wt switch --clobber` (and `wt step relocate --clobber`) move a blocking directory aside via `back_up_clobbered_path`, which used `renamore::rename_exclusive` — an atomic no-overwrite rename with no fallback. On filesystems that don't implement `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` (NFS, overlayfs, FUSE, older kernels) the syscall returns `EINVAL`, which renamore maps to `ErrorKind::Unsupported`, so the command aborts with a bare `unsupported`. Source and destination are siblings in the same directory, so this is not `EXDEV`.

## Solution

Swap `renamore::rename_exclusive` for `renamore::rename_exclusive_fallback` in `src/commands/backup.rs`. The fallback variant degrades to a non-atomic `try_exists()` + `rename` when the atomic syscall is unsupported, and still returns `AlreadyExists` on a name collision — so the `-N` count-up loop is unaffected. The small race window the fallback reintroduces applies only on those filesystems, and is preferable to failing the command outright. Both clobber call sites (`worktree/switch.rs`, `relocate.rs`) route through this single helper, so the one swap covers both.

The module/function docstrings are updated to explain the `_fallback` choice.

## Testing

- `cargo test --bins backup` — all 8 existing `back_up_clobbered_path` tests pass, confirming the swap preserves observable behavior (fresh suffix, collision count-up, error-on-missing-source, timestamped suffix).
- `cargo clippy --bins` — clean.

The actual `Unsupported` failure requires a filesystem without `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)`; CI's tmpfs/ext4 supports atomic rename, so that specific failure path is not reproducible here. The root cause is verified against the [renamore 0.3.2 API](https://docs.rs/renamore/0.3.2/renamore/) — `rename_exclusive_fallback` returns `Result<bool>` (atomic vs. non-atomic) and still errors on collision, matching the behavior this helper relies on.

title: ci: install codecov CLI from PyPI to dodge broken Keybase GPG import
body:
## Problem

The non-required `code-coverage` job failed on `main` (run [27075953927](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/27075953927)). All tests passed (1942 / 1238 / 703, 0 failed); the failure was in the `codecov/codecov-action@v6.0.1` upload step:

```
==> Finishing downloading linux:latest
      Version: v11.2.8
gpg: no valid OpenPGP data found.
gpg: Total number processed: 0
==> Verifying GPG signature integrity
gpg: Signature made Tue Apr 21 19:28:03 2026 UTC
gpg:                using RSA key 27034E7FDB850E0BBC2C62FF806BB28AED779869
gpg: Can't check signature: No public key
==> Could not verify signature. Please contact Codecov if problem continues
    Exiting...
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

**Root cause (confirmed upstream).** The action downloads the Codecov CLI from `cli.codecov.io` and verifies its GPG signature against a public key fetched from `https://keybase.io/codecovsecurity/pgp_keys.asc`. That URL is currently returning `404 SELF-SIGNED PUBLIC KEY NOT FOUND`, so the key import produces "no valid OpenPGP data found", the keyring stays empty, and the signature check aborts with "No public key" — before any upload happens. Tracked in [codecov/codecov-action#1955](https://github.com/codecov/codecov-action/issues/1955) (opened the same day) and the related [#1876](https://github.com/codecov/codecov-action/issues/1876).

**Why a fix and not a rerun.** This exact failure shape fired three times in ~24h — [#2993](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/2993), [#2996](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/2996), and this run. #2996's diagnosis explicitly flagged that a third occurrence should escalate to a durable mitigation, crossing the `running-tend` repeat-occurrence threshold from transient to durable. `v6.0.1` is already the latest action release, so bumping the pin doesn't help.

## Solution

Set `use_pypi: true` on both `codecov-action` steps in `ci.yaml` (the test-results upload in the `test` matrix and the coverage upload in `code-coverage`). This is the workaround documented in #1955: it installs the Codecov CLI from PyPI instead of `cli.codecov.io`, bypassing the binary download and its broken Keybase GPG-key import entirely. Both call sites are subject to the same failure mode, so both are patched.

`use_pypi` is a documented input on `codecov-action@v6.0.1` (`action.yml` line 155: *"Use the pypi version of the CLI instead of from cli.codecov.io"*).

## Testing

YAML validated with `yaml.safe_load`. Behavioral verification is the `code-coverage` job passing on this PR — it exercises the patched upload path. The maintainer can revert `use_pypi: true` once Codecov restores the Keybase key (the `# (codecov/codecov-action#1955)` comments mark both sites).

title: feat(step): add --branch arg to wt step diff
body:
## Problem

`wt step diff` could only diff the current worktree. #2994 (part of the effort to extend `--branch` to more commands) asks for a `--branch` flag so the diff can target another worktree's branch without leaving the current one.

## Solution

Add `-b/--branch` to `wt step diff`, mirroring the existing flag on `wt step commit`. When provided, the repo is rooted at that branch's worktree (via `worktree_for_branch` + `Repository::at`) so both the diff and its target/merge-base resolution operate there. The branch must have a checked-out worktree; otherwise it errors with `no worktree for branch '<b>'`.

## Testing

Two integration tests in `tests/integration_tests/step_diff.rs`:

- `test_step_diff_branch_arg` — runs `wt step diff --branch feature` from the main worktree and asserts the output matches `test_step_diff_committed_changes` (the same diff run from inside the feature worktree).
- `test_step_diff_branch_no_worktree` — asserts the error path for a branch without a worktree.

Docs regenerated via `test_docs_are_in_sync`; `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. The only failing tests locally are the `case_4` nushell shell-wrapper tests, which fail because `nu` isn't installed in this sandbox — unrelated to this change.

title: fix(shell): install nushell wrapper to vendor-autoload dir (#2878)
body:
Fixes #2878.

Implements the approach agreed in the issue: query `$nu.vendor-autoload-dirs` directly and install to its last (user-writable) entry, with cross-platform tests and stranded-file cleanup on install/uninstall.

## The bug

The nushell integration wrote `wt.nu` to `$nu.default-config-dir/vendor/autoload`, which Nushell **never autoloads**. It happened to work on macOS/Windows because there `$nu.default-config-dir == $nu.data-dir`, so the wrong subpath resolved to the real vendor dir; on Linux the wrapper was written but silently never loaded — so `wt` was never wrapped.

Verified against `nu` 0.113.1: `$nu.vendor-autoload-dirs | last` is `<data-dir>/vendor/autoload`, and `$nu.default-config-dir/vendor/autoload` is in neither `$nu.vendor-autoload-dirs` nor `$nu.user-autoload-dirs`.

## The fix

- **Resolve the install target from `$nu.vendor-autoload-dirs | last`** (one memoised `nu` spawn that also reads `$nu.default-config-dir` for legacy cleanup).
- **Fallback when `nu` isn't on PATH** mirrors nushell's own `nu_path::data_dir`: `XDG_DATA_HOME` (when absolute) wins on every platform, otherwise `dirs::data_dir()` — matching nushell on Linux/macOS/Windows.
- **Wrapper-based shells now always write to the canonical location** (`paths.first()`), so a wrapper stranded at a legacy path can't become the write target. (No-op for fish, which has a single canonical path.)
- **Stranded-file cleanup**: install writes the correct path and removes any worktrunk-managed wrapper left under the legacy `<config-dir>/vendor/autoload` locations; uninstall already iterates every candidate, which now includes those legacy paths. Legacy files are only removed when they carry the `# worktrunk shell integration for nushell` header, so a user's own `wt.nu` is never touched.
- `config_line`, the `wt config shell init` manual-setup help, and the FAQ/shell-integration docs now use `$nu.vendor-autoload-dirs | last | path join wt.nu`.

## Tests

- New `WORKTRUNK_TEST_NU_VENDOR_AUTOLOAD_DIR` override pins the install dir so the install/uninstall/cleanup tests are **deterministic on Linux, macOS, and Windows** and don't depend on `nu` being installed.
- New `test_nushell_install_target_is_a_vendor_autoload_dir` (gated on `shell-integration-tests`, where CI has `nu`) runs the **real `nu` flow** and asserts the wrapper worktrunk wrote is a member of `$nu.vendor-autoload-dirs`. This fails against `main` (the old config-dir path is in neither autoload list) and passes with the fix.
- New `test_nushell_install_cleans_stranded_legacy` and a reworked `test_uninstall_nushell_cleans_all_candidate_locations` cover the migration cleanup.
- Existing nushell tests updated to the data-dir path; full suite green (`cargo test --lib` + `cargo test --test integration`, and the nushell subset with real `nu` under `--features shell-integration-tests`).

## Not in scope

"Not best practice" cleanup flagged in the issue (the overlap between the candidate-building helpers, and the dubious

title: fix(diagnostic): escape control bytes in subprocess preview so diagnostic.md uploads as a gist
body:
## Problem

The `-vv` diagnostic hint tells users to upload the report with `gh gist create --web <path>/diagnostic.md`, but the upload fails:

```
failed to collect files for posting: failed to upload .../diagnostic.md: binary file not supported
```

Root cause: `diagnostic.md` inlines `trace.log`, whose bounded subprocess previews keep raw **NUL bytes** verbatim. NUL-separated git output — `git config --list -z` and `git for-each-ref --format=…%00…`, both run early on every command — lands in the preview mid-line. `gh gist create` sniffs content type with the `mimetype` library (`shared.IsBinaryFile`); a NUL byte in the first ~3 KB makes it classify the file as binary and refuse the upload.

`format_stream_bounded` built each preview line via `String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes).lines()`. NUL is valid UTF-8 and isn't a line terminator, so it survived into `trace.log` → `diagnostic.md`.

## Solution

Escape C0/C1 control characters (other than tab) in the **bounded** preview before it's logged. NUL renders as the compact `\0`; the rest go through `escape_default` (e.g. `\u{1b}`). Tab is preserved — git output is full of legitimate tabs and it isn't a problem byte.

Scope is deliberately narrow: only the human-facing bounded preview (the copy that reaches `trace.log`, stderr, and `diagnostic.md`) is sanitized. The uncapped `subprocess.log` (`SUBPROCESS_FULL_TARGET`), which is contractually the raw byte stream, is untouched.

## Testing

- Added two unit tests in `shell_exec.rs`: NUL bytes are escaped to `\0` (and no raw NUL survives), and tabs are preserved.
- Verified end-to-end against `gh`'s own detection by cloning `cli/cli` and running `shared.IsBinaryFile`:
  - A NUL-bearing file → `IsBinaryFile=true` (the reported failure).
  - The regenerated `diagnostic.md` after this fix → `IsBinaryFile=false` (accepted).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` and `cargo fmt --check` clean. Full suite passes except 10 `shell_wrapper` `case_4` tests, which require the `nu` binary (not installed in this sandbox; CI provides it via `setup-nu`).

title: fix(git): clearer error when default branch has no commits
body:
## Problem

In a freshly `git init`'d repo whose default branch is unborn (no commits yet), commands that resolve the default branch — `wt step diff` in the report, also `merge`/`rebase`/`squash`/`push` — fail with a misleading error:

```
✗ Default branch main does not exist locally
↳ Reset the cached value with wt config state default-branch clear, or set it explicitly with wt config state default-branch set BRANCH
```

`main` *does* exist locally — it's the checked-out branch — it just has no commits. The cache-reset hint sends the user down the wrong path: the cached default branch is correct.

Root cause: `require_target_branch` / `require_target_ref` (in `src/git/repository/config.rs`) check whether the resolved branch ref exists. An unborn branch has no `refs/heads/<branch>` ref, so the check fails and the code returns `GitError::StaleDefaultBranch` — the same error used when the cache points at a genuinely deleted branch.

## Solution

Distinguish the two cases. A new `GitError::UnbornDefaultBranch` is returned when the resolved default branch is checked out as an unborn HEAD (detected via `git worktree list --porcelain` — the worktree carries the branch name with the null-OID HEAD). The message and hint are accurate for that state:

```
✗ Default branch main has no commits yet
↳ Make an initial commit on main first, or pass an explicit target.
```

The stale-cache path (branch genuinely deleted) is unchanged and still suggests clearing/resetting the cache.

## Testing

- Added `test_require_target_ref_surfaces_unborn_default_branch` next to the existing stale-branch test, asserting an unborn default branch surfaces `UnbornDefaultBranch` rather than `StaleDefaultBranch`.
- Manually reproduced both paths against a built binary: unborn `main` now reports "has no commits yet"; a deleted cached branch still reports "does not exist locally" with the reset hint.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean; `test_docs_are_in_sync` and the repository/merge/diff/default_branch integration groups pass. (The only failures in the full run were the `case_4` nushell shell-wrapper tests — nushell isn't installed in this sandbox — unrelated to this change.)

title: feat(commit-generation): deprecate `commits` squash template variable
body:
Step 1 of the deprecation cycle for the `commits` squash template variable, tracked in #2984 and requested in https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2983#issuecomment-4637273025.

## What

`commit_details` (added in #2983) is a strict superset of `commits`. This PR makes that superset relationship total — so the deprecation can be **auto-migrated** by `wt config update` rather than requiring a hand edit.

- Each `commit_details` element now renders as its bare subject (`{{ detail }}` yields the subject line) while still exposing `.subject` / `.body`. So a template that iterates the list and prints the loop variable directly behaves exactly like the old `commits` list of subject strings.
- `commits` is added to the standard `DEPRECATED_VARS` framework. A user `squash-template` that still references it renders unchanged, emits the framework's one-time deprecation warning, and is rewritten by `wt config update`:

  ```
  ▲ User config: template variable commits is deprecated in favor of commit_details
  ↳ To see details, run wt config show; to apply updates, run wt config update
  ```

- The default squash template, the [variable docs](https://worktrunk.dev/llm-commits/#template-variables), and the example config iterate `commit_details` and use `.subject`.

## Design notes

**The shape change is dissolved, so the rename is mechanical.** The original version of this PR argued `commits` couldn't go through `DEPRECATED_VARS` because the shape changes (string → object): a template would need `{{ commit }}` rewritten to `{{ commit.subject }}` by hand. Making `commit_details` elements render as their subject removes that gap entirely — `{% for c in commit_details %}{{ c }}` reads identically to the old `{% for c in commits %}{{ c }}`, so the existing identifier-rename machinery (`normalize_template_vars` / `wt config update`) handles it with no special-casing. The bespoke render-time warning in `build_prompt` is gone; detection and rewrite both live in the standard framework.

Implementation: a minijinja `Object` (`CommitDetailValue`) with `repr = Map` (for `.subject` / `.body` access) and a `render` override that emits the subject. minijinja coerces an object to a string via `render`, so string filters (`{{ c | upper }}`) operate on the subject too — the rename stays transparent across filter usages, not just bare prints.

**`commit_details`'s experimental badge was dropped** (final commit 36db58e), per the maintainer's request in https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2985#issuecomment-4699113462, which also removed `commits` from the docs. Note the name remains transitional per the cycle in #2984: once `commits` is fully retired we may re-introduce `commits` as the list-of-objects form, at which point `commit_details` would itself be deprecated.

## Tests

- `test_config_update_migrates_commits_squash_var` — `wt config update` rewrites a `commits` squash template to `commit_details`, leaving the bare loop variable untouched.
- `test_step_squ

title: Expose commit bodies to squash templates
body:
Closes #2982

This addresses the issue with an additive template variable, leaving `commits` unchanged.

- Adds `commit_details` to squash prompt templates as a list of `{ subject, body }`.
- Derives the existing subject-only `commits` value from `commit_details`.
- Uses the existing repository command to collect bodies with `git log` `%b` and NUL delimiters to preserve multiline bodies.
- Documents the variable and adds unit/integration coverage.

## Example

After this change, squash templates can include commit bodies:

```jinja
{% for c in commit_details -%}
- {{ c.subject }}
{% if c.body -%}
{{ c.body | trim | indent(2, true) }}
{% endif -%}
{% endfor %}
```

## Verification

```bash
cargo test -p worktrunk commit_message_details
cargo test -p worktrunk llm::tests
cargo test --test integration test_step_squash_show_prompt_custom_template_renders_commit_details
```

title: refactor(commit-generation): drop the CLAUDECODE= nesting workaround
body:
worktrunk stripped `CLAUDECODE` before spawning the `[commit.generation]` LLM command, and the recommended Claude Code command carried a leading `CLAUDECODE=`, both to get past Claude Code's nested-session check that rejected `claude -p` launched from inside another Claude Code session.

That check is gone. It's absent from the `claude` binary across every current build (2.1.157 through 2.1.162), and `CLAUDECODE=1 claude -p …` runs cleanly (exit 0, empty stderr). So the workaround is no longer needed.

This drops it: `src/llm.rs` no longer calls `.env_remove("CLAUDECODE")`, and the recommended command loses the `CLAUDECODE=` prefix in the source of truth (`dev/config.example.toml`), the `wt config --help` text, and the Taskfile bench command. Docs, the skill reference, and the config help snapshots are regenerated to match.

Caveat: there's no published guarantee the nested-session check stays gone, and a Claude Code old enough to still have it (older than roughly late May 2026) would again block nested commit generation. Since the check is absent from the implementation across all current builds, that risk is low.

Tests: 1236 lib + 693 integration pass; fmt and clippy clean.

title: chore(list): tidy collect/mod.rs docstring and drain-timeout diag
body:
Three small quality fixes surfaced during the nightly code survey, all in `src/commands/list/collect/mod.rs`. They're independent and itemized below — happy to split if preferred.

## 1. Stale docstring reference

The "Measured Phase Timings" note said the 23-command pre-skeleton count "is above the '6-8 commands' target above" — but no "6-8 commands" target exists anywhere earlier. The figure actually documented above is the **five-to-six critical-path forks** in the "Forks on the Critical Path" section. Repointed the audit note at that real baseline.

## 2. `.unwrap()` in a `Result`-returning fn

`default_branch_cell` / `url_template_cell` were read with `into_inner().unwrap()`. Both cells are unconditionally `set()` inside the `rayon::scope` above, so the value is identical — but `.unwrap()` in a `Result`-returning function violates the no-unwrap rule in CLAUDE.md, and the structurally identical sibling cells later in the same function (`previous_branch_cell`, `snapshot_cell`) already use `.into_inner().flatten()`. Switched these two to `.flatten()` for consistency and to drop the one panic path.

## 3. Silent truncation in the drain-timeout diagnostic

`format_drain_timeout_diag` listed at most 5 blocked tasks via `.take(5)` but gave no signal when more were blocked — a user with 8 hung worktrees saw only 5 with no hint the list was cut. Append a `… and N more` line (house ellipsis style) when the list exceeds 5, with a regression test covering the >5 case. The truncation path was previously untested.

## Testing

- `cargo test --lib --bins format_drain_timeout_diag` — 3 tests pass (incl. the new truncation test).
- `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes` — fmt + clippy clean; the only test failures are the 10 `shell_wrapper::unix_tests::*::case_4` (nushell) cases, which fail with "Unable to spawn nu … No viable candidates found in PATH" because `nu` isn't installed in this sandbox. Unrelated to this change (diff is one file, list-collection only); CI installs nu via `hustcer/setup-nu`.

The switch page documented the `pr:N` / `mr:N` shortcuts prominently but mentioned the web-URL form only in a trailing parenthetical. Pasting a PR link straight from the browser is a common way in, so the URL now sits as a co-equal form: in the lead sentence of the "Pull requests and merge requests" section, in the top examples block, and paired with each shortcut in the PR/MR example block. All edits go through the primary source (`src/cli/mod.rs`); the generated mirrors and the help snapshot are regenerated.

Also adds a `gitlab.com/.+/-/merge_requests` exclusion to `.config/lychee.toml`, mirroring the existing GitHub-PR rule, so the realistic GitLab MR example URL doesn't 403 the link check in CI. The old doc only avoided this by ending its example in a literal `N`.

title: fix(help): quit less on Ctrl-C on Windows to avoid wedged terminal
body:
## Problem

On Windows, `wt <cmd> --help` pipes its output through `less`. Pressing `q` exits cleanly, but pressing **Ctrl-C** leaves the terminal unresponsive (#2968). @ofek confirmed the key symptom: the `less` window disappears and the prompt is redrawn, but input no longer echoes.

Root cause: on Windows, Ctrl-C delivers a `CTRL_C_EVENT` to *every* process attached to the console — both `less` and the blocked `wt` parent ([`child.wait()`](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/6fd1bf4566bba0252f2c257fe22d7b94a6561843/src/help_pager.rs#L119-L131)). `less` is terminated before it restores the console input mode it switched into, and `wt` has no Windows console handler to coordinate teardown (signal forwarding is [Unix-only](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/6fd1bf4566bba0252f2c257fe22d7b94a6561843/src/signal_forwarder.rs#L1-L6)). The console is left with echo / line-input disabled, so the shell looks wedged. `q` works because `less` then exits cleanly and restores the mode.

## Approach in this PR

Pass `-K` (`--quit-on-intr`) to `less` via the `LESS` env var, **Windows only**. Per the [`less(1)` manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/less.1.html), `-K` makes `less` *exit* on an interrupt (status 2) instead of returning to its prompt — routing Ctrl-C through the same clean-exit/deinit path as `q`, which restores the console.

This is deliberately the smallest change that targets the mechanism:

- **No new dependency, no FFI / `SetConsoleCtrlHandler`.** I floated a Windows console-handler approach earlier in the thread; this avoids that entirely.
- **Windows-only.** On Unix the signal forwarder already coordinates teardown, and many users rely on Ctrl-C returning `less` to its prompt rather than quitting — so that path is untouched.
- `compute_less_flags` is split into a platform-parameterized core (`compute_less_flags_for`) so both branches are unit-tested on any host.

## ⚠️ Not verified on Windows — opening as a draft

I run in Linux CI and **cannot exercise the Windows console teardown**, so I have not confirmed this end-to-end on real hardware. The reasoning is grounded in the documented `-K` behavior and @ofek's confirmation that `q` (clean exit) restores the terminal, but the residual unknown is whether `less` completes its console-restore deinit before the concurrent `CTRL_C_EVENT` to `wt` matters in practice. I'm opening this as a draft at @ofek's request so a maintainer can see the concrete change and test it on Windows before deciding.

If it works, this is a one-flag fix. If `-K` proves insufficient (e.g. the restore races the parent's termination), the heavier console-handler route remains the fallback.

## Testing

- `cargo test --bin wt compute_less_flags` — 5 tests pass, covering both the Unix (`-FRX`) and Windows (`-FRX -K`) branches.
- `cargo clippy` / `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- **Windows runtime behavior: unverified** (see above).

title: Release v0.56.0
body:
v0.56.0.

`cargo semver-checks` reports a breaking library API change: the config-deprecation refactor (#2946) replaced the public `Deprecations` struct with a `Vec<DeprecationKind>` alias, removing the struct shape. Not intentional public API, but it forces a minor bump pre-1.0.

## CHANGELOG

### Improved

- **`wt list` JSON output includes `repo_url`**: Each item now carries `repo_url`, the repository's web URL derived from the primary remote (absent when there's no parseable forge remote). It's the local checkout's repo — distinct from `ci.repo_url`, which is the repo a PR/MR targets. ([#2941](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2941), thanks @bendrucker)

### Fixed

- **Bare-repo prompts**: Two UX fixes. `wt config create --project` run in a bare repo with no linked worktrees now explains the next step (`wt switch <branch>` first, then create from inside the worktree) instead of failing with a generic "no worktree found". And the bare-repo worktree-path prompt no longer fires for symbolic identifiers (`-`, `@`, `^`, `pr:`/`mr:`), where the example paths would be misleading — it waits for the next switch to a concrete branch name. ([#2951](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2951), thanks @ammachado)

- **Context gauge spacing in the Claude Code statusline**: The context-gauge moon emoji rendered flush against the percent (`🌕42%`). Most terminals draw the emoji double-width and bleed it into the next cell, so the moon collided with the digits; it now carries a trailing space (`🌕 42%`). ([#2944](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2944))

- **Console storm on Windows**: Detached background hook processes were created with `DETACHED_PROCESS`, which could flash a burst of console windows. They now use `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` and spawn fully hidden. ([#2959](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2959), thanks @nathanbabcock)

### Documentation

- **Codex commit-generation model bumped to `gpt-5.4-mini`**: The recommended `[commit.generation]` command for Codex — shown by `wt config create` and in the LLM-commits docs — now uses `gpt-5.4-mini` (was `gpt-5.1-codex-mini`). ([#2949](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2949))

### Internal

- **Config-deprecation layer refactor**: The deprecation detector now returns a `Vec<DeprecationKind>` instead of a struct of per-field flags, and the per-section config-table walks collapse into two combinators. Behavior-neutral — warning text and migration output are byte-for-byte unchanged. ([#2946](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2946))

title: docs(skills): fast-forward release branch to main before cutting a release
body:
The release worktree's branch only resets to `main` after a release lands, so between releases it can sit behind `main`. Cutting from a stale branch silently drops everything merged since — this came up live: a release was about to ship from a branch 8 commits behind `main`, which would have dropped a Windows console-storm fix, bare-repo UX fixes, and a `feat(list)` addition.

Adds an explicit first step to the release skill that fetches and fast-forwards the release branch to `origin/main` with `--ff-only`, which **fails** (rather than creating a merge commit or discarding work) if the branch has diverged.

Spelled out as raw git rather than `wt up` because the `up` alias rebases each branch onto its own upstream (`origin/release`), not `main` — so it would not bring main's commits onto the release branch. Subsequent steps are renumbered (12 → 13) and the two internal cross-references updated.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max_
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md (+21/-15)
@@ -9,29 +9,35 @@ metadata:
 
 ## Steps
 
-1. **Run tests**: `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes`
-2. **Check current version**: Read `version` in `Cargo.toml`
-3. **Review commits**: Check commits since last release to understand scope of changes. Audit the cumulative diff for the data-loss surface (see [Data-Loss Surface Review](#data-loss-surface-review)) before proceeding.
-4. **Check library API compatibility**: Run `cargo semver-checks check-release -p worktrunk` (install with `cargo install cargo-semver-checks --locked` if missing). If it reports breaking changes, the bump must be minor (pre-1.0) or major (post-1.0). See "Library API Compatibility" below.
-5. **Credit contributors**: Check for external PR authors and issue reporters (see "Credit External Contributors" and "Credit Issue Reporters" below)
-6. **Determine release type**: Pick the bump from the changes (including semver-checks result). Ask the user only if the choice is genuinely ambiguous (see below).
-7. **Bump version** (must run on a clean tree — before editing CHANGELOG):
+1. **Sync the release branch with `main`**: The release worktree's branch lags `main` between releases — it's only reset to `main` after a release lands. Cutting from a stale branch silently drops everything merged since. Fast-forward to the tip of `main` before anything else:
    ```bash
-   cargo release X.Y.Z -p worktrunk -x --no-publish --no-push --no-tag --no-verify --no-confirm && cargo check
+   git fetch origin
+   git merge --ff-only origin/main
    ```
-   This bumps `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`, then auto-commits. We'll reset this commit in step 9 to fold in the CHANGELOG.
-8. **Update CHANGELOG**: Add `## X.Y.Z` section at top with changes (see MANDATORY verification below)
-9. **Commit**: Reset the auto-commit from step 7, stage everything, and create the final release commit:
+   `--ff-only` advances the branch when it's a strict ancestor of `origin/main` and **fails** (rather than creating a merge commit or discarding work) if it has diverged — reconcile manually before continuing. This is the release-branch equivalent of `wt up`, spelled out because the `up` alias rebases each branch onto its own upstream (`origin/release`), not `main`.
+2. **Run tests**: `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes`
+3. **Check current version**: Read `version` in `Cargo.toml`
+4. **Review commits**: Check commits since last release to understand scope of changes. Audit the cumulative diff for the data-loss surface (see [Data-Loss Surface Review](#data-loss-surface-review)) before proceeding.
+5. **Check library API compatibility**: Run `cargo semver-checks check-release -p worktrunk` (install with `cargo install cargo-semver-checks --locked` if missing). If it reports breaking changes, the bump must be minor (pre-1.0) or major (post-1.0). See "Library API Compatibility" below.
+6. **Credit contributors**: Check for external PR authors and issue reporters (see "Credit External Contributors" and "Credit Issue Reporters" below)
+7. **Determine release type**: Pick the bump from the changes (including semver-checks result). Ask the user only if the choice is genuinely ambiguous (see below).
+8. **Bump version** (must run on a clean tree — before editing CHANGELOG):
    ```bash
-   git reset --soft HEAD~1 && git add -A && git commit -m "Release vX.Y.Z"
+   cargo release X.Y.Z -p worktrunk -x --no-publish --no-push --no-tag --no-verify --no-confirm && cargo check
    ```
-10. **Merge to main**: `/gpk` — opens a PR, waits for CI, merges via PR (preserves worktree)
-11. **Tag the merge commit and push**: After `/gpk` squash-merges, the local branch HEAD is not the commit on main. Tag the PR's merge commit explicitly so the tag is reachable from main:
+   This bumps `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`, then auto-commits. We'll reset this commit in step 10 to fold in the CHANGELOG.
+9. **Update CHANGELOG**: Add `## X.Y.Z` section at top with changes (see MANDATORY verification below)
+10. **Commit**: Reset the auto-commit from step 8, stage everything, and create the final release commit:
+    ```bash
+    git reset --soft HEAD~1 && git add -A && git commit -m "Release vX.Y.Z"
+    ```
+11. **Merge to main**: `/gpk` — opens a PR, waits for CI, merges via PR (preserves worktree)
+12. **Tag the merge commit and push**: After `/gpk` squash-merges, the local branch HEAD is not the commit on main. Tag the PR's merge commit explicitly so the tag is reachable from main:
     ```bash
     MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view --json mergeCommit --jq '.mergeCommit.oid')
     git tag vX.Y.Z "$MERGE_SHA" && git push origin vX.Y.Z
     ```
-12. **Wait for the release workflow**: The tag push triggers `release.yaml`. Launch a ci-reporter agent to monitor the run through to completion (avoid `gh run watch` — it can hang); the run ID comes from:
+13. **Wait for the release workflow**: The tag push triggers `release.yaml`. Launch a ci-reporter agent to monitor the run through to completion (avoid `gh run watch` — it can hang); the run ID comes from:
     ```bash
     gh run list --workflow=release.yaml --event=push --branch=vX.Y.Z --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId'
     ```

title: test(switch): cover Azure DevOps PR URLs end-to-end
body:
Adds test coverage for passing an Azure DevOps PR web URL to `wt switch`. No behavior change.

This follows up on a question from [#2941](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2941#issuecomment-4599678110):

> Was going to follow up with accepting URL on `switch` only to find #2898 🙌🏻
>
> (though would it need a change for the Azure format?)

The Azure format already works. URL detection in #2898 is shape-based, not host-based: `parse_ref_url_parts` scans path segments for a `pull` / `pulls` / `pullrequest` / `merge_requests` marker followed by a number, ignoring the host. Azure URLs reduce to `pr:N` and dispatch to `AzureDevOpsProvider` through the normal path. The gap was test coverage, not behavior.

## Changes

- Adds `test_switch_pr_azure_web_url`, the first end-to-end test that passes a real web URL to `wt switch`. Every prior switch PR/MR test used the `pr:N` / `mr:N` shortcut directly, so the URL → `pr:N` → `AzureDevOpsProvider` path had only been exercised as two separate halves. The new snapshot is byte-identical to `switch_pr_azure_same_repo` apart from the recorded `args`, confirming the URL and shortcut forms converge.
- Pins the legacy `*.visualstudio.com` host shape in the `parse_ref_url_azure_devops` unit test, which previously only covered `dev.azure.com`.

This is low importance, since the behavior was already correct and covered indirectly. Happy to trim it to just the unit-test assertion, or close it altogether.

## References

- #2898 added URL acceptance on `switch`
- #2941 is where the question came up

title: refactor(diff): symmetric merge_base equality skip + drop stale ref-vs-sha note
body:
## Summary

`compute_ahead_behind` in `src/git/repository/diff.rs` carries a stale comment explaining why the `merge_base == base` skip wasn't applied. The rationale ("base is typically a refname like 'main' while merge_base is a SHA") no longer holds — `compute_ahead_behind`'s only caller is `ahead_behind_by_sha`, so both arguments are commit SHAs, and `merge_base_by_sha` returns a SHA too. Verified via `grep -rn "compute_ahead_behind\b" src/`.

This PR:

- Drops the stale comment.
- Applies the equality skip symmetrically (`merge_base == base` short-circuits `behind`, mirroring the existing `merge_base == head` skip for `ahead`).
- Routes the inner `merge_base` lookup through `merge_base_by_sha` to match the rest of this SHA-keyed path (the surrounding code already uses `_by_sha` variants consistently).

`behind == 0` is the common case for a feature branch purely ahead of its base, so the symmetric skip elides one `rev-list --count` on every cache miss for that shape.

## Test plan

- [x] Existing `test_ahead_behind_reads_cache` already exercises the `(1, 0)` shape (feature ahead of main), which hits the `merge_base == base` path. No new test added since behavior is unchanged — this is a perf optimization plus comment cleanup.
- [x] `cargo check` passes
- [x] All 9 `ahead_behind` tests pass locally

title: skills(running-tend): install Nix during weekly MSRV bump
body:
## Summary

Codifies what max-sixty asked for in [#2948 (comment)](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2948#issuecomment-4599890148): allow the agent to install Nix itself during weekly maintenance, instead of waiting for the maintainer to refresh `flake.lock` manually after every MSRV bump.

The weekly skill already tells the agent to run `nix flake update` after the toolchain bump, but Nix isn't in the `claude-setup` action so that line was non-executable — every weekly MSRV bump shipped a stale lock and the next nightly `nix-flake` job failed (as on #2948 itself).

## Changes

- **`Weekly Maintenance: MSRV & Toolchain`** — add the Determinate Systems installer one-liner before `nix flake update`. Daemon-mode, `--no-confirm`, sources the daemon profile, and uses `--extra-experimental-features 'nix-command flakes'` so the command works on a fresh install without a pre-existing `nix.conf`. Tested in the tend-mention run from the linked comment: it ran cleanly, refreshed the lock for #2948, and the resulting `flake.lock` evaluates against `channel = 1.95.0`.
- **`Investigating codecov failures in CI`** — narrow the existing "`cargo install` / `curl | sh` are blocked by the sandbox" claim. The actual failure mode is source-compiling installs (long-running cargo compiles) cascading into bash-tool interrupts; pre-built single-script installers like Determinate Nix's run fine. The narrower wording keeps the codecov-investigation guidance intact while not contradicting the new MSRV recipe.

## Test plan

- [ ] Next weekly run picks up the new recipe and produces a `flake.lock` refresh inside the same PR as the toolchain bump (no follow-up needed from the maintainer).
- [ ] `nix-flake` job passes on the weekly PR head.

title: fix: prevent console storm on windows
body:
**Tl;dr:** Background steps during hooks like `[post-start]` briefly spawn visible consoles on Windows. The fix is to use `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. Apart from suppressing the console windows, it functions identically. --- From [**Process Creation Flags** (Microsoft Learn)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/process-creation-flags): `DETACHED_PROCESS` — `0x00000008` > For console processes, the new process does not inherit its parent's console (the default). The new process can call the [`AllocConsole`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/allocconsole) function at a later time to create a console. For more information, see [Creation of a Console](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/creation-of-a-console). This value cannot be used with `CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE`. `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` — `0x08000000` > The process is a console application that is being run without a console window. Therefore, the console handle for the application is not set. This flag is ignored if the application is not a console application, or if it is used with either `CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE` or `DETACHED_PROCESS`. --- Verified locally on a `wt.toml` that had 4 pre-start hooks (some semi long-running like a `pnpm install`)
BeforeAfter
[worktrunk-console-storm-before.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e88b798-e2d0-43a1-a750-da1eb41ece76) [worktrunk-console-storm-after.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d572cc6d-7d39-40ff-a851-afb5ff733972)

title: fix(bare-repo): UX fixes for worktree-path prompt and `wt config create --project` in bare repos
body:
## Problem

Three UX issues in the bare-repository workflow documented in [Tips & Patterns](https://worktrunk.dev/tips-patterns/#bare-repository-layout).

### Bug 1: Example paths use a hardcoded placeholder branch

When `wt switch` detects a bare repo at a hidden path (`.git`, `.bare`), the warning and prompt previously showed:

```
▲ Bare repo at camel/.git — worktrees will be at camel/.git.feature-auth
```

The `feature-auth` placeholder was hardcoded regardless of the branch being switched to. Switching to `main` produced a confusing mismatch between what was shown and what would actually happen.

### Bug 2: Symbolic identifiers showed unresolved input in the prompt

Switching with `wt switch @`, `wt switch -`, `wt switch ^`, or `wt switch pr:123` triggered the prompt with the literal symbol in the example path (`camel/.git.@`, etc.), which is meaningless. The symbol isn't a branch name — it gets resolved later. Skip the prompt for those; it surfaces on the next switch with a concrete branch.

### Bug 3: `wt config create --project` gives an unhelpful error in bare repos with no worktrees

Running `wt config create --project` from a bare repo root with no linked worktrees yet failed with:

```
Cannot determine project config location — no worktree found
```

No indication of why this happened or what to do next.

### Bug 4: Docs are vague about the bare-repo setup order

The Tips & Patterns bare-repo section told users to set `worktree-path` globally in user config, affecting all repos. It didn't mention the per-project `[projects."..."]` override, didn't clarify that `wt switch main` (without `--create`) works for existing branches on a freshly cloned bare repo, and didn't explain that the project config must be created from inside a worktree.

---

## Solution

1. **Pass the actual branch into `offer_bare_repo_worktree_path_fix`** and use it (with `/` and `\` sanitized to `-`) in the warning and preview messages.
2. **Skip the prompt for symbolic identifiers** (`-`, `@`, `^`, `pr:N`, `mr:N`).
3. **Bare-repo-aware error for `wt config create --project`** — points the user at `wt switch <branch>` as the next step.
4. **Restructure the Tips & Patterns bare-repo section** into three subsections (Configure the worktree path / Create the first worktree / Set up the project config) explaining the per-project `[projects."..."]` scope, when `--create` is needed, and the chicken-and-egg constraint on `.config/wt.toml`.

---

## Out of scope

The original PR also added a per-clone `worktrunk.worktree-path` git-config key as a third scope alongside per-remote and global user-config. That's a more invasive change (new exception in the config-resolution chain) and is split out into a follow-up PR — see #2953.

---

## Testing

- `test_bare_repo_worktree_path_prompt_auto_accept` / `..._non_interactive_warning` — snapshots now show the actual branch name (`feature`) instead of hardcoded `feature-auth`.
- `test_bare_repo_worktree_path_prompt_skipped_for_sym

title: docs(commit-generation): bump Codex model to gpt-5.4-mini
body:
## Summary

Bump the Codex `[commit.generation]` recommendation: `gpt-5.1-codex-mini` → `gpt-5.4-mini`.

## Why

`gpt-5.1-codex-mini` is no longer listed on the [Codex models page](https://developers.openai.com/codex/models). The current Codex lineup is:

| Model | Capability | Speed | API access | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gpt-5.5` | ★★★★★ | ★★★ | yes | Recommended default for most tasks |
| `gpt-5.4` | ★★★★★ | ★★★ | yes | Flagship |
| `gpt-5.4-mini` | ★★★ | ★★★★ | yes | "Fast, efficient mini model for responsive coding tasks and subagents" |
| `gpt-5.3-codex` | ★★★★★ | ★★★ | yes | Coding specialist |
| `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` | ★★★ | ★★★★★ | **no** | Research preview, ChatGPT Pro only |
| `gpt-5.2` | ★★★★ | ★★★ | yes | Previous generation |

The `running-tend` skill says to pick "the one the vendor's models page currently positions as fastest/smallest" for commit-message generation. `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` has more flashes but no API access, so it can't be invoked from `codex exec`. The next-fastest with full API access is `gpt-5.4-mini`, which the page explicitly recommends "when you want a faster, lower-cost option for lighter coding tasks or subagents" — exactly the commit-message use case.

## Notes

- Verifying `codex -m gpt-5.4-mini` end-to-end isn't possible in the CI sandbox (codex CLI not installed); the model ID is taken from the upstream docs page.
- `test_docs_are_in_sync` propagates `dev/config.example.toml` and `src/cli/mod.rs` to the docs/skills mirrors. The same literal string appears in all sites, so this PR updates them in lockstep; the test should pass without further regeneration.
- Closes the loop on #2890 (the original bot triage issue, closed in favor of opening a PR per #2891).

title: refactor(deprecation): Vec<DeprecationKind> + config-table combinators
body:
Two behavior-neutral refactors of the config-deprecation layer (`src/config/deprecation.rs`). No warning text, migration output, or snapshot changes — the full pre-merge gate is green.

**1. `Deprecations` struct → `Vec<DeprecationKind>`.** Each detected pattern becomes a `DeprecationKind` variant carrying exactly the payload its warning needs. `format_deprecation_warnings` collapses from one if-block per field (~127 lines) into a single match over the kinds, and `is_empty` is now just `Vec::is_empty()`. `detect_deprecations_from_doc` pushes kinds in warning-emission order, so iterating the `Vec` reproduces the prior output byte-for-byte. The silent `-create` → `-start` hook rename deliberately gets no variant, so it still emits no warning. The `approved_commands` field read in `wt config update` becomes a `matches!(k, DeprecationKind::ApprovedCommands)` predicate.

**2. Config-table scope walks → two combinators.** The repeated "top-level + per-project" walk (~10 sites) is replaced by `any_config_table` (detect, short-circuits on first true) and `for_each_config_table_mut` (migrate, ORs per-scope changes). The closure receives the scope key (`None` for top-level, `Some(key)` for `[projects.*]`) so callers can build display paths. `find_approved_commands_from_doc` and `remove_approved_commands_doc` stay bespoke — neither fits the combinator shape cleanly.

`CLAUDE.md`'s "add a deprecation" checklist is updated to match the new shape (and fixes a stale `migrate_negated_bool_in_section` reference).

title: docs(skills): add data-loss-surface review to tend and release
body:
Follow-up to #2939, where the Claude plugin's `WorktreeRemove` hook shipped `wt remove -D` and force-deleted an unmerged branch on session exit, silently discarding committed-but-unpushed work. The hook fix landed in #2940; this adds process guardrails so a destructive flag in shipped automation is caught before it reaches users again.

**Tend PR review** (`running-tend/references/review-pr.md`): a "Data-Loss Surface: Hold for Human Review" gate. Flag any PR that introduces a destructive command (`wt remove -D`/`-f`, `git branch -D`, `git worktree remove --force`, `reset --hard`, `rm -rf`, `fs::remove_*`) or edits a file that already contains one. The second case is the subtle one: a change near the force-delete path can shift its behavior without the destructive line appearing in the diff. On a match, name it, request review from @max-sixty, and don't authorize the merge even when it looks acceptable.

**Release** (`release/SKILL.md`): a cumulative second gate. Rather than trust a keyword grep, fan out 3-5 independent finder subagents over the whole diff since the last release and the code it touches. Most get no grep, so they reason from the code instead of anchoring on a pattern list; the grep survives as one cross-check finder. The find phase optimizes for recall (over-report, accept false positives); the analyze phase adjudicates each candidate against the data-safety invariants for precision.

Docs-only: two internal skill files, no code or test changes.

Thanks to @jbeda for raising #2939 with a clear repro, and for confirming the dangling-ref recovery.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max_
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md (+30/-1)
@@ -11,7 +11,7 @@ metadata:
 
 1. **Run tests**: `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes`
 2. **Check current version**: Read `version` in `Cargo.toml`
-3. **Review commits**: Check commits since last release to understand scope of changes
+3. **Review commits**: Check commits since last release to understand scope of changes. Audit the cumulative diff for the data-loss surface (see [Data-Loss Surface Review](#data-loss-surface-review)) before proceeding.
 4. **Check library API compatibility**: Run `cargo semver-checks check-release -p worktrunk` (install with `cargo install cargo-semver-checks --locked` if missing). If it reports breaking changes, the bump must be minor (pre-1.0) or major (post-1.0). See "Library API Compatibility" below.
 5. **Credit contributors**: Check for external PR authors and issue reporters (see "Credit External Contributors" and "Credit Issue Reporters" below)
 6. **Determine release type**: Pick the bump from the changes (including semver-checks result). Ask the user only if the choice is genuinely ambiguous (see below).
@@ -38,6 +38,35 @@ metadata:
 
 `release.yaml` builds binaries and publishes to crates.io, Homebrew, and winget automatically.
 
+## Data-Loss Surface Review
+
+Worktrunk's worst failure is silently destroying a user's work. The per-PR review (`running-tend`, "Data-Loss Surface") is the first gate; the release is the second, where the whole diff since the last release is visible at once.
+
+This review optimizes for recall: find every change that could touch the deletion surface, accept false positives, then adjudicate each candidate. Missing one real loss path costs far more than reviewing a false alarm.
+
+A keyword grep alone is insufficient. It finds only what someone thought to pattern-match, and an agent handed the grep anchors on it and inherits its blind spots. So fan out independent finders, most of them without the grep, and analyze every candidate they surface.
+
+### Find: independent finders, recall over precision
+
+Launch 3-5 finder subagents in parallel over the cumulative diff (`git log v<last-version>..HEAD -p`) and the code it touches, including anything that calls into or is called by the changed code. Each works independently: do not let them share findings during this phase, and do not collapse them onto one method. Each returns candidate locations with a one-line reason, erring toward over-reporting.
+
+Give each a distinct charter. At least two receive no grep and no keyword list, so they reason from the code instead of pattern-matching:
+
+- **Behavioral (no grep):** read each change and ask what it could destroy: files, branches, worktrees, uncommitted or untracked work, committed-but-unpushed commits. Flag any change whose worst case is lost user data.
+- **Blast-radius (no grep):** for every function and file the diff touches, trace callers and callees. Flag any path that can now reach a destructive primitive (branch deletion, worktree removal, filesystem removal, history rewrite), even when that call sits outside the diff.
+- **Automation diff (no grep):** compare shipped automation before and after: `plugins/*/hooks/hooks.json`, `hooks/hooks.json`, `hooks/wt.sh`, and skill or alias examples users copy. Flag any new or altered invocation that removes or force-overwrites anything.
+- **Keyword scan (grep):** one finder runs the pattern filter over the full diff as a cross-check, never as the primary method. It takes no pathspec; a path allowlist would recreate the blind spots the no-grep finders exist to avoid (the densest destructive code, the trash sweep in `src/commands/process.rs`, sits outside `src/git/`).
+  ```bash
+  git log v<last-version>..HEAD -p \
+    | grep -nE -- '--force-delete|--force| -D| -f |branch -[dD]|worktree remove|reset --hard|checkout -f|clean -[fdx]|remove_dir_all|remove_file|rm -rf'
+  ```
+
+### Analyze: adjudicate each candidate
+
+Pool the candidates, dedupe, and analyze each against the data-safety invariants in `CLAUDE.md` and the FAQ "What can Worktrunk delete?" inventory: does it preserve data on failure, require explicit consent for destructive ops, and avoid silent side-effect deletion? Mark each real risk / acceptable / needs change, with the reasoning.
+
+Surface the full adjudicated list and get explicit sign-off before tagging. Do not tag a release with an unresolved deletion-surface candidate, even if it looks acceptable.
+
 ## CHANGELOG Review
 
 Check commits since last release for missing entries:
--- .claude/skills/running-tend/references/review-pr.md (+27/-0)
@@ -1,5 +1,32 @@
 # PR Review — Worktrunk Specifics
 
+## Data-Loss Surface: Hold for Human Review
+
+Worktrunk's worst failure is silently destroying a user's work, and the deletion
+surface is where it leaks in. A change that touches it is not an agent's to
+merge: a force-flag bypass can read as harmless and still discard committed work.
+
+Flag a PR when its diff **introduces** any of these, or **edits a file that
+already contains** one:
+
+- `wt remove`, especially `-D` / `--force-delete` or `-f` / `--force`
+- `git branch -D` / `-d`, `git worktree remove --force`
+- `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -f`, `git clean` with `-f` / `-d` / `-x`
+- `rm -rf`, `std::fs::remove_dir_all`, `std::fs::remove_file`
+- shipped automation that runs the above: `plugins/*/hooks/hooks.json`,
+  `hooks/hooks.json`, `hooks/wt.sh`, and skill or alias examples users copy
+
+Both directions matter. A PR that adds a call is obvious. A PR that edits a file
+already holding one is the subtle case: a change near the force-delete path in
+`src/git/remove.rs` can alter its behavior without the destructive line
+appearing in the diff.
+
+On a match:
+
+1. Name the command and file in the review.
+2. Request review from @max-sixty.
+3. Do not approve or authorize the merge, even if it looks acceptable.
+
 ## Review Criteria
 
 **Idiomatic Rust and project conventions:**

title: fix(statusline): space the context gauge emoji from its percent
body:
The context gauge in the Claude Code statusline rendered the moon-phase emoji flush against the percent (`🌕42%`). Most terminals draw emoji as double-width and bleed the glyph into the cell to its right, so the moon visually collided with the digits. This adds a trailing space — `🌕 42%`.

The flush-packing convention still holds for ASCII and narrow markers (`@+1`, `↓1`, `●`); emoji are the exception. That distinction is now documented in the `writing-user-outputs` skill so future output keeps it consistent.

Tests, the three inline statusline snapshots, nine rate-limit `.snap` files, and the hand-authored docs example (auto-synced to the skill reference) are all updated.

title: Release v0.55.0
body:
v0.55.0.

`cargo semver-checks` reports breaking library API changes (9 inherent methods removed from `Repository` / `ShellConfig` by the dead-code cut-overs in #2931 — `is_ancestor`, `same_commit`, `has_added_changes`, `trees_match`, `head_tree_matches_branch`, `has_merge_conflicts`, `has_merge_conflicts_by_tree`, `merge_integration_probe`, `is_posix`). None are intentional public API, but they force a minor bump pre-1.0.

Headline user-visible changes:
- `wt switch` accepts forge PR/MR URLs anywhere `pr:N` / `mr:N` works (#2898, thanks @thiagowfx for the request).
- Claude Code plugin keeps unmerged branches during worktree cleanup — the `WorktreeRemove` hook drops `-D` (#2940, thanks @jbeda for reporting).
- `wt list` and `wt step prune` degrade gracefully on unborn worktrees (#2937, thanks @nedtwigg for reporting).
- `-vv` startup pointer now names `diagnostic.md` (#2919).
- Doc-site and `--help` prose cleanup (#2922, #2925); internal cut-over of duplicated/dead code paths (#2931, #2932, #2934).

Full CHANGELOG entry in this PR.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max_
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- CHANGELOG.md (+22/-0)
@@ -1,5 +1,27 @@
 # Changelog
 
+## 0.55.0
+
+### Improved
+
+- **`wt switch` accepts forge PR/MR URLs**: `wt switch https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123` now resolves the same way as `wt switch pr:123`, and the URL form works anywhere a `pr:N` / `mr:N` shortcut does (positional argument and `--base`). Detection is shape-based, not host-based — any `http(s)://` URL whose path contains `/pull/N`, `/pulls/N`, `/-/merge_requests/N`, or `/pullrequest/N` matches, covering GitHub (including Enterprise), GitLab, Gitea, and Azure DevOps, including self-hosted instances. ([#2898](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2898), thanks @thiagowfx for the request)
+
+- **`-vv` startup pointer names `diagnostic.md`**: The `-vv` pointer now lists the shared log directory once with all three files it will contain — `trace.log`, `subprocess.log`, and `diagnostic.md` — so the diagnostic bundle is discoverable at startup rather than only when the gist hint fires at exit. The pointer verb reads `Writing to …` instead of `Tracing to …`. ([#2919](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2919))
+
+### Fixed
+
+- **Claude Code plugin keeps unmerged branches during worktree cleanup**: The plugin's `WorktreeRemove` hook passed `-D` (`--force-delete`) to `wt remove`, which removes a branch even when it carries commits that aren't merged or pushed. The hook now uses the default removal: a merged or integrated branch is removed cleanly, while one with unmerged commits is kept, with a `wt remove -D <branch>` hint for deleting it deliberately. ([#2940](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2940), thanks @jbeda for reporting)
+
+- **`wt list` and `wt step prune` degrade gracefully on unborn worktrees**: A linked worktree created with `git worktree add --orphan` sits on an unborn branch whose `HEAD` is the null OID. `wt list` used to show `working-tree-diff (fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD')` and a merge-tree error in its columns, and `wt step prune` aborted its entire scan with `fatal: Needed a single revision`, blocking pruning of every other worktree. Both now treat an unborn worktree as having no commits: `wt list` renders `·` for the commit-dependent columns, and `wt step prune` skips it (as it does locked worktrees) and continues. ([#2937](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2937), thanks @nedtwigg for reporting)

([#2922](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2922), [#2925](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2925))

([#2931](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2931), [#2932](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2932), [#2934](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/2934))

title: feat(list): add repo_url to JSON output
body:
Adds a top-level `repo_url` to `wt list --format=json` and `wt list statusline --format=json`, derived locally from the primary remote. Consumers that want a link to the repository itself (not the PR) currently shell out to `git remote get-url` and convert SSH to HTTPS by hand; `repo_url` does that from the already-parsed remote.

Also adds `ci.repo_url`: the repository a PR/MR targets, derived from `ci.url`. In a fork checkout the primary remote is the contributor's fork while the PR lives upstream, so the two can differ — `repo_url` names the local repo, `ci.repo_url` names the PR target. I kept them as separate fields so neither has to guess which one the consumer meant.

## Notes

- `GitRemoteUrl::web_url()` owns the per-forge shape, including the Azure `dev.azure.com` / `*.visualstudio.com` split; it calls `azure::fork_remote_url` rather than duplicating the format.
- `repo_url_from_ref_url()` shares a tokenizer with the existing `parse_ref_url`, so PR/MR URL shapes live in one place.
- Both derive from local state — no network access, consistent with the local-first policy.

title: fix(plugin): drop -D from WorktreeRemove hook to preserve unmerged branches
body:
## Problem

The Claude Code plugin's `WorktreeRemove` hook (`plugins/worktrunk/hooks/hooks.json`) ran `wt remove -D --foreground` on session exit. Claude Code auto-fires this hook for any worktree with a clean working tree — including ones whose branch holds **committed-but-unpushed** work — so `-D` (`--force-delete`) silently routed to `git branch -D`, discarding the only copy of the commits. Recovery was only possible via `git fsck` for the dangling object.

The recent remove-safety work (#2870, #2903) doesn't catch this because `-D` is the explicit override that bypasses `delete_branch_if_safe`. As #2903 notes: "Force-delete keeps `git branch -D` (explicit override)." The plugin hook was opting out of every safety check.

Reproduced locally with `wt remove -D --foreground my-branch` after committing (but not pushing) a file change — branch deleted, no reflog, commit only recoverable via `git fsck`.

## Solution

Drop `-D` from the `WorktreeRemove` hook command. The safe default now applies:

- Branch is **safe to delete** (merged, ancestor, same tree, etc.) → worktree and branch both removed cleanly. No behavior change for the common case.
- Branch has **unmerged commits** → worktree removed, branch retained, user sees `wt remove -D <branch>` hint. Data preserved.
- Worktree **dirty** → Claude Code doesn't auto-fire `WorktreeRemove` (unchanged).

The reporter's blog-post scenario in the issue (unpushed commit on an isolation worktree) now leaves the branch behind for recovery instead of force-deleting it.

## Testing

- Added an assertion in `test_plugin_layout_is_consolidated` that the `WorktreeRemove` hook command contains neither ` -D` nor `--force-delete`. Verified the test fails on the prior `hooks.json` and passes on the fix.
- Reproduction script confirmed before/after:
  - Before: `Removed my-branch worktree & branch (--force-delete)` → branch gone, no reflog.
  - After: `Removed my-branch worktree` + `↳ Branch unmerged; to delete, run wt remove -D my-branch` → branch retained.
- Full `config_show` (124 tests) and `remove::` (101 tests) suites pass locally.

Updated `skills/wt-switch-create/SKILL.md` to describe the new safe-default behavior of the hook.

---
Closes #2939 — automated triage

title: fix(list, prune): degrade gracefully on unborn worktrees
body:
## Problem

`git worktree add --orphan` creates a linked worktree on an unborn branch — `worktree list --porcelain` reports its `HEAD` as the null OID. Two paths then fail:

- `wt list` shows `working-tree-diff (fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD')` and `working-tree-conflicts (fatal: 0000… is not a valid object)` because the diff and merge-tree probes try to resolve HEAD / treat the null OID as a commit.
- `wt step prune` aborts the entire scan with `fatal: Needed a single revision` because `integration_reason` runs `git rev-parse --verify <unborn-branch>`, blocking pruning of any other worktrees in the repo.

## Solution

- `src/commands/list/collect/execution.rs`: add `WorkingTreeDiff` and `WorkingTreeConflicts` to `COMMIT_TASKS`. Both seed defaults (`None` and `Some(None)`) already exist and render as `·`, matching how the other commit-dependent columns degrade for unborn worktrees.
- `src/commands/step/prune.rs`: skip `!wt.has_commits()` worktrees in `gather_check_items` — they can't be integrated and aren't auto-prune candidates. Mirrors the existing skip for locked worktrees.

Two existing tests (`test_list_shows_warning_on_git_error` and the diagnostic `corrupt_worktree_head` helper) used to write `0000…` into a ref/HEAD file and rely on the resulting error warnings. After the fix those inputs read as unborn and skip silently, so both are updated to use `0000…001` — a non-null invalid SHA that still exercises the warning surfacing they were written to test.

## Testing

- `test_list_unborn_worktree_no_task_failures` — fails on `main`, passes after the list fix.
- `test_prune_skips_unborn_worktree` — fails on `main` with `Needed a single revision`, passes after the prune fix and leaves the unborn worktree in place while still pruning the merged sibling.
- Full `cargo test --test integration` clean (skipping pre-existing nushell flakes where `nu` isn't installed in this runner).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --check` clean.
