-            "command": "wt config state marker clear || true"
+            "command": "bash \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/.claude-plugin/hooks/wt.sh\" config state marker clear || true"
           }
         ]
       }
@@ -37,7 +37,7 @@
         "hooks": [
           {
             "type": "command",
-            "command": "jq -r '.name' | xargs -I{} wt switch --create {} --no-cd --format=json | jq -r '.path'"
+            "command": "jq -r '.name' | xargs -I{} bash \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/.claude-plugin/hooks/wt.sh\" switch --create {} --no-cd --format=json | jq -r '.path'"
           }
         ]
       }
@@ -47,7 +47,7 @@
         "hooks": [
           {
             "type": "command",
-            "command": "jq -r '.worktree_path' | xargs wt remove -D --foreground"
+            "command": "jq -r '.worktree_path' | xargs bash \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/.claude-plugin/hooks/wt.sh\" remove -D --foreground"
           }
         ]
       }
--- .claude-plugin/hooks/wt.sh (+39/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cross-platform wrapper for the worktrunk CLI.
+# If WORKTRUNK_BIN is set, uses that path exclusively.
+# Otherwise, on Windows (MSYS/Cygwin), prefers git-wt.exe over wt and
+# rejects wt if it resolves to Windows Terminal (.../WindowsApps/wt.exe).
+# On other platforms, uses wt directly.
+# Usage: wt.sh [args...]
+
+if [[ -n "$WORKTRUNK_BIN" ]]; then
+    if ! command -v "$WORKTRUNK_BIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        echo "worktrunk: WORKTRUNK_BIN is set to '$WORKTRUNK_BIN' but it was not found" >&2
+        exit 1
+    fi
+    WT="$WORKTRUNK_BIN"
+elif [[ "$(uname -o 2>/dev/null)" =~ ^(Msys|Cygwin)$ ]]; then
+    # check for bash on Windows (on Windows, Claude Code defaults to Git Bash)
+    if command -v git-wt.exe >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        # prefer git-wt over wt if available
+        WT=git-wt.exe
+    elif command -v wt >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        # reject wt if it's the Windows Terminal alias
+        if [[ "$(command -v wt)" == *WindowsApps* ]]; then
+            echo "worktrunk: 'wt' resolves to Windows Terminal; install worktrunk as git-wt.exe or remove the Windows Terminal alias. See https://worktrunk.dev/worktrunk/#install" >&2
+            exit 1
+        fi
+
+        WT=wt
+    fi
+else
+    # non-Windows, always use wt
+    WT=wt
+fi
+
+if [[ -z "$WT" ]] || ! command -v "$WT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "worktrunk: could not find 'wt' in PATH" >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+
+"$WT" "$@"

title: fix: use primary worktree for project config path in bare repos
body:
## Problem

In bare repos, `wt hook approvals add` reports "No project configuration found" even when a project config exists and is visible via `wt config show`. This happens because:

- `config create --project`, `config show`, and `hook approvals add` computed the config path using `current_worktree().root()`, which in bare repos falls back to the bare repo directory
- `ProjectConfig::load` (the actual config loader) uses `primary_worktree()` for bare repos (#1691), which points to the default branch worktree — a different path

So the config gets created/displayed at one location but looked up at another.

## Solution

Added `Repository::expected_project_config_path()` that centralizes the config path logic to match `ProjectConfig::load`:
- **Bare repos**: primary worktree (default branch worktree), falling back to bare repo root only when no primary worktree exists
- **Normal repos**: current worktree root (unchanged behavior)

Updated all consumers to use this method:
- `config create --project` — now creates config in primary worktree for bare repos
- `config show` — now displays the correct path
- `hook approvals add` — error message now points to the right location
- `hook list`, `config update`, `diagnostic` — consistent paths

## Testing

- Added `test_add_approvals_bare_repo_config_in_primary_worktree` — verifies `hook approvals add` finds config in primary worktree
- Added `test_config_create_project_bare_repo_uses_primary_worktree` — verifies `config create --project` places config in primary worktree, not bare repo root
- Existing `test_bare_repo_ignores_config_in_bare_root` (#1691 regression test) continues to pass

---
Closes #1744 — automated triage
author: worktrunk-bot

title: fix: use correct tend plugin skill names in workflows
body:
The generated workflows referenced skills as `/tend:tend-*` (e.g., `/tend:tend-review`), but the plugin is named `tend-ci-runner` and the skills are `review`, `triage`, etc. The correct format is `/tend-ci-runner:review`.

This caused the silent review failure on #1736 — Claude resolved the skill client-side, found nothing, and returned "Unknown skill" with zero tokens. The CI check showed green because the process exited cleanly.

The root cause is the published `uvx tend` generator (v0.0.2) still uses the old naming convention. A new release of the generator will fix it for future `uvx tend init` runs; this PR fixes the existing generated files.

title: fix(ci): set uv cache-dependency-glob to silence CI warning
body:
The `setup-uv` action enables caching by default with a `cache-dependency-glob` that looks for Python dependency files (`requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, etc.). Since this is a Rust project, none match, producing this warning on every CI run:

> No file matched to [...]. The cache will never get invalidated.

The uv cache does help — with a cache hit, `uv tool install pre-commit` resolves and prepares 10 packages in ~170ms from cached wheels instead of downloading from PyPI. Set the glob to `.pre-commit-config.yaml` so the cache invalidates when pre-commit hook configuration changes.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of @max-sixty_
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- .github/actions/claude-setup/action.yaml (+2/-0)
@@ -34,6 +34,8 @@ runs:
 
     - name: Install uv
       uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7.6.0
+      with:
+        cache-dependency-glob: .pre-commit-config.yaml
 
     - name: Install pre-commit
       shell: bash

body:
Remove the separate `VCS_METADATA_DIRS` const and derive the hardcoded directory check from `BUILTIN_COPY_IGNORED_EXCLUDES` instead. One list, one source of truth.

- **for-each**: Replaced near-verbatim restatement with only-new-info ("summary at the end")

title: fix: suppress false positive shell integration warning for wrapper files
body:
**Problem**: `wt config show` emitted a false positive "Found wt in ... but not detected as integration" warning for Nushell (and Fish) wrapper files. These files ARE the integration (they contain the shell function definition), not config files that source it, so `is_shell_integration_line()` correctly doesn't match their contents, but the warning logic didn't account for this.

**Fix**: Before emitting unmatched candidate warnings, collect paths already confirmed as integration files by `scan_shell_configs`. For Fish/Nushell (standalone wrapper files), any action means the file was recognized. For eval-based shells (Bash/Zsh), only `AlreadyExists` counts. Skip those paths when checking for unmatched candidates.

Fixes #1735
author: saschabratton

title: Add tend guidance for suggesting aliases on feature requests
body:
## Summary

- Adds guidance to the `running-tend` skill for suggesting tested aliases when triaging feature requests
- Covers when to suggest aliases (behavioral variants of existing commands), how to respond (draft, test, post with examples), and when to use shell functions vs `wt step` aliases

Prompted by #1726, where a shell alias solved the user's need for idempotent create-or-switch.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify skill file renders correctly and is loaded by tend workflows

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: worktrunk-bot
diff:
--- .claude/skills/running-tend/SKILL.md (+18/-34)
@@ -60,40 +60,24 @@ If surrounding lines also need updating, note that in your reply.
 
 When a bug may already be fixed, ask the reporter: `wt --version`
 
-### Feature requests addressable with aliases
-
-When triaging a feature request, check whether the requested behavior can be
-composed from existing commands using a `wt step` alias or a shell
-function/alias. Worktrunk intentionally keeps its flag surface small — aliases
-let users test workflows before features are added natively.
-
-If the feature can be addressed with an alias:
-
-1. **Draft the alias** — Write a `wt step` alias (in `[aliases]` config) or
-   shell function that achieves the requested behavior.
-2. **Test it** — Set up a temporary repo, configure the alias, and verify it
-   works for both the happy path and edge cases (e.g., branch exists vs.
-   doesn't exist).
-3. **Post the alias in your comment** — Include both the config snippet and
-   usage example. Link to the [aliases documentation](https://worktrunk.dev/step/#aliases)
-   so the user can learn more.
-4. **Mention the shell alternative** — A shell function is often more ergonomic
-   for commands that need positional arguments (aliases use `--var name=value`).
-
-Example comment structure:
-
-> This can be done today with a `wt step` alias. Add to `~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml`:
->
-> ```toml
-> [aliases]
-> sw = "wt switch -c {{ name }} 2>/dev/null || wt switch {{ name }}"
-> ```
->
-> Then: `wt step sw --var name=my-branch`
->
-> Or as a shell function: `wts() { wt switch -c "$1" 2>/dev/null || wt switch "$1"; }`
->
-> See [Aliases](https://worktrunk.dev/step/#aliases) for more details.
+### Suggesting Aliases for Feature Requests
+
+When a feature request can be addressed with a shell alias or `wt step` alias,
+compose and test one before responding. This lets users try workflows
+immediately rather than waiting for a native flag.
+
+**When to suggest an alias:**
+- The request is for a behavioral variant of an existing command (e.g.,
+  idempotent create-or-switch, auto-push after merge)
+- The behavior can be composed from existing `wt` commands
+- A shell one-liner or `wt step` alias covers the use case
+
+**How to respond:**
+1. Draft the alias (shell function or `wt step` alias, whichever fits better)
+2. Test it in a scratch repo — verify it works for both the happy path and the
+   fallback case
+3. Post the tested alias in the issue with usage examples
+4. Link to the [aliases docs](https://worktrunk.dev/step/#aliases) for context
 
 ## Per-Workflow References

title: feat: use append semantics for alias merging
body:
Alias merging now uses append semantics across all layers, matching how hooks merge:

**Within user config** (global + per-project): both run on name collision (global first). Uses `CommandConfig::merge_append()`.

**Across configs** (user + project): both run (user first, then project). Project commands always need approval — the old bypass that skipped approval when user had the same alias name is removed.

The alias value type changes from `String` to `CommandConfig` — the same type hooks use. This stores each command separately and enables the named-table TOML format for multi-command aliases.

Key changes:
- `merge_alias_maps()` and `UserConfig::aliases()` use `CommandConfig::merge_append()` on collision
- `step_alias()` iterates over `CommandConfig.commands()`, running each command separately (fail-fast)
- `approve_alias_commands()` approves each project-config command individually
- `alias_needs_approval()` simplified — always returns project commands if they exist

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of @max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

title: feat: use append semantics for alias merging
body:
Per-project alias merging changes from "override on collision" to "append" semantics, matching how hooks merge. When both global and per-project user configs define the same alias name, both commands run in sequence (global first, then per-project).

The alias value type changes from `String` to `CommandConfig` — the same type hooks use. This stores each command separately and enables the named-table TOML format for multi-command aliases. Key changes:

- `merge_alias_maps()` and `UserConfig::aliases()` use `CommandConfig::merge_append()` on collision
- `step_alias()` iterates over `CommandConfig.commands()`, running each command separately (fail-fast on first failure)
- `approve_alias_commands()` approves each project-config command individually via the existing batch approval system
- Project-vs-user merge stays as override (user wins) for security — only the global-vs-per-project *user* merge uses append

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of @max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

title: refactor: accept AsRef<OsStr> in Cmd::env for path compatibility
body:
`Cmd::env()` took `impl Into<String>`, forcing callers to convert paths with `.to_str().unwrap()`. Changed to `impl AsRef<OsStr>` to match `Command::env`'s interface — `&Path`, `PathBuf`, and `OsString` now work directly alongside string literals.

Internal storage changed from `Vec<(String, String)>` to `Vec<(OsString, OsString)>`. All existing callers (`"literal"`, `String`, `&str`) continue to work since `str: AsRef<OsStr>`.

Also fixes a stale example in `tests/CLAUDE.md` that referenced `repo.git_command(&[...])` instead of `repo.run_git(&[...])`.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of maximilian_
author: max-sixty

title: perf: parallelize copy-ignored with rayon
body:
Parallelizes the copy-ignored directory walks with rayon for `wt step copy-ignored`.

The copy logic (`copy_dir_recursive`, `remove_if_exists`, `create_symlink`) is extracted from `step_commands.rs` into a new `src/copy.rs` library module, making the production code accessible to benchmarks.

Benchmarking thread scaling (1, 2, 4, 8 threads × deep/wide directory layouts) showed performance peaks at 2–4 threads and regresses at 8+ due to SSD I/O contention. `copy_dir_recursive` now creates a dedicated 4-thread pool rather than using the global pool (which is sized at 2x CPU cores for network I/O).

The `benches/cow_copy.rs` benchmark compares serial vs production-parallel copying across two directory shapes: deep (Rust target/ — narrow tree) and wide (many sibling directories).

Part of #1720

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of maximilian_
author: worktrunk-bot

title: refactor: change test git_command() to return Cmd instead of Command
body:
The test infrastructure's `git_command()` returned `std::process::Command`, so test git commands bypassed `Cmd`'s debug logging (`$ git status [ctx]`) and timing traces (`[wt-trace]`). This changes it to return `worktrunk::shell_exec::Cmd`.

## Approach

Added `configure_git_env(Cmd, &Path) -> Cmd` alongside the existing `configure_git_cmd(&mut Command)`. The `Command` version is kept because `configure_wt_cmd` (which configures wt binary commands) still needs it — wt commands go through `Command`, not `Cmd`.

Key changes in `tests/common/mod.rs`:
- `TestRepoBase::git_command()` and `TestRepo::git_command()` now return `Cmd`
- All wrapper methods (`run_git`, `git_output`, `head_sha`, etc.) use `.run()` instead of `.output()`
- `BareRepoTest::new()` and `NestedBareRepoTest::new()` use `Cmd::new("git")` for init

247 call sites across 25 files converted: `.output()` → `.run()` and `.status()` → `.run()` on git command chains. Zero `Command::new("git")` remaining in the test directory.

Follows #1714 and #1716 which converted raw `Cmd::new("git")` and `Command::new("git")` in test bodies to `repo.run_command()`.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of maximilian_
author: max-sixty

title: fix: picker alt-r removal for detached worktrees
body:
Resolve the removal target by path (via `list_worktrees`) instead of always using `RemoveTarget::Branch`. Detached worktrees have no branch name, so `Branch("(detached)")` failed silently — the item vanished from the picker but the worktree persisted. Now any worktree item resolves to `RemoveTarget::Path`, with `Branch` as fallback for branch-only items.

Adds `test_do_removal_removes_detached_worktree` unit test. Verified interactively via tmux-cli.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of maximilian_

title: feat: structure-driven hook execution ordering
body:
Post-* hooks all run concurrently in the background. When one hook depends on another (e.g., `npm run build` needs `npm install` to finish first), there's no way to express ordering today.

Rather than per-command flags, the TOML data structure itself determines execution order:

- **String** — single command (unchanged)
- **Map** (table) — concurrent commands (unchanged)
- **List** (array) — serial pipeline, steps execute in order

```toml
[hooks]
post-start = [
    { install = "npm install" },
    { build = "npm run build", lint = "npm run lint" }
]
```

`install` runs first. After it completes, `build` and `lint` run concurrently. The entire pipeline runs in the background as one detached compound shell command — the user sees a summary line and nothing else.

**Key files:** `src/config/commands.rs` (HookStep enum, 3-form deserialization), `src/commands/hooks.rs` (compound shell command building, pipeline spawning), `src/commands/command_executor.rs` (PreparedStep).

**Design decisions:**
- Backward compatible — existing string/map configs route through the unchanged flat path. Pipeline path only activates for multi-step list configs.
- User and project pipelines run independently (user first, project second). No cross-source merging of pipeline structure.
- Pre-* hooks unchanged — always serial, fail-fast regardless of structure.
- `commands()` returns `impl Iterator` for zero-allocation flat access. `steps()` returns `&[HookStep]` for pipeline-aware execution.
- Compound shell commands wrap each step in `{ ...; }` to prevent operator precedence issues between steps.

**Testing:** Unit tests cover all deserialization forms, serialization round-trips, and flattening. Integration tests cover project pipelines, template variable expansion in pipelines, mixed user-pipeline + project-flat configs, pipeline serial ordering (marker file verification), and pipeline failure propagation.

+// ============================================================================
+// User Post-Commit Hook Tests (Background, via `wt step commit`)
+// ============================================================================
+
+/// Helper for step commit snapshots
+fn snapshot_step_commit(
+    test_name: &str,
+    repo: &TestRepo,
+    args: &[&str],
+    cwd: Option<&std::path::Path>,
+) {
+    let settings = setup_snapshot_settings(repo);
+    settings.bind(|| {
+        let mut cmd = make_snapshot_cmd(repo, "step", &[], cwd);
+        cmd.arg("commit");
+        cmd.args(args);
+        cmd.env(
+            "WORKTRUNK_COMMIT__GENERATION__COMMAND",
+            "cat >/dev/null && echo 'feat: test commit'",
+        );
+        assert_cmd_snapshot!(test_name, cmd);
+    });
+}
+
+#[rstest]
+fn test_user_post_commit_hook_executes(mut repo: TestRepo) {
+    // Create feature worktree with staged changes
+    let feature_wt = repo.add_worktree("feature");
+    fs::write(feature_wt.join("new_file.txt"), "content").unwrap();
+
+    // Write user config with post-commit hook
+    repo.write_test_config(
+        r#"[post-commit]
+notify = "echo 'USER_POST_COMMIT_RAN' > user_postcommit.txt"
+"#,
+    );
+
+    snapshot_step_commit("user_post_commit_executes", &repo, &[], Some(&feature_wt));
+
+    // Post-commit runs in background in the worktree where the commit happened
+    let marker_file = feature_wt.join("user_postcommit.txt");
+    wait_for_file_content(&marker_file);
+
+    let contents = fs::read_to_string(&marker_file).unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        contents.contains("USER_POST_COMMIT_RAN"),
+        "User post-commit hook should have run, got: {contents}"
+    );
+}
+
+#[rstest]
+fn test_user_post_commit_skipped_with_no_verify(mut repo: TestRepo) {
+    // Create feature worktree with staged changes
+    let feature_wt = repo.add_worktree("feature");
+    fs::write(feature_wt.join("new_file.txt"), "content").unwrap();
+
+    // Write user config with post-commit hook
+    repo.write_test_config(
+        r#"[post-commit]
+notify = "echo 'USER_POST_COMMIT_RAN' > user_postcommit.txt"
+"#,
+    );
+
+    snapshot_step_commit(
+        "user_post_commit_skipped_no_verify",
+        &repo,
+        &["--no-verify"],
+        Some(&feature_wt),
+    );
+
+    // Wait to ensure background hook would have had time to run
+    thread::sleep(SLEEP_FOR_ABSENCE_CHECK);
+
+    let marker_file = feature_wt.join("user_postcommit.txt");
+    assert!(
+        !marker_file.exists(),
+        "User post-commit hook should be skipped with --no-verify"
+    );
+}
+
+#[rstest]
+fn test_user_post_commit_failure_does_not_block_commit(mut repo: TestRepo) {
+    // Create feature worktree with staged changes
+    let feature_wt = repo.add_worktree("feature");
+    fs::write(feature_wt.join("new_file.txt"), "content").unwrap();
+
+    // Write user config with failing post-commit hook
+    repo.write_test_config(
+        r#"[post-commit]
+failing = "exit 1"
+"#,
+    );
+
+    snapshot_step_commit("user_post_commit_failure", &repo, &[], Some(&feature_wt));
+
+    // The commit should have succeeded despite post-commit hook failure

+        .args(["log", "--oneline", "-1"])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
+    assert!(
+        stdout.contains("feat: test commit"),
+        "Commit should have succeeded despite post-commit hook failure, got: {stdout}"
+    );
+}

title: fix: run pre/post-remove hooks during picker alt-r removal
body:
## Summary

- Run **pre-remove hooks** silently before picker removal — non-zero exit aborts the removal, preventing data loss from safety-check bypass
- Spawn **post-remove hooks** in background after successful removal — cleanup hooks (stopping services, cleaning ports) now fire as expected
- Add `run_hooks_silently()` helper for TUI contexts where writing to stderr would corrupt the display

Closes #1704

## Implementation

Hooks run inside the existing background thread that handles git operations (not on skim's main event loop, which would freeze the TUI). Pre-remove hooks use `run_hooks_silently()` which executes each command with suppressed stdout/stderr and checks exit codes. Post-remove hooks use the existing `spawn_background_hooks` infrastructure which logs to files.

Template variables match the normal `wt remove` flow: `{{ target }}`, `{{ target_worktree_path }}` for pre-remove; full removed worktree context for post-remove.

title: fix: picker alt-r removal — validate before removing, use fast path
body:
Two bugs in picker alt-r removal, plus consolidation of the removal code path.

**Validate before removing from list.** Previously, `invoke()` removed items from the picker list optimistically, then ran `prepare_worktree_removal` in a background thread. If validation failed (dirty worktree, locked, etc.), the item was already gone from the UI. Now `prepare_worktree_removal` runs synchronously in `invoke()` (~15-20ms) and the item is only removed if validation passes.

**Use the fast removal path.** The picker called `git worktree remove` (slow — worktree directory persists until the command finishes). Now `execute_removal` tries rename-to-trash first (instant on same filesystem), falling back to `git worktree remove` on cross-filesystem setups. This is the same `stage_worktree_removal` primitive the background handler uses. The foreground `--foreground` path also gets the fast path, which means it now handles non-writable subdirectories that previously caused `git worktree remove` to fail.

**Branch-only deletion.** `do_removal` previously returned `Ok(())` for `BranchOnly` items. Now it calls `delete_branch_if_safe`, matching what `wt remove` does.

Other changes: `prepare_worktree_removal` takes `current_path: Option<PathBuf>` for CWD-independence, CWD check uses `changed_directory` from `RemoveResult` instead of re-listing worktrees, test helper extracted, tests use `repo.run_command()`.

TUI-only code in `invoke()` can't be tested without interactive skim — verified via tmux-cli.

title: refactor: extract shared execute_removal for worktree removal
body:
The picker (`PickerCollector::execute_removal`) and output handler (`handle_removed_worktree_output`) independently implemented the same three git operations for worktree removal: fsmonitor stop, `remove_worktree`, `delete_branch_if_safe`. This extracts a shared `execute_removal` function in `commands::worktree` that both callers now use.

The return type `Result<Option<Result<BranchDeletionResult>>>` preserves caller-specific error handling — the outer Result covers worktree removal failures, while the inner Option+Result lets the picker silently ignore branch deletion errors and the handler process them for user-facing display. Background removal paths (which use a different rename-then-prune mechanism) are unchanged.

`RemovalDisplayInfo::from_actual` is renamed to `from_branch_result` to accept the pre-computed branch deletion result instead of calling `delete_branch_if_safe` itself.

title: fix: defer picker removal git ops to background thread
body:
Skim 0.20 calls `CommandCollector::invoke()` synchronously on the main event loop thread (confirmed by reading skim source at `reader.rs:87`). The previous implementation ran `prepare_worktree_removal` + `execute_removal` (5-8 git commands, ~300ms+) on that thread, freezing the TUI during in-place removal (alt-r).

Split `invoke()` into two phases:
- **Fast path** (main thread): read signal file, remove item from list, update CWD, stream remaining items — all <1ms
- **Background thread**: `prepare_worktree_removal` + `execute_removal` runs asynchronously via named `std::thread::Builder`

Also fixes CWD comparison to use `dunce::canonicalize` for macOS `/var` vs `/private/var` symlink resolution.

Trade-off: item disappears from picker before git confirms removal. If background removal fails (rare — dirty worktree, locked), item is gone from list but worktree still exists. User can re-open picker to see it.

Ref #1695

body:
The alt-r keybinding for in-place worktree removal has poor UX — cursor resets to the top after each removal due to a skim 0.20 limitation (#1695). This hides the feature from the picker legend and documentation so users don't discover it until fixed. The keybinding itself remains functional for power users who already know about it.

title: fix: disable picker timeout in tests to prevent macOS CI flakiness
body:
## Problem

The `test_switch_picker_with_multiple_worktrees` test failed on macOS CI ([run](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/23455369236)) with a snapshot mismatch — a `·` stale placeholder appeared in the Upstream column for the `main` worktree.

The picker has a 500ms default data collection timeout (`[switch-picker] timeout-ms`). On slow macOS CI runners, the Upstream task sometimes doesn't complete within this window, causing `render_list_item_stale()` to show `·` instead of an empty cell. The triggering commit (`a437238e`) was docs-only, confirming this is a pre-existing timing flake.

## Solution

Disable the picker timeout (`timeout-ms = 0`) in all picker snapshot tests via `write_test_config`. This ensures all task results arrive before rendering, making snapshots deterministic regardless of CI runner speed.

Added a `disable_picker_timeout()` helper that appends the config to the test config file, working correctly both when the file is empty (most tests) and when it already has content (`test_switch_picker_respects_list_config`).

## Testing

- `test_switch_picker_with_multiple_worktrees` passes locally
- Fix applied to all 8 picker tests that use snapshot assertions

---

title: docs: changelog entry for hook rationalization
body:
Adds a changelog entry for #1679 (hook rationalization) to the 0.31.0 release notes. Covers the rename, new hook, post-merge behavior change, and deprecation path.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max-sixty_
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- CHANGELOG.md (+2/-0)
@@ -4,6 +4,8 @@
 
 ### Improved
 
+- **Hooks rationalized**: Every lifecycle event now has a symmetric `pre-` (blocking) / `post-` (background) pair. This required one rename: `post-create` → `pre-start`, reflecting that it runs *before* `post-start` as a blocking dependency step. A new `post-commit` hook fires in the background after commits (including squash commits during merge). `post-merge` is now background instead of blocking, consistent with all other `post-*` hooks. Configs using `post-create` get a deprecation warning on any `wt` command; run `wt config update` to rename automatically. The old name continues to work during the deprecation period. ([#1679](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1679), closes [#1670](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/1670))
+
 - **Hook template variables consolidated**: Bare variables (`branch`, `worktree_path`, `commit`) now consistently point to the Active worktree — the destination for switch/create, the source for merge/remove. New directional variables (`{{ base }}`, `{{ base_worktree_path }}`, `{{ target_worktree_path }}`, `{{ cwd }}`) give hooks explicit access to both sides of two-worktree operations. (Breaking: `{{ worktree_path }}` changed in pre-switch for existing worktrees and in post-merge — use `{{ cwd }}` or `{{ base_worktree_path }}` for the previous behavior.) [Docs](https://worktrunk.dev/hook/) ([#1655](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1655), [#1660](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1660), [#1663](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1663))

Non-interactive environments show the config to add manually. ([#1656](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1656), thanks @seakayone for reporting [#1279](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/1279))

title: fix: load project config from primary worktree in bare repos
body:
## Problem

In bare repository layouts, project config (`.config/wt.toml`) placed in the primary worktree (e.g., `main/`) is not found when running commands from the bare repo root directory.

This happens because `ProjectConfig::load()` resolves the config path via `current_worktree().root()`, which for bare repos at the root runs `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` — this fails (no working tree), so it falls back to the bare directory itself. The config is only found if it happens to be placed in the bare root.

```
myproject/
├── .git/           # bare repository
├── main/           # primary worktree — config lives here
│   └── .config/
│       └── wt.toml # ← not found when running from myproject/
├── feature/
└── bugfix/
```

## Solution

When no `.config/wt.toml` is found at the current worktree root and the repository is bare, fall back to checking the primary worktree (default branch worktree) for the config file. This matches user expectations since the primary worktree is the natural home for shared project config in bare repo setups.

## Testing

Added `test_bare_repo_project_config_found_from_bare_root` integration test that:
1. Creates a bare repo with a primary worktree containing `.config/wt.toml` with a post-start hook
2. Runs `wt switch --create` from the bare repo root (not from within a worktree)
3. Verifies the hook from the primary worktree's config executes

---
Closes #1691 — automated triage

title: fix: background post-merge hook tests race condition
body:
## Problem

`test_hook_post_merge_target_is_current_branch` fails on CI because it reads `target-branch.txt` immediately after `wt hook post-merge --yes` returns, but since efad9312 changed `post-merge` to run in the background, the file hasn't been written yet.

Three merge tests (`test_merge_post_merge_command_success`, `test_merge_post_merge_runs_with_nothing_to_merge`, `test_merge_post_merge_runs_from_main_branch`) have the same latent race — `wt merge` also spawns post-merge hooks in the background — but happen to pass due to timing.

## Solution

- **approval_ui test**: Add `--foreground` flag to `wt hook post-merge` so the hook completes before the assertion. This is the correct flag for tests that need synchronous hook execution.
- **merge tests**: Replace `assert!(marker_file.exists(), ...)` with `wait_for_file(&marker_file)` which polls with exponential backoff (up to 15s timeout), matching the pattern used by other background-hook tests in the codebase.

## Testing

All 11 `post_merge` tests pass locally.

title: fix(ci): acknowledge when PR author responds to bot review concerns
body:
## Summary

- Fix silent exit when a PR author responds to review concerns the bot raised
- Add explicit guidance in the mention workflow prompt that author responses to bot review concerns are "directed at" the bot and should be acknowledged

## Evidence

**Run 23425832678** (claude-mention on PR #1676): The bot reviewed PR #1676 and raised 3 concerns about behavioral differences in the workflow migration. The author ([max-sixty](https://github.com/max-sixty)) posted a [detailed response](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1676#issuecomment-4108507152) explaining all three are handled inside `tend@v1`. The bot read the comment, internally concluded "The concerns I raised have been addressed with a clear explanation. No further action needed" — but never posted a reply. The run was marked FAILURE.

**Root cause**: The mention prompt says "Only respond if the comment is directed at you, asks a question you can help with, or requests changes you can make." The bot interpreted the enumeration narrowly — the author's response wasn't asking a question or requesting changes, and the bot didn't treat it as "directed at" the bot despite it being a direct response to the bot's review.

**Fix**: Add a sentence clarifying that comments responding to the bot's review concerns are directed at the bot: "A comment that responds to concerns you raised in a review is directed at you — briefly acknowledge that the concerns are resolved (or explain why they aren't)."

**Gate assessment**:
- Evidence level: Critical (clearly wrong outcome — author got silence after responding to bot review)
- Occurrences: 1 (sufficient for Critical)
- Change type: Targeted fix (one sentence added to prompt)
- Both gates pass

title: fix: suppress spurious mismatch warning for detached worktree switches
body:
When switching to a detached worktree by path (`wt switch /path/to/worktree`), a spurious "Branch-worktree mismatch" warning appeared. Phase 2b of `plan_switch` was using the directory name as the `branch` field in `SwitchPlan::Existing`, then `handle_switch` fed that fake branch name to `path_mismatch()` which computed an expected path from a non-existent branch.

Makes `SwitchPlan::Existing.branch` and `SwitchBranchInfo.branch` use `Option<String>` where `None` means detached HEAD. This matches the pattern already used by `worktree_display_name` (branch `None` → "detached"), `RemoveResult` (`branch_name: Option<String>`), and `CommandContext` (`branch: Option<&str>`). Callers skip `path_mismatch` when branch is `None`, and derive display names from the path for output.

Also removes the now-redundant `test_switch_detached_worktree_by_path` (absolute path variant) since `test_switch_detached_worktree_by_relative_path` covers the same case without volatile temp paths in snapshot metadata.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of @max-sixty_

title: refactor: inline worktree removal into callers
body:
The three `handle_remove` / `handle_remove_path` / `handle_remove_current` functions in `src/commands/worktree/remove.rs` were near-identical wrappers that called `Repository::current()` and then `repo.prepare_worktree_removal()` with a different `RemoveTarget` variant. Every call site already had a `&Repository` in scope, making the wrapper purely redundant — it re-discovered the repository on every call (including inside a loop in `validate_remove_targets`).

This PR inlines the calls, deleting `remove.rs` entirely. In `validate_remove_targets`, `BranchDeletionMode::from_flags()` is now hoisted before the loop instead of recomputed per iteration.

title: fix(skills): fix jq pipe precedence bug causing duplicate approvals
body:
## Summary

- Fixes jq pipe precedence bug in `LAST_REVIEW_SHA` query that caused the bot to miss its own prior approvals and post duplicates
- The expression `.body | length > 0 or .state == "APPROVED"` evaluates `.state` against the body string (not the review object) when the body is empty, because jq's `|` has lower precedence than `or`
- Fix: parenthesize as `(.body | length) > 0` to scope the pipe correctly

## Evidence

| Run | PR | Effect |
|-----|-----|--------|
| 23421108245 | #1665 | `LAST_REVIEW_SHA` silently set to empty |
| 23421547291 | #1676 | Duplicate approval (1st of 2) |
| 23423087012 | #1676 | Duplicate approval (2nd of 2) |

Reproduction:
```bash
BOT_LOGIN="worktrunk-bot"
# Bug (fails with "expected an object but got: string"):
gh pr view 1676 --json reviews \
  --jq "[.reviews[] | select(.author.login == \"$BOT_LOGIN\" and (.body | length > 0 or .state == \"APPROVED\"))] | last | .commit.oid // empty"

# Fix (works correctly):
gh pr view 1676 --json reviews \
  --jq "[.reviews[] | select(.author.login == \"$BOT_LOGIN\" and ((.body | length) > 0 or .state == \"APPROVED\"))] | last | .commit.oid // empty"
```

## Test plan

- [x] Verified fix returns correct SHA with `gh pr view 1676 --json reviews`
- [x] Verified original expression reproduces the error
- [ ] Monitor next review runs for correct `LAST_REVIEW_SHA` detection

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

 # The REST API (`gh api .../reviews`) uses `.commit_id` — don't confuse the two.

-  --jq "[.reviews[] | select(.author.login == \"$BOT_LOGIN\" and (.body | length > 0 or .state == \"APPROVED\"))] | last | .commit.oid // empty")
+  --jq "[.reviews[] | select(.author.login == \"$BOT_LOGIN\" and ((.body | length) > 0 or .state == \"APPROVED\"))] | last | .commit.oid // empty")
 ```

title: feat!: rationalize hooks — rename post-create, add post-commit, background post-merge
body:
Implements the hook rationalization from #1670, establishing a symmetric `pre-` (blocking) / `post-` (background) pattern for every lifecycle event.

## Changes

**Rename `post-create` → `pre-start`**: The old name suggested it ran *after* creation, but it actually runs *before* `post-start` as a blocking dependency step. Both names accepted for one release cycle — config deprecation detection, migration file generation, `wt config update` support, and CLI alias all in place. `merge_with` folds old-name hooks into new-name so cross-config combinations don't silently drop hooks.

**Add `post-commit` hook**: New background hook firing after successful commits (including squash commits), completing the commit lifecycle pair. Included in approval batches for `wt step commit`, `wt step squash`, and `wt merge`.

**Change `post-merge` to background**: Was blocking with `Warn` strategy, now runs in background like all other `post-` hooks. `--foreground` flag available for debugging.

The hook table is now a clean symmetric grid:

| Event | `pre-` (blocking) | `post-` (background) |
|-------|-------------------|---------------------|
| start | `pre-start` | `post-start` |
| switch | `pre-switch` | `post-switch` |
| commit | `pre-commit` | `post-commit` |
| merge | `pre-merge` | `post-merge` |
| remove | `pre-remove` | `post-remove` |

## Testing

868 lib + 483 bin + 1227 integration tests pass, all 13 lint checks pass. The deprecation has 23 dedicated unit tests covering detection at all three config scopes, migration, empty table filtering, cross-config merge safety, and integration with `wt config show` / `wt config update`.

Closes #1670

title: feat: drop low-priority columns when Summary needs space
body:
When Summary is present but hasn't reached 50 chars, columns with effective priority lower than Summary's are dropped to reclaim space. The threshold is graduated by priority distance — columns within 4 priority levels of Summary (Commit, Time, Message) use a 50-char threshold, while columns further away (e.g., no-data Path at 7+10=17 via EMPTY_PENALTY) use MAX_SUMMARY (70).

Previously, only no-data columns could be dropped (via a separate loop), and Message had its own drop-at-40 check. Now both mechanisms are unified into a single priority-based filter in one loop. The EMPTY_PENALTY that already existed for allocation ordering now also drives the drop decision — no special `has_data` check needed.

Drop order is highest effective priority first: Message (13) → Time (12) → Commit (11) → no-data Path (17, dropped at wider widths since gap > 4).

title: feat: in-place worktree removal in picker via alt-r
body:
Pressing alt-r in the `wt switch` picker now removes the selected worktree in-place without leaving the picker. The item disappears from the list and the user can continue selecting or removing more worktrees.

Uses skim's `CommandCollector` trait with a signal file: `execute-silent` writes the selected item's identifier, then `reload` triggers the collector which performs removal and streams the updated item list. This avoids exiting and re-entering the picker for each removal.

Key design decisions:
- **`execute_removal()`** extracted to `remove.rs` as shared silent removal logic (fsmonitor stop → `remove_worktree` → `delete_branch_if_safe`) — no output, no hooks, no cd directives. The picker calls this directly instead of `handle_remove_output`, which would corrupt skim's TUI with stderr output and emit cd directives mid-picker.
- **Detached HEAD support**: the collector looks up worktree data from the shared items list to detect detached worktrees and uses `handle_remove_path` (path-based removal) instead of `handle_remove` (branch-based). The `retain` filter also matches by worktree path for detached items to avoid removing all `"(detached)"` entries.
- **Signal file cleanup** handled by `PreviewState::Drop`, covering normal exit, ctrl-c, and crash paths.
- **Cursor resets to first item** after reload — a skim 0.20 limitation documented in the code. The fix path is skim 4.0's `Action::Custom(ActionCallback)`.

Safe removal only (no `-D`, no `-f`). Dirty worktrees and unmerged branches are silently skipped (item stays in the list).

title: docs: document --yes scope and non-interactive hint patterns
body:
## Summary

- Documents the design distinction between **workflow prompts** (`--yes` bypasses: hook approval, config update) and **setup prompts** (`--yes` has no effect: LLM config, shell integration)
- Documents the three non-TTY degradation patterns: hint (repeats every run), silent skip (when separate fallback exists), error (only for unsafe-to-skip workflow prompts)
- Key invariant: hints in non-TTY mode must not set skip flags, and `--yes` means "I anticipated this prompt"

Added as a new section in the `writing-user-outputs` skill, between command suggestion patterns and blank line rules.

## Test plan

- [x] Documentation-only change, no code affected
- [x] Verified section reads coherently in context

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max-sixty_

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- .claude/skills/writing-user-outputs/SKILL.md (+38/-0)
@@ -459,6 +459,44 @@ Use `suggest_command()` from `worktrunk::styling` for proper shell escaping.
 **Section titles:** For sectioned output (`wt hook show`, `wt config show`), use
 `format_heading()` from `worktrunk::styling` (documented above).
 
+## Interactive Prompts vs Non-Interactive Hints
+
+Prompts and hints serve different purposes and have different `--yes` behavior.
+
+**Prompts** are expected steps in a workflow — the user ran a command knowing
+it would ask for confirmation. Hook approval during `wt merge`, config update
+confirmation, shell install confirmation. `--yes` bypasses these because the
+user anticipated the question and wants to pre-answer it (e.g., in CI).
+
+**Setup prompts** are unexpected — the user ran `wt merge` and got asked about
+LLM config or shell integration they didn't know about. `--yes` must NOT
+bypass these. A user passing `--yes` to skip hook approval did not consent to
+auto-configuring their shell. In non-interactive mode (no TTY), these should
+degrade to a hint or be skipped silently — never error.
+
+| Type | Example | `--yes` | Non-TTY behavior |
+|------|---------|---------|------------------|
+| Workflow prompt | Hook approval, config update | Bypasses | Error (`NotInteractive`) |
+| Setup prompt | LLM config, shell integration | No effect | Hint or silent skip |
+
+**Non-TTY degradation patterns:**
+
+- **Hint** — when the user benefits from knowing about the option on every run.
+  Shell integration hint: `↳ To enable automatic cd, run wt config shell install`
+- **Silent skip** — when a hint would be noise. Commit generation setup prompt
+  skips silently because a separate fallback hint (`emit_hint_if_needed`)
+  already covers the unconfigured case on every commit.
+- **Error** — only for workflow prompts where proceeding without consent is
+  unsafe (hook approval). The error includes a hint for the fix:
+  `↳ To skip prompts in CI/CD, add --yes`
+
+**Key invariants:**
+
+- Hints shown in non-TTY mode must NOT set skip flags — hints are not prompts,
+  and should repeat on every non-TTY run
+- `--yes` means "I anticipated this prompt" — it applies to workflow prompts
+  the user chose to invoke, not to setup/config discovery prompts
+
 ## Blank Line Principles
 
 **Core principle:** When presenting the user with text to read and consider, add

title: feat(config): add copy-ignored exclude patterns
body:
Add configurable exclusions to `wt step copy-ignored`, and make the command safer by skipping known tool-state directories by default.

- `wt step copy-ignored` always skips built-in excluded directories (VCS metadata like `.jj/`, `.hg/` and tool-state like `.conductor/`, `.worktrees/`)
- Users can add more excludes with `[step.copy-ignored] exclude = [...]` in user config, per-project user overrides, or project config (`.config/wt.toml`)
- All exclusion sources are combined; scalar config values replace, everything else appends (global first)

Closes #1653

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of maximilian_

title: docs: changelog and migration note for template variable redesign
body:
Adds changelog entry for the template variable redesign (breaking + improved) and a migration section in the hook docs explaining what changed and how to update existing hooks.

Ref #1633

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of @max-sixty_
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- CHANGELOG.md (+10/-0)
@@ -1,5 +1,15 @@
 # Changelog
 
+## Unreleased
+
+### Breaking
+
+- **Hook template variable `worktree_path` changed meaning** in two hook types: in **pre-switch** (existing worktrees), `{{ worktree_path }}` now points to the destination worktree instead of the source; in **post-merge**, it now points to the feature worktree (active) instead of the merge target. Use `{{ base_worktree_path }}` or `{{ cwd }}` for the previous behavior. ([#1655](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1655), [#1660](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1660))
+
+### Improved
+
+- **Directional template variables for hooks**: New `{{ base }}`, `{{ base_worktree_path }}`, `{{ target }}`, `{{ target_worktree_path }}`, and `{{ cwd }}` variables give hooks explicit access to both sides of two-worktree operations (switch, merge, remove). Bare variables (`branch`, `worktree_path`, `commit`) consistently point to the active branch — the destination for switch/create, the source for merge/remove. ([#1655](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1655), [#1660](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1660), [#1663](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1663))
+
 ## 0.30.1
 
 ### Fixed

title: fix: allow removing detached HEAD worktrees from picker
body:
## Problem

The switch picker (`wt switch` TUI) fails to remove detached HEAD worktrees when pressing `alt-r`. All detached worktrees resolve to the identifier `"(detached)"`, which is then passed to branch-based removal — causing the error:

```
✗ No branch named (detached)
```

Additionally, there was no CLI way to remove a detached worktree from outside it (`wt remove @` only works from within the worktree).

## Solution

Add path-based worktree resolution as a fallback in `resolve_worktree_arg` for the `Remove` context. When branch-name lookup fails, the argument is tried as a filesystem path. This means:

- **CLI**: `wt remove /path/to/detached-worktree` now works
- **Picker**: Uses `handle_remove_path()` — the same codepath as the CLI

The picker doesn't do anything the CLI can't do.

## Changes

- `resolve_worktree_arg`: path-based fallback for `Remove` context (absolute or relative paths)
- `handle_remove_path`: new function for path-based worktree removal
- `validate_remove_targets`: handles `branch: None` (detached worktrees) via path-based removal
- Picker uses `handle_remove_path` for detached worktrees instead of directly calling `prepare_worktree_removal`
- CLI help text updated: arg description says "Branch name or path", detached HEAD section added to `--help`

## Testing

- Existing test: `wt remove (detached)` → fails with "No branch named (detached)"
- New test: `wt remove /path/to/worktree` → successfully removes detached worktree
- All existing tests pass

Thanks to @mjakl for reporting in #1661

---
Closes #1661

title: feat: complete template variable redesign follow-ups
body:
Follow-up fixes and documentation for the template variable redesign (#1655, #1660).

**Code fixes:**
- `commit` derivation now uses `rev-parse <branch>` instead of `rev-parse HEAD`, so `{{ commit }}` follows the Active branch
- `base` / `base_worktree_path` now available in post-switch for existing switches (previously only creates)
- post-remove `{{ target }}` now correctly resolves to the destination branch, not the removed branch

**Documentation:**
- Restructured template variable table — Active vars grouped first, directional vars second, repo-level vars last
- Added arrive/depart table explaining what bare vars, `base`, and `target` point to per operation
- Documented when `cwd` differs from `worktree_path` (pre-switch existing, post-remove, post-merge with removal)

**Tests:** 4 new integration tests for directional var semantics.

Ref #1633

title: feat!: point bare template vars to Active worktree identity
body:
Phase 2 of the template variable redesign. **Breaking change**: `worktree_path` now points to the Active worktree (the subject of the operation) rather than always the execution directory.

## Changes

**pre-switch (existing worktrees):** `worktree_path` now points to the destination worktree, not the source. Use `base_worktree_path` or `cwd` for the source.

**pre-switch (creates):** `worktree_path` keeps its default (source worktree = cwd). The planned destination path isn't available until after pre-switch hooks complete.

**post-merge:** `worktree_path` now points to the feature worktree (Active), not the merge target. Use `target_worktree_path` or `cwd` for where code landed. Feature identity (path, name, commit) is captured before removal so it's available even after the worktree is deleted.

**Empty extra_vars removal mechanism removed** — it was added and then removed in the same PR as the pre-switch create approach changed.

## The model

- **Arriving ops** (switch, create): Active = destination
- **Departing ops** (merge, remove): Active = source

Mnemonic: *"Are you going there, or is it going away?"*

Ref #1633

title: feat: offer to fix worktree-path for bare repos with hidden directory names
body:
When a bare repo lives at a hidden path like `.git` or `.bare`, the `{{ repo }}` template variable resolves to that directory name, producing broken worktree paths (e.g., `project/.git.feature-auth` instead of `project/feature-auth`).

This adds detection and an interactive prompt on `wt switch` (and the interactive picker) offering to set a project-level `worktree-path` override. No heuristics — the user makes an explicit choice, saved to their config.

**Interactive prompt:**
```
▲ Bare repo at project/.git — worktrees will be at project/.git.feature-auth

❯ Configure worktree-path to place worktrees at project/feature-auth? [y/N/?]
```

**Non-interactive** (piped stdin, CI, scripts) shows the config to add:
```
▲ Bare repo at project/.git — worktrees will be at project/.git.feature-auth
↳ To place worktrees at project/feature-auth, add to ~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml:
   ┃ [projects."~/project/.git"]
   ┃ worktree-path = "{{ repo_path }}/../{{ branch | sanitize }}"
```

`--yes` has no effect on this prompt — it modifies user config, which requires interactive confirmation. Declining saves a skip flag in the repo's git config so the prompt won't recur.

The `?` preview shows the exact TOML that would be written. Template variable detection uses `minijinja::undeclared_variables()` (not hand-rolled parsing).

**Testing:** 2 non-PTY snapshot tests + 3 PTY snapshot tests (accept, decline, preview). Template detection has 8 unit tests. All existing tests pass.

Thanks to @seakayone for reporting in #1279.

Closes #1279

title: feat: add directional template vars to all two-worktree hooks
body:
Phase 1 of the template variable redesign discussed in #1633. Adds directional vars (`base`, `target`, `target_worktree_path`, `cwd`) to all two-worktree hooks — non-breaking additions only, no existing behavior changes.

## New variables

- **`cwd`** — execution directory, always exists on disk (all hooks). Enables the Active model in Phase 2 where `worktree_path` becomes identity rather than execution context.
- **`target_worktree_path`** — target worktree path, added alongside existing `target` for merge hooks (pre-merge, post-merge) and remove hooks (pre-remove, post-remove).
- **`base` / `base_worktree_path`** — source branch/worktree, added to pre-switch hooks. For existing destinations, `target` / `target_worktree_path` are also provided.

These follow the "Active" model where each two-worktree operation has a base (source/origin) and target (destination) side:
- **Arriving ops** (switch, create): Active = destination. `base` = where you came from.
- **Departing ops** (merge, remove): Active = source. `target` = where it's going.

Mnemonic: *"Are you going there, or is it going away?"*

Phase 2 (separate PR) will change bare var semantics so `worktree_path` consistently points to the Active worktree, with `cwd` as the execution-context escape hatch.

Ref #1633

title: fix(ci): set trigger_phrase and provide review-response prompt
body:
The `claude-code-action` defaults `trigger_phrase` to `@claude`. When `claude-review.yaml` handled `pull_request_review` events on bot-authored PRs, it passed an empty prompt (`''`), causing the action to fall back to trigger detection — which looked for `@claude` in the review text. Since nobody writes `@claude` in reviews, the action always skipped. This meant formal reviews on bot-authored PRs were silently ignored by `claude-review` (only handled incidentally via `claude-mention`'s `pull_request_review_comment` path when inline comments were present).

Two fixes:
- Set `trigger_phrase: "@worktrunk-bot"` in both interactive workflows (`claude-review`, `claude-mention`) so the action never defaults to `@claude`
- Provide a non-empty prompt for the `pull_request_review` path in `claude-review.yaml`, so the action runs the prompt directly instead of falling back to trigger detection

The five automated workflows (ci-fix, hourly, nightly, renovate, triage) are unchanged — they all provide explicit prompts, making `trigger_phrase` irrelevant.

Evidence from PR #1557: run 23132865052 logged `No trigger was met for @claude` / `Context prompt: NO PROMPT` / `No trigger found, skipping remaining steps` despite the workflow's `if:` condition correctly selecting the event.

title: fix: prevent `wt list` hang from fsmonitor daemon pipe inheritance
body:
`git fsmonitor--daemon start` forks a long-lived daemon that inherits piped stdio file descriptors from `Command::output()`. The daemon holds the write end of the pipe open indefinitely, so `read_to_end()` blocks forever waiting for EOF that never comes. This causes `wt list` to hang at the "(loading...)" stage on macOS with builtin fsmonitor enabled.

Confirmed via `sample` — one rayon worker thread stuck in `start_fsmonitor_daemon_at` → `Cmd::run` → `Command::output` → `read` syscall. The specific daemon (PID 33559, watching `worktrunk.jj-struct`) held the same pipe FD (`0x33a071def7d89bb5`) as the frozen `wt` process.

Fix: use `Command::status()` with `Stdio::null()` instead of `Cmd::run()`. No pipes = nothing to inherit. Also removes the unused `start_fsmonitor_daemon()` wrapper — only `start_fsmonitor_daemon_at` had callers.

title: fix(skills): prevent tracking comment overwrite in review-reviewers
body:
## Summary

- Fixes the tracking comment overwrite pattern in the review-reviewers skill (5 occurrences across runs)
- Adds explicit instructions to download existing comment body and append new findings, rather than replacing
- Restructures the comment format template so each run gets its own `## Run` heading for clearer history

## Root cause

The skill said "edit it to include any new findings" but the bot interpreted "edit" as "replace the body with new content." Each hourly run overwrote the previous run's per-incident detail (run IDs, session files, evidence descriptions), leaving only aggregate counts. This degraded the historical evidence trail needed for accurate gate evaluation.

| 23387421034 | Same pattern — lost per-occurrence detail from prior runs |
| 3 earlier runs | Documented in tracking issue #1611 (4 prior occurrences) |

- Evidence level: **High** (consistent pattern, 5 occurrences)
- Change type: **Targeted fix** (adds clarifying instructions + example commands to existing section)
- Both gates pass

body:
Aliases configured in user/project config now appear as completable subcommands when tab-completing `wt step <TAB>`. Previously, only built-in step commands (commit, push, rebase, etc.) appeared since aliases are dynamic — they're resolved at runtime via the `external_subcommand` catch-all, which clap's completion engine doesn't know about.

The fix injects alias names as synthetic clap subcommands in the completion-only command tree. Each alias subcommand includes `--dry-run`, `--yes`/`-y`, and `--var` flags matching the real alias flag parser. Aliases that shadow built-in step commands are skipped. Shells that support it (fish, zsh) show the alias template as help text.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of @max-sixty_

title: fix(skills): document single review comment fetch endpoint
body:
## Summary

- Add the correct GitHub API endpoint for fetching a single PR review comment to the running-in-ci skill
- The bot consistently uses `pulls/{number}/comments/{id}` (404) instead of `pulls/comments/{id}` (correct)

## Root cause

The running-in-ci skill documents the reply endpoint (`pulls/{number}/comments/{id}/replies`) but not the read endpoint. The bot extrapolates the wrong path by combining the PR number with the comment ID, producing a nonexistent endpoint.

## Evidence

**6 occurrences** across sessions (High confidence):
- Run 23278574410 (session c8ae6db2): 404 on comment fetch, fell back to listing all comments
- Run 23279109424 (session 4d1bbc49): same pattern
- Run 23366805756 (session 8b460692): `repos/max-sixty/worktrunk/pulls/1625/comments/2968389530` → 404, fell back to listing all
- Plus 3 additional occurrences documented in tracking issue #1611

PR #1632 fixed the REPO-variable variant of 404 churn but not this endpoint-path variant.

## Gate assessment

- **Evidence level**: High (consistent pattern, 6 total occurrences across runs)
- **Change type**: Targeted fix (3-line addition documenting correct endpoint)
- **Both gates pass**: 6 occurrences exceeds the 2–3 threshold for High evidence; targeted fix needs Normal evidence bar

title: Summary reclaims space from no-data columns
body:
After Summary's initial expansion, columns where `has_data()` is false are dropped (lowest priority first) and their space reclaimed for Summary.

In progressive mode, only Path can be no-data — when all worktree paths are predictable from branch names (no `branch_worktree_mismatch`). At moderate terminal widths (~170 chars), Path consumed ~30 chars of redundant content, leaving Summary truncated and dropping Message entirely. At wide terminals, both columns still coexist.

The mechanism is general (drops any no-data column, lowest priority first) but currently only fires for Path. It slots into the existing post-allocation sequence between Summary's initial expansion and the Message threshold check.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of @max-sixty_
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- src/commands/list/layout.rs (+263/-2)
@@ -112,12 +112,20 @@
 //!    - Within the visibility gate, follows normal two-tier priority
 //!      (BranchDiff: 6/16, CiStatus: 5/15)
 //!
-//! 2. **Summary** - Flexible sizing with post-allocation expansion
+//! 2. **No-data columns** yield to Summary
+//!    - After Summary's initial expansion, columns where `has_data()` is false
+//!      are dropped (lowest priority first) and their space reclaimed for Summary
+//!    - Currently only Path can be no-data in progressive mode (when all paths
+//!      are predictable from branch names, i.e., no branch-worktree mismatch)
+//!    - When Path has data (mismatch exists), it is kept at priority 7
+//!
+//! 3. **Summary** - Flexible sizing with post-allocation expansion
 //!    - Allocated at priority 10 with minimum width 10
 //!    - After all columns allocated, expands up to 70 using leftover space
+//!    - Reclaims no-data columns before Message drop
 //!    - Expands BEFORE Message, so Summary gets priority for space
 //!
-//! 3. **Message** - Flexible sizing, gated on Summary readability
+//! 4. **Message** - Flexible sizing, gated on Summary readability
 //!    - Allocated at priority 13 with minimum width 10
 //!    - **Only kept if Summary reaches 40 chars** — below that, Summary needs
 //!      all flexible space and Message is dropped (its space reclaimed for Summary)
@@ -751,6 +759,35 @@ fn allocate_columns_with_priority(
         max_summary_len = summary_col.width;
     }
 
+    // Drop no-data columns if Summary hasn't reached its max. Columns without
+    // data are showing empty/redundant content (e.g., Path when all paths are
+    // predictable from branch names) and should yield space to Summary.
+    while max_summary_len > 0 && max_summary_len < MAX_SUMMARY {
+        // Find the lowest-priority no-data column (highest base_priority value)
+        let drop_pos = pending
+            .iter()
+            .enumerate()
+            .filter(|(_, col)| !col.spec.kind.has_data(&metadata.data_flags))
+            .max_by_key(|(_, col)| col.spec.base_priority)
+            .map(|(i, _)| i);
+
+        let Some(pos) = drop_pos else { break };
+
+        let reclaimed = pending[pos].width + spacing;
+        pending.remove(pos);
+        remaining += reclaimed;
+
+        if let Some(summary_col) = pending
+            .iter_mut()
+            .find(|col| col.spec.kind == ColumnKind::Summary)
+        {
+            let expansion = remaining.min(MAX_SUMMARY - summary_col.width);
+            summary_col.width += expansion;
+            remaining -= expansion;
+            max_summary_len = summary_col.width;
+        }
+    }
+
     // Drop Message if Summary didn't reach the readability threshold, reclaiming
     // its width (+ spacing) so Summary can expand further.
     if max_summary_len > 0
@@ -1675,6 +1712,230 @@ mod tests {

title: fix(skills): inline REPO definition to prevent API 404 churn
body:
## Summary

- Inline `REPO=$(gh repo view ...)` into each code block that uses `$REPO` in the review-reviewers skill, instead of a standalone block (env vars don't persist across Bash tool calls)

## Root cause

The review-reviewers bot repeatedly guesses the repo name incorrectly (e.g., "anthropics/worktrunk" instead of "max-sixty/worktrunk"), causing 404 errors and wasted API calls. The skill referenced `$REPO` in code blocks without defining it, leaving the bot to guess.

## Approach

Each Bash tool call starts a fresh shell — env vars set in one call don't persist to the next. The fix inlines `REPO=$(gh repo view ...)` into each code block that uses `$REPO`, matching the pattern already used in `review-pr/SKILL.md`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Next review-reviewers run uses `$REPO` from `gh repo view` instead of guessing
- [ ] No more 404 churn from wrong repo names in future sessions

+/// Test that worktrunk works correctly when `worktree.useRelativePaths` is enabled.
+///
+/// Git 2.48+ supports `worktree.useRelativePaths`, which stores relative paths in the
+/// `.git` file of linked worktrees instead of absolute paths. This makes worktree
+/// directories relocatable. We verify that worktrunk's path handling (which canonicalizes
+/// paths internally) works correctly with this configuration.
+///
+/// See: https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/1630
+#[rstest]
+fn test_switch_with_relative_worktree_paths(repo: TestRepo) {
+    // Enable relative paths for worktrees
+    repo.run_git(&["config", "worktree.useRelativePaths", "true"]);
+
+    // Create a new worktree via wt switch --create
+    snapshot_switch(
+        "switch_create_relative_paths",
+        &repo,
+        &["--create", "relative-test"],
+    );
+
+    // Verify the .git file in the worktree contains a relative path
+    let worktree_path = repo
+        .root_path()
+        .parent()
+        .unwrap()
+        .join("repo.relative-test");
+    let git_file = std::fs::read_to_string(worktree_path.join(".git")).unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        !git_file.contains(repo.root_path().to_str().unwrap()),
+        "Expected relative path in .git file, but found absolute path: {git_file}"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        git_file.contains("gitdir: ../"),
+        "Expected relative gitdir in .git file: {git_file}"
+    );
+
+    // Verify wt list shows the worktree (path resolution works)
+    let settings = setup_snapshot_settings(&repo);
+    settings.bind(|| {
+        let mut cmd = make_snapshot_cmd(&repo, "list", &[], None);
+        assert_cmd_snapshot!("list_with_relative_paths", cmd);
+    });
+
+    // Verify switching to the relative-path worktree works
+    snapshot_switch("switch_to_relative_paths", &repo, &["relative-test"]);
+}

title: fix: remove prefix filtering from HookCommandCompleter for shell consistency
body:
`HookCommandCompleter::complete()` was pre-filtering completions by prefix, preventing fish/zsh users from doing substring matching on hook command names. `BranchCompleter` was already fixed for this in #1471, but `HookCommandCompleter` was missed.

The bash-specific prefix filter in `maybe_handle_env_completion()` already handles bash correctly — this just removes the redundant (and harmful) filter from the completer itself, matching `BranchCompleter`'s approach.

Also inlines `complete_hook_commands()` (single call site) and fixes a stale docstring (`wt step` → `wt hook`).

- Add `shrinkable` flag to `ColumnSpec` — shrinkable columns degrade gracefully to whatever width fits (down to header width) instead of being dropped entirely when their ideal width doesn't fit

title: refactor: consolidate merge/remove removal validation
body:
## Summary

Extracts composable helpers from the removal validation logic so `wt merge` and `wt remove` share guards without duplicating implementations.

### Shared helpers (new)

| Helper | Purpose | `wt remove` behavior | `wt merge` behavior |
|--------|---------|---------------------|---------------------|
| `is_primary_worktree()` | Main-worktree + bare-repo default-branch guard | Not used (Phase 2 uses `!is_linked()` directly) | Returns `None` (skip silently) |
| `check_not_default_branch()` | Reject removing default branch without force | Error | Error (same) |
| `compute_integration_reason()` | Pre-compute integration status | Called via `prepare_worktree_removal` | Called directly |

### What changed

- **Deleted `prepare_merge_removal`** — it duplicated Phase 2/3/5 logic from `prepare_worktree_removal` in a parallel implementation (+55 library lines was the wrong direction)
- **Extracted `is_primary_worktree()`** — combines `!is_linked()` and bare-repo-default-branch checks into one shared helper
- **Made `check_not_default_branch` and `compute_integration_reason` `pub(crate)`** — merge calls them directly
- **Merge builds `RemoveResult` directly** using the shared helpers, with merge-specific values (explicit target branch, `SafeDelete`, `changed_directory: true`)

Net **-39 library lines** vs the previous approach's +55.

title: fix: replace reset --hard with safe read-tree for worktree sync
body:
## Summary

- Replace `reset --hard` with `read-tree -m -u` (two-tree merge) in the no-ff merge worktree sync path — refuses to overwrite locally modified tracked files instead of silently discarding them (TOCTOU safety)
- Add CLAUDE.md guidance: favor data-retaining git operations over destructive ones

Follow-up to #1619 per [review feedback](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1619#discussion_r2961921489).

## Details

The no-ff merge path uses `update-ref` to advance the target branch, then syncs the target worktree. Previously this used `reset --hard HEAD`, which would silently discard any tracked-file modifications added between the pre-push dirty check and the sync.

`reset --keep` would be the natural safe alternative, but it can't be used here: after `update-ref`, HEAD already points to the merge commit, so `reset --keep HEAD` sees old==new and is a no-op.

`read-tree -m -u <old_tip> <merge_sha>` performs a two-tree merge that correctly updates the index and working tree, and refuses if any tracked files have local modifications — exactly the TOCTOU safety behavior we want.

**Audit results:** This was the only `reset --hard` in production code (`src/`). The remaining uses in `tests/` are for deliberate test state setup (behind/diverged scenarios) and are appropriate.

## Test plan

- [x] All 11 `test_merge_no_ff*` tests pass
- [x] All 10 `test_push*` tests pass  
- [x] Lints pass

title: fix: filter completions by prefix for bash shell
body:
Bash's programmable completion (`complete -F`) does not filter `COMPREPLY` by prefix — whatever the completion function puts in the array is displayed as-is. After #1471 removed prefix filtering to enable fish/zsh substring matching, bash users saw all branches regardless of what they'd typed. For users with many branches (the reporter had 80), `wt switch feat<TAB>` prompts "Display all 80 possibilities?" instead of showing only the `feature/*` branches.

When the requesting shell is bash (`COMPLETE=bash`), filter completion candidates by prefix before outputting them. Fish and zsh still receive all candidates so they can apply their native substring/fuzzy matching. The filtering runs in `maybe_handle_env_completion()` after `engine::complete()` returns, so it handles all argument forms correctly (`--base=m` → `--base=main`, `-b m` → `main`, etc.).

Adds `test_completion_cross_shell_filtering_contract` which verifies the same branches with the same typed prefix produce different results per shell — the test that would have caught the #1471 regression.

Thanks to @altruic for reporting in #1621.

Closes #1621

title: fix: protect default branch worktree from removal in bare repos
body:
## Problem

In bare repos, all worktrees are linked (`is_linked() = true`), so the `in_main` guard in `wt merge` always evaluated to `false`. This meant the default branch worktree had no protection against removal — running `wt merge <target>` from the default branch worktree could remove it, deleting the user's primary working directory.

Reported in #1618: user ran `wt merge` from master in a bare repo and the master worktree was removed.

## Solution

Extended the primary worktree check to also consider bare repos: if the repo is bare and the current branch is the default branch, treat the worktree as primary and skip removal. Renamed `in_main` to `in_primary` to reflect the broader scope (matches the project's terminology: "primary worktree" = main worktree for normal repos, default branch worktree for bare repos).

## Testing

- Added `test_bare_repo_merge_preserves_default_branch_worktree` which creates a bare repo with main + feature worktrees at the same commit, runs `wt merge feature` from the main worktree, and verifies the main worktree is preserved with the "primary worktree" message.
- Existing `test_bare_repo_merge_workflow` continues to pass (feature branch removal still works).
- Updated snapshot files for the message change ("main worktree" → "primary worktree").

Closes #1618 — automated triage

title: fix: disable submodule recursion in local push and reset
body:
## Summary

- Add `--recurse-submodules=no` to the local `git push` in `wt merge`/`wt step push` to prevent `submodule.recurse=true` from interfering with worktree-to-worktree ref updates
- Add regression tests for both fast-forward and no-ff push with `submodule.recurse=true` config

The `reset --hard` fix from the original PR is no longer needed — #1623 replaced `reset --hard` with `read-tree -m -u`, which doesn't recurse into submodules.

Closes #1604

## Test plan

- [x] New test `test_push_with_submodule_recurse_config` — verifies fast-forward push succeeds with `submodule.recurse=true`
- [x] New test `test_push_no_ff_with_submodule_recurse_config` — verifies no-ff push succeeds with `submodule.recurse=true`
- [x] All existing push tests still pass
- [x] Lints pass

title: test: width survey snapshots for picker layout at various sizes
body:
## Summary

- Adds snapshot tests showing `wt list` layout at 30, 40, 50, 60, 80, 100, and 120 columns
- Includes picker-equivalent widths (terminal_width/2) simulating `wt switch` in Right layout
- Three test scenarios: typical branches, long branches, and picker Right-layout simulation

No code changes — just snapshots to visualize current behavior.

## Key findings visible in snapshots

**Branch column dropped at narrow widths with long names** (`width_survey_long_30`):
At 30 cols with long branch names (`feature/implement-oauth2-social-login`, `fix/database-connection-pool-exhaustion`), the Branch column is **entirely absent** — only Status, HEAD±, and main↕ show. This is the `try_allocate()` all-or-nothing behavior: the branch column's ideal width (longest name) exceeds available space, so it gets 0 allocation.

**Typical branches survive down to 30 cols** (`width_survey_typical_30`):
With shorter branch names (`feature/auth-redesign`, ~22 chars), Branch still fits at 30 cols — but Status column is dropped.

**Picker in Right layout at 60-col terminal** (`width_survey_picker_right_60`):
List gets 30 cols. Branch + Age fit — Status and all other columns hidden. Usable but minimal.

**Picker in Right layout at 80-col terminal** (`width_survey_picker_right_80`):
List gets 40 cols. Branch + Status + Age fit. Reasonable.

**Column progression summary (typical branches):**

| Width | Columns visible |
|-------|----------------|
| 30 | Branch, Age |
| 40 | Branch, Status, Age |
| 60 | Branch, Status, HEAD±, main↕, Age |
| 80 | Branch, Status, HEAD±, main↕, Remote⇅, Commit, Age |
| 100+ | Branch, Status, Dirty, HEAD±, main↕, Remote⇅, Commit, Age, Path |

## Context

Requested in https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1564#issuecomment-4087034190

## Test plan

- [x] All 3 new tests pass (`cargo test --test integration "width_survey"`)
- [x] Existing spacing edge case tests unaffected
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes (excluding lychee)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

+    }
+}

+    repo.add_worktree("fix/login-timeout");

+    let auth_path = repo.worktrees.get("feature/auth-redesign").unwrap();

title: fix(review-pr): add verification checklist for multi-line suggestions
body:
## Summary

- Replaces the vague "minimize the range" instruction for multi-line suggestions with a concrete 4-step verification checklist
- Addresses the root cause of #1607: the bot constructs suggestion ranges that are wider than the replacement text, silently deleting correct code when applied

## Root cause analysis

Investigated all three known cases:

1. **#1310** (PR #1309): `start_line: 18, line: 22` — 5-line range replaced with fewer lines, deleting the `git-wt` fallback branch
2. **#1326** (PR #1322): `start_line: 289, line: 291` — range included a closing ` ``` ` fence that GitHub consumed as the suggestion's own delimiter
3. **#1598**: `start_line: 93, line: 127` — 35-line range replaced with a shorter rewrite, deleting the `gh issue view` code block

Common thread: the bot sets a line range covering more content than it intends to replace. The replacement text is shorter, so the surplus lines are silently deleted. The existing instruction ("minimize the range") didn't give the bot a way to verify correctness.

## Fix

The new checklist requires the bot to:
1. **Read the exact lines** in the range before posting
2. **Verify no silent deletions** — every line must appear in the replacement or be intentionally removed
3. **Cap range at ~10 lines** — larger suggestions should be split or pushed as commits
4. **Avoid spanning markdown fences** — prevents delimiter collision

## Test plan

- [ ] Review a PR with a multi-line suggestion opportunity and verify the bot follows the checklist
- [ ] Verify the bot splits or commits changes larger than ~10 lines instead of using a suggestion

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: worktrunk-bot
diff:
--- .claude/skills/review-pr/SKILL.md (+16/-2)
@@ -276,8 +276,22 @@ array indices to object keys, which GitHub rejects.
 - If a review has both suggestions and prose observations, put the suggestions
   as inline comments and the prose in the review body.
 - Multi-line suggestions: set `start_line` and `line` to define the range.
-  **Minimize the range** — only include lines that actually need changing. A
-  range that's too wide can delete correct code adjacent to the fix.
+  GitHub **replaces** every line in that range with the suggestion content — any
+  line in the range that isn't reproduced in the replacement is **deleted**.
+
+  **Before posting any multi-line suggestion, verify it:**
+
+  1. **Read the exact lines** `start_line` through `line` from the diff hunk.
+  2. **Diff mentally**: every line in that range must either appear (possibly
+     modified) in the replacement text, or be a line you intend to delete. If
+     any line would be silently dropped, **shrink the range** or include the
+     line in the replacement.
+  3. **Cap the range at ~10 lines.** Larger suggestions are error-prone and hard
+     to review. For changes spanning more than 10 lines, split into multiple
+     suggestions or push a fix commit instead.
+  4. **Never span markdown fences.** If the range includes a `` ``` `` line,
+     GitHub's suggestion parser may consume it as a delimiter, corrupting the
+     result. Either shrink the range to avoid the fence or push a commit.
 
 ### 5. Monitor CI
