title: fix(skill): disambiguate .commit.oid vs .commit_id in review-pr
body:
## Summary

- All 4 `claude-review` sessions from the past hour used `.commit_id` instead of `.commit.oid` for the `LAST_REVIEW_SHA` jq extraction, causing the early-exit deduplication check to always return empty
- The skill already had the correct field (`.commit.oid` on line 33), but the nearby `.commit_id` reference (line 311, for a different REST API endpoint) likely caused the LLM to conflate the two
- Added explicit `IMPORTANT` comments at both locations to distinguish `gh pr view --json` fields from REST API fields

## Evidence

All 4 review runs from the past hour (23023490903, 23024511249, 23024512682, 23024613508) generated:

```bash
# What the bot wrote (WRONG for gh pr view --json):
... | last | .commit_id // empty")
```

Instead of the skill's documented:

```bash
# What the skill says (CORRECT for gh pr view --json):
... | last | .commit.oid // empty")
```

This means `LAST_REVIEW_SHA` was always empty, so:
- The "already reviewed this commit" early-exit never fires
- The incremental-diff optimization between reviews doesn't work
- The bot re-processes the full diff on every trigger

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify next review-bot run extracts `LAST_REVIEW_SHA` correctly
- [ ] Verify re-trigger on already-reviewed commit exits silently

--- .claude/skills/review-pr/SKILL.md (+3/-0)
@@ -29,6 +29,8 @@ HEAD_SHA=$(gh pr view <number> --json commits --jq '.commits[-1].oid')
 # Find the bot's most recent substantive review (any state).
 # Include reviews with a non-empty body OR approvals (LGTM uses --approve -b "").
 # Uses "| length > 0" instead of "!= \"\"" to avoid bash ! history expansion.
+# IMPORTANT: `gh pr view --json reviews` returns `.commit.oid` (NOT `.commit_id`).
+# The REST API (`gh api .../reviews`) uses `.commit_id` — don't confuse the two.
 LAST_REVIEW_SHA=$(gh pr view <number> --json reviews \
   --jq "[.reviews[] | select(.author.login == \"$BOT_LOGIN\" and (.body | length > 0 or .state == \"APPROVED\"))] | last | .commit.oid // empty")
 ```
@@ -307,6 +309,7 @@ approach:
 Post exactly one review per run. API calls can succeed server-side while
 appearing to hang, so always verify before calling `gh pr review`:
 ```bash
+# NOTE: REST API uses .commit_id (not .commit.oid which is the gh pr view --json field)
 gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls/<number>/reviews" \
   --jq "[.[] | select(.user.login == \"$BOT_LOGIN\" and .commit_id == \"$HEAD_SHA\")] | last | .submitted_at // empty"
 ```

title: docs: add manual commit message recipes
body:
## Summary

- Adds a "Manual commit messages" section to tips & patterns, addressing #1467
- Shows a config-based approach using `commit.generation.command` to read a message from the terminal
- Shows an env var alias approach (`WORKTRUNK_COMMIT__GENERATION__COMMAND`) for per-command overrides without changing the default LLM config

Closes #1467

## Test plan

- [x] Doc sync test passes (`test_command_pages_and_skill_files_are_in_sync`)
- [ ] CI green

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: worktrunk-bot
diff:
--- docs/content/tips-patterns.md (+22/-0)
@@ -114,6 +114,28 @@ EOF
 
 This catches issues locally before pushing — like running CI locally.
 
+## Manual commit messages
+
+The `commit.generation.command` receives the rendered prompt on stdin and returns the commit message on stdout. To write commit messages by hand instead of using an LLM, point it at `$EDITOR`:
+
+```toml
+# ~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml
+[commit.generation]
+command = '''f=$(mktemp); printf '\n\n' > "$f"; sed 's/^/# /' >> "$f"; ${EDITOR:-vi} "$f" < /dev/tty > /dev/tty; grep -v '^#' "$f"'''
+```
+
+This comments out the rendered prompt (diff, branch name, stats) with `#` prefixes, opens your editor, and strips comment lines on save. A couple of blank lines at the top give you space to type; the prompt context is visible below for reference.
+
+To keep the LLM as default but use the editor for a specific merge, add a [worktrunk alias](@/step.md#aliases):
+
+```toml
+# ~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml
+[aliases]
+mc = '''WORKTRUNK_COMMIT__GENERATION__COMMAND='f=$(mktemp); printf "\n\n" > "$f"; sed "s/^/# /" >> "$f"; ${EDITOR:-vi} "$f" < /dev/tty > /dev/tty; grep -v "^#" "$f"' wt merge'''
+```
+
+Then `wt step mc` opens an editor for the commit message while plain `wt merge` continues to use the LLM.
+
 ## Track agent status
 
 Custom emoji markers show agent state in `wt list`. The Claude Code plugin sets these automatically:

title: fix(test): update stale doc comment about border character
body:
## Summary

- Fixes stale doc comment on `wait_for_stable_with_content` in `switch_picker.rs` that recommended including `│` border characters in test expectations — the opposite of what #1464 established

In the review of PR #1464 (run [23007859402](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/23007859402)), the reviewer correctly identified this stale doc comment at lines 408-409 and offered to fix it. title: fix: suppress GPG signature output in all git log calls
body:
# Problem

`wt list` fails on repositories where `log.showSignature` is set. When git logs a signed commit with `--format=%ct %s`, it emits GPG verification lines to stdout before the format line:

```
gpg: Signature made Wed Mar 11 18:18:28 2026 CET
gpg:                using EDDSA key 0000...
gpg: Good signature from "A U Thor <author@example.com>" [ultimate]
1773249428 fix: some commit message
```

The parsing code expected only the format output, so `split_once(' ')` would fail on the `gpg:` prefix.

# Fix

Pass `--no-show-signature` to all `git log` calls to suppress GPG verification output at the source. This protects all four call sites (`commit_details`, `commit_timestamps`, `commit_subjects`, `recent_commit_subjects`) rather than adding GPG-aware parsing to just one.

# disclaimer

The original fix, tests, and PR were fully generated by claude. The revision to use `--no-show-signature` was also applied by claude based on reviewer feedback.

title: fix: refuse to remove default branch worktree unless -D
body:
`wt remove` allowed removing the default branch worktree (e.g. main) because the default branch is trivially "integrated" into itself — `check_integration` returns `SameCommit`. `wt list` already guards against this (`is_main` check in `check_integration_state`), but `wt remove` didn't have the same guard.

title: fix: resolve flaky PTY/timing issues in integration tests

1. **Timing assertion in `test_list_progressive_api`** — `total_duration < 5s` fails under load due to the 1s minimum drain wait. Removed (tests correctness, not performance).

The bot has pushed to `origin` on fork PRs three times (#1411, #1434, run 22985929574), creating stray branches on the upstream repo. title: fix: fire post-switch hooks when removing current worktree
body:
## Problem

When removing the current worktree (`wt remove` from within the worktree being removed), post-switch hooks don't fire even though the user is implicitly switched back to the primary worktree.

**Root cause:** `spawn_hooks_after_remove` creates a fresh `Repository::at(main_path)`, but `load_project_config()` internally calls `current_worktree()` which uses the global process cwd — the removed worktree. Since that path no longer exists (or lacks `.config/wt.toml`), the config lookup silently returns `None` and no project hooks are found.

## Solution

Pre-warm the project config cache from `main_path` before any hook preparation in `spawn_hooks_after_remove`. This ensures both post-remove and post-switch hooks can find the project config.

Added:
- `ProjectConfig::load_at()` — loads config from a specific worktree root (refactored from `load()`)
- `Repository::load_project_config_at()` — loads and caches project config from a specific worktree path

## Testing

- Added `test_remove_current_worktree_fires_post_switch_hook` — reproduces the exact scenario from #1450 (create worktree, cd into it, remove it, verify post-switch hook fires)
- Test confirmed failing before the fix and passing after
- All pre-existing tests continue to pass

---
Closes #1450 — automated triage

title: fix: return Option from cwd_removed_hint, drop trailing periods
body:
Follow-up to #1238. Two small refinements to the CWD-removed hint system:

- `cwd_removed_hint()` now returns `Option<String>` instead of `String` — when no repository can be found, there's no actionable hint to give, so `None` is more accurate than a plain string. The caller in `main.rs` uses `info_message` for the no-hint case instead of `hint_message`.
- Dropped trailing period from the `wt list` fallback hint to match the `wt switch ^` hint (consistency).

Ref #1168

title: feat(switch): make --no-cd print-only in picker mode
body:
## Summary

Draft implementation per @max-sixty's [suggestion](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1404#issuecomment-4041170944): reuse `--no-cd` to make the picker print-only instead of adding a separate `--print` flag.

- When `wt switch --no-cd` opens the interactive picker (no branch argument), selecting a branch prints its name to stdout and exits — no switching, no cd directive, no hooks
- When `wt switch --no-cd <branch>` is used with an explicit branch, behavior is unchanged (switches without cd)
- `alt-r` (remove) is blocked in print mode since it's a read-only operation

This avoids adding a new CLI flag while giving the same scripting capability that #1404 proposed.

title: fix(skill): add pre-commit and duplicate-PR checks to running-in-ci
body:
## Summary

- Add "Before creating a PR" guidance: check for existing PRs and fix branches before creating duplicates
- Add "Before committing code changes" guidance: run `cargo fmt` (minimum) or full pre-merge before committing

## Evidence

In [run 22946109451](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/22946109451) (`claude-mention` on issue #1415), the bot:

1. **Created a duplicate PR.** PR #1416 (created 2026-03-10) already addressed the same issue — excluding remote branches from switch completions. The bot created #1442 with a different approach without checking for existing work. Both PRs are authored by `worktrunk-bot`. The session log shows the bot went directly from reading the issue to editing code — no `gh pr list` or branch check.

2. **Skipped `cargo fmt` before committing.** The bot ran `cargo check` to verify compilation but not `cargo fmt`. CI failed on the pre-commit hook's format check, requiring a second "style: rustfmt" commit and another full CI polling cycle (~11 minutes of additional `sleep 60` polls).

<details><summary>Session log: tool call sequence (run 22946109451)</summary>

```
Skill: running-in-ci
Bash: gh issue view 1415 ...
Read: src/completion.rs
Edit: src/completion.rs          ← code change
Grep: complete_branches          ← searched for tests, found none
Bash: cargo check                ← compilation only, no fmt
Bash: git checkout -b ...
Bash: git add && git commit      ← committed unformatted code
Bash: git push && gh pr create   ← created PR #1442 (duplicate of #1416)
... 11 CI poll cycles ...
Bash: gh run view --log-failed   ← discovered fmt failure
Bash: cargo fmt                  ← fixed formatting
Bash: git add && git commit      ← second commit
... 11 more CI poll cycles ...
```

</details>

## Root cause

The `running-in-ci` skill (loaded by all CI workflows) had no guidance on either checking for existing PRs or formatting code before committing. The `triage-issue` skill already had both — Step 3 ("Check for duplicates") and Step 6.3 (`cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes`) — but this guidance didn't extend to the `claude-mention` workflow.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify the skill file renders correctly
- [ ] Observe future `claude-mention` runs for improved behavior (check for existing PRs, run `cargo fmt`)

title: fix(completion): exclude remote branches when total exceeds 100
body:
## Summary

- When tab-completing `wt switch`, exclude remote-only branches if the total branch count exceeds 100
- This prevents the "do you wish to see all N possibilities?" prompt in bash/zsh for repos with many remote branches
- Threshold of 100 aligns with bash's default `completion-query-items`
- Repos with ≤100 branches are unaffected — remote branches still appear in completions
- Users can always reach remote branches via the interactive picker (`wt switch` without args)

Closes #1415

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify compilation and existing tests pass in CI
- [ ] Manual: in a repo with >100 remote branches, `wt switch <TAB>` should show only local/worktree branches
- [ ] Manual: in a repo with ≤100 branches, `wt switch <TAB>` should include remote branches as before

title: fix(skill): don't approve PRs with active maintainer design concerns
body:
## Summary

- Adds "maintainer design concerns in PR comments" as an explicit confidence-decreasing factor in the review-pr skill
- Adds a new rule: when a maintainer has posted comments questioning a feature's value or direction, the bot must not approve — it should use `+1` reaction instead and let the maintainer decide

## Evidence

In [run 22941561692](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/22941561692) reviewing PR #1438, the maintainer posted a comment at 04:58 UTC questioning whether the `--no-ff` feature belongs in the project:

> how much do folks want this?
> ...I would claim that the use case for `wt merge` — generally personal projects where we favor moving quickly & the transparency of commit histories — means that squashing is almost always better
> ...and we want to avoid collecting all the git options in `wt`

Despite this, the bot posted an APPROVE review at 07:29 UTC with a verbose confirmatory body describing what the code does — violating both the "approve with empty body" rule and, more importantly, approving a feature whose inclusion was actively under discussion by the maintainer.

The bot's approval was technically correct on code quality, but the decision to approve was wrong. The bot cannot judge whether a feature belongs in the project — that's a maintainer decision.

**Secondary issue**: The approve review body also violated the existing "don't explain what the code does" and "approve with empty body" rules, but those rules are already documented. The missing piece was guidance about deferring to maintainer judgment on design questions.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify the skill file renders correctly
- [ ] Monitor future review sessions on PRs with maintainer discussion to confirm the bot defers instead of approving

title: merge: add --no-ff flag for merge commit (semi-linear history)
body:
## Summary

- Add `--no-ff` / `--ff` CLI flags to `wt merge`
- Add `[merge] no-ff` config option (project and user config)
- Refactor `handle_push` into a reusable `MergeContext` struct, eliminating duplication between fast-forward and merge-commit paths
- Create merge commits via git plumbing (`commit-tree` + `update-ref`) without checking out the target branch

## Motivation

I prefer rebased commits on the feature branch, plus a merge commit on the target.

This is equivalent to GitLab's "Merge commit with semi-linear history" strategy and GitHub's "Create a merge commit" option (after rebasing).

## Pipeline behaviour with `--no-ff`

The merge pipeline runs identically up through rebase and pre-merge hooks. At the merge step, instead of fast-forwarding the target ref, a merge commit is created:

```
git commit-tree HEAD^{tree} -p <target-tip> -p HEAD -m "Merge branch '<branch>' into <target>"
git update-ref refs/heads/<target> <new-merge-commit> <old-target-tip>
```

The target worktree (if present) is then synced via `reset --hard`.

## Config

```toml
[merge]
no-ff = true   # always create a merge commit
```

Override per-invocation with `--ff` to force fast-forward even when config says `no-ff = true`.

## Test coverage

11 integration tests covering:
- Basic single-commit `--no-ff`
- Multi-commit `--no-ff` (no squash)
- `--no-ff` with squash (squash first, then merge commit)
- `--no-ff` from config, with `--ff` CLI override
- `--no-ff` with rebase (diverged branches)
- `--no-ff` already up to date
- `--no-ff` with diverged branches and `--no-rebase` (error path)
- `--no-ff` syncs target worktree via `reset --hard`
- `--no-ff` with non-overlapping dirty target (autostash/restore)
- `--no-ff` with overlapping dirty target (safe failure, no data loss)
- `--no-ff` when target has no checked-out worktree

## Notes

I developed this PR with assistance from AI.

## Summary

- Rewrite the hourly reviewer's Step 7 ("Report findings") to prefer creating PRs over issues
- PRs are now the default for any fixable problem (skill edits, workflow tweaks, CLAUDE.md updates)

- Instructs the bot to keep findings cohesive (grouped PRs, not many small patches)

This eliminates the duplication problem from #1425/#1426, where the hourly reviewer created an issue and the triage bot raced to also fix it. With the reviewer going straight to PR, there's no issue for triage to pick up.

title: docs: add Xcode DerivedData cleanup recipe
body:
## Summary

For iOS developers, this PR add a `post-remove` hook recipe to Tips & Patterns that cleans up Xcode's DerivedData when removing a worktree.

## Context

Xcode's DerivedData directory names are hashed from the `.xcodeproj` path, making them hard to match by name alone. Each DerivedData directory contains an `info.plist` with a `WorkspacePath` field that records the original project path. This recipe leverages that to find and remove only the matching cache.
author: RickeyBoy
diff:
--- docs/content/tips-patterns.md (+20/-0)
@@ -267,6 +267,26 @@ To create a worktree and immediately attach:
 wt switch --create feature -x 'tmux attach -t {{ branch | sanitize }}'
 ```
 
+## Xcode DerivedData cleanup
+
+Clean up Xcode's DerivedData when removing a worktree. Each DerivedData directory contains an `info.plist` recording its project path — grep for the worktree path to find and remove the matching build cache:
+
+```toml
+# ~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml
+[post-remove]
+clean-derived = """
+  grep -Fl {{ worktree_path }} \
+    ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/*/info.plist 2>/dev/null \
+  | while read plist; do
+      derived_dir=$(dirname "$plist")
+      rm -rf "$derived_dir"
+      echo "Cleaned DerivedData: $derived_dir"
+    done
+"""
+```
+
+This precisely targets only the DerivedData for the removed worktree, leaving caches for other worktrees and the main repository intact.
+
 ## Subdomain routing with Caddy

body:
## Summary

- Add fork-PR guidance to the `running-in-ci` skill: check `headRepositoryOwner` before pushing commits to a PR branch
- Add guidance to avoid referencing commit SHAs from temporary/deleted branches

Fixes #1411 — in [run 22862093653](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/22862093653), the bot pushed a branch to upstream before discovering PR #1408 was from a fork, then had to delete it.

+## Fork PRs
+
+Before pushing commits to a PR branch, check whether it's a fork PR:
+
+```bash
+gh pr view <number> --json headRepositoryOwner --jq '.headRepositoryOwner.login'

+
+If the owner is **not** `max-sixty`, it's a fork PR. The key rule: **never

+Instead, push directly to the fork's PR branch:

+gh pr checkout <number>

+# After making changes, push back to the fork
+git push
+```

+If pushing to the fork fails (e.g., "Allow edits from maintainers" is disabled),

+temporary or deleted branches — those links will 404. Post the code inline

title: fix(review-pr): use JSON payload for review comments instead of broken -f flag syntax
body:
## Summary
- Replace broken `gh api -f 'comments[0][path]=...'` syntax in the review-pr skill with a JSON payload approach using `--input`
- The `-f` flag syntax converts array indices to object keys (`{"0": {...}}` instead of `[{...}]`), which GitHub rejects
- Add a warning note to prevent future regression to the broken pattern

Closes #1409

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify next claude-review run posts inline comments successfully on first attempt (no "Invalid request" recovery)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: worktrunk-bot
diff:
--- .claude/skills/review-pr/SKILL.md (+22/-7)
@@ -333,17 +333,32 @@ the diff, offer to push a fix commit instead.
 **Correct — inline suggestion on the line:**
 
 `````bash
+cat > /tmp/review-payload.json << 'ENDJSON'
+{
+  "event": "COMMENT",
+  "comments": [
+    {
+      "path": ".claude/skills/example/SKILL.md",
+      "line": 3,
+      "body": "```suggestion\ndescription: new text here\n```"
+    }
+  ]
+}
+ENDJSON
+
+# Read body from file to avoid shell expansion issues
+BODY=$(cat /tmp/review-body.md)
+jq --arg body "$BODY" '.body = $body' /tmp/review-payload.json > /tmp/review-final.json
+
 gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls/<number>/reviews" \
   --method POST \
-  -f event=COMMENT \
-  -f body="Summary of suggestions" \
-  -f 'comments[0][path]=.claude/skills/example/SKILL.md' \
-  -f 'comments[0][line]=3' \
-  -f 'comments[0][body]=```suggestion
-description: new text here
-```'
+  --input /tmp/review-final.json
 `````
 
+**Do not** use `-f 'comments[0][path]=...'` flag syntax — `gh api` converts
+array indices to object keys (`{"0": {...}}` instead of `[{...}]`), which
+GitHub rejects.
+
 - Use suggestions for any small fix — no limit on count.
 - If a review has both suggestions and prose observations, put the suggestions
   as inline comments and the prose in the review body.

title: feat: add github enterprise hostname parsing to wt switch logic
body:
## Summary
- Fix `wt switch pr:<number>` for repositories hosted on GitHub Enterprise (or other non-`github.com` hosts) by passing `--hostname` to the `gh` CLI
- Extract the hostname from the repository's primary remote URL using the existing `GitRemoteUrl::parse()` utility, falling back to `github.com` if the URL can't be parsed
## Problem
When checking out a PR in a repository hosted on a GitHub Enterprise instance (e.g., `github.example.com`), the `gh api` call in `fetch_pr_info` did not specify which host to authenticate against. The `gh` CLI defaults to `github.com`, so PR checkout silently failed for any other GitHub host.
The `gh api` command accepts a `--hostname` flag to target a specific GitHub host, but it was not being used.
## Solution
This PR extracts the hostname from the repository's configured remote URL and passes it to `gh api --hostname`. The extraction is best-effort so if the remote URL can't be parsed for any reason, it falls back to `"github.com"`, preserving the existing behavior.
The hostname parsing reuses the existing `GitRemoteUrl::parse()` to support all remote URL formats (`https://`, `ssh://`, `git@`, `git://`, `http://`).
## Notes
I'm not that experienced in Rust, so I'm happy to implement any PR feedback and add tests if necessary.
author: TomRomeo

title: fix(review-pr): specify PUT method for dismiss API call
body:
## Summary

- Adds explicit `-X PUT` and a code example to the dismiss instruction in the review-pr skill
- The GitHub dismiss endpoint requires PUT, not POST (the `gh api` default when using `-f`)
- Sessions using POST get 404, leaving stale approvals when CI fails — this was the root cause of #1405

## Evidence

Run [22845135867](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/22845135867) on the same fork PR (#1404) shows both methods tried:
- POST → 404
- PUT → success (state: DISMISSED)

This supersedes the deferred-approval approach in #1406, which works as a workaround but adds unnecessary complexity.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify next review session that encounters CI failure uses PUT and successfully dismisses
- [ ] Confirm no regression on same-repo PRs

Closes #1405

## Summary

- Changes both `review-pr` and `running-in-ci` skills to use `gh pr checks --required` instead of `gh pr checks`
- The bot now only waits for **required** checks to complete, ignoring non-required checks (e.g., benchmarks)
- This eliminates unbounded polling when non-required checks are stuck pending

In run [22837325148](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/22837325148), the bot polled 55 times (~55 min) waiting for a `benchmarks` check that was stuck pending. With `--required`, it would have completed immediately after the required checks passed.

Closes #1402

## Test plan

title: feat(switch): add no-cd config option
body:
## Summary
- Add `[switch] no-cd = true` config option to disable directory change by default
- Add `--cd` flag to override config when directory change is desired
- Implement 3-way precedence: `--cd` flag → `--no-cd` flag → config → default (false)

## Motivation
Users who manage worktrees via tmux sessions (one session per worktree) handle directory changes themselves. For these workflows, having `wt switch` automatically change directories is unnecessary — they switch tmux sessions instead. This config option lets users disable the default cd behavior while retaining `--cd` for occasional use.
author: jradtilbrook

title: Add session log investigation guidance to running-in-ci skill
body:
## Summary

A bot asked to diagnose another CI run's behavior searched `gh run view --log`, found only workflow boilerplate (`show_full_output` defaults to false), and confabulated a structural analysis instead of downloading the session log artifact. The `running-in-ci` skill had no guidance about artifacts existing.

Adds an "Investigating Other CI Runs" section covering:
- Why console logs don't contain the conversation
- How to download session log artifacts (`gh run download`)
- jq recipes for parsing JSONL (skills loaded, tool calls, reasoning)
- Finding the right run when multiple workflows trigger on the same event
- Cross-reference bullet in the Thoroughness section

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify bot in CI loads this guidance when investigating other runs
- [ ] Confirm jq recipes work on actual session log artifacts

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max-sixty_

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- .claude/skills/running-in-ci/SKILL.md (+64/-1)
@@ -1,6 +1,6 @@
 ---
 name: running-in-ci
-description: CI environment rules for GitHub Actions workflows. Use when operating in CI — covers security, CI monitoring, and comment formatting.
+description: CI environment rules for GitHub Actions workflows. Use when operating in CI — covers security, CI monitoring, comment formatting, and investigating session logs from other runs.
 ---
 
 # Running in CI
@@ -198,6 +198,66 @@ session. This makes PRs easier to review, revert, and bisect.
 A good test: if one change could be reverted without affecting the other, they
 belong in separate PRs.
 
+## Investigating Other CI Runs
+
+When asked to diagnose what a bot did in a previous CI run, the primary evidence
+is the session log artifact — not the console output. Console output
+(`gh run view <id> --log`) contains only workflow boilerplate because
+`show_full_output` defaults to `false`. The actual conversation is in the
+artifact.
+
+### Downloading session logs
+
+All Claude workflows upload session logs as artifacts named
+`claude-session-logs`. Download with:
+
+```bash
+gh run download <run-id> -n claude-session-logs -D /tmp/session-logs-<run-id>
+```
+
+The artifact contains JSONL files under a path like
+`-home-runner-work-worktrunk-worktrunk/<session-id>.jsonl`.
+
+### Parsing session logs
+
+Each JSONL line is a message with a `type` field (`user`, `assistant`, `system`).
+
+```bash
+# Skills loaded
+jq -r 'select(.type == "assistant") | .message.content[]? |
+  select(.type == "tool_use" and .name == "Skill") | .input.skill' <FILE>.jsonl
+
+# Tool calls
+jq -r 'select(.type == "assistant") | .message.content[]? |
+  select(.type == "tool_use") |
+  "\(.name): \(.input | tostring | .[0:100])"' <FILE>.jsonl
+
+# Assistant reasoning
+jq -r 'select(.type == "assistant") | .message.content[]? |
+  select(.type == "text") | .text' <FILE>.jsonl
+```
+
+### Finding the right run
+
+Multiple workflows may trigger on the same event. Use the event type to narrow:
+
+```bash
+gh api 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs?per_page=30' \
+  --jq '.workflow_runs[] | select(.name | startswith("claude-")) |
+    {id, name, event, head_branch, created_at, conclusion}'
+```
+
+Check which runs have artifacts before downloading:
+
+```bash
+gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/<run-id>/artifacts \
+  --jq '.artifacts[] | {name, size_in_bytes}'
+```
+
+Review-response runs triggered by `pull_request_review` or
+`pull_request_review_comment` events sometimes produce no artifact when the
+session is very short.
+
 ## Thoroughness — Grounded Analysis
 
 CI runs are not interactive chat. There is no back-and-forth — the user reads
@@ -219,6 +279,9 @@ actually examined.
 - **Distinguish what you verified from what you inferred.** If you couldn't
   verify something (e.g., logs weren't available), say so explicitly rather than
   hedging with "may" or "suggests."
+- **Check artifacts, not just console logs.** Console output from Claude runs is
+  hidden by default. Session log artifacts are the primary evidence source — see
+  "Investigating Other CI Runs" above.
 
 The user can't ask follow-up questions in the same session. Treat every response
 as your final answer.

title: Increase drain timeout from 30s to 120s to fix flaky CI
body:
The drain deadline in `wt list` was 30 seconds — too tight for CI environments
where process spawning for ~70 work items (5 worktrees × ~14 tasks) can be
slow under load. When the deadline fires, a timeout warning goes to stderr,
breaking snapshot comparisons for tests like `test_list_full_with_no_ci_checks`
and `test_list_full_with_status_context::case_1_pending`.

Increased to 120s and extracted a `DRAIN_TIMEOUT` constant so the value and
diagnostic messages stay in sync.

remaining negation patterns in the codebase:

title: refactor(tests): replace multi-assert with inline snapshots
body:
Replace `assert!(x.contains(...))` chains with single `assert_snapshot!` calls
across the test suite. Consolidate one-test-per-input into one-test-per-belief,
and delete tests that only verify constructors or dependencies.

34 files changed, net reduction of ~711 lines while maintaining equivalent
coverage. Test count dropped from ~558 to ~482 through consolidation (not
removal of coverage).

Key patterns applied:
- Chains of `assert!(x.contains("a")); assert!(x.contains("b"))` → single `assert_snapshot!(x)`
- 8 identical mutual-exclusivity tests → 1 table-driven test
- 6 parse-error tests → 1 test with 6 snapshots
- Tests verifying only `Style::new().bold()` produces bold → deleted (tests the dependency)
- Platform-dependent error messages (OS error text) kept as `contains` checks

Added test style guidance to `tests/CLAUDE.md`.

title: Use @ before paths in all section headings
body:
Unify the `@ path` convention across all user-facing output. Previously
headings (`USER CONFIG`, `PROJECT HOOKS`, etc.) showed bare paths while
status messages used `@ path`. Now everything uses `@ path` consistently.

Also changes `format_heading` separator from double-space to single-space.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of @max-sixty_
author: max-sixty
diff:

-format_heading("USER CONFIG", Some("~/.config/wt.toml"))
-// => "USER CONFIG  ~/.config/wt.toml" (title cyan, suffix plain)
+format_heading("USER CONFIG", Some("@ ~/.config/wt.toml"))
+// => "USER CONFIG @ ~/.config/wt.toml" (title cyan, suffix plain)
 ```
 
 ## stdout vs stderr

 `worktrunk::path`. This function replaces home directory prefixes with `~` for
 readability (e.g., `/Users/alex/projects/repo` → `~/projects/repo`).
 
-**Use `@` (not "at") before paths in status messages.** This is the codebase
-convention for associating an entity with a location:

+codebase convention for associating an entity with a location — in status
+messages, section headings, hints, and everywhere else:

+// BAD - heading without @
+format_heading("USER HOOKS", Some(&format_path_for_display(p)))
 ```
 
-**Exception:** Prose contexts (error descriptions, doc comments, help text) use
-"at" — `@` is for terse status messages only.
+**Exception:** Prose contexts (doc comments, help text) use "at" — `@` is for
+terse output only.

title: fix(output): replace quoted names with bold styling in error messages
body:
Replace single-quoted command and branch names with `cformat!` bold styling
in `bail!`/`.with_context()` error messages, per the output guidelines
("Never quote commands or branch names. Use styling to make them stand out").

Three call sites fixed:
- `switch.rs` — "Failed to fetch branch **{branch}**" (was `'{branch}'`)
- `switch.rs` — "Failed to create local branch **{branch}**" (was `'{branch}'`)
- `repository_ext.rs` — "Expected stash entry: **{name}**. Check **git stash list**." (was `'{name}'` and `'git stash list'`)

title: feat(help): syntax-highlight code blocks in --help
body:
Code blocks in `--help` were rendered as plain dimmed text — the markdown
language identifier (` ```toml `, ` ```console `) was discarded. Now they use
the existing gutter formatting with language-aware syntax highlighting:

- **TOML** blocks get synoptic highlighting (table headers cyan, strings green,
  comments dimmed)
- **console/bash/sh** blocks get tree-sitter-bash highlighting (commands blue,
  flags cyan, strings green)
- **Other** languages get dimmed text with gutter

Also makes TOML highlighting consistently dimmed (matching bash style) and
removes the 2-space indent from help tables so block elements are flush-left.

title: feat(hook): make hook_type and hook_name available as template variables
body:
These were already included in the JSON context piped to stdin but couldn't be used as `{{ hook_type }}` or `{{ hook_name }}` in templates — the values were inserted into `cmd_context` *after* template expansion.

Now both code paths (`expand_commands` for execution, `expand_command_template` for `wt hook show --expanded`) include them before rendering. Also added to `TEMPLATE_VARS` so `--var hook_type=...` works for testing.

title: feat(alias): add typo suggestions for unknown step commands
body:
When the user types an unknown step command or alias name, suggest the closest match using Jaro similarity (same algorithm and 0.7 threshold as clap). Checks both built-in step commands and configured aliases.

Also fixes error message styling per output guidelines: bold for names instead of quotes, no second-person pronouns ("perhaps" instead of "did you mean").

Examples:
- `wt step comit` → `Unknown step command comit — perhaps commit?`
- `wt step deplyo` (with alias `deploy`) → `Unknown step command deplyo — perhaps deploy?`
- `wt step zzz` (no close match) → `Unknown alias zzz (available: deploy, hello)`

title: fix(output): use bash formatting for verbose expansion gutter
body:
The `-v` template expansion output was using `format_with_gutter` (plain text)
instead of `format_bash_with_gutter` (dim + syntax highlighting) for shell
commands. Now template and result render with proper bash styling, matching
how commands appear elsewhere in the output.

Template and result are formatted as separate bash gutter blocks with a dim
`→` arrow between them, since the arrow can't go through the syntax
highlighter.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of @max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

 Format for template expansion:
 ```
 ○ Expanding name
- ┃ template → result
+ ┃ template (bash-highlighted)
+ ┃ → (dim)
+ ┃ result (bash-highlighted)
 ```
 
 - **Info message** for header (`○` symbol, "Expanding" + bold name)
-- **Gutter** for quoted content (template → result)
-- Arrow `→` is dim
-- For multiline: template lines, dim `→` on its own line, result lines
+- **Bash gutter** for template and result (dim + syntax highlighting via
+  `format_bash_with_gutter`)
+- **Plain gutter** for dim `→` separator (bypasses syntax highlighter)
+- Template and result are always on separate gutter blocks from the arrow,
+  because the `→` can't go through the bash syntax highlighter
 
 **`-vv` (debug):** Developer-facing logging output. MAY violate these guidelines.
 Uses `log::debug!()` with structured format for deep debugging. Not intended for

-        let content = if template.contains('\n') || result.contains('\n') {

title: feat(hook): add --dry-run flag to wt hook
body:
When `--dry-run` is passed to `wt hook <type>`, shows what commands would
run with template variables expanded, without executing them. Follows the
same pattern as `wt step <alias> --dry-run`. Skips approval prompts since
nothing is executed.

Also simplifies `run_hook()` by hoisting shared extra_vars computation
and hook config lookup out of the per-type match, reducing it from 6 arms
to 3 (FailFast, background, Warn).

```
$ wt hook pre-merge --dry-run
○ pre-merge project:lint would run:
  pre-commit run --all-files
○ pre-merge project:test would run:
  cargo test
```

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of @max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

title: Simplify: cache regexes, remove TOCTOU, fix silent wrong results
body:
Cache deprecated-variable regexes in a `LazyLock` static instead of compiling
4 regexes per call. Remove redundant `path.exists()` checks before
`read_to_string()` (TOCTOU). Replace `unwrap_or_default()` with error
propagation in `same_commit()`/`trees_match()` — previously malformed git
output would silently compare `"" == ""` and return `true`.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of @max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

title: docs: fix home page SEO — canonical dedup and consistent tagline
body:
The home page (`/`) and `/worktrunk/` serve identical content (the index
template renders `worktrunk.content` directly), but each declared its own
canonical URL. Google saw two competing pages and wasn't indexing either as
the home page result.

- Set canonical + og:url on `/worktrunk/` to point to `/`
- Fix home page og:title/twitter:title — was just "Worktrunk", now uses the
  full tagline from `config.extra.site_description`
- Align `worktrunk.md` description with `site_description`

title: test(remove): verify squash-merge detection via origin/main
body:
Add integration tests for the real GitHub workflow: push feature → squash-merge
on remote → `git fetch` → `wt remove`. The `effective_integration_target()`
code path that checks against `origin/main` (when local `main` is behind) had
no test coverage.

Two tests:
- Simple squash merge on remote — detected via `TreesMatch`
- Squash merge + main advances — detected via `MergeAddsNothing`

Both use `repo_with_remote` fixture with a simulated "GitHub side" (clone the
bare remote, squash-merge there, push back). Feature branches have multiple
commits to exercise real squash behavior.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of @max-sixty_
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- tests/integration_tests/remove.rs (+125/-0)
@@ -1159,6 +1159,131 @@ fn test_remove_squash_merged_then_main_advanced(repo: TestRepo) {
     ));
 }
 
+/// Simulate a GitHub squash merge: push feature to origin, squash-merge on
+/// the remote side (via a temporary clone), fetch locally, then `wt remove`.
+///
+/// This is the exact workflow that users hit:
+///   1. Create worktree, commit, push, open PR
+///   2. Squash-merge on GitHub
+///   3. `git fetch` locally
+///   4. `wt remove <branch>` — should detect integration via origin/main
+///
+/// The integration detection must use `effective_integration_target()` to check
+/// against `origin/main` (which is ahead of local `main` after fetch).
+#[rstest]
+fn test_remove_squash_merged_on_remote(#[from(repo_with_remote)] repo: TestRepo) {
+    let remote_path = repo.remote_path().unwrap();
+
+    // Create a feature branch with multiple commits (realistic PR)
+    repo.run_git(&["checkout", "-b", "feature-remote-squash"]);
+    std::fs::write(repo.root_path().join("feature.txt"), "initial").unwrap();
+    repo.run_git(&["add", "feature.txt"]);
+    repo.run_git(&["commit", "-m", "Add feature file"]);
+    std::fs::write(repo.root_path().join("feature.txt"), "revised").unwrap();
+    repo.run_git(&["add", "feature.txt"]);
+    repo.run_git(&["commit", "-m", "Revise feature"]);
+    std::fs::write(repo.root_path().join("feature.txt"), "final version").unwrap();
+    repo.run_git(&["add", "feature.txt"]);
+    repo.run_git(&["commit", "-m", "Finalize feature"]);
+    repo.run_git(&["push", "-u", "origin", "feature-remote-squash"]);
+
+    // Go back to main locally (don't pull — local main stays behind)
+    repo.run_git(&["checkout", "main"]);
+
+    // Simulate GitHub squash merge: clone the bare remote into a temp dir,
+    // squash-merge there, push back to the bare remote
+    let github_sim = repo.home_path().join("github-sim");
+    repo.run_git_in(
+        repo.home_path(),
+        &["clone", remote_path.to_str().unwrap(), "github-sim"],
+    );
+    // Squash merge feature into main (like GitHub's "Squash and merge" button)
+    repo.run_git_in(
+        &github_sim,
+        &["merge", "--squash", "origin/feature-remote-squash"],
+    );
+    repo.run_git_in(&github_sim, &["commit", "-m", "Add feature (#1)"]);
+    // Push the squash merge back to the bare remote
+    repo.run_git_in(&github_sim, &["push", "origin", "main"]);
+
+    // Fetch locally — origin/main now has the squash merge, local main does not
+    repo.run_git(&["fetch", "origin"]);
+
+    // Verify setup: local main is behind origin/main
+    let local_main = repo.git_output(&["rev-parse", "main"]);
+    let origin_main = repo.git_output(&["rev-parse", "origin/main"]);
+    assert_ne!(
+        local_main, origin_main,
+        "local main should be behind origin/main"
+    );
+
+    // Remove the feature branch — should detect as integrated via origin/main
+    assert_cmd_snapshot!(make_snapshot_cmd(
+        &repo,
+        "remove",
+        &["feature-remote-squash"],
+        None
+    ));
+}
+
+/// Like `test_remove_squash_merged_on_remote`, but main advances on the
+/// remote after the squash merge.
+/// Tests that `MergeAddsNothing` detection works through origin/main.
+#[rstest]
+fn test_remove_squash_merged_on_remote_then_advanced(#[from(repo_with_remote)] repo: TestRepo) {
+    let remote_path = repo.remote_path().unwrap();
+
+    // Create a feature branch with multiple commits (realistic PR)
+    repo.run_git(&["checkout", "-b", "feature-remote-squash2"]);
+    std::fs::write(repo.root_path().join("feature2.txt"), "draft").unwrap();
+    repo.run_git(&["add", "feature2.txt"]);
+    repo.run_git(&["commit", "-m", "WIP: start feature 2"]);
+    std::fs::write(repo.root_path().join("feature2.txt"), "done").unwrap();
+    repo.run_git(&["add", "feature2.txt"]);
+    repo.run_git(&["commit", "-m", "Complete feature 2"]);
+    repo.run_git(&["push", "-u", "origin", "feature-remote-squash2"]);
+
+    // Go back to main locally
+    repo.run_git(&["checkout", "main"]);
+
+    // Simulate GitHub: squash merge, then main advances with another commit
+    let github_sim = repo.home_path().join("github-sim2");
+    repo.run_git_in(
+        repo.home_path(),
+        &["clone", remote_path.to_str().unwrap(), "github-sim2"],
+    );
+    repo.run_git_in(
+        &github_sim,
+        &["merge", "--squash", "origin/feature-remote-squash2"],
+    );
+    repo.run_git_in(&github_sim, &["commit", "-m", "Add feature 2 (#2)"]);
+    // Main advances with another commit after the squash merge
+    std::fs::write(github_sim.join("other.txt"), "other content").unwrap();
+    repo.run_git_in(&github_sim, &["add", "other.txt"]);
+    repo.run_git_in(&github_sim, &["commit", "-m", "Unrelated commit"]);
+    repo.run_git_in(&github_sim, &["push", "origin", "main"]);
+
+    // Fetch locally
+    repo.run_git(&["fetch", "origin"]);
+
+    // Verify setup: local main is behind origin/main
+    let local_main = repo.git_output(&["rev-parse", "main"]);
+    let origin_main = repo.git_output(&["rev-parse", "origin/main"]);
+    assert_ne!(
+        local_main, origin_main,
+        "local main should be behind origin/main"
+    );
+
+    // Remove the feature branch — should detect as integrated via origin/main
+    // even though origin/main has advanced past the squash merge
+    assert_cmd_snapshot!(make_snapshot_cmd(
+        &repo,
+        "remove",
+        &["feature-remote-squash2"],
+        None
+    ));
+}
+

title: fix(ci): check issue author in verify-engagement step
body:
## Summary

- Fix the verify-engagement step in `claude-mention` to check issue **authorship** in addition to bot comments for plain issues
- This mirrors the existing PR author check (`PR_AUTHOR == worktrunk-bot`) but for issues

## Root cause

When `worktrunk-bot` opens an issue (e.g., via triage), the verify step only checked whether the bot had *commented* on the issue. If the bot authored the issue but hadn't commented yet, subsequent non-mention comments were incorrectly skipped — the bot silently ignored them.

This is exactly what happened on #1332: the bot opened the issue, @max-sixty commented without an `@` mention, the verify step found zero bot comments, and all subsequent steps were skipped. A second comment with `@worktrunk-bot` was needed to get a response (since mentions bypass the verify step entirely).

<details><summary>Workflow run evidence</summary>

[Run 22806824478](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/22806824478) (triggered by the first comment at 20:40:23) shows:
- `🔍 Verify bot engagement`: conclusion `success` (but `continue-on-error: true` masks the actual `outcome: failure`)
- All subsequent steps (`📂 Checkout code`, `🤖 Run Claude Code`, etc.): `skipped`

The verify step exited 1 because `BOT_COMMENTS` was 0 — the bot authored the issue but hadn't commented on it.

</details>

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify the workflow YAML is valid (CI will check this)
- [ ] Confirm that a non-mention comment on a bot-authored issue now triggers Claude (can test on a future bot-opened issue)

Closes #1332

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: worktrunk-bot
diff:
--- .github/workflows/claude-mention.yaml (+5/-1)
@@ -64,7 +64,11 @@ jobs:
             ISSUE_NUMBER="${{ github.event.issue.number }}"
 
             if [ -z "${{ github.event.issue.pull_request.url }}" ]; then
-              # Plain issue — check if bot has commented
+              # Plain issue — check if bot authored or commented
+              ISSUE_AUTHOR="${{ github.event.issue.user.login }}"
+              if [ "$ISSUE_AUTHOR" = "worktrunk-bot" ]; then
+                exit 0
+              fi
               BOT_COMMENTS=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$ISSUE_NUMBER/comments" \
                 --jq '[.[] | select(.user.login == "worktrunk-bot")] | length')
               if [ "$BOT_COMMENTS" -gt "0" ]; then

title: fix(skill): use +1 as soft signal, reinforce self-authored CI skip
body:
## Summary

- Reinforce self-authored CI skip as an early-return ("done, stop here") instead of a preamble — the bot ignored it in 1/2 self-authored sessions
- Change `+1` reaction semantics: use it as a standalone "looks good but not confident enough to approve" signal instead of always pairing it with approval. Approvals no longer require a reaction.

Fixes #1349, fixes #1350.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify next claude-review approval session does **not** post a +1 reaction
- [ ] Verify next review where bot is unsure posts +1 reaction without approving
- [ ] Verify next self-authored PR review skips CI monitoring

@@ -248,13 +248,24 @@ silent if there are none.
 - **Confident** (small, mechanical, well-tested): Approve.
 - **Moderately confident** (non-trivial but looks correct): Approve.

+When approving with no issues, approve with an empty body:

+  logic, want human eyes): Don't approve. Instead, add a `+1` reaction to

+  reaction with a COMMENT review. If there's nothing to say beyond "looks fine

title: feat(step): add alias command for user-defined command templates
body:
## Summary

- Adds `wt step <alias-name>` for running user-defined command templates configured in `[aliases]` sections of user or project config
- Aliases support the same template variables as hooks (`{{ branch }}`, `{{ worktree }}`, etc.) plus custom `--var KEY=VALUE` variables
- Project-config aliases require the same command approval flow as project hooks; user-config aliases are trusted. `--dry-run` skips approval since it's a read-only preview
- Alias names matching built-in step commands are filtered from the "available" list in error messages (shadowed by the built-in)
- Introduces `Phase` enum (`Hook(HookType)` | `Alias`) replacing the old `hook_type` + `phase_override` pattern in the approval system
- Renames `HookCommand` to `ApprovableCommand` since it now covers both hooks and aliases

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for `AliasOptions::parse` (name-only, --dry-run, --yes, --var, empty key rejection, positional arg rejection)
- [x] Integration tests for alias execution, dry-run (without --yes), exit code propagation
- [x] Integration tests for shadowing (filtered from available list)
- [x] Integration tests for user/project config merging
- [x] Integration tests for approval flow (project prompts, user skips, override skips, already-approved, --yes bypass, decline)
- [x] Unit tests for `merge_alias_maps` coverage
- [x] Sync test: `BUILTIN_STEP_COMMANDS` matches actual `StepCommand` clap variants

## Summary

- Remove `CLICOLOR_FORCE: 1` from all 7 Claude workflow env blocks
- Simplify `list-recent-runs.sh` (no longer needs to unset `CLICOLOR_FORCE`)

`CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` overrides `NO_COLOR` per the clicolors spec, causing `gh` to emit ANSI color codes in JSON output even in non-TTY contexts. This breaks `jq` parsing in 5 of 9 review sessions (2-5 wasted tool calls each). `CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always` already handles cargo output coloring.

Fixes #1346

- [ ] Verify `cargo test` still shows colored output (controlled by `CARGO_TERM_COLOR`)

title: refactor(git): replace porcelain commands with plumbing alternatives
body:
Replace porcelain git commands with plumbing alternatives for robustness:

- **`working_tree.rs`**: `git branch --show-current` and `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` → `git rev-parse --symbolic-full-name HEAD` with `symbolic-ref` fallback for unborn branches. Structured output (`refs/heads/<branch>` vs `HEAD`) instead of empty-string detection.
- **`diff.rs`**: `git show -s --format=` → `git log -1 --format=` (single commit) and `git log --no-walk --format=` (multi-commit). `git log` correctly resolves annotated tags to their underlying commit, unlike `git show` which outputs tag metadata before the formatted commit info.
- **`collect/mod.rs`**: Updated 3 stale comments referencing `git show`.

title: fix(output): prune summary & post-remove hook display path
body:
Two fixes to `wt step prune` output:

**Post-remove hook display path**: when removing a non-current worktree (the
common prune case), post-remove hooks run at `main_path` but the user stays at
cwd. Previously `post_hook_display_path(main_path)` was used unconditionally,
suppressing `@ path` when shell integration is active. Now uses
`pre_hook_display_path(main_path)` when `changed_directory` is false, correctly
showing the path when the user isn't there.

**Prune summary**: use ampersand pattern for paired worktree + branch removals,
matching the progress messages' "worktree & branch" phrasing. Unpaired items
(detached worktrees, orphan branches) list separately.

- `Pruned 1 worktree (with branch)` → `Pruned 1 worktree & branch`
- `Pruned 3 worktrees (with branches)` → `Pruned 3 worktrees & branches`
- `Pruned 1 worktree (with branch), 1 branch` → `Pruned 1 worktree & branch, 1 branch`
- `Pruned 1 branch, 1 detached worktree` → `Pruned 1 worktree, 1 branch`

title: docs: use .localhost subdomains instead of .lvh.me for Caddy routing
body:
Replace `.lvh.me` with `.localhost` in all Caddy subdomain routing examples
(docs, CLI help, tests). `.localhost` resolves to 127.0.0.1 via the OS on
macOS and Linux with systemd-resolved — no external DNS dependency.

Also fixes a flaky PTY test: `WORKTRUNK_TEST_DELAYED_STREAM_MS` was missing
from `STANDARD_TEST_ENV` in shell_wrapper.rs, causing `git worktree add`
output to appear non-deterministically under heavy parallel load.

Closes #1334

title: fix(skill): guide bot to offer fix commits when inline suggestions are impossible
body:
## Summary

- The review-pr skill told the bot to "add inline suggestions fixing each occurrence" when finding the same pattern in other files, but GitHub's review API only allows inline comments on lines in the diff
- When the bot reviewed #1336 (which only changed `flake.nix`), it found `pkgs.system` in `nix/home-manager-module.nix` too — but couldn't post an inline suggestion because that file wasn't in the diff, so it fell back to a code block in the review body
- Updated the skill to: (1) explain the API limitation, (2) prefer pushing a fix commit when possible, (3) when a commit isn't appropriate, clearly describe the fix and explain why an inline suggestion isn't available

## Test plan

- [ ] Review the skill wording for clarity
- [ ] Verify the bot uses the updated guidance on a future PR with out-of-diff suggestions

Closes #1341

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: worktrunk-bot
diff:
--- .claude/skills/review-pr/SKILL.md (+6/-2)
@@ -147,8 +147,9 @@ the same broken path across all workflow files.
 rg 'env\.HOME' .github/workflows/
 ```
 
-If the same issue exists elsewhere, add inline suggestions fixing each
-occurrence.
+If the same issue exists in files already in the diff, add inline suggestions
+fixing each occurrence. If the occurrence is in a file **not in the diff**,
+offer to push a fix commit with the correction.
 
 **Duplication check (mandatory for new functions/types):**
 
@@ -308,6 +309,9 @@ exact line — never as a code block in the review body. Inline suggestions let
 the author apply with one click; code blocks in the body force them to find the
 line and copy-paste manually.
 
+**Exception: lines outside the diff.** If a fix targets a file or line not in
+the diff, offer to push a fix commit instead.
+
 **Anti-pattern — code block in review body:**
 
 > The description on line 3 should be updated:

title: fix(prune): use plumbing command for branch listing
body:
During an interactive rebase, `git branch --format=%(refname:lstrip=2)` includes
a synthetic `(no branch, rebasing <name>)` entry. The orphan branch scan in
`step prune` passed this to `integration_reason()`, which tried to resolve it as
a git revision and crashed.

Switch `all_branches()` from `git branch` (porcelain) to `git for-each-ref
refs/heads/` (plumbing), which only iterates actual refs. Delete the
near-duplicate `local_branches()` — it was identical minus sorting, and neither
caller needed a specific order.

title: fix: pass --no-cd flag through to interactive picker
body:
## Problem

The `--no-cd` flag on `wt switch` was ignored when using the interactive picker (no branch argument). Running `wt switch --no-cd` and selecting a branch from the picker would still emit a cd directive, changing the shell's working directory.

This affected users with tmux-based workflows who use `--no-cd` because their post-switch hooks handle navigation (e.g., switching tmux sessions).

## Root cause

`handle_select()` hardcoded `change_dir: true` when calling `handle_switch_output()` — the `--no-cd` flag was never plumbed through from the CLI to the picker's switch path.

## Solution

Added a `change_dir: bool` parameter to `handle_select()` and passed `!no_cd` from both call sites:
- `wt switch` (no branch arg) → passes `!no_cd`
- `wt select` (deprecated) → passes `true` (always cd, matching prior behavior)

## Testing

- All 554 unit tests pass
- All 1146 integration tests pass on Linux, macOS, and Windows
- The `codecov/patch` failure is expected: the changed line is inside the interactive picker TUI code path which requires a real terminal and was already uncovered before this change (the previous hardcoded `true` on the same line was equally uncovered)

---
Closes #1330 — automated triage

- Unsets `CLICOLOR_FORCE` in `list-recent-runs.sh` before setting `NO_COLOR=1`
- `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` (set by the Claude Code environment) overrides `NO_COLOR` per the [clicolors spec](https://bixense.com/clicolors/), causing `gh` to emit ANSI codes in JSON output that break `jq` parsing

## Context

PR #1317 added `NO_COLOR=1` to fix ANSI codes in `gh` output, but the Claude Code environment also sets `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` which takes precedence. Every hourly review run fails at startup because `list-recent-runs.sh` can't parse the colorized JSON.

title: feat(switch): experimental Gitea PR support via pr: shortcut
body:
Add experimental Gitea PR support to `wt switch pr:<number>`.

The `pr:` syntax already resolved GitHub PRs; this teaches it to also resolve Gitea PRs via the `tea` CLI. GitLab continues to use `mr:`.

## Dispatch

`pr:N` now goes through `choose_pr_provider`:

1. `[forge] platform` in `.config/wt.toml` if set (`github` / `gitea` / `gitlab`)
2. Primary remote URL detection (host contains `github` / `gitea` / `gitlab`)
3. CLI auth lookup: if `tea` is configured for this host (per `~/.config/tea/config.yml`) but `gh` is not (per `gh auth token --hostname <host>`), pick Gitea
4. Default to GitHub

There is no longer an "ambiguous" fallback that tries both providers and wraps both errors — users on self-hosted Gitea instances either run `tea login add <host>` (auto-detected) or set `[forge] platform = "gitea"`.

## New code

- `src/git/remote_ref/gitea.rs` — `GiteaProvider` implementing `RemoteRefProvider` via `tea api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>`; reuses the shared `cli_api_error` / `run_cli_api` helpers.
- `src/git/remote_ref/info.rs` — `PlatformData::Gitea { host, head_owner, head_repo, base_owner, base_repo }`, wired into `source_ref()`, `prefixed_local_branch_name()`, and `find_remote()`.
- `src/git/url.rs` — `GitRemoteUrl::is_gitea()`.

Shared helpers introduced in this PR:

- `mod.rs::extract_host_from_html_url()` (used by github + gitea; identical 7-line chains collapsed).
- `github::is_authed_for()` (wraps `gh auth token --hostname`).
- `gitea::is_authed_for()` (reads tea's config.yml; never invokes `tea` to avoid OAuth refresh on lookup).

## Docs

User-facing copy says "GitHub PR" by default; one paragraph in `wt switch --help` mentions Gitea support, marked experimental.

## Tests

- 13 new integration tests covering Gitea same-repo, fork, error responses (401/403/404/5xx/malformed JSON/deleted fork/no source branch), `tea` not installed, `forge.platform` overrides, GitLab-remote-with-`pr:` bail, self-hosted defaults-to-GitHub, and self-hosted-with-`tea`-login routes-to-Gitea.
- Unit tests for `extract_source_branch` edge cases and the tea config parser.

## Compatibility

No CLI flag or config file changes. The `tea` CLI is only required for Gitea PRs; GitHub-only users see no change.

title: fix(ci): move concurrency to job level in claude-review
body:
## Summary

- Moves `concurrency` from workflow level to job level in `claude-review.yaml`
- Same fix as #1305 applied to `claude-mention.yaml`

## Problem

GitHub Actions evaluates workflow-level `concurrency` before job-level `if:`. When the review bot posts a review on a bot-authored PR, the `pull_request_review` event enters the concurrency group and cancels the in-progress run — then gets filtered out by the `if:` condition (which excludes `worktrunk-bot`'s own reviews). The result: the in-progress review response is killed with no replacement.

This was flagged by the review bot on #1305: "claude-review.yaml has the same pattern."

## Fix

Move `concurrency:` from workflow level to job level (after the `if:` block). Runs that don't pass the `if:` condition are skipped before entering the concurrency group, so they can't cancel in-progress runs.

-concurrency:
-  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
-  cancel-in-progress: true
-

title: fix: move concurrency to job level in claude-mention to prevent race
body:
## Summary

- Moves `concurrency` from workflow level to job level in `claude-mention.yaml`
- Fixes a race condition where bot comments from the hourly reviewer cancelled in-progress mention runs

## Problem

GitHub Actions evaluates workflow-level `concurrency` before job-level `if:`. When the hourly reviewer posted a bot comment on an issue, it triggered a new `claude-mention` workflow run that entered the concurrency group and cancelled the in-progress run. The new run then evaluated the job `if:` (which filters out bot comments) and skipped — but the cancellation had already happened. This caused the bot to silently drop responses to user comments (documented timeline in #1292).

## Fix

Job-level `concurrency` is evaluated after job-level `if:`, so a skipped job never enters the concurrency group and never cancels other runs.

## Test plan

- [x] Verify YAML is valid and the workflow parses correctly
- [ ] Observe that bot comments from hourly reviewer no longer cancel in-progress mention runs

Closes #1292

title: refactor(ci): extract run-fetching into reusable script with time-window filtering
body:
## Summary

- Extracts run-fetching logic into a reusable `.github/scripts/list-recent-runs.sh` script
- Dynamically discovers `claude-*` workflows instead of maintaining a hardcoded list
- Uses a two-step time filter: fetches runs started in the past 3 hours, then keeps only completed runs whose `updatedAt` is within the past hour (see #1301 for why)
- Simplifies the hourly review workflow prompt to just reference the script

Fixes #1301

## Test plan

- [ ] Next hourly review run should skip any in-progress jobs without polling

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: worktrunk-bot
diff:
--- .github/scripts/list-recent-runs.sh (+37/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Lists recently completed Claude CI runs.
+#
+# Fetches runs started in the past 3 hours, then filters to only those that
+# are completed and whose updatedAt is within the past hour. This two-step
+# approach is needed because `gh run list --created` filters by *start* time,
+# not *end* time — a run started 2h ago may have just finished, and a run
+# started 50min ago may still be running. See #1301 for details.
+#
+# Output: JSON array of {databaseId, conclusion, createdAt, updatedAt} objects.
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# Dynamically discover all claude-* workflows instead of maintaining a hardcoded list.
+mapfile -t WORKFLOWS < <(gh workflow list --json name --jq '.[].name | select(startswith("claude-"))')
+
+CREATED_SINCE=$(date -d '3 hours ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S)
+COMPLETED_AFTER=$(date -d '1 hour ago' +%s)
+
+all_runs="[]"
+
+for wf in "${WORKFLOWS[@]}"; do
+  runs=$(gh run list \
+    --workflow "${wf}" \
+    --created ">=${CREATED_SINCE}" \
+    --json databaseId,conclusion,createdAt,updatedAt \
+    --limit 50 2>/dev/null || echo "[]")
+  all_runs=$(echo "$all_runs" "$runs" | jq -s 'add')
+done
+
+# Filter: drop in-progress (empty conclusion), keep only recently finished
+echo "$all_runs" | jq --argjson cutoff "$COMPLETED_AFTER" '
+  [ .[]
+    | select(.conclusion != null and .conclusion != "")
+    | select((.updatedAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $cutoff)
+  ]
+'
--- .github/workflows/claude-hourly-review-reviewers.yaml (+2/-8)
@@ -54,15 +54,9 @@ jobs:

-            for wf in claude-review claude-ci-fix claude-issue-triage claude-mention claude-renovate claude-hourly-review-reviewers claude-nightly-cleaner; do

title: docs: add empty system prompt to codex command for speed
body:
## Summary

- Add `-c system_prompt=''` to the Codex example command to skip the default system prompt, reducing tokens and latency for commit message generation

Follow-up from #1295 — @max-sixty asked about using empty system prompts for speed.

**opencode**: Does not currently support disabling the system prompt. The system prompt is always injected, and even the plugin system has a safety fallback that restores the original if emptied. There are open feature requests ([#1242](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/1242), [#1894](https://github.com/sst/opencode/issues/1894), [#5005](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/5005)) but nothing available yet.

**Codex**: Has an undocumented `system_prompt` config key that can be overridden via `-c system_prompt=''`. There are feature requests for dedicated `--system-prompt` flags ([#6023](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/6023), [#11588](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/11588)) but not yet merged.

title: fix: use platform-aware config dir for nushell vendor autoload path
body:
## Problem

On Windows, `wt config shell install` installs the Nushell integration script to `~/.config/nushell/vendor/autoload/git-wt.nu` (the Linux/XDG default path) instead of the Windows-appropriate `AppData/Roaming/nushell/vendor/autoload/git-wt.nu`. This causes the shell integration to silently fail because Nushell on Windows doesn't look in `~/.config/`.

The root cause is in `nushell_config_candidates()` — it had a macOS-specific fallback (`~/Library/Application Support/nushell`) but no Windows equivalent, so Windows always fell back to the hardcoded `~/.config/nushell`.

## Solution

Replace the `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` candidate with `etcetera::choose_base_strategy().config_dir().join("nushell")`, which returns the correct platform config directory on all platforms:

- **Linux**: `~/.config/nushell` (unchanged)
- **macOS**: `~/Library/Application Support/nushell` (unchanged)
- **Windows**: `AppData/Roaming/nushell` (previously missing)

The existing `~/.config/nushell` fallback is retained as a universal XDG candidate. Deduplication handles overlaps on Linux.

## Testing

- All 554 unit tests pass (including all 9 nushell path tests)
- All 41 `configure_shell` integration tests pass
- Added assertion that platform config dir from `etcetera` is included in candidates
- Clippy clean

---
Closes #1293 — automated triage

title: fix: use marker file in fish completions test to avoid PTY race
body:
## Problem

`test_fish_completions_registered` failed on macOS CI with empty PTY output. The test relied on reading `__COMPLETION_REGISTERED__` from the PTY combined output, but PTY buffer flushing is unreliable on CI — the output was completely empty despite the script running successfully (exit code 0).

This is a flaky test, not caused by the commit under test (`dc7f5bca` — bright-black to underline formatting change).

## Solution

Use the marker file pattern already established by `test_zsh_wrapper_function_registered` (line 1930). Instead of checking PTY output for the marker string, the fish script writes its result to a file, and the test polls for that file using `wait_for_file_content()`.

This is the right level to fix because:
- The zsh test already uses this pattern with the comment "PTY buffer flushing is unreliable on CI"
- The fish test was the only remaining shell registration test relying on PTY output
- The marker file + polling approach is robust against PTY timing issues

## Alternatives considered

- **Retry the CI run**: Would work short-term but the flake would recur
- **Add a sleep before reading PTY output**: Unreliable, the zsh test already moved away from this approach

## Testing

- Ran `cargo test --test integration test_fish_completions_registered --features shell-integration-tests` — passes locally

---

title: fix: propagate repo_path() errors via Result instead of fallback
body:
## Summary

Alternative approach to #1225, as [requested by @max-sixty](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1225#issuecomment-4002706305).

Instead of silently falling back when `is_bare()` fails in `repo_path()`, this PR changes `repo_path()` to return `Result<&Path>` and propagates errors to callers:

- Changes `repo_path()` from `get_or_init` to `get_or_try_init`, returning `anyhow::Result<&Path>`
- Propagates the error via `?` at ~20 call sites across 18 files
- `build_hook_context()` and `format_path()` also updated to return `Result`
- Best-effort contexts (deprecation warnings, log formatter) use `.ok()` / `let Ok(..) else` to silently handle failures

**Tradeoff vs #1225:** More code churn but a cleaner failure mode — git failures surface early with clear errors instead of caching a potentially wrong path.

- [x] All 554 unit tests pass
- [x] All 1144 integration tests pass (including 21 bare repo tests)
- [x] Clippy clean, no warnings
- [ ] CI (linux, macos, windows)

title: fix(ci): reply to inline review comments in-thread
body:
## Problem

When triggered by an inline review comment (`pull_request_review_comment` event), the bot posts its response as a new top-level conversation comment instead of replying in the review thread. This separates the response from the code it references — see [PR #1266](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1266) where the bot's response to an inline comment about `strip_remote_prefix` landed in the conversation tab.

## Solution

Two changes to route inline review comment responses to the right place:

1. **`running-in-ci` skill** — added a "Replying to Comments" section that instructs Claude to detect comment types (inline review vs conversation) and use the GitHub review comment replies API (`/pulls/{number}/comments/{id}/replies`) for inline comments.

2. **`claude-mention` workflow** — added a dedicated prompt path for `pull_request_review_comment` events that passes the review comment ID and explicit instructions to reply in-thread using `gh api`.

Conversation comments (`issue_comment` events) are unchanged — GitHub doesn't support threading for these, so a new comment is correct.

## Testing

- YAML validated with `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"`
- Workflow changes are prompt/instruction only — no code logic to unit test
- Will verify behavior on next inline review comment trigger

title: fix(skill): add mandatory duplication check to pr-review
body:
## Summary

- Adds a mandatory **duplication check** step to the pr-review skill's review checklist: for every new function/type in a diff, search for (1) existing functions with similar names/signatures and (2) code with overlapping subgoals and the shared helpers it consumes
- Strengthens the low-confidence section to explicitly call out LLM-authored PRs and first-time contributors as requiring the duplication check

Closes #1267.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: worktrunk-bot
diff:
--- .claude/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md (+41/-3)
@@ -150,6 +150,40 @@ rg 'env\.HOME' .github/workflows/
 If the same issue exists elsewhere, add inline suggestions fixing each
 occurrence.
 
+**Duplication check (mandatory for new functions/types):**
+
+For every new public or module-level function added in the diff, search the
+codebase for existing functions that do the same thing. LLM-generated code
+frequently reinvents internal APIs — this is the highest-value check for
+externally contributed PRs.
+
+Two search strategies, both required:
+
+1. **Similar names and signatures.** Search for functions with similar names,
+   return types, or parameter types:
+
+   ```bash
+   # For a new `detect_pr_provider` function, search for existing detection
+   rg "fn detect.*provider|fn get.*platform|fn .*_provider" --type rust
+   ```
+
+2. **Overlapping subgoals.** Identify the intermediate steps the new code
+   performs (e.g., iterating remotes, parsing URLs, resolving an org name) and
+   search for existing code that does the same sub-tasks. Then read the
+   functions *that code* consumes — shared helpers often already exist one
+   layer down:
+
+   ```bash
+   # New code iterates remotes and parses URLs — who else does that?
+   rg "all_remote_urls|remote_url|GitRemoteUrl::parse" --type rust
+   # New code shells out to `git remote -v` — is there an existing wrapper?
+   rg "git remote|remote_urls" --type rust
+   ```
+
+If an existing function does substantially the same thing, flag it — reuse is
+almost always better than a parallel implementation. If shared helpers exist
+for the sub-steps, suggest using them instead of reimplementing.
+
 ### 4. Submit
 
 #### Staleness check
@@ -230,9 +264,13 @@ Increases confidence: small diffs, existing test coverage, mechanical changes,

title: fix(test): use marker file for fish binary-not-found test on macOS
body:
## Problem

The `test_fish_binary_not_found_clear_error::case_1` test fails on macOS CI because PTY output capture for fish shell returns empty output. The test asserts on `output.combined.contains("wt: command not found")`, but the combined output string is empty on macOS.

This is a known macOS PTY behavior — the sibling test `test_fish_wrapper_binary_not_found_no_infinite_loop` already documents and works around this:
> "This is reliable even when PTY output capture fails on macOS"

## Solution

Apply the same marker-file pattern used by the sibling test:

1. Write the exit code to a marker file from within the fish script
2. Use the marker file as the **primary check** (exit code = 127)
3. Demote the PTY output assertion to a **secondary check** that only runs when output is actually captured

This matches the established pattern in the codebase and is robust across platforms.

## Alternatives considered

- **Retry/increase timeout**: Wouldn't help — the empty output is a consistent PTY behavior on macOS, not a timing issue
- **Skip on macOS**: Too broad — the test logic is valid, just the verification method was fragile

## Testing

- Test passes locally on Linux: `cargo test --test integration test_fish_binary_not_found_clear_error --features shell-integration-tests`
- Waiting for macOS CI to confirm the fix

---

body:
## Summary

- Fixes `wt switch --remotes` failing with "No branch named origin/username/feature-1" when selecting a remote branch with `/` in its name
- Adds `Repository::strip_remote_prefix()` to detect and strip the remote prefix from remote-tracking ref names (e.g., `origin/username/feature-1` → `username/feature-1`)
- Uses this in `resolve_switch_target` so DWIM can create a local tracking branch from the remote ref

Fixes #1260

- [x] New test: `test_switch_remote_prefix_stripped` — switching with `origin/remote-feature` works
- [x] New test: `test_switch_remote_prefix_stripped_slash_in_branch` — switching with `origin/username/feature-1` works (the exact scenario from #1260)
- [x] All existing non-PR/MR switch tests pass

+    // Strip the remote prefix so DWIM can create a local tracking branch.
+    if !create && let Some(local_name) = repo.strip_remote_prefix(&resolved_branch) {

+
     // Resolve and validate base (only when --create is set)

--- src/git/repository/remotes.rs (+30/-0)
@@ -214,4 +214,34 @@ impl Repository {
         ])
         .is_ok()
     }
+
+    /// Strip the remote prefix from a remote-tracking branch name.
+    ///
+    /// Given a name like `origin/username/feature-1`, returns `Some("username/feature-1")`
+    /// if it's a valid remote-tracking ref. Returns `None` if the name isn't a remote ref
+    /// or the remote can't be identified.
+    ///
+    /// This handles remote names that don't contain `/` (the common case). It lists
+    /// all configured remotes and finds the one that matches the prefix.
+    ///
+    /// TODO: A cleaner approach would be to strip the prefix upstream — either have
+    /// `list_remote_branches()` return `(remote, local_branch, sha)` tuples, or track
+    /// `is_remote` on `ListItem` so the picker outputs just the local branch name.
+    /// Either would eliminate this runtime `git remote` call. See #1260.
+    pub fn strip_remote_prefix(&self, ref_name: &str) -> Option<String> {
+        // Quick check: is this actually a remote-tracking ref?
+        if !self.is_remote_tracking_branch(ref_name) {
+            return None;
+        }
+
+        // List all remotes and find the one that is a prefix of ref_name
+        let output = self.run_command(&["remote"]).ok()?;
+        output.lines().find_map(|remote| {
+            let prefix = format!("{}/", remote.trim());
+            ref_name
+                .strip_prefix(&prefix)
+                .filter(|branch| !branch.is_empty())
+                .map(|branch| branch.to_string())
+        })
+    }
 }

title: fix: keep GitHub blob/repo link checking with better resilience
body:
## Problem

CI failed on `main` ([run 22680048718](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/22680048718)) because the `lychee-system` link checker hit transient HTTP/2 protocol errors on GitHub URLs. Both the `lint` and `test (macos)` jobs failed.

The failing URLs included blob links, user profiles, and stargazers — patterns not covered by the existing exclusions.

## Solution

Improve lychee's resilience while **keeping blob/repo link checking intact** (these are the links most likely to go stale in our docs):

1. **Retry tuning**: bumped `max_retries` to 6, added `retry_wait_time = 2` to space out retries
2. **Concurrency reduction**: added `max_concurrency = 8` to reduce thundering herd effects against GitHub
3. **Targeted new exclusions** for URLs we don't control and that are prone to rate limiting/502s:
   - Stargazers pages
   - Release tag pages
   - Bare user/org profile pages (e.g., `github.com/username`)

Existing exclusions for commits, issues, PRs, and actions are retained. Blob and repo-level links continue to be checked.

## Testing

- `pre-commit run lychee-system --all-files` passes locally
- Full `pre-commit run --all-files` — all hooks pass
- CI is green

---
🤖 Automated fix for [failed run](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/22680048718)
author: worktrunk-bot
diff:
--- .config/lychee.toml (+10/-2)
@@ -5,9 +5,11 @@
 root_dir = "docs/static"
 
 # Network resilience - handles transient failures
-max_retries = 5
+max_retries = 6
+retry_wait_time = 2
 timeout = 20
 max_redirects = 5
+max_concurrency = 8
 
 # Accepted HTTP status codes
 accept = [200, 206, 429]
@@ -25,11 +27,17 @@ exclude = [
     # Private or authenticated GitHub resources
     "github\\.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues",
 
-    # GitHub immutable resources (occasionally return 502/504 on heavy load)
+    # GitHub resources that are either immutable or not our content to maintain
+    # (user profiles, stargazers, commit SHAs, external repo issues/PRs/actions)
     "github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/commit",
     "github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/issues",
     "github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/pull",
     "github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/actions",
+    "github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/stargazers",
+    "github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/releases/tag",
+
+    # GitHub user/org profiles (no content we control, frequently 429/502)
+    "github\\.com/[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$",
 
     # Social media (blocks GitHub Actions)
     "twitter\\.com",
