author: max-sixty
diff:
--- .claude/skills/worktrunk-review/SKILL.md (+64/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,64 @@
+---
+name: worktrunk-review
+description: Reviews a pull request for idiomatic Rust, project conventions, and code quality. Use when asked to review a PR or when running as an automated PR reviewer.
+argument-hint: "[PR number]"
+---
+
+# Worktrunk PR Review
+
+Review a pull request to worktrunk, a Rust CLI tool for managing git worktrees.
+
+**PR to review:** $ARGUMENTS
+
+## Setup
+
+Load these skills first:
+
+1. `/reviewing-code` — systematic review checklist (design review, universal
+   principles, completeness)
+2. `/developing-rust` — Rust idioms and patterns
+
+Then read CLAUDE.md (project root) to understand project-specific conventions.
+
+## Instructions
+
+1. Read the PR diff with `gh pr diff <number>`.
+2. Read the changed files in full (not just the diff) to understand context.
+3. Follow the `reviewing-code` skill's structure: design review first, then
+   tactical checklist.
+
+## What to review
+
+**Idiomatic Rust and project conventions:**
+
+- Does the code follow Rust idioms? (Iterator chains over manual loops, `?` over
+  match-on-error, proper use of Option/Result, etc.)
+- Does it follow the project's conventions documented in CLAUDE.md? (Cmd for
+  shell commands, error handling with anyhow, accessor naming conventions, etc.)
+- Are there unnecessary allocations, clones, or owned types where borrows would
+  suffice?
+
+**Code quality:**
+
+- Is the code clear and well-structured?
+- Are there simpler ways to express the same logic?
+- Does it avoid unnecessary complexity, feature flags, or compatibility layers?
+
+**Correctness:**
+
+- Are there edge cases that aren't handled?
+- Could the changes break existing functionality?
+- Are error messages helpful and consistent with the project style?
+
+**Testing:**
+
+- Are the changes adequately tested?
+- Do the tests follow the project's testing conventions (see tests/CLAUDE.md)?
+
+## How to provide feedback
+
+- Use inline comments for specific code issues.
+- Use `gh pr comment` for a top-level summary.
+- Be constructive and explain *why* something should change, not just *what*.
+- Distinguish between suggestions (nice to have) and issues (should fix).
+- Don't nitpick formatting — that's what linters are for.
--- .github/workflows/claude-review.yaml (+70/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
+name: claude-review
+# Runner versions pinned; see ci.yaml header comment for rationale.
+
+# Automatic code review on PRs from external contributors.
+# Uses pull_request_target so secrets are available for fork PRs.
+on:
+  pull_request_target:
+    types: [opened, synchronize, ready_for_review, reopened]
+
+concurrency:
+  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+env:
+  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
+  CLICOLOR_FORCE: 1
+
+jobs:
+  review:
+    # Skip draft PRs
+    # To skip PRs from repo members, uncomment the author_association conditions:
+    # github.event.pull_request.author_association != 'OWNER' &&
+    # github.event.pull_request.author_association != 'MEMBER' &&
+    if: >-
+      github.event.pull_request.draft == false
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # Scoped environment — only CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is needed.
+    # Publishing tokens etc. are not accessible.
+    environment: claude-review
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+      pull-requests: write
+      issues: write
+      id-token: write
+      actions: read
+    steps:
+      - name: 📂 Checkout code
+        uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/merge
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - name: 🔧 Configure git for Claude
+        run: |
+          git config --global user.name "Claude Code"
+          git config --global user.email "claude@anthropic.com"
+
+      - name: 🤖 Review PR with Claude
+        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
+        with:
+          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
+          github_token: ${{ github.token }}
+          additional_permissions: |
+            actions: read
+          use_sticky_comment: true
+          prompt: |
+            Use /worktrunk-review ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
+          claude_args: |
+            --model opus
+            --allowedTools Bash,Edit,Read,Write,Glob,Grep,WebSearch,WebFetch,Task,Skill
+            --append-system-prompt "You are operating in a GitHub Actions CI environment. Use /running-in-ci before starting work."
+
+      - name: 📋 Upload Claude Code session logs
+        if: always()
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v6
+        with:
+          name: claude-session-logs
+          path: ~/.claude/
+          retention-days: 30
+          if-no-files-found: warn

body:
When `nu` is in PATH, `wt config shell install` now creates the vendor/autoload directory automatically instead of skipping nushell. The directory was introduced in nushell v0.96.0 and isn't always pre-created, causing install to silently skip nushell users.

Follows the existing PowerShell pattern: detect the shell binary, then set should_configure and allow_create so the directory gets created on the user's behalf.

This fixes issue reported in #964 about installation being skipped on nushell

title: fix(select): screen artifacts left after interactive picker exits
body:
Fixes #1027.

skim-tuikit's cleanup sends `rmcup` in partial-height mode even though `smcup` was never sent, leaving the TUI on screen.

`no_clear_start(true)` forces tuikit to use `cursor_goto + erase_down` instead.
author: davidbeesley
diff:
--- src/commands/select/mod.rs (+4/-0)
@@ -160,6 +160,10 @@ pub fn handle_select(branches: bool, remotes: bool, config: &UserConfig) -> anyh
     // Configure skim options with Rust-based preview and mode switching keybindings
     let options = SkimOptionsBuilder::default()
         .height("90%".to_string())
+        // Workaround for skim-tuikit bug: partial-height mode skips smcup but
+        // cleanup still sends rmcup, leaving artifacts. no_clear_start forces
+        // cursor_goto + erase_down cleanup instead. See skim-rs/skim#880.
+        .no_clear_start(true)
         .layout("reverse".to_string())
         .header_lines(1) // Make first line (header) non-selectable
         .multi(false)
--- tests/integration_tests/switch_picker.rs (+3/-4)
@@ -787,14 +787,13 @@ branches = true
     );
 
     let env_vars = repo.test_env_vars();
-    // Wait for orphan-branch to appear before sending Escape
-    // Under CI load, the branch list may take time to render fully
-    let result = exec_in_pty_with_input_expectations(
+    // Capture screen BEFORE sending Escape. Screen must stabilize with orphan-branch visible.
+    let result = exec_in_pty_capture_before_abort(
         wt_bin().to_str().unwrap(),
         &["switch"], // No --branches flag - config should enable it
         repo.root_path(),
         &env_vars,
-        &[("\x1b", Some("│orphan-branch"))], // Wait for branch to appear (│ = border drawn)
+        &[("", Some("│orphan-branch"))], // Wait for orphan-branch to appear before abort
     );
 
     assert_valid_abort_exit_code(result.exit_code);

title: fix(statusline): scope branch diff to sparse checkout cone
body:
In sparse checkout repos, `branch_diff_stats()` runs `git diff --numstat merge_base..HEAD`, a commit-to-commit diff covering all files in the repo, not just the sparse cone. This produces inflated line counts (e.g. `^+4M -2M`) that don't reflect the user's working set.

## Changes

- Add cached `sparse_checkout_paths()` on `Repository` that runs `git sparse-checkout list` and returns cone paths (empty for non-sparse repos)
- Pass sparse checkout paths as pathspecs (`-- path1 path2`) to `git diff --numstat` in `branch_diff_stats()`
- Distinguish expected exit code 128 (non-sparse) from unexpected failures with `log::debug!`

Working tree diff (`@+N -N`) is already correct,`git diff --numstat HEAD` respects sparse checkout. Commit counts are unchanged since they count commits, not files.

## Testing

- `test_sparse_checkout_paths_empty_for_normal_repo`
- `test_sparse_checkout_paths_returns_cone_paths`
- `test_sparse_checkout_paths_cached`
- `test_branch_diff_stats_scoped_to_sparse_checkout`,verifies scoped stats are smaller than full-repo stats

title: fix: unset CLAUDECODE env var for LLM subprocess
body:
## Summary

- Strip `CLAUDECODE` env var before spawning LLM commands in `execute_llm_command`
- Claude Code sets `CLAUDECODE=1` in all subprocesses and blocks nested invocations, even non-interactive `claude -p` — this breaks `wt step commit` / `wt merge` from within Claude Code
- Companion to #1020 (doc fix); this is the code fix that handles it for all users regardless of config

## Test plan

- [x] All unit and integration tests pass (1026 integration, 499 unit)
- [x] Pre-commit lints pass
- [ ] Verify `wt step commit` works from within Claude Code without `CLAUDECODE=` in config

author: max-sixty
diff:
--- src/llm.rs (+7/-0)
@@ -297,10 +297,17 @@ fn execute_llm_command(command: &str, prompt: &str) -> anyhow::Result<String> {
     }
 
     let shell = ShellConfig::get();
+    // TODO(claude-code-nesting): Claude Code sets CLAUDECODE=1 and blocks nested
+    // invocations, even non-interactive `claude -p`. Remove this env_remove if
+    // Claude Code relaxes the check for non-interactive mode. If they don't fix
+    // it, replace with a deprecation warning + config.new migration to have users
+    // add `CLAUDECODE=` to their command string themselves.
+    // https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/25803
     let output = Cmd::new(shell.executable.to_string_lossy())
         .args(&shell.args)
         .arg(command)
         .stdin_bytes(prompt)
+        .env_remove("CLAUDECODE")
         .run()
         .context("Failed to spawn LLM command")?;

title: fix(docs): unset CLAUDECODE in Claude Code commit command
body:
## Summary

- Add `CLAUDECODE=` prefix to the Claude Code command example in LLM commit docs
- Claude Code sets `CLAUDECODE=1` in subprocess environments and blocks nested invocations, which breaks `wt step commit` / `wt merge` when run from within a Claude Code session

title: fix(ci): exclude GitHub index URLs from lychee link checker
body:
## Problem

The macOS CI job failed because lychee (link checker) got a 502 Bad Gateway when checking `https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues`. The lychee config already excludes GitHub issue/PR/commit/actions URLs to avoid transient failures, but the exclusion patterns required a trailing slash:

```
"github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/issues/"
```

This matches `/issues/123` but **not** `/issues` (the index page). Six docs files link to `https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues` without a trailing slash, so they weren't excluded and failed on a transient 502.

## Solution

Remove the trailing slash from the `commit`, `issues`, and `pull` exclusion patterns so they match both index pages (`/issues`) and specific items (`/issues/123`). The `actions` pattern already lacked a trailing slash and was unaffected.

## Alternatives considered

Could also add the specific URL `github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues` as a separate exclusion, but fixing the generic patterns is more robust — it prevents the same issue for any GitHub repo URL referenced in docs.

## Testing

- Ran `lychee --config .config/lychee.toml` on the six affected files — 0 errors (previously 6)
- Verified the patterns still match specific item URLs (e.g., `/issues/123`)
- `cargo test --lib --bins` passes (491 tests)

---
🤖 Automated fix for [failed run](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/22014481654)
author: worktrunk-bot
diff:
--- .config/lychee.toml (+3/-3)
@@ -26,9 +26,9 @@ exclude = [
     "github\\.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues",
 
     # GitHub immutable resources (occasionally return 502/504 on heavy load)
-    "github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/commit/",
-    "github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/issues/",
-    "github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/pull/",
+    "github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/commit",
+    "github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/issues",
+    "github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/pull",
     "github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/actions",
 
     # Social media (blocks GitHub Actions)

title: feat: add `wt config state vars` for per-branch custom variables
body:
Adds `wt config state vars set/get/list/clear` commands for storing custom variables per branch in git config (`worktrunk.state.{branch}.vars.{key}`). Variables are available in all template contexts via `{{ vars.key }}` syntax (hooks, `wt step eval`), with JSON dot access (`{{ vars.config.port }}`) and default filters (`{{ vars.env | default('dev') }}`).

Uses `KEY=VALUE` syntax for `set` — `wt config state vars set env=staging` — matching Docker `-e`, Heroku `config:set`, Fly `secrets set`, and worktrunk's own `--var KEY=VALUE` convention. Splits on first `=` only, so values can contain `=` (URLs, JSON).

The database-per-worktree example now uses `vars` to store the connection string during `post-start`, replacing the `.env.local` heredoc pattern. The URL is accessible outside hooks via `$(wt config state vars get db-url)`.

Includes vars data in `wt list --format=json` output and `wt config state get` display. Builds on #1004 (`wt step eval`). Part of #947.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for vars template injection (empty, with data, no branch, JSON dot access, shell escaping)
- [x] Integration tests for vars CLI commands (set, get, list, clear, clear --all, --branch flag)
- [x] Edge-case tests for KEY=VALUE parsing (values containing `=`, empty values)
- [x] Integration tests for vars in JSON output (present with data, absent when empty)
- [x] All 493 unit + 1294 integration tests pass

title: fix(ci): remove secrets from job-level if in claude-mention workflow
body:
## Summary

- Remove `secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from job-level `if:` in `claude-mention.yaml` — the `secrets` context isn't available there ([actions/runner#520](https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/520)), causing GitHub to fail workflow validation on every push to every branch
- Replace the fork-PR detection with `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`, which uses the always-resolvable `github` context

## Test plan

- [ ] Push to branch triggers ci/release workflows but **not** a failed claude-mention run
- [ ] `@claude` mention on a same-repo PR still triggers the workflow
- [ ] `@claude` review comment on a fork PR is cleanly skipped (no red X)

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of @max-sixty_
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- .github/workflows/claude-mention.yaml (+8/-10)
@@ -18,17 +18,15 @@ env:
 
 jobs:
   claude:
-    # Only run when body/comment contains @claude AND secrets are available.
-    # Review comments on fork PRs don't receive repository secrets (GitHub
-    # security restriction) so the job skips. Use a regular PR comment on the
-    # Conversation tab to trigger @claude on fork PRs instead.
+    # Only run when body/comment contains @claude.
+    # Note: secrets cannot be used in job-level `if:` (actions/runner#520) —
+    # doing so causes GitHub to fail the workflow on push validation. For review
+    # comments on fork PRs (which don't receive secrets), we detect forks via
+    # github.event context instead. Use a Conversation tab comment for fork PRs.
     if: |
-      secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN != '' &&
-      (
-        (github.event_name == 'issues' && contains(github.event.issue.body, '@claude')) ||
-        (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude')) ||
-        (github.event_name == 'pull_request_review_comment' && contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude'))
-      )
+      (github.event_name == 'issues' && contains(github.event.issue.body, '@claude')) ||
+      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude')) ||
+      (github.event_name == 'pull_request_review_comment' && contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude') && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository)
     runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
     permissions:
       contents: write # Allow pushing commits

title: feat: add `wt step eval` for template expression evaluation
body:
## Summary

- Add experimental `wt step eval` subcommand that evaluates a minijinja template in the current worktree context and prints the result to stdout
- Reuses existing hook template infrastructure — all variables (`branch`, `repo`, `worktree_path`, etc.) and filters (`hash_port`, `sanitize`, `sanitize_db`) are available
- Output goes to stdout with no decoration or shell escaping, designed for scripting and shell substitution

```
$ wt step eval '{{ branch | hash_port }}'
16066

$ curl http://localhost:$(wt step eval '{{ branch | hash_port }}')/health
```

This is the first step from the [IDEAS.md](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/blob/arbitrary-data/IDEAS.md) design doc, directly addressing the user request in #947 — "found no way to run it on a single branch."

--- .claude/skills/running-in-ci/SKILL.md (+54/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,54 @@
+---
+name: running-in-ci
+description: CI environment rules for GitHub Actions workflows. Use when operating in CI — covers security, CI monitoring, and PR comment formatting.
+---
+
+# Running in CI
+
+## Security
+
+NEVER run commands that could expose secrets (`env`, `printenv`, `set`,
+`export`, `cat`/`echo` on config files containing credentials). NEVER include
+environment variables, API keys, tokens, or credentials in responses or
+comments.
+
+## CI Monitoring
+
+After pushing changes to a PR branch, monitor CI until all checks pass:
+
+1. Monitor with `gh pr checks` or `gh run list --branch <branch>`
+2. Wait for completion with `gh run watch`
+3. If CI fails, diagnose with `gh run view <run-id> --log-failed`
+4. Fix issues, commit, push, and repeat
+5. Do not return until CI is green — local tests alone are not sufficient (CI
+   runs on Linux, Windows, macOS)
+
+## PR Comment Formatting
+
+Keep PR comments concise. Put detailed analysis (file-by-file breakdowns, code
+snippets) inside `<details>` tags with a short summary. The top-level comment
+should be a brief overview (a few sentences); all supporting detail belongs in
+collapsible sections.
+
+Example:
+
+```
+<details><summary>Detailed findings (6 files)</summary>
+
+...details here...
+
+</details>
+```
+
+## Tone
+
+You are a helpful reviewer raising observations, not a manager assigning work.
+Never create checklists or task lists for the PR author. Instead, note what you
+found and let the author decide what to act on.
+
+## PR Review Comments
+
+For PR review comments on specific lines (shown as `[Comment on path:line]` in
+`<review_comments>`), ALWAYS read that file and examine the code at that line
+before answering. The question is about that specific code, not the PR in
+general.

title: fix(test): increase STABILIZE_TIMEOUT to 10s for slow macOS CI
body:
## Problem

The `test_switch_picker_respects_list_config` test was consistently failing on macOS CI with the error:

```
Warning: Screen did not fully stabilize within 5s
thread 'integration_tests::switch_picker::test_switch_picker_respects_list_config' panicked
orphan-branch should appear when [list] branches = true in config.
```

The test waits for the string "│orphan-branch" to appear in the switch picker when `[list] branches = true` is configured. Under heavy CI load on macOS, the async branch loading didn't complete within the 5-second `STABILIZE_TIMEOUT`, causing the test to fail.

**Root cause**: The test uses `exec_in_pty_with_input_expectations` with a content expectation `Some("│orphan-branch")`, which blocks until both:
1. The screen content stabilizes (no changes for `STABLE_DURATION`)
2. The expected content appears

On slow macOS CI runners under load, the branch list population takes longer than 5 seconds, triggering the timeout.

## Solution

Increase `STABILIZE_TIMEOUT` from 5 seconds to 10 seconds to match the existing `READY_TIMEOUT` value. Both timeouts are documented as "Long timeout ensures reliability on slow CI" - this change makes them consistent.

The fix addresses the symptom (timeout too short) at the right level - this is a PTY test infrastructure constant that affects all picker tests, not a problem with the test logic or the feature being tested.

## Alternatives considered

1. **Fix only this specific test**: Could add a longer timeout just for this test case, but that would be inconsistent with other picker tests and create maintenance burden.

2. **Investigate why branch loading is slow**: This would be investigating the wrong thing - the branch loading works correctly, it's just that macOS CI is slower under load. The test already uses the best practices (waiting for content to appear rather than fixed delays).

3. **Make the test less strict**: Could remove the content expectation and only wait for time-based stability, but that would make the test weaker and potentially flaky in different ways.

The chosen fix (increasing the timeout constant) is the simplest and most appropriate solution - it acknowledges that CI can be slow and gives adequate time for operations to complete.

## Testing

- Test passes locally consistently (previously took ~6s, now allows up to 10s)
- The test logic and assertions remain unchanged
- All other picker tests inherit the same timeout increase, making them more robust

---

title: fix: wait for orphan-branch to appear in switch picker test
body:
## Problem

The `test_switch_picker_respects_list_config` test was failing on macOS CI (run 21874692808) because it immediately sent Escape without waiting for the branch list to fully render. Under CI load, the "orphan-branch" item might not appear within the 500ms time-based stability window.

The test creates an orphan branch (branch without a worktree), sets config `[list] branches = true`, and expects the switch picker to show that branch. However, the test output showed only the worktree branches (main, active-worktree, feature-a, feature-b) but not the orphan-branch, indicating it hadn't rendered yet when the test captured the screen.

## Solution

Use `exec_in_pty_with_input_expectations` and wait for `"│orphan-branch"` to appear before sending Escape. This ensures:
1. The branch list has fully loaded
2. The TUI border (`│`) has been drawn (not just the text content)

This is the same pattern used in the fix from #969 for preview panels, which addressed identical timing issues under CI load.

## Alternatives considered

Could also increase the `STABLE_DURATION` constant globally, but that would slow down all tests. Fixing at the individual test level with content expectations is more precise and only adds delay when needed.

Could also change just this test to use `exec_in_pty_with_input` with a longer timeout, but that wouldn't guarantee the content has rendered - it would just wait longer and hope. Content expectations are more reliable.

## Testing

Verified the fix locally:
```bash
cargo test --test integration test_switch_picker_respects_list_config --features shell-integration-tests
```

Test passes consistently. The fix follows the exact pattern established in #969 for handling async content rendering in PTY tests.

title: fix: preserve all terminal rows in TUI snapshot tests
body:
## Problem
The test `test_switch_picker_preview_panel_log` was failing on macOS CI after commit fbbe29b3. The test expected the preview panel to show many blank lines (lines 14-31 in the snapshot), but the new output was truncating them.

**Root cause**: The previous fix (PR #962, commit fbbe29b3) attempted to preserve blank lines by keeping `last_content_idx + 4` lines, but this was insufficient and didn't match what the PR description claimed it would do.

The PR description for #962 said the fix would be:
```rust
if result.ends_with('\n') {
    result.pop();
}
```

But the actual code committed was:
```rust
let last_content_idx = lines.iter().rposition(|line| !line.is_empty()).unwrap_or(0);
let keep_lines = (last_content_idx + 4).min(lines.len());
lines.truncate(keep_lines);
```

The `+ 4` was an arbitrary value that worked for some tests but not for `test_switch_picker_preview_panel_log`, which has ~18 blank preview lines that need to be preserved.

## Solution
Remove the truncation logic entirely and simply join all terminal rows. The preview panel's blank lines are intentional and should be preserved for cross-platform consistency.

Changed from:
```rust
let last_content_idx = lines.iter().rposition(|line| !line.is_empty()).unwrap_or(0);
let keep_lines = (last_content_idx + 4).min(lines.len());
lines.truncate(keep_lines);
lines.join("\n")
```

To:
```rust
// Join all lines - preserve blank lines for cross-platform consistency
// The preview panel intentionally shows blank lines even when empty
lines.join("\n")
```

This preserves all 30 terminal rows as rendered by the vt100 parser, ensuring consistent snapshots across platforms.

## Alternatives considered
**Keep the truncation with a larger offset** - Could change `+ 4` to `+ 20` or similar, but this is fragile and arbitrary. Different tests have different numbers of blank lines.

**Platform-specific snapshots** - Could create separate snapshots for macOS vs Linux, but this hides issues and doubles maintenance burden.

**This fix (no truncation)** - Preserves the actual terminal screen as rendered, ensuring tests verify consistent behavior. The terminal is only 30 rows, so we're not preserving excessive blank lines.

## Testing
All 10 switch_picker tests pass locally on Linux:
```bash
cargo test --test integration switch_picker --features shell-integration-tests
# ✓ 10 tests passed including test_switch_picker_preview_panel_log
```

title: fix(switch): pr:NNNN fails for same-repo PRs in repos without fetch refspecs
body:
## Summary

- Fix `wt switch pr:NNNN` and `wt switch mr:NNNN` failing with "No branch named X" for same-repo PRs/MRs in repos with limited or missing fetch refspecs (bare repos, single-branch clones)
- Apply the same fix to GitLab MRs, unifying the GitHub/GitLab same-repo fetch logic

## Problem

Two issues in the same-repo PR/MR flow when `remote.origin.fetch` is limited or absent:

1. **Fetch didn't create the tracking ref** — `git fetch origin <branch>` only updates `FETCH_HEAD`; it only creates `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` if the configured fetch refspec covers that branch.

2. **`git worktree add` DWIM failed** — even after fixing (1), `git worktree add <path> <branch>` relies on DWIM (Do What I Mean) to auto-create a local branch from the remote tracking ref. DWIM also requires configured fetch refspecs.

## Fix

1. Use an explicit refspec (`+refs/heads/<branch>:refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>`) when fetching, so the tracking ref is always created regardless of repo config.

2. When the branch doesn't exist locally but exists on exactly one remote, explicitly use `git worktree add -b <branch> <path> <remote>/<branch>` instead of relying on DWIM.

3. Unify GitHub PR and GitLab MR same-repo resolution into a single `match` with shared fetch logic. Move GitLab URL parsing to the boundary (`fetch_mr_info`) so `host`/`base_owner`/`base_repo` are available in `PlatformData::GitLab`.

## Test plan

## Summary

- Add system-wide config file support for organization-wide defaults
- Config loading order: system config → user config → environment variables
- System config search locations follow platform conventions

## System config locations

- `$WORKTRUNK_SYSTEM_CONFIG_PATH` (explicit override)
- `$XDG_CONFIG_DIRS` directories (colon-separated, Unix)
- Linux: `/etc/xdg/worktrunk/config.toml`
- macOS: `/Library/Application Support/worktrunk/config.toml`
- Windows: `%PROGRAMDATA%\worktrunk\config.toml`

## Merge behavior

Uses the same format as user config. The config crate deep-merges TOML tables:
- **Different named hooks** from system + user coexist (e.g., org defines `company-lint`, user adds `my-lint`)
- **Same-named hooks**: user replaces system
- **Different hook types** are independent

Visible in `wt config show` with a hint when no system config exists.

## Prior art

- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings#when-to-use-each-scope

title: fix: preserve blank lines in TUI snapshot tests for cross-platform consistency
body:
## Problem

The `test_switch_picker_abort_with_escape` test (and potentially other TUI snapshot tests) was failing on macOS CI but passing on Linux. The test was expecting 24 blank lines in the preview panel after "○ main has no uncommitted changes", but on macOS it was only getting 1 blank line.

**Root cause**: The `render_terminal_screen()` function in `switch_picker.rs` used aggressive trailing blank line trimming:

```rust
// Trim trailing empty lines
while result.ends_with("\n\n") {
    result.pop();
}
```

This `while` loop removes ALL consecutive trailing empty lines. The snapshots expect the full terminal height (30 rows) to be preserved with blank lines in the preview panel. On Linux, the vt100 terminal parser apparently preserves these blank lines (possibly due to cursor positioning or terminal state), but on macOS CI, the parser doesn't capture them the same way. When the trimming logic ran on macOS, it removed all the blank preview lines down to just 1.

## Solution

Replace the aggressive trimming with minimal trimming - only remove the single trailing newline that comes from the last row iteration:

```rust
// Trim only the final trailing newline if present (preserve blank lines for consistent snapshots)
if result.ends_with('\n') {
    result.pop();
}
```

This preserves all blank lines that are part of the actual terminal screen rendering, ensuring consistent snapshots across platforms.

## Why This is the Right Fix

**Alternative 1: Platform-specific snapshots** - Could create separate snapshots for macOS vs Linux, but this hides the real issue and doubles maintenance burden. The terminal screen SHOULD render the same way on all platforms.

**Alternative 2: Keep aggressive trimming and update snapshots** - Would make snapshots fragile and platform-dependent. Tests would be less meaningful because they'd accept different outputs on different platforms.

**This fix (minimal trimming)** - Preserves the actual terminal screen content as rendered by vt100, ensuring tests verify the same behavior across platforms. The blank lines are intentional - they're part of the TUI preview panel layout.

## Testing

All tests pass locally on Linux:

```bash
cargo insta test --test-runner nextest --dnd --check --features shell-integration-tests
# ✓ 2397 tests passed
```

title: docs(hooks): add -sTCP:LISTEN to lsof in hook examples
body:
After being surprised a couple of times by a random browser tab closing when removing a worktree, I tracked it down to the `lsof` invocation in the hook examples.

   Without `-sTCP:LISTEN`, `lsof -ti :PORT` matches **any** process with a connection to that port — including browsers with an open tab to `localhost:PORT`. So the `xargs kill` was taking out the browser process along with the dev server.

   Adding `-sTCP:LISTEN` restricts the match to processes that are actually **listening** on the port (i.e., the dev server itself), leaving clients alone.
   
   I can't think of a case where using `-sTCP:LISTEN` would be worse than the current behavior, but I might be missing some edge case

   ## Changes

   - Added `-sTCP:LISTEN` flag to all `lsof` invocations in hook examples and project config"

title: fix: 3 bugs found via adversarial testing
body:
## Summary

- **Shell escape corruption with template filters**: Shell escaping was applied before minijinja rendering, so filters like `sanitize` corrupted already-escaped strings. Fixed by using `set_formatter` to escape at output time.
- **AlreadyAt corrupts switch history**: `set_switch_previous` was called unconditionally, so `wt switch foo` while already in `foo` broke `wt switch -` ping-pong. Fixed by gating on `!already_at_worktree`.
- **`--base` resolved before `--create` check**: `resolve_worktree_name(base_str)` ran before checking `!create`, producing errors instead of the expected warning. Fixed by checking `!create` first.

## Test plan

- [x] 475 unit tests pass

title: fix(ci): exclude api.star-history.com from link checks
body:
## Problem

The `lychee-system` link checker is failing in CI with a 503 Service Unavailable error from `https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=max-sixty/worktrunk&type=Date`.

This is a transient external service failure, not a broken link. The star-history API has reliability issues and should not cause CI failures when it's temporarily down.

## Solution

Added `api.star-history.com` to the lychee exclude list in `.config/lychee.toml`, alongside other sites with reliability issues in CI like stackoverflow.com, npmjs.com, and git-scm.com.

This is the right level to fix the issue because:
- The service reliability issue is documented as a pattern (multiple sites already excluded for this reason)
- The star history chart is a nice-to-have visual element, not a critical link
- Failing CI on external service downtime blocks legitimate development work

## Alternatives considered

Could add more aggressive retry logic or increase timeouts, but this would:
- Slow down CI for all runs
- Still fail if the service is down for extended periods
- Not address the fundamental issue that external service availability shouldn't block CI

The exclude approach is consistent with how we handle other unreliable third-party services.

## Testing

Verified the configuration file syntax is correct and the pattern matches the failing URL.

CI will verify that lychee-system now passes with this exclusion in place.

title: chore: update GitHub Actions and Rust nightly versions
body:
## Summary
Weekly CI renovation check found the following updates:

**GitHub Actions:**
- `astral-sh/setup-uv`: v7 → v7.2.1
- `codecov/test-results-action`: v1 → v1.2.1
- `codecov/codecov-action`: v5 → v5.5.2
- `clechasseur/rs-cargo`: v4 → v4.0.1
- `taiki-e/install-action`: v2 → v2.67.18

**Rust nightly:**
- Updated from `nightly-2025-11-10` to `nightly-2026-01-15` for cargo-udeps compatibility

## Changes
- Updated pinned action versions in `ci.yaml` and `publish-docs.yaml`
- Updated Rust nightly version in check-unused-dependencies job

## Notes
- Runner versions remain correctly pinned to current `-latest` equivalents:
  - `ubuntu-24.04` matches `ubuntu-latest` (migrated Jan 2025)
  - `macos-15` matches `macos-latest` (migrated Sept 2025)
  - `windows-2022` remains pinned due to [D: drive issues](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/12677) in windows-2025
- All other GitHub Actions already at latest versions (actions/checkout@v6, actions/cache@v5, etc.)

---
🤖 Automated weekly renovation
author: worktrunk-bot
diff:
--- .github/workflows/ci.yaml (+5/-5)
@@ -89,7 +89,7 @@ jobs:
       shell: pwsh
 
     - name: Install uv
-      uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
+      uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7.2.1
       with:
         # Silence "no file matched" warning; uv is only used to install pre-commit
         cache-dependency-glob: ".pre-commit-config.yaml"
@@ -121,7 +121,7 @@ jobs:
 
     - name: 📊 Upload test results to Codecov
       if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.repository_owner == 'max-sixty' }}
-      uses: codecov/test-results-action@v1
+      uses: codecov/test-results-action@v1.2.1
       with:
         token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
         files: target/nextest/default/junit.xml
@@ -173,7 +173,7 @@ jobs:
       uses: actions/checkout@v6
 
     # cargo-udeps requires nightly; update date periodically
-    - run: rustup override set nightly-2025-11-10
+    - run: rustup override set nightly-2026-01-15
 
     - name: 💰 Cache
       uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
@@ -182,7 +182,7 @@ jobs:
       with:
         crate: cargo-udeps
 
-    - uses: clechasseur/rs-cargo@v4
+    - uses: clechasseur/rs-cargo@v4.0.1
       with:
         command: udeps
         args: --all-targets
@@ -251,7 +251,7 @@ jobs:
     - name: Upload to codecov.io
       # Codecov action raises errors on forks; allow running on PRs to main repo
       if: github.repository_owner == 'max-sixty'
-      uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5
+      uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5.5.2
       with:
         files: cobertura.xml
         fail_ci_if_error: true
--- .github/workflows/publish-docs.yaml (+1/-1)
@@ -22,7 +22,7 @@ jobs:
         uses: actions/checkout@v6
 
       - name: Setup Zola
-        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
+        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.67.18
         with:
           tool: zola@0.21.0

title: Unify background hook output into single line
body:
## Summary

- Combine contiguous post-switch and post-start hooks into a single output line when both are present (common in `wt switch --create`)
- Drop redundant "hooks" word from output, move path to end
- Old format showed 2 lines, new format shows 1 line

**Before:**
```
◎ Running post-switch hooks @ ~/repo.feature: user:foo
◎ Running post-start hooks @ ~/repo.feature: project:bar
```

**After:**
```
◎ Running post-switch: user:foo; post-start: project:bar @ ~/repo.feature
```

## Test plan

- [x] Added `test_switch_combined_post_switch_and_post_start_hooks` verifying combined format
- [x] Updated ~20 snapshot files with new output format
- [x] All integration tests pass (996 tests)
- [x] Shell integration tests pass (1112 tests)
- [x] `wt hook pre-merge --yes` passes

title: test(templates): add tests for prefix stripping with built-in Jinja
body:
## Summary

- Add test demonstrating that minijinja's built-in `replace` filter and slicing syntax can strip prefixes from branch names
- Documents native Jinja solutions for the use case in #900 without requiring custom filters

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test test_expand_template_strip_prefix` passes
- [x] Pre-commit checks pass

Closes #900

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of @max-sixty_
author: max-sixty
diff:
--- src/config/expansion.rs (+81/-0)
@@ -608,6 +608,87 @@ mod tests {
         );
     }
 
+    #[test]
+    fn test_expand_template_strip_prefix() {
+        let test = test_repo();
+        let mut vars = HashMap::new();
+
+        // Built-in replace filter strips prefix (replaces all occurrences)
+        vars.insert("branch", "feature/foo");
+        assert_eq!(
+            expand_template(
+                "{{ branch | replace('feature/', '') }}",
+                &vars,
+                false,
+                &test.repo,
+                "test"
+            )
+            .unwrap(),
+            "foo"
+        );
+
+        // Replace + sanitize for worktree paths
+        assert_eq!(
+            expand_template(
+                "{{ branch | replace('feature/', '') | sanitize }}",
+                &vars,
+                false,
+                &test.repo,
+                "test"
+            )
+            .unwrap(),
+            "foo"
+        );
+
+        // Branch without prefix passes through unchanged
+        vars.insert("branch", "main");
+        assert_eq!(
+            expand_template(
+                "{{ branch | replace('feature/', '') }}",
+                &vars,
+                false,
+                &test.repo,
+                "test"
+            )
+            .unwrap(),
+            "main"
+        );
+
+        // Slicing for prefix-only removal (avoids replacing mid-string)
+        vars.insert("branch", "feature/nested/feature/deep");
+        assert_eq!(
+            expand_template("{{ branch[8:] }}", &vars, false, &test.repo, "test").unwrap(),
+            "nested/feature/deep"
+        );
+
+        // Conditional slicing for safe prefix removal
+        assert_eq!(
+            expand_template(
+                "{% if branch[:8] == 'feature/' %}{{ branch[8:] }}{% else %}{{ branch }}{% endif %}",
+                &vars,
+                false,
+                &test.repo,
+                "test"
+            )
+            .unwrap(),
+            "nested/feature/deep"
+        );

title: refactor(config): eliminate Settings types, add accessor methods to Config types
body:
## Summary

- Replace parallel Settings type hierarchy with accessor methods on Config types
- Rename `EffectiveConfig` → `ResolvedConfig`, `effective()` → `resolved()`

## Before

```
ListConfig (Options) → ListSettings (concrete) → EffectiveConfig
MergeConfig          → MergeSettings           →
CommitConfig         → CommitSettings          →
SelectConfig         → SelectSettings          →
```

## After

```
ListConfig (with .full(), .branches() etc) → ResolvedConfig
MergeConfig (with .squash(), .commit() etc) →
CommitConfig (with .stage())                →
SelectConfig (with .pager())                →
```

Config types now do double duty:
1. **Serde**: `Option<T>` fields for parsing/merging
2. **Runtime**: Accessor methods return concrete values with defaults

Call sites change from field access to method calls:
```rust
// Before
resolved.merge.squash

// After  
resolved.merge.squash()
```

title: docs(relocate): document main worktree behavior
body:
## Summary

- Adds documentation explaining the behavioral difference when relocating the main worktree vs linked worktrees
- Main worktree can't use `git worktree move`, so relocate switches to the default branch and creates a new linked worktree
- Documents that untracked and gitignored files remain at the original location

+## Main worktree behavior
+
+The main worktree can't be moved with `git worktree move`. Instead, relocate
+switches it to the default branch and creates a new linked worktree at the
+expected path. Untracked and gitignored files remain at the original location.

title: fix(ci): use compile-time binary path for nextest compatibility
body:
## Summary

- Replace `get_cargo_bin("wt")` (runtime lookup) with `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_wt")` (compile-time macro) via a new `wt_bin()` helper
- Remove the `cargo build --bin wt` workaround from the pre-merge hook

## Problem

Tests using `insta_cmd::get_cargo_bin("wt")` were failing on CI because `cargo nextest` doesn't build the main binary—only test binaries. The runtime lookup would fall back to searching `target/debug/wt`, which didn't exist.

## Solution

Use `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_wt")` instead. This compile-time macro tells Cargo that the tests depend on the binary, so Cargo builds it automatically when compiling tests. Works with both `cargo test` and `cargo nextest`.

- [x] `test_switch_with_execute_through_wrapper` passes with nextest
- [x] All 74 shell_wrapper tests pass
- [x] Lints pass

title: refactor(config): split user.rs into focused module files
body:
## Summary

Split the large `src/config/user.rs` (3217 lines) into a module directory with 9 focused files averaging ~200 lines each:

| File | Lines | Purpose |
|------|-------|---------|
| `mod.rs` | 186 | UserConfig struct, load(), re-exports |
| `sections.rs` | 374 | Config section structs with Merge impls |
| `accessors.rs` | 167 | Project-aware getters (commit_generation, list, hooks, etc.) |
| `mutation.rs` | 277 | Mutation methods with file locking |
| `persistence.rs` | 393 | Save methods, TOML formatting, validation |
| `path.rs` | 54 | Config path management |
| `schema.rs` | 43 | Schema helpers for unknown key detection |
| `merge.rs` | 28 | Merge trait definition |
| `tests.rs` | 1846 | All unit tests |

This improves maintainability by separating concerns: data structures, query methods, mutation methods, I/O, and tests.

**No public API changes** - all existing exports remain available through `config/mod.rs`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --lib --bins` - 466 unit tests pass
- [x] `cargo test --test integration` - 986 integration tests pass
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` - all lints pass
- [x] No warnings

+//! Project-aware configuration accessors.
+//!
+//! These methods on `UserConfig` return the effective configuration for a given
+//! project by merging global settings with project-specific overrides.
+
+use crate::config::HooksConfig;
+
+use super::UserConfig;
+use super::merge::{Merge, merge_optional};
+use super::sections::{
+    CommitConfig, CommitGenerationConfig, ListConfig, MergeConfig, SelectConfig,
+};
+
+use crate::config::expansion::expand_template;
+
+/// Default worktree path template
+fn default_worktree_path() -> String {
+    "../{{ repo }}.{{ branch | sanitize }}".to_string()
+}
+
+impl UserConfig {
+    /// Returns the worktree path template, falling back to the default if not set.
+    pub fn worktree_path(&self) -> String {
+        self.configs
+            .worktree_path
+            .clone()
+            .unwrap_or_else(default_worktree_path)
+    }
+
+    /// Returns true if the user has explicitly set a custom worktree-path.
+    pub fn has_custom_worktree_path(&self) -> bool {
+        self.configs.worktree_path.is_some()
+    }
+
+    /// Returns the worktree path template for a specific project.
+    ///
+    /// Checks project-specific config first, falls back to global worktree-path,
+    /// and finally to the default template if neither is set.
+    pub fn worktree_path_for_project(&self, project: &str) -> String {
+        self.projects
+            .get(project)
+            .and_then(|p| p.overrides.worktree_path.clone())
+            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.worktree_path())
+    }
+
+    /// Returns the commit generation config for a specific project.
+    ///
+    /// Merges project-specific settings with global settings, where project
+    /// settings take precedence for fields that are set.
+    ///
+    /// Checks locations in order of precedence:
+    /// 1. `[commit.generation]` (new format)
+    /// 2. `[commit-generation]` (deprecated format)
+    /// 3. Per-project overrides
+    pub fn commit_generation(&self, project: Option<&str>) -> CommitGenerationConfig {
+        // Get global config: prefer new location, fall back to deprecated
+        let global = self
+            .configs
+            .commit
+            .as_ref()
+            .and_then(|c| c.generation.as_ref())
+            .or(self.commit_generation.as_ref())
+            .cloned()
+            .unwrap_or_default();
+
+        // Get project override (also checks both locations)
+        let project_config = project.and_then(|p| self.projects.get(p)).and_then(|c| {
+            c.overrides
+                .commit
+                .as_ref()
+                .and_then(|cc| cc.generation.as_ref())
+                .or(c.commit_generation.as_ref())
+        });
+
+        match project_config {
+            Some(pc) => global.merge_with(pc),
+            None => global,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Returns the list config for a specific project.
+    ///
+    /// Merges project-specific settings with global settings, where project
+    /// settings take precedence for fields that are set.
+    pub fn list(&self, project: Option<&str>) -> Option<ListConfig> {
+        let project_config = project
+            .and_then(|p| self.projects.get(p))
+            .and_then(|c| c.overrides.list.as_ref());
+        merge_optional(self.configs.list.as_ref(), project_config)
+    }
+
+    /// Returns the commit config for a specific project.
+    ///
+    /// Merges project-specific settings with global settings, where project
+    /// settings take precedence for fields that are set.
+    pub fn commit(&self, project: Option<&str>) -> Option<CommitConfig> {
+        let project_config = project
+            .and_then(|p| self.projects.get(p))
+            .and_then(|c| c.overrides.commit.as_ref());
+        merge_optional(self.configs.commit.as_ref(), project_config)
+    }
+
+    /// Returns the merge config for a specific project.
+    ///
+    /// Merges project-specific settings with global settings, where project
+    /// settings take precedence for fields that are set.
+    pub fn merge(&self, project: Option<&str>) -> Option<MergeConfig> {
+        let project_config = project
+            .and_then(|p| self.projects.get(p))
+            .and_then(|c| c.overrides.merge.as_ref());
+        merge_optional(self.configs.merge.as_ref(), project_config)
+    }
+
+    /// Returns the select config for a specific project.
+    ///
+    /// Merges project-specific settings with global settings, where project
+    /// settings take precedence for fields that are set.
+    pub fn select(&self, project: Option<&str>) -> Option<SelectConfig> {
+        let project_config = project
+            .and_then(|p| self.projects.get(p))
+            .and_then(|c| c.overrides.select.as_ref());
+        merge_optional(self.configs.select.as_ref(), project_config)
+    }
+
+    /// Returns effective hooks for a specific project.
+    ///
+    /// Merges global hooks with per-project hooks using append semantics.
+    /// Both global and per-project hooks run (global first, then per-project).
+    pub fn hooks(&self, project: Option<&str>) -> HooksConfig {
+        let global = &self.configs.hooks;
+        let project_hooks = project
+            .and_then(|p| self.projects.get(p))
+            .map(|c| &c.overrides.hooks);
+
+        match project_hooks {
+            Some(ph) => global.merge_with(ph),
+            None => global.clone(),
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Format a worktree path using this configuration's template.
+    ///
+    /// # Arguments
+    /// * `main_worktree` - Main worktree directory name (replaces {{ main_worktree }} in template)
+    /// * `branch` - Branch name (replaces {{ branch }} in template; use `{{ branch | sanitize }}` for paths)
+    /// * `repo` - Repository for template function access
+    /// * `project` - Optional project identifier (e.g., "github.com/user/repo") to look up
+    ///   project-specific worktree-path template
+    pub fn format_path(
+        &self,
+        main_worktree: &str,
+        branch: &str,
+        repo: &crate::git::Repository,
+        project: Option<&str>,
+    ) -> Result<String, String> {
+        use std::collections::HashMap;
+        let template = match project {
+            Some(p) => self.worktree_path_for_project(p),
+            None => self.worktree_path(),
+        };
+        let mut vars = HashMap::new();
+        vars.insert("main_worktree", main_worktree);
+        vars.insert("repo", main_worktree);
+        vars.insert("branch", branch);
+        expand_template(&template, &vars, false, repo, "worktree-path")
+    }
+}

+//! Merge trait for configuration layering.
+//!
+//! Provides the mechanism for project-specific config to override global config,
+//! where unset fields fall back to the global value.
+
+/// Trait for merging configuration structs.
+///
+/// Project-specific config fields override global fields when set.
+/// Fields that are `None` in the override fall back to the base value.
+pub trait Merge {
+    /// Merge with another config, where `other` takes precedence for set fields.
+    fn merge_with(&self, other: &Self) -> Self;
+}
+
+/// Merge optional global and project configs, returning the effective config.
+///
+/// - Both set: merge (project takes precedence for set fields)
+/// - Only project set: clone project
+/// - Only global set: clone global
+/// - Neither set: None
+pub fn merge_optional<T: Merge + Clone>(global: Option<&T>, project: Option<&T>) -> Option<T> {
+    match (global, project) {
+        (Some(g), Some(p)) => Some(g.merge_with(p)),
+        (None, Some(p)) => Some(p.clone()),
+        (Some(g), None) => Some(g.clone()),
+        (None, None) => None,
+    }

title: chore(ci): pin runner versions and add weekly renovation workflow
body:
## Summary

- Pin all GitHub Actions runners to specific versions instead of `-latest` labels
- Use stable job names (`test (linux)`, `test (macos)`, `test (windows)`) so branch protection doesn't need updating when versions change
- Add weekly `claude-renovate` workflow to check for dependency updates

## Changes

**Runner pinning:**
- `ubuntu-latest` → `ubuntu-24.04`
- `macos-latest` → `macos-15`
- `windows-2022` stays pinned (Windows 2025 lacks D: drive per [actions/runner-images#12677](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/12677))

**Stable job names:**
- Test jobs now use platform names (`linux`, `macos`, `windows`) instead of version numbers
- Branch protection updated to match

**New workflow:**
- `claude-renovate.yaml` runs weekly (Sundays 9:17 UTC) to check for:
  - Runner version updates (comparing pinned vs current `-latest`)
  - GitHub Actions version updates
  - Rust nightly version updates for cargo-udeps
- Creates PRs automatically when updates are available

## Test plan

- [x] CI passes on all platforms
- [x] Branch protection updated to use new job names

+name: claude-renovate
+
+# Weekly renovation check - reviews CI dependencies and creates PRs for updates
+on:
+  schedule:
+    # Run at 9:17 AM UTC every Sunday (off-peak minute)
+    - cron: '17 9 * * 0'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+# Consistent with ci.yaml for cache compatibility
+env:
+  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
+  CLICOLOR_FORCE: 1
+  RUSTFLAGS: "-C debuginfo=0"
+  RUSTDOCFLAGS: "-Dwarnings"
+
+jobs:
+  renovate:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+      pull-requests: write
+      actions: read
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - name: 📂 Checkout code
+        uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          ref: main
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          fetch-tags: true
+          token: ${{ secrets.WORKTRUNK_BOT_TOKEN }}
+
+      - name: 🔧 Configure git for Claude
+        run: |
+          git config --global user.name "Claude Code"
+          git config --global user.email "claude@anthropic.com"
+
+      - name: 💰 Cache
+        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
+        with:
+          prefix-key: ${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
+          save-if: false
+
+      - name: 🤖 Run Claude Code for renovation
+        id: claude
+        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
+        with:
+          model: opus
+          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
+          github_token: ${{ secrets.WORKTRUNK_BOT_TOKEN }}
+          additional_permissions: |
+            actions: read
+
+          prompt: |
+            SECURITY: NEVER run commands that could expose secrets (env, printenv, set, export, cat/echo on config files containing credentials). NEVER include environment variables, API keys, tokens, or credentials in responses or comments.
+
+            You are running as part of a weekly renovation workflow. Your job is to check for updates to CI dependencies and create PRs if updates are available.
+
+            ## What to check
+
+            1. **GitHub Actions runner versions**:
+               - Check what the current `-latest` labels resolve to:
+                 - `ubuntu-latest` - what Ubuntu version?
+                 - `macos-latest` - what macOS version?
+                 - `windows-latest` - what Windows version?
+               - Compare against what we have pinned in our workflow files
+               - Note: `windows-latest` has D: drive issues (actions/runner-images#12677), so stay on windows-2022
+
+            2. **GitHub Actions versions**:
+               - Check for updates to actions we use (actions/checkout, actions/cache, etc.)
+               - Look at the current versions in .github/workflows/*.yaml
+               - Check if newer versions are available
+
+            3. **Rust nightly version** (in check-unused-dependencies job):
+               - We pin a specific nightly for cargo-udeps (check the actual version in ci.yaml)
+               - Periodically update to a recent nightly that works with cargo-udeps
+
+            ## How to check
+

title: fix(ci): use windows-2022 instead of windows-latest
body:
## Problem
The CI test job on Windows is failing with the error:
```
##[error]Could not find a part of the path 'D:\a'.
```

This is caused by GitHub Actions' migration of `windows-latest` from Windows Server 2022 to Windows Server 2025. The new Windows 2025 images **no longer have a D: drive**, which breaks workflows that rely on the traditional `D:\a\` working directory structure.

The migration rolled out between September 2-30, 2025, and is now complete.

## Solution
Pin the test matrix to `windows-2022` instead of `windows-latest`. This ensures consistent behavior and avoids the breaking change introduced by Windows Server 2025 images.

Windows Server 2022 will continue to receive support for three additional years, giving us time to evaluate whether to migrate to Windows 2025 (and adjust for the C-drive-only environment) or to continue using Windows 2022.

## Alternatives considered
1. **Keep windows-latest and adapt to C-drive-only environment**: Would require investigating what's trying to use the D: drive and changing it to use C: drive instead. However, since the error occurs during job setup (before our code even runs), this is likely a GitHub Actions infrastructure issue that we can't directly control.

2. **Migrate to windows-2025 explicitly**: Could work, but requires more investigation into what's failing and whether it's something we can fix or if it's a GitHub Actions runner issue.

3. **Use windows-2022 (chosen approach)**: This is the safest fix - it maintains the current working environment and gives us time to properly evaluate the Windows 2025 migration when we have more information about what's causing the D: drive access.

## Testing
The fix can be verified by checking that the Windows test job completes successfully on this PR's CI run.

## References
- [GitHub Actions Windows-latest migration issue #12677](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/12677)
- Windows Server 2025 key change: D: drive removed (only C: drive available)

title: fix(tests): strip OSC 8 hyperlinks in select test output normalization
body:
## Problem

The `test_select_preview_panel_main_diff` integration test was failing on macOS (run [#21373466012](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/21373466012)) but passing on Linux. The failure showed extra lines appearing in the snapshot diff:

```diff
-27       │-                                                            │+    assert_eq!(42 * 2, 84);
+     27 │+                                                            │+    assert_eq!(42 * 2, 84);
+     28 │+
+     29 │+^D
```

**Root cause**: macOS git (and potentially other platforms with newer git versions) generates OSC 8 terminal hyperlinks in diff output. The vt100 parser used in PTY-based tests passes these through as raw escape sequences, which then appear as garbage characters (like `^D`) in the rendered terminal output. This was introduced by the recent upgrade to clap 4.5.28+ which added OSC 8 hyperlink support—git itself may also be generating these sequences in diff output on platforms with newer git versions.

## Solution

Added `strip_osc8_hyperlinks()` to the test's `normalize_output()` function in `tests/integration_tests/select.rs`. This function uses the same logic as `src/help.rs::strip_osc8_hyperlinks()` to remove OSC 8 hyperlink sequences while preserving other ANSI codes and the visible link text.

This is the right level to fix because:
- **Shared test infrastructure**: The `normalize_output()` helper is used by all select tests to ensure snapshot stability across environments
- **Platform consistency**: Tests should produce the same output regardless of whether the underlying tools (git, terminal emulator) generate hyperlinks
- **Single point of normalization**: All platform-specific output variations should be normalized in this shared helper

## Alternatives considered

1. **Fix only this specific test**: Could have added OSC 8 stripping just for `test_select_preview_panel_main_diff`, but that would mean other tests could fail with the same issue if git output changes.

2. **Update the snapshot to include the OSC 8 sequences**: This would make snapshots platform-specific and harder to maintain, defeating the purpose of the normalization layer.

3. **Configure git to disable hyperlinks**: There's no reliable way to disable OSC 8 generation at runtime in modern git—it depends on terminal capabilities detection which we can't easily override in tests.

Fixing the shared helper prevents similar issues across all tests that render git output through PTY emulation.

## Testing

- Verified test passes on Linux (already passing before)
- macOS CI will verify the fix resolves the failure

+def extract_commands_from_tape(
+    tape_path: Path, repo_root: Path, command_prefixes: tuple[str, ...] = ("wt", "git")
+) -> list[str]:
+    """Extract shell commands from a VHS tape file.
+
+    Parses the tape looking for Type "command" followed by Enter patterns,
+    filtering to commands that start with specified prefixes (default: wt, git).
+
+    Only extracts commands after Show directive (visible part of demo).
+    Skips commands in Hide blocks.
+
+    Args:
+        tape_path: Path to the .tape template file
+        repo_root: Root of the repository (for resolving Source paths)
+        command_prefixes: Tuple of command prefixes to extract (default: wt, git)
+
+    Returns:
+        List of commands in order they appear in the tape
+    """
+    # Render tape with dummy replacements to inline Source directives
+    rendered = render_tape(tape_path, {}, repo_root)
+    if not rendered:
+        return []
+
+    commands = []
+    in_visible_section = False
+    lines = rendered.split("\n")
+    i = 0
+
+    while i < len(lines):
+        line = lines[i].strip()
+
+        # Track visibility
+        if line == "Show":
+            in_visible_section = True
+        elif line == "Hide":
+            in_visible_section = False
+
+        # Look for Type "command" pattern
+        if in_visible_section and line.startswith("Type "):
+            # Extract command from Type "..." or Type '...'
+            match = re.match(r'Type\s+["\'](.+)["\']', line)
+            if match:
+                cmd = match.group(1)
+                # Check if Enter follows (possibly with Sleep in between)
+                j = i + 1
+                while j < len(lines):
+                    next_line = lines[j].strip()
+                    if not next_line:
+                        j += 1
+                        continue
+                    if next_line.startswith("Sleep "):
+                        j += 1
+                        continue
+                    if next_line == "Enter":
+                        # Only include commands with specified prefixes
+                        if any(cmd.startswith(prefix) for prefix in command_prefixes):
+                            commands.append(cmd)
+                    break
+        i += 1
+
+    return commands
+
+
+def record_snapshot(
+    demo_env: "DemoEnv",
+    tape_path: Path,
+    output_snap: Path,
+    repo_root: Path,
+) -> None:
+    """Record command output snapshot for regression testing.
+
+    Extracts commands from the tape and runs them in a fish shell with full
+    shell integration (just like the GIF demos). The snapshot format is:
+
+        $ wt list
+        <output>
+
+        $ wt switch alpha
+        <output>
+
+    This captures semantic output (what commands produce) rather than visual
+    rendering (how it looks in a terminal). Small diffs are expected when
+    output formats change; the goal is catching unexpected regressions like
+    new hints or warnings creeping in.
+
+    Args:
+        demo_env: Demo environment with repo and home paths
+        tape_path: Path to the .tape template file
+        output_snap: Path to write snapshot output
+        repo_root: Root of the repository
+
+    Raises:
+        RuntimeError: If no commands found in tape
+    """
+    commands = extract_commands_from_tape(tape_path, repo_root)
+    if not commands:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"No snapshotable commands found in {tape_path.name}")
+
+    # Build environment matching the GIF demos
+    env = os.environ.copy()
+    env.update(
+        {
+            "HOME": str(demo_env.home),
+            "XDG_CONFIG_HOME": str(demo_env.home / ".config"),
+            "PATH": f"{repo_root / 'target' / 'debug'}:{demo_env.home / '.local' / 'bin'}:{os.environ.get('PATH', '')}",
+            "TERM": "xterm-256color",
+            "LANG": "en_US.UTF-8",
+            "LC_ALL": "en_US.UTF-8",
+        }
+    )
+
+    # Generate a fish script that:
+    # 1. Initializes shell integration (like shared-commands.tape)
+    # 2. Runs each command, printing "$ cmd" before and blank line after
+    script_lines = [
+        "# Initialize shell integration",
+        "wt config shell init fish | source",
+        "source ~/.config/fish/completions/wt.fish",
+        f"cd {demo_env.repo}",
+        "",
+    ]
+
+    for i, cmd in enumerate(commands):
+        # Echo the command prompt, run command (merging stderr)
+        script_lines.append(f"echo '$ {cmd}'")
+        script_lines.append(f"{cmd} 2>&1")
+        # Blank line between commands (not after last)
+        if i < len(commands) - 1:
+            script_lines.append("echo ''")
+
+    script_content = "\n".join(script_lines)
+    script_path = demo_env.out_dir / ".snapshot-script.fish"
+    script_path.write_text(script_content)
+
+    # Run the script in fish
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        ["fish", str(script_path)],
+        env=env,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+    )
+
+    # Combine stdout and stderr
+    output = (result.stdout + result.stderr).rstrip()
+
+    # Normalize temp paths to stable placeholder
+    temp_path = str(demo_env.out_dir)
+    temp_path_real = str(demo_env.out_dir.resolve())
+    output = output.replace(temp_path_real, "<DEMO_DIR>")
+    output = output.replace(temp_path, "<DEMO_DIR>")
+
+    # Write snapshot
+    output_snap.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    output_snap.write_text(output + "\n")
+

title: fix(demos): suppress hints and fix parallel download race
body:
## Summary

- Suppress "To customize worktree locations..." hint in demo recordings by pre-marking it as shown in git config
- Fix parallel download race condition when multiple demo builds run simultaneously

## Details

The demos were showing hints like "To customize worktree locations, run wt config create" which added visual noise. This pre-marks the hint as shown during demo repo setup.

Also includes a fix for a race condition in the Claude binary download - when running demos in parallel, multiple processes could try to rename `.tmp` to the final destination simultaneously, causing failures.

## Test plan

- [x] Rebuilt all demos with hint suppressed
- [x] Verified hint no longer appears in demo output
- [x] Published updated assets to worktrunk-assets

title: fix(test): update PTY filter to handle optional ANSI codes
body:
## Problem

The `test_install_preview_with_gutter` test started failing on macOS CI after commit 020b790c switched to anstream for TTY-aware output.

The test uses a regex filter to remove echoed user input from PTY output:
```rust
settings.add_filter(r"(\[y/N/\?\]\x1b\[22m) [yn]", "$1 ");
```

This filter expected the ANSI reset code `\x1b[22m` after `[y/N/?]`, but anstream strips ANSI codes in non-TTY environments (when TERM isn't set, which is common in CI test environments).

On macOS CI, the actual output is:
```
❯ Install shell integration? [y/N/?] y
```

But the filter only matched:
```
❯ Install shell integration? [y/N/?]\x1b[22m y
```

So the echoed `y` wasn't being filtered out, causing the snapshot comparison to fail.

## Solution

Update the regex filter to make the ANSI code optional:
```rust
settings.add_filter(r"(\[y/N/\?\](?:\x1b\[22m)?) [yn]", "$1 ");
```

This handles both cases:
- **With ANSI codes** (TTY environment): `[y/N/?]\x1b[22m y` → `[y/N/?]\x1b[22m `
- **Without ANSI codes** (non-TTY): `[y/N/?] y` → `[y/N/?] `

## Alternatives considered

Could have updated the snapshot to expect the echoed `y`, but that would make the snapshot fragile to PTY echo timing variations (which is exactly what the filter was designed to handle).

The filter-based approach is more robust because it normalizes timing-dependent PTY behavior across different platforms and environments.

## Testing

Verified locally:
```bash
cargo test --test integration 'integration_tests::configure_shell::pty_tests::test_install_preview' --features shell-integration-tests
```

Both tests pass:
- `test_install_preview_with_gutter`
- `test_install_preview_declined`

+/// Regression test for issue #839: untracked files not deleted on Windows.
+/// Verifies the worktree directory is actually removed, not just that the command succeeds.
+#[rstest]
+fn test_remove_force_actually_deletes_directory_with_untracked(mut repo: TestRepo) {
+    let worktree_path = repo.add_worktree("feature-untracked-delete");
+
+    // Make a commit so the branch is ahead of main (unmerged)
+    repo.git_command()
+        .args(["commit", "--allow-empty", "-m", "feature commit"])
+        .current_dir(&worktree_path)
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+
+    // Create untracked files (the scenario from issue #839)
+    std::fs::write(worktree_path.join("untracked.txt"), "untracked content").unwrap();
+    std::fs::create_dir_all(worktree_path.join("untracked_dir")).unwrap();
+    std::fs::write(
+        worktree_path.join("untracked_dir/nested.txt"),
+        "nested untracked",
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+
+    // Verify worktree exists before removal
+    assert!(
+        worktree_path.exists(),
+        "Worktree should exist before removal"
+    );
+
+    // Remove with --force -D (the flags from issue #839)
+    let output = repo
+        .wt_command()
+        .args([
+            "remove",
+            "--force",
+            "-D",
+            "--foreground",
+            "feature-untracked-delete",
+        ])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+
+    assert!(
+        output.status.success(),
+        "wt remove --force -D should succeed, stderr: {}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
+    );
+
+    // The critical assertion: directory must actually be gone
+    assert!(
+        !worktree_path.exists(),
+        "Worktree directory should be deleted after `wt remove --force -D`, but it still exists"
+    );
+
+    // Verify branch is also deleted
+    let branch_list = repo
+        .git_command()
+        .args(["branch", "--list", "feature-untracked-delete"])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&branch_list.stdout)
+            .trim()
+            .is_empty(),
+        "Branch should be deleted with -D flag"
+    );
+}

title: refactor: simplify deprecation migration file logic
body:
## Summary

Simplify deprecation migration file deduplication from hint-based to file-existence based:

- Migration file write skipped if `.new` file already exists (instead of checking git config hint)
- `wt config show` always regenerates (bypasses the skip via `show_brief_warning=false`)
- Removed `user_deleted_migration` field and "To regenerate..." hint
- Hint is cleared when config is fixed, so future deprecations get full treatment

## Behavior

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| First deprecation warning | Writes `.new` file automatically |
| Subsequent commands | Skips write if `.new` exists, shows brief warning |
| `wt config show` | Always regenerates `.new` file |
| User deletes `.new` file | Regenerates on next command run |

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --test integration deprecated` - all deprecation tests pass
- [x] `test_user_config_deprecated_variables_deduplication` - verifies file-existence deduplication
- [x] `test_wt_list_skips_migration_file_after_first_write` - verifies skip behavior
- [x] `test_deleted_migration_file_regenerated` - verifies regeneration when file deleted

title: fix: prevent spurious [commit] header in config migration
body:
## Summary
- Fixes bug where config migration created spurious `[commit]` section header at end of file
- Uses `set_implicit(true)` to suppress empty parent table headers in toml_edit
- Adds snapshot tests showing unified diffs of migration output

## Test plan

- [x] Integration tests pass (939 tests)
- [x] Verified fix on actual user config file

-            // Ensure [commit] section exists
+            // Ensure [commit] section exists.
+            // Mark as implicit so it doesn't render a separate [commit] header
+            // (only [commit.generation] will render)
             if !doc.contains_key("commit") {
-                doc["commit"] = toml_edit::Item::Table(toml_edit::Table::new());

+                commit_table.set_implicit(true);
+                doc.insert("commit", toml_edit::Item::Table(commit_table));
             }

@@ -310,10 +314,12 @@ pub fn migrate_commit_generation_sections(content: &str) -> String {

-                        // Ensure [projects."...".commit] section exists
+                        // Ensure [projects."...".commit] section exists.
+                        // Mark as implicit so it doesn't render a separate header
                         if !project_table.contains_key("commit") {
-                            project_table
-                                .insert("commit", toml_edit::Item::Table(toml_edit::Table::new()));
+                            let mut commit_table = toml_edit::Table::new();

@@ -1615,4 +1621,133 @@ other = "value"
         let result = migrate_commit_generation_sections(content);
         assert_eq!(result, content, "Invalid TOML should be returned unchanged");
     }
+
+    // Snapshot tests for migration output (showing diffs)
+
+    /// Generate a unified diff between original and migrated content
+    fn migration_diff(original: &str, migrated: &str) -> String {
+        use similar::{ChangeTag, TextDiff};
+        let diff = TextDiff::from_lines(original, migrated);
+        let mut output = String::new();
+        for change in diff.iter_all_changes() {
+            let sign = match change.tag() {
+                ChangeTag::Delete => "-",
+                ChangeTag::Insert => "+",
+                ChangeTag::Equal => " ",
+            };
+            output.push_str(&format!("{}{}", sign, change));
+        }
+        output
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn snapshot_migrate_commit_generation_simple() {
+        let content = r#"
+[commit-generation]
+command = "llm -m haiku"
+"#;
+        let result = migrate_commit_generation_sections(content);
+        insta::assert_snapshot!(migration_diff(content, &result));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn snapshot_migrate_commit_generation_with_args() {
+        let content = r#"
+[commit-generation]
+command = "llm"
+args = ["-m", "claude-haiku-4.5"]
+"#;
+        let result = migrate_commit_generation_sections(content);
+        insta::assert_snapshot!(migration_diff(content, &result));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn snapshot_migrate_with_trailing_sections() {
+        // This is the bug case: [commit-generation] in the middle of the file
+        // followed by other sections. The migration should not add an extra
+        // [commit] section at the end.
+        let content = r#"# Config file
+worktree-path = "../{{ repo }}.{{ branch | sanitize }}"
+
+[commit-generation]
+command = "llm"
+args = ["-m", "claude-haiku-4.5"]
+
+[list]
+branches = true
+remotes = false
+"#;
+        let result = migrate_commit_generation_sections(content);
+        insta::assert_snapshot!(migration_diff(content, &result));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn snapshot_migrate_preserves_existing_commit_section() {
+        let content = r#"
+[commit]
+stage = "all"
+
+[commit-generation]
+command = "llm -m haiku"
+"#;
+        let result = migrate_commit_generation_sections(content);
+        insta::assert_snapshot!(migration_diff(content, &result));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn snapshot_migrate_project_level() {
+        let content = r#"
+[projects."github.com/user/repo"]
+approved-commands = ["npm test"]
+
+[projects."github.com/user/repo".commit-generation]
+command = "llm"
+args = ["-m", "gpt-4"]
+"#;
+        let result = migrate_commit_generation_sections(content);
+        insta::assert_snapshot!(migration_diff(content, &result));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn snapshot_migrate_combined_top_and_project() {
+        let content = r#"
+[commit-generation]
+command = "llm -m haiku"
+
+[projects."github.com/user/repo".commit-generation]
+command = "llm -m gpt-4"
+
+[list]
+branches = true
+"#;
+        let result = migrate_commit_generation_sections(content);
+        insta::assert_snapshot!(migration_diff(content, &result));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_set_implicit_suppresses_parent_header() {
+        // Verifies that set_implicit(true) prevents an empty parent table from
+        // rendering its own header. This is the key technique used in
+        // migrate_commit_generation_sections to avoid creating spurious [commit]
+        // headers when migrating [commit-generation] to [commit.generation].
+        use toml_edit::{DocumentMut, Item, Table};
+
+        let mut doc: DocumentMut = "[foo]\nbar = 1\n".parse().unwrap();
+        let mut commit_table = Table::new();
+        commit_table.set_implicit(true);
+        let mut gen_table = Table::new();
+        gen_table.insert("command", toml_edit::value("llm"));
+        commit_table.insert("generation", Item::Table(gen_table));
+        doc.insert("commit", Item::Table(commit_table));
+        let result = doc.to_string();
+
+        assert!(
+            !result.contains("\n[commit]\n"),
+            "set_implicit should suppress separate [commit] header"
+        );
+        assert!(
+            result.contains("[commit.generation]"),
+            "Should have [commit.generation] header"
+        );
+    }
 }

title: feat: add --hook flag to wt config state logs get (#803)
body:
## Summary

- Adds `--hook` flag to `wt config state logs get` to retrieve the path to a specific hook's log file
- Introduces `HookLog` enum as single source of truth for log file naming (used by both log creation and lookup)
- Supports explicit format: `source:hook-type:name` for hooks (e.g., `user:post-start:server`) or `internal:op` for internal operations (e.g., `internal:remove`)

This enables easy log streaming:
```bash
tail -f "$(wt config state logs get --hook=user:post-start:server)"
```

Closes #803

title: refactor: use shell_escape crate instead of manual quote escaping
body:
## Summary

- Replace manual single-quote escaping in `diagnostic.rs` with `shell_escape` crate
- Use `shell_escape::unix::escape` for consistent POSIX-style escaping across platforms
- Normalize Windows paths (backslashes → forward slashes) before escaping for cross-platform consistency
- Add `shell_escape_path()` helper with documentation explaining the rationale

## Why manual escaping elsewhere

The remaining manual escaping in `output/global.rs` and `commands/process.rs` is intentional:
- These generate shell commands for the user's actual shell (bash/zsh/fish/PowerShell)
- PowerShell uses different quote escaping (`''`) than POSIX (`'\''`)
- No Rust crate handles PowerShell escaping — `shell_escape` only supports POSIX and cmd.exe

- [x] Integration test handles both quoted (Windows) and unquoted (Unix) path formats
- [x] All platforms pass (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows)
